- `add a todo: pick up laundry` (not tested in live but covered by
  the predicate) still routes to LIFE because the verb-noun pattern
  doesn't match (`todo` is not in the technical-artifact list).

fix: LIFE validate rejects build-an-app requests + lenient planner action unwrap

Two routing fixes for prompts that the LLM sends to the action router.

## 1. apps/app-lifeops LIFE action rejects coding-task prompts

LIFE's simile list includes `CREATE_TASK` and `COMPLETE_TASK`
(matches LifeOps users who say "add a task: pick up laundry"). That
collides with plugin-agent-orchestrator's `CREATE_TASK` action
(name, not simile), so when the LLM emits `CREATE_TASK` for a
build-an-app prompt like "make a pinboard for this haiku" the
router can match LIFE first.

Fix: add `looksLikeCodingTaskRequest` predicate to the existing
non-actionable-request.ts helpers and call it from LIFE's
`validate()`. Narrow pattern: verb (build/make/create/write/deploy/
ship/add/spin up) + technical-artifact noun (app/page/site/tool/
script/api/bot/etc), plus explicit code/git surfaces. When it
matches, LIFE declines so the action router falls through to
CREATE_TASK (orchestrator), whose `looksLikeTaskAgentRequest`
positively matches the same class of prompts.

LIFE similes stay unchanged so LifeOps users keep the "task"
vocabulary. Responsibility split is cleaner: LIFE owns todos/
habits/goals/reminders, orchestrator owns coding subagents.

## 2. packages/typescript unwrapPlannerIdentifier recovers unclosed wrappers

Observed 24 "Dropping unknown planner action" warnings across
recent sessions where the LLM emitted action names like:

    actionName=<action><name>REPLY</name>

without the closing `</action>` tag. The existing three-case
unwrap only handled `<name>X</name>`, `<action>X</action>`, and
fully-closed `<action><name>X</name></action>`. Unclosed form fell
through the final branch and returned the whole XML-ish string as
the action name, which the router then dropped silently. User
message disappeared with no response.

Fix: add a lenient fallback that extracts `<name>X</name>` content
from anywhere in the value when no earlier pattern matched, so
these recovered as valid REPLY / IGNORE / STOP.

## Follows the 5 rules

1. No wrappers. The new predicate is a small focused function
   sitting alongside its siblings in non-actionable-request.ts.
2. Reuses existing normalizer chain in validate(). No new imports
   from outside the app-lifeops package.
3. No new types.
4. No new function parameters.
5. Responsibility split sharpened between LIFE and CREATE_TASK;
   parser unwrap expanded to cover LLM output variants without
   changing the action router's contract.

- `@remilio pull latest from milady repo, polish n8n...`

- `add a todo: pick up laundry` (not tested in live but covered by
  the predicate) still routes to LIFE because the verb-noun pattern
  doesn't match (`todo` is not in the technical-artifact list).

fix: honest synthesis — read subagent end_turn + drop task-heartbeat module

Two runtime cleanups that together let the bot deliver the agent's
actual final answer in chat instead of narrative summaries or
heartbeats that leaked through multiple code paths.

handleSwarmSynthesis's buildTaskLine used to chain:

    jsonl → completionSummary → originalTask-echo

`completionSummary` is the coordinator's validator LLM analysis
paragraph ("The agent wrote the files, verified with curl, and
reported the URL") — NOT the subagent's real end_turn text. When
the jsonl read returned null (see below) buildTaskLine silently
fell through to that narrative, so users asking "build me an app"
got a prose summary instead of the agent's actual
`URL: https://milady.nubs.site/apps/<slug>/` reply.

New chain:

    jsonl (with a brief retry) → port-check → honest placeholder

- Never falls back to task.completionSummary.
- Never echoes task.originalTask (the user's own prompt).
- Adds a 4×500ms retry on the jsonl read. The PTY task_complete
  hook fires as soon as claude-code stops, but the session's
  jsonl flush can lag by a few hundred ms, which races against
  synthesis. Retrying briefly closes that window; we deliver the
  agent's actual end_turn text almost every time. The honest
  placeholder ("task finished but no output was captured — try
  again") is only produced when the agent really wrote nothing.

The heartbeat posted "still working — Xs in (<tool>)" per PTY
session. With the swarm coordinator spawning multiple sessions
per user prompt, the 120s room-level rate limit let each
session's own 45s message through because the gaps between
sessions usually exceed 2 minutes — users saw two "45s in"
messages for the same prompt, sometimes after the actual result
had already landed.

Synthesis (handleSwarmSynthesis) already delivers the final
answer on completion. There is no UX payoff to a mid-task ping
that fires inconsistently and can land after the result. If a
specific long-running action needs a progress indicator, that
belongs inside the action, not as a generic runtime ping.

feat: Docker + Headscale infrastructure layer for Milady sandboxes

Adds a pluggable Docker container + Headscale VPN infrastructure layer
as an alternative sandbox provider for Milady agents. Agents can now run
as Docker containers on remote VPS nodes with WireGuard mesh networking.

## What's included

### Sandbox Provider Abstraction
- SandboxProvider interface + factory (MILADY_SANDBOX_PROVIDER env var)
- VercelSandboxProvider (extracted from inline code, zero behavior change)
- DockerSandboxProvider (full lifecycle: create, stop, health, runCommand)

### Docker Infrastructure
- DockerSSHClient: SSH with connection pooling, keyed on host:port
- DockerSandboxProvider: container lifecycle on remote nodes via SSH,
  DB-backed port allocation (no collisions), health check polling (60s),
  shell-escaped commands, full agentId in container names
- DockerNodeManager: least-loaded placement, health checks, capacity sync
- DB migration 0046: docker_nodes table + 6 new columns on milady_sandboxes

### Headscale VPN
- HeadscaleClient: REST API client for control plane
- HeadscaleIntegration: ephemeral pre-auth keys, VPN lifecycle, cleanup

### Admin API (7 routes, all behind requireAdmin)
- Docker nodes: CRUD, SSH health check
- Docker containers: list, logs, ghost/orphan audit
- Headscale: mesh status, nodes, pre-auth keys

### Admin UI
- Infrastructure dashboard (1,284 lines): nodes, containers, mesh tabs
- Milady sandboxes table with Docker metadata
- Agent detail page with docker info card
- Docker logs viewer with search/copy/download

### Code Review Fixes (all 12 findings addressed)
- resolveContainer() hydrates from DB after restart (not first-node fallback)
- create() uses DockerNodeManager for least-loaded placement
- Port allocation queries DB for existing assignments
- Shell injection prevented via shellQuote() on all args
- agentId validated before shell use
- Health check polls with retry (3s interval, 60s timeout)
- Container names use full UUID (no truncation collision)
- Strongly-typed DockerSandboxMetadata interface
- parseDockerNodes() cached at module level

### Naming
All code uses 'milady' naming to match dev branch conventions.
Legacy MILAIDY_ env vars accepted as fallback.

Rebased onto dev. 0 new type errors.

fix: address critical security and billing issues in service proxy

Five security/reliability fixes for the service billing framework:

1. Rate Limiting (DoS Protection)
   - Add 100 req/min limit to Solana RPC to prevent credit exhaustion
   - Protects against malicious users draining org credits
   - Prevents upstream API abuse and quota exhaustion

2. Cache Invalidation Race Condition (Billing Accuracy)
   - Double invalidation (before + after DB update) prevents stale pricing
   - Eliminates window where users get charged incorrect amounts
   - Critical for billing correctness

3. Missing Pricing Fallback (Availability)
   - Add $1.00 hardcoded fallback if DB pricing is misconfigured
   - Prevents service outage if _default row deleted
   - Intentionally high to alert admins via cost spike
   - Logs ERROR/WARN on fallback to ensure quick fixes

4. Method Whitelist (Input Validation)
   - Whitelist 60+ allowed Solana RPC methods across all tiers
   - Prevents calling arbitrary/expensive undocumented methods
   - Validates both single and batch requests
   - Returns clear error: "Method not supported"

5. API Key Logging Sanitization (Security)
   - Mask API keys in all error logs (https://...?api-key=***)
   - Helius requires API key in URL (no header support)
   - Prevents key leakage in logs, monitoring, error tracking

Impact:
- BEFORE: Vulnerable to DoS, billing errors, arbitrary RPC calls, key leaks
- AFTER: Rate limited, billing accurate, input validated, logs sanitized

- Invalid characters could cause unexpected behavior
- Potential buffer overflow attempts
- No input sanitization on user-provided addresses

**Solution:**
Created shared validation utility:
- lib/services/proxy/services/solana-validation.ts
  - isValidSolanaAddress(): Validates base58 format
  - validateSolanaAddress(): Throws descriptive errors
  - Regex: /^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$/
  - Excludes confusing characters (0, O, I, l)
  - Validates length (32-44 chars, most commonly 43-44)

Applied to all convenience routes:
- app/api/v1/solana/assets/[address]/route.ts
- app/api/v1/solana/token-accounts/[address]/route.ts
- app/api/v1/solana/transactions/[address]/route.ts

**Validation Logic:**
1. Check address type and existence
2. Check length bounds (performance optimization)
3. Validate base58 encoding format
4. Return 400 with descriptive error if invalid

**Security Benefits:**
- ✅ Prevents DoS via excessively long strings
- ✅ Rejects invalid characters early
- ✅ Protects against buffer overflow attempts
- ✅ Provides clear error messages for debugging
- ✅ Fails fast before proxying to expensive RPC calls

**Example Error Response:**
```json
{
  "error": "Invalid Solana address format",
  "details": "Address must be 32-44 base58-encoded characters"
}
```

Severity: Medium - Input validation security issue

- Mitigation: Short TTL, high fallback ($1.00), monitoring
- Accepted risk: Complexity vs consistency trade-off

- Low probability of occurrence

- Unacceptable complexity/latency trade-offs

fix(auth): try refreshSession on login page before showing UI

Shadow reported still getting logged out of elizacloud. Traced the
bug: when the client-side refresh loop hasn't fired yet (e.g. came
back after server-rendered navigation with expired access cookie),
the middleware redirects to /login. The login page calls
`auth.getSession()` \u2014 which returns null if expired \u2014 and shows
the login UI even though a 30-day refresh token is still sitting in
localStorage.

Now the login page tries `auth.refreshSession()` before falling back
to the UI. If it succeeds, sets the cookie and redirects the user
back to where they were going. Fast-path for the "valid session"
case is preserved.

fix(auth): recover from expired access token instead of logging out

The silent-logout bug: when an access token sat idle long enough to
fully expire (browsers throttle setInterval in background tabs, so a
15-min idle was enough), the auto-refresh loop had already given up
because it only ran when `secs > 0`. On top of that, syncToken would
delete the server cookie as soon as it saw an expired token, killing
any chance of server-side recovery.

This refactor:
- Drops the `secs > 0` gate in checkAndRefresh so we try to refresh
  even when the access token is fully expired (the refresh token is
  typically still valid for 30 days).
- Moves the "clear server cookie" decision to AFTER refresh fails
  instead of firing on every expired-token observation.
- Adds a visibilitychange listener so we immediately attempt a refresh
  when a tab becomes visible again (covers the 'came back from lunch'
  case where background setInterval was throttled).
- Runs an eager refresh check on mount (covers hard reload after idle).

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>

fix(inmemory-adapter): sort getMemories desc to match plugin-sql

InMemoryDatabaseAdapter.getMemories returned insertion order (oldest-first),
diverging from plugin-sql's MemoryStore.get which sorts by createdAt desc,
id desc. With count: N, the in-memory adapter returned the N oldest memories
once a room exceeded N, silently breaking tests/benchmarks and runtime
consumers that expected newest-first.

Sort the filtered list desc by createdAt (tiebreak on id desc) before
slicing, aligning with plugin-sql.

Tests:
- Update existing start/end assertions to reflect newest-first ordering.
- Add ordering parity, overflow, and id-tiebreak tests.

fix(lifeops): correct Managed Google client URL prefix from eliza/ to milady/

GoogleManagedClient was calling /api/v1/eliza/google/* on Eliza Cloud. Those
routes do not exist (they live at /api/v1/milady/google/*). The Milady LifeOps
backend treats the resulting 404 as "disconnected" via its 404-swallowing
branch, so real cloud-side Google connections surfaced as "Google not
connected / 0 / 6" in the LifeOps Setup panel.

Verified against production: with the corrected URL, GET /api/v1/milady/google/
status?side=owner returns connected: true with the exact connectionId the user
sees in the dashboard (3038d918-...). The old eliza/google path returns a
Next.js 404 HTML page.

Added a unit test pinning every endpoint URL in GoogleManagedClient so this
prefix cannot silently drift again, plus a targeted case asserting that the
client relays side=owner verbatim for legacy/dashboard-created connections
(which the cloud generic adapter already maps to connectionRole="owner").

from apps. app-core was importing CodingAgentControlChip, CodingAgentSettingsSection,

(an app), which was also a real bidirectional cycle — task-coordinator
imports app-core (useApp, client, CodingAgentSession, etc).

Replace direct imports with a slot registry:

1. New `packages/app-core/src/app-shell/task-coordinator-slots.tsx`:
   - TaskCoordinatorSlots shape + registerTaskCoordinatorSlots()
   - Thin wrapper components (CodingAgentSettingsSection, PtyConsoleBase,
     CodingAgentTasksPanel, CodingAgentControlChip) that render the
     registered implementation or null if not registered
   - Exported via new "./app-shell/task-coordinator-slots" subpath

2. Rewire 5 app-core consumers to import from the slot module:
   DetachedShellRoot, SettingsView, ChatView, TasksPageView,
   agent-orchestrator.tsx. Call sites unchanged; the slot wrappers
   have the same prop shape.

3. New `apps/app-task-coordinator/src/register-slots.ts`:
   - Side-effect module that imports the real components and calls
     registerTaskCoordinatorSlots. Exposed via "./register-slots".
   - Also added @elizaos/app-core as explicit dependency (was already
     a de-facto undeclared peer).

4. Two template main.tsx files get the side-effect import alongside
   the existing @elizaos/app-lifeops/widgets registration.

   slot module instead of @elizaos/app-task-coordinator.

fix(lifeops): bedtime target stays on sleep-day, not calendar-day

The `LifeOpsScheduleInsight.relativeTime.bedtimeTargetAt` anchor was rolling
forward to "tomorrow night" whenever `now` was past midnight, producing
nonsense values like `minutesUntilBedtimeTarget = 1354` at 12:56 AM after
an 11:30 PM target. `localHourInstantMs` was always anchored on `now`'s
local date and ratcheted forward so the candidate was never in the past,
which is wrong for post-midnight / pre-wake hours — those still belong to
the previous sleep-day.

Anchor the bedtime target on the sleep-day (the local date of the wake
anchor: `wakeAt`/`lastSleepEndedAt`/`firstActiveAt`) so a just-passed
bedtime is reported as "bedtime was ~86m ago" instead of "bedtime in
22h 34m". A ±24h window around `now` still advances the target when the
wake anchor is genuinely stale (multi-day gap) without clobbering the
fresh "just past bedtime" case.
fix(lifeops): bedtime target stays on sleep-day, not calendar-day

fix(lifeops): roll stale meal windows forward

The schedule overview widget surfaces `nextMealWindowStartAt` from the
merged schedule state. `meal_window_likely` observations carry a 6-hour
TTL, so a dinner window produced at 9:30 PM would still be treated as
"relevant" after midnight and re-emitted as the upcoming meal — giving
"Next dinner window Apr 20, 9:30 PM" when the clock already reads
Apr 21.

Guard the merge output so `nextMealWindowStartAt` is always `>= now` or
`null`: skip `meal_window_likely` observations whose `windowStartAt` is
already in the past, and only fall back to a snapshot-level value when
that value is still in the future. When no upcoming window qualifies,
all four meal-window fields (label, start, end, confidence) clear
together instead of drifting out of sync.

ios(ci): wire Fastlane into apps/app/ios + parameterize bundle id

The CI workflow runs `bundle exec fastlane release` from apps/app/ios,
but Fastfile/Appfile/Matchfile only existed at
eliza/packages/app-core/platforms/ios/fastlane/. Every Apple release run
since the Milady rename has failed because (a) fastlane couldn't find
its config, (b) all three fastlane files hardcoded the old elizaOS
bundle id, and (c) the WebsiteBlockerContentExtension had no
provisioning-profile mapping. This change:

- Parameterizes app_identifier via APP_IDENTIFIER env var across
  Fastfile/Appfile/Matchfile, with the ai.elizaos.app fallback only
  when no value is supplied.
- Adds APP_IDENTIFIER_EXTRA for bundle ids of embedded extensions
  (e.g. com.miladyai.milady.WebsiteBlockerContentExtension). Matchfile
  and Fastfile build_app use the combined list so match fetches both
  profiles in one pass.
- Adds an `ios-overlay` mode to run-mobile-build.mjs that replays
  overlayIosNativeFiles() without rebuilding, and extends the overlay
  to copy Gemfile + fastlane/ from the platform template into
  apps/app/ios/ so CI and local dev see the same tooling.
- Ships the Milady-specific IPA name (Milady.ipa) instead of the stale
  ElizaOSApp.ipa.

a caller omitted them. That meant the 66 branded services registered
via `definePlaybook` (Netflix, Spotify, Disney+, Max, Prime, YouTube
Premium, ChatGPT Plus, Apple Music, etc.) would "cancel" a subscription
by opening the management URL and taking a screenshot — no clicks, no
confirmation — and the action reported `success: true` to the owner.

Changes:

  now `steps?: SubscriptionAutomationStep[]` (may be undefined). The
  default `definePlaybook` helper no longer fabricates open+screenshot

  entries that opted in to real click-flows (google_play,
  apple_subscriptions, fixture_streaming, fixture_login_required,
  fixture_phone_only) have steps; the remaining 66 branded services
  are now correctly marked as "no real playbook". Exports a shared
  `PLAYBOOK_NOT_IMPLEMENTED_ERROR` constant so callers can

fix(auth): preempt steward session expiry with eager server+client refresh

Shadow reported being signed out after ~15min, which matches the access
token TTL exactly. Two gaps in our refresh story that made this happen:

1. Server middleware only triggered /auth/refresh when the access token
   was ALREADY expired. If the user's first navigation after a long idle
   coincided with the token expiring milliseconds ago, the refresh
   window was racy. Now we preemptively refresh whenever the token has
   less than 180s remaining on any protected-path request.

2. Client-side interval timer (checkAndRefresh every 60s, triggers when
   <120s left) is unreliable in background tabs. Chrome throttles
   setInterval to roughly 1 call per minute in inactive tabs and can
   suspend them entirely when memory-pressure hits. A user returning to
   an idle-for-15-min tab would find their token gone and the interval
   hadn't fired its check. Added visibilitychange + online event
   handlers that force an immediate check-and-refresh when the tab
   becomes visible or the network reconnects.

Together these close the window in which an expired token reaches any
server request handler. The server-side middleware is the real backstop
since it runs for every protected request regardless of tab state.

fix(reflection,providers): reduce prompt bloat that blows long-context cap

Three targeted cuts against the action-planner / reflection pipeline that were
shipping duplicate and oversized context on every chat turn. Verified live on
a self-hosted deployment where messages from a busy discord channel were
hitting ~500K input tokens per user turn and bouncing off the Max subscription
'Extra usage is required for long context requests' threshold. Same cuts drop
that to ~60-80K input tokens per turn with no behavior change.

1) trust + advanced-capabilities reflection evaluators
   Before rendering `existingRelationships` into the LLM prompt, strip to
   the 4 fields the model actually uses for dedup (sourceEntityId,
   targetEntityId, tags, relationshipType). The raw DB records were growing
   unbounded (700KB+ observed) because `metadata.indicators` arrays
   accumulate every signal the bot ever captured, and every reflection call
   was re-reading that whole history. The LLM never uses indicator history
   to emit new relationship rows, so shipping it is pure token bloat.

2) reflectionEvaluatorTemplate (prompts.ts)
   Drop the `{{providers}}` block. It was emitting the Conversation Messages
   block a second time inside the same prompt because `{{recentMessages}}`
   is already present. Captured a live 1MB reflection request where
   `# Conversation Messages` appeared twice verbatim.

3) ProviderSelection + KnowledgeProviderDecision templates (message.ts)
   Same dedup. Both planner prompts had `available provider catalog:
   {{providers}}` AND `recent conversation: {{recentMessages}}`, and
   `{{providers}}` in this context includes the recent conversation as
   rendered by provider `RECENT_MESSAGES`. Dropping the redundant
   `{{providers}}` catalog line keeps the planner's actual task intact
   and halves the per-call token budget.

No behavior change in any test, just smaller prompts. The trajectory output
users see is identical.

fix(dev): default ELIZA_NAMESPACE to milady

The dev orchestrator scripts and runtime helpers fell back to 'eliza'
when ELIZA_NAMESPACE was unset, causing the process to read
~/.eliza/eliza.json instead of the expected ~/.milady/milady.json.

Also collapse duplicated code left over from the MILADY_*/ELIZA_* alias
unification (profile.ts, namespace-defaults.ts, credentials.ts,
coordinator-preflight.ts had every env read and write twice in
identical form).

fix(wallet): honor state-dir for steward credentials path

Every reader/writer of steward-credentials.json hardcoded
~/.eliza/steward-credentials.json, so when ELIZA_NAMESPACE=milady (or any
MILADY_STATE_DIR / ELIZA_STATE_DIR override) the runtime persisted to
~/.milady/ but looked in ~/.eliza/ on boot, and Steward-backed wallets
never hydrated.

Route every call site through resolveStateDir() so the file lives next to
milady.json (or any configured state dir). Adds a resolveStewardCredentialsPath()
helper in packages/agent/src/config/paths.ts. app-core and app-steward use the
canonical @elizaos/core resolveStateDir() for the same path.
fix(wallet): honor state-dir for steward credentials path

feat(wallet): unify EVM auto-enable around signing capability

Replace the hard ENABLE_EVM_PLUGIN gate with a capability-driven check that
auto-enables @elizaos/plugin-evm whenever the runtime can actually sign:

  1. env EVM_PRIVATE_KEY, or
  2. Steward credentials (STEWARD_API_URL + STEWARD_AGENT_TOKEN),
     with cloud-provisioned and self-hosted paths sharing the same bridge.

Split isStewardCloudProvisioned() into two predicates:
  - isStewardSigningReady(): capability gate used by the pre/post-boot bridge
  - isStewardCloudProvisioned(): informational (cloud vs self-hosted)

Remove the phantom BRIDGE simile comment — runtime only normalizes simile
names and never dispatches them to requireActionSpec, so the crash it claimed
to guard against cannot occur.

fix(runtime): cap hot-reload shutdown at 2s so provider switches don't block on PTY teardown

runtime.stop() awaits every service.stop() sequentially. PTYService.stop
goes through PTYManager.shutdown(), which drains each active PTY
session with a per-session timeout (up to ~5s). Any one idle PTY
session therefore turns a provider-dropdown click into a multi-second
block, during which server.ts's providerSwitchInProgress flag +
agentState === "restarting" guard reject further clicks with 409 —
which is why flipping through providers rapidly feels stuck and
second selections sometimes appear to "revert".

Wrap shutdownRuntime() in the hot-reload onRestart path with a 2s
cap: if the old runtime finishes stopping inside that window, great;
otherwise log a warning and bring up the new runtime anyway. Services
that didn't finish cleanly get GC'd as the reference drops. This is
safe for an explicit user-initiated restart — the user asked for a
new runtime; in-flight work on the old one is already obsolete.

Fix lives at the agent layer rather than in plugin-agent-orchestrator
because we resolve PTYService from a nested submodule outside our
write scope; bounding shutdown at the caller side addresses every
service, not just PTY.

fix(character): tokenize name occurrences on save so renames propagate

The character editor has had `{{name}}` / `{{agentName}}` token
resolution on *load* for a while (replaceNameTokens), seeded by the
onboarding presets. But `prepareDraftForSave` never ran the reverse
pass — so the first time a user saved via the editor, the expanded
literals persisted and the tokens were lost forever. From that point
on, renaming the agent in Identity settings stopped propagating to
bio / system / message examples / post examples / style / topics —
every one of those fields still contained the old name as dead text.

Make save the mirror of load:

- Add `tokenizeNameOccurrences(text, name)` next to `replaceNameTokens`.
  Whole-word, case-sensitive, idempotent; refuses single-character names.
- `prepareDraftForSave(draft, previousName?)` runs the tokenizer over
  every free-text field on the character — bio, system, topics,
  postExamples, style.{all,chat,post}, messageExamples body text —
  using both the current draft name and (optionally) the previous
  saved name so a rename within the same save also catches stale
  old-name literals.
- Thread `characterData?.name` through from `useCharacterState` as the
  previous name.

Tests: 15 cases covering whole-word matching, case sensitivity,
idempotency, guardrails (single-char, regex special chars), and full
round-trip symmetry with replaceNameTokens after a rename.

No explicit one-shot migration needed — the first save after this
change tokenizes the character in place, and the load path already
renders tokens back to literals for display.

fix(message): preserve SPAWN_AGENT against metadata action correction

findOwnedActionCorrectionFromMetadata scores the planner's chosen
action against the user message via keyword overlap, and replaces it
if any other registered action scores meaningfully higher. This works
for upgrades like REPLY → OWNER_SEND_MESSAGE when the user says
"text mom," but it silently breaks coding-delegation: SPAWN_AGENT has
no user-message keywords to match against, so for requests like
"send a small PR to elizaOS/eliza" it scores ~0 while OWNER_SEND_MESSAGE
scores ~37 via overlap on "send" / "discord" / "workflow." The planner's
deliberate [REPLY, SPAWN_AGENT] gets rewritten to [OWNER_SEND_MESSAGE],
whose params then fail validation (the corrector doesn't replan), and
the action is dropped — so the agent sits silent with no reply and no
task dispatch.

Introduce EXPLICIT_INTENT_ACTIONS (starts with SPAWN_AGENT) and bail
out of correction when the planner already picked one. These actions
represent explicit delegation / orchestration intent that keyword
overlap cannot evaluate, so we must defer to the planner rather than
second-guess it.

Export findOwnedActionCorrectionFromMetadata and add a focused
regression test covering the SPAWN_AGENT-present and
SPAWN_AGENT-alone paths plus the empty-actions baseline.

fix: remove PGlite :memory: artifacts and prevent recurrence (#25)

Four PGlite in-memory database directories were accidentally committed
under typescript/:memory:<UUID>/ during test runs. These paths contain
colons, which are valid on macOS/Linux but illegal as Windows filenames.
This caused git checkout to fail on every Windows CI runner, blocking
the Milady Electrobun release build for 3+ days.

Fixes:
- Remove all four typescript/:memory:<UUID>/ subtrees from git history
- Add :memory:*/ and typescript/:memory:*/ to .gitignore
- Update vitest.config.ts to set PGDATA env to OS tmpdir so PGlite
  never writes database files into the working tree during test runs

Root cause: PGlite initializes with a :memory:<UUID> path that resolves
relative to CWD when no explicit data directory is configured. On
macOS/Linux the files are created silently and can be staged with
git add -A. The PGDATA env redirect prevents this entirely.

fix(character): tokenize name occurrences on save so renames propagate

The character editor has had `{{name}}` / `{{agentName}}` token
resolution on *load* for a while (replaceNameTokens), seeded by the
onboarding presets. But `prepareDraftForSave` never ran the reverse
pass — so the first time a user saved via the editor, the expanded
literals persisted and the tokens were lost forever. From that point
on, renaming the agent in Identity settings stopped propagating to
bio / system / message examples / post examples / style / topics —
every one of those fields still contained the old name as dead text.

Make save the mirror of load:

- Add `tokenizeNameOccurrences(text, name)` next to `replaceNameTokens`.
  Whole-word, case-sensitive, idempotent; refuses single-character names.
- `prepareDraftForSave(draft, previousName?)` runs the tokenizer over
  every free-text field on the character — bio, system, topics,
  postExamples, style.{all,chat,post}, messageExamples body text —
  using both the current draft name and (optionally) the previous
  saved name so a rename within the same save also catches stale
  old-name literals.
- Thread `characterData?.name` through from `useCharacterState` as the
  previous name.

Tests: 15 cases covering whole-word matching, case sensitivity,
idempotency, guardrails (single-char, regex special chars), and full
round-trip symmetry with replaceNameTokens after a rename.

No explicit one-shot migration needed — the first save after this
change tokenizes the character in place, and the load path already
renders tokens back to literals for display.

matching the convention.

manage-tasks.ts validate admits the action when looksLikeTaskIntent
matches either the current message or any of the last 4 room messages.

TEXT_SMALL extraction occasionally classifying vague prompts as
operation=list, the action could fire on a message that did not ask
for a task list at all.

Add a defensive guard at the top of the LIST branch using a tighter
LIST_INTENT_TERMS subset ("list tasks", "show tasks", "my tasks",
"what are my tasks", "task list"). If the current message does not
match list intent, the action returns success=false with an error and

  and before `deployWorkflow` in both `generateWorkflowDraft` and

    1. typeVersion clamp        — pick highest valid ≤ requested, fallback

    2. authentication backfill  — when credentials block has exactly one

fix(api): merge versions across same-name entries in /types/nodes.json

n8n's /types/nodes.json lists ONE ENTRY PER VERSIONED-NODE CLASS, not
one entry per node type. e.g. Gmail appears twice — once with
`version: [2, 2.1]` (the modern class) and once with `version: 1`
(the legacy class). The previous parser overwrote the map on each
.set(), so the runtime version registry only contained whatever
versions appeared LAST per name.

Symptom (Session 21 live dogfood): validateAndRepair clamped Gmail
typeVersion 2.2 to 1 (instead of 2.1) and Discord 2 to 1 (instead
of staying at 2), because the runtime∩catalog intersect was [1] for
both — the modern-class entries were being silently overwritten.

Fix: accumulate versions into a Set keyed by name, then materialize
to a sorted array at the end. Closes the false-floor regression
that defeated the runtime-clamp pass.

live dogfood (Discord post arrived with empty Subjects field):

  parseExpressions in src/utils/outputSchema.ts only matched dot

  The LLM emitted {{ $json["concatenate_subject"] }} (bracket
  notation, missing 'd') and validateAndRepair walked past it.

  silently concatenated 10 empty strings; the synthetic schema
  for Summarize emitted "concatenated_subject" lowercase
  (derived from the wrong field name); Discord's bracket
  reference compounded by also using the wrong case AND a typo.

  validateAndRepair.ts. For each Summarize node, walks
  fieldsToSummarize.values[], looks up upstream node's known
  output schema, deterministically case-corrects on CI match;
  flags as ValidationError otherwise (kicked to Layer 3 retry).

fix(security): set COOP same-origin-allow-popups on /app-auth/* routes

The OAuth popup-callback flow opens a provider popup, polls
window.closed to detect completion or cancellation, and then exchanges
the returned code/token. Default Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy of
'same-origin' (or any CORP-isolated default) makes that closed-check
throw, so the parent window never notices the popup finishing and the
user is stuck in a re-prompt loop.

'same-origin-allow-popups' keeps the page cross-origin-isolated for
its own resources but exempts popups it opened, which is the contract
the Steward + Privy SDKs are coded against.

default. No other change to the existing CSP/security header set.

fix(n8n,api): hero-chat workflow create now resolves credentials end-to-end

The Automations hero chat ("Describe a task or workflow…") posts to
POST /api/n8n/workflows/generate, which proxied straight to n8n's REST
API after generation. That bypassed `service.deployWorkflow` —
specifically `resolveCredentials` — so the LLM-emitted
`credentials: { discordBotApi: { id: "{{CREDENTIAL_ID}}" } }` blocks
reached n8n with the placeholder unresolved. n8n stored the workflow
fine, but on activation/execute it crashed with
"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'execute')" because no
credential matched the placeholder id, OR silently no-op'd the node
(seen in dogfood: cron fired every minute, Discord node ran but never
posted because the cred lookup returned undefined).

Three fixes:

1. `n8n-routes.ts:handleGenerateWorkflow` — route through
   `service.deployWorkflow(draft, agentId)` instead of the proxy chain.
   That mints n8n credentials server-side, replaces the
   `{{CREDENTIAL_ID}}` placeholders, then writes the workflow with real
   credential ids. Falls back to the legacy proxy when the workflow
   service isn't available (test/CI shapes).

2. Use `resolveAgentId(ctx)` for the `userId` arg — the plugin's
   `getUserTagName` calls `runtime.getEntityById(userId)` which fails
   with a SQL error if `userId` isn't a valid UUID. The agent's id is
   always a real entity in Milady local.

3. `client-n8n.ts:generateN8nWorkflow` — bump the fetch timeout from
   the 10s default to 120s. LLM-driven workflow generation runs
   keyword extraction, node search, generation, multiple correction
   passes, and feasibility assessment sequentially — easily 30-90s on
   cold cache, so the 10s default surfaced as
   "Request timed out after 10000ms" in the UI even when the backend
   would have succeeded.

fix(n8n): split deploy/read try blocks so getWorkflow failure doesn't trigger legacy re-deploy

Greptile P1: handleGenerateWorkflow had `getWorkflow` (read) inside the
same try/catch as `deployWorkflow` (commit). On a transient n8n GET
failure after a successful deploy, the catch fell through to the legacy
proxy path — which re-invokes the LLM and POSTs/PUTs a new workflow,
either duplicating the just-deployed workflow or PUT-overwriting it with
unresolved `{{CREDENTIAL_ID}}` placeholders.

Fix: split into two try blocks. The outer try wraps only operations
that have not yet committed a side effect to n8n — `generateWorkflowDraft`
(pure LLM call) and `deployWorkflow` (the write). Failures here can
safely fall through to the legacy proxy. Once `deployWorkflow` returns,
the workflow is committed in n8n and any further failure (e.g. the
follow-up `getWorkflow` read) returns the deploy summary instead of
falling through. The legacy path is never re-entered after a successful
commit.

Behavior changes:
- Pre-deploy failure: same as before — falls through to legacy proxy.
- Successful deploy + successful read: same as before — returns full body.
- Successful deploy + failed read (NEW): returns deploy summary
  (id, name, active, missingCredentials) with a warning log instead
  of corrupting the workflow via legacy re-deploy.

fix(telegram): emit MESSAGE_RECEIVED on Milady-shim Telegram messages so event-kind triggers fire (Session 17c, DoD-F4)

DoD-F4 was blocked because the Milady runtime has its own
ensureTelegramBotPolling shim at runtime/eliza.ts:659-808 that runs
alongside @elizaos/plugin-telegram. The shim was created originally
because the upstream plugin's bot.launch() was silently failing on
Bun/Windows (see the comment at lines 482-484). However, the shim's
bot.on('message', ...) handler does its own useModel(TEXT_LARGE) reply
and bypasses runtime.messageService.handleMessage entirely — so the
MESSAGE_RECEIVED emit at @elizaos/core's DefaultMessageService.handleMessage
(packages/typescript/src/services/message.ts:3080) never fires for
Telegram messages.

Result: an event-kind trigger with eventKind=MESSAGE_RECEIVED fires
correctly on Discord (Session 17b verified) and on manual fire via
POST /api/triggers/events/MESSAGE_RECEIVED, but never on real Telegram
messages — the G1 trigger-event-bridge (Session 2) has no event to
catch.

Fix: inject runtime.emitEvent(EventType.MESSAGE_RECEIVED, ...) into the
shim's bot.on('message') handler right after the inbound message is
captured (between the username log and the chat-history push), before
the LLM reply. Builds a minimal Memory with deterministic uuids:
  roomId = stringToUuid('telegram:<chatId>')
  entityId = stringToUuid('telegram-user:<username>:<chatId>')

The Memory shape satisfies the trigger-event-bridge contract — the
bridge only reads roomId, source, and the eventKind it was registered
for. Wraps the emit in try/catch so a transient emit failure does NOT
break the chat-reply path that follows.

fix(triggers): unblock CREATE_TRIGGER_TASK dispatch on page-automations (Gap #1)

The Automations chat was emitting LLM replies that contained structured
plans but never dispatching CREATE_TRIGGER_TASK. Two distinct causes:

Bug A — looksLikeTriggerIntent keyword gap. The shared i18n keyword list
has 'every day/week/month/hour' but no 'every N seconds/minutes'. A prompt
like "every 2 minutes, write 'ping' to the log" matched zero terms, so
validate() returned false and the action-planner never saw the action.
Added a local regex \bevery\s+\d+\s*(second|minute|hour|day|week|month)s?\b
alongside the existing keyword path — keeps i18n coverage intact, widens
the common English phrasing users type on the Automations view.

Bug B — page-automations system addendum named the actions in camelCase
('createTriggerTaskAction', 'manageTasksAction') which the planner XML
parser (<action><name>...) does not recognize, and never showed the LLM
the dispatch format. Rewrote the addendum to use the canonical SNAKE_CASE
names inside the XML schema the planner already expects, so the model has
one consistent wire spec to produce. Bumped PAGE_SCOPE_VERSION 11→12 to
segregate the new prompt-regime cohort from MIPRO/GEPA training samples
collected under the old addendum.

feat(app-core): apps open in dedicated native windows (Ghost-style)

Every app — internal tool, overlay, registry/catalog — now launches in
its own Electrobun BrowserWindow with slug-based dedupe, persisted
per-slug bounds, and a unified AppWindowRenderer that mounts only the
app's content (no surrounding Milady shell chrome).

UI / renderer
- AppWindowRenderer: new full-bleed renderer at /apps/<slug> (apps/app
  in appWindow=1 mode). Three branches:
    1. internal tool slug → lazy-loaded tab component (PluginsPageView,
       SkillsView, …; LifeOps via @elizaos/app-lifeops/ui)
    2. overlay slug → overlay's Component with exitToApps=window.close
    3. registry/catalog slug → client.launchApp + viewer iframe with
       postMessage auth handshake (mirrors GameViewOverlay)
- AppsView: handleLaunch routes the Electrobun branch through
  openAppRouteWindow only; web fallback preserves iframe + setTab paths.
  Removes nativeSurfaceForInternalToolTab dead code, drops the global
  "Keep new windows on top" toggle (per-window pin remains).
- internal-tool-apps: every internal tool now declares an explicit
  windowPath; new getInternalToolAppWindowPath / getInternalToolAppDescriptors
  helpers expose the data to bun-side code.
- navigation: APPS_SUB_TABS gains inventory + elizamaker entries so the
  new /apps/<slug> windows resolve to the right tab component.
- per-app-config + launch-history modules added (foundation for the
  upcoming AppDetailsView; not yet wired to a UI surface).

Electrobun bun side
- desktopOpenAppWindow accepts a slug and threads it through
  DesktopManager → SurfaceWindowManager → ManagedWindowRecord.
- SurfaceWindowManager.findWindowBySlug + slug-based dedupe in
  createManagedWindow focus an existing window instead of spawning a
  duplicate (id format becomes ${surface}_${slug} when slug is given).
- Per-slug bounds persistence: BoundsStore interface + optional
  boundsStore option; createManagedWindow restores saved frame on slug
  match and saves on resize/move (debounced 500ms). Backed by
  userData/app-window-bounds.json with frame validation that rejects
  minimized-state geometry so a saved window can't be invisible next
  launch.
- Application menu: per-surface submenus (Chat / Plugins / Connectors /
  Triggers / Cloud / Browser) replaced with one "Apps" menu enumerating
  every known app. Bun-side mirror APP_MENU_ENTRIES keeps the renderer
  module out of the bun bundle.
- Tray menu: one "tray-app-<slug>" entry per app, routed through
  handleApplicationMenuAction via a new tray-clicked listener.
- Deep links: <scheme>://apps/<slug> now opens or focuses the matching
  app window via findAppMenuEntryBySlug + getDesktopManager().openAppWindow.
  Anything unrecognized still falls through to shareTargetReceived.

feat(app-core): App Details page for apps that need config

Apps that declare configurable runtime / settings / widgets now show a
Details page (config + diagnostics + widget toggles + Launch button)
when clicked, instead of launching directly. Zero-config apps keep the
existing direct-launch behavior.

Per-app declaration
- internal-tool-apps: new optional `hasDetailsPage?: boolean` field on
  InternalToolAppDefinition. Marked true for LifeOps, Fine Tuning,
  Steward, ElizaMaker — the four internal tools with real configuration
  surface area. The other 8 viewers/inspectors stay zero-config and
  open straight in their dedicated window.
- New helper `getInternalToolAppHasDetailsPage(name)` and exposed
  `InternalToolAppDescriptor.hasDetailsPage` for cross-layer mirroring.

AppDetailsView
- New page at packages/app-core/src/components/pages/AppDetailsView.tsx
  (~510 lines). Resolves slug → app via three sources:
    1. internal-tool descriptors (windowPath match)
    2. overlay registry (getAppSlug match, via overlayAppToRegistryInfo)
    3. catalog (client.listApps + client.listCatalogApps, findAppBySlug)
  Sections: Header (hero/name/source/running count), About (description
  + capabilities chips), Recent Runs, Launch Diagnostics (last 5 from
  launch-history.ts), Widgets (own plugin's widgets with enable toggle
  via existing chat-sidebar visibility store + collapsible live
  preview), Config (launch mode + always-on-top), Launch button.
- Launch button reads loaded per-app config (per-app-config.ts):
    * launchMode "window" → invokeDesktopBridgeRequest("desktopOpenAppWindow")
    * launchMode "inline" + internal-tool → setTab(targetTab)
    * launchMode "inline" + overlay → setState("activeOverlayApp", name)
    * launchMode "inline" + other → falls back to window mode
  Inline mode is disabled in the radio for apps that don't support it.
- Helper `appNeedsDetailsPage(name)` exported for AppsView routing.
  Defaults: catalog apps → true, overlays → false, internal tools →
  declared value.

AppsView routing
- New `parseAppsRoute(path)` helper — recognizes /apps/<slug>/details
  and returns {slug, action: "details" | null}.
- `appsDetailsSlug` state with hashchange + popstate listeners so
  back/forward navigation unmounts AppDetailsView.
- pushAppsUrl(slug, subPath?) extended to accept a "details" sub-path.
- handleLaunch checks `appNeedsDetailsPage` first: if true, navigates
  to /apps/<slug>/details and returns (no bridge call). Falls through
  to the existing window/iframe flow for direct-launch apps.
- Auto-launch-from-URL effect skips when action === "details" so
  refreshing the details URL doesn't cause a redirect loop.
- Render mounts <AppDetailsView slug={appsDetailsSlug}> in the apps
  content area when the slug is set, otherwise the catalog grid.

Bun-side menu / tray dispatch

  in APP_MENU_ENTRIES.
- handleApplicationMenuAction for `apps:<slug>` and `tray-app-<slug>`:
    * if entry.hasDetailsPage → restoreWindow() + sendToActiveRenderer
      ("desktopAppDetailsRequested", {slug})
    * else → existing direct getDesktopManager().openAppWindow()
- AppsView subscribes to "desktopAppDetailsRequested" and navigates the
  apps URL to /apps/<slug>/details. Switches to the apps tab + browse
  sub-tab so the user lands on the details page reliably.

fix(electrobun): keep node-llama-cpp out of the bun bundle

The Electrobun bun-side bundle was failing to build because
node-llama-cpp ships per-platform sibling packages
(@node-llama-cpp/<plat>) as runtime dynamic imports. Only the host
platform's sibling is installed, so Bun.build cannot resolve the rest
and aborts with 13 unresolved imports inside compileLLamaCpp.js.

Two changes:

1. native/steward.ts — switch saveStewardCredentials to the deep
   specifier @elizaos/app-steward/services/steward-credentials. The
   barrel @elizaos/app-steward re-exports plugin/routes/UI, several of
   which import @elizaos/app-core, whose graph reaches the
   embedding-manager and local-inference engine that dynamic-import
   node-llama-cpp. Importing only the credentials helper severs that
   edge. Matches what the existing test mock already expects.

2. electrobun.config.ts — add `external: ["node-llama-cpp",
   "@node-llama-cpp/*"]` to build.bun. The Electrobun bun process never
   loads node-llama-cpp directly (the API runs as a child process and
   owns embeddings), so leaving it as a runtime-resolved external is
   correct and prevents future transitive edges from re-introducing the
   same failure.

`bun run dev:desktop` now bundles cleanly and the app boots.
fix(electrobun): keep node-llama-cpp out of the bun bundle

perf(bundle): drop dead lazy() wrappers, fix dynamic↔static collisions

Vite/Rollup folds a `lazy(() => import(X))` back into the main chunk
whenever any other importer pulls X eagerly — same X can't be both
the entry of a deferred chunk and a synchronous import. The renderer
had ~10 of these collisions (the warning lists at every build) plus a
circular `app-lifeops ↔ workspace-app-core` chunk and an empty
`vendor-utils` chunk from a stale manualChunks marker.

This commit converts the colliding lazy wrappers to static imports
so the load path is honest and the warnings clear. The Suspense
boundaries around them stay (they're already cheap once the import
resolves synchronously) but the fake lazy is gone.

Static-now (used by AppWindowRenderer + main shell + DetachedShellRoot):
- ChatView, DatabasePageView, InventoryView, LogsPageView,
  MemoryViewerView, PluginsPageView, RelationshipsView, RuntimeView,
  SkillsView, TasksPageView, TrajectoriesView, FineTuningView
- CharacterEditor (statically re-exported by `./browser.ts`)

Still real lazy in App.tsx (only owner of import path → real splits):
- AppsPageView, AutomationsView, BrowserWorkspaceView, ConnectorsPageView,
  ContactsPageView, DesktopWorkspaceSection, MessagesPageView,
  PhonePageView, SettingsView, StreamView, MiladyOsAppsView

Module-level fixes:
- BootstrapStep: drop `await import("../../api")` → static `client`
  import. The lazy was defensive but the test seam (exchangeFn
  injection) already exists; the lazy didn't help tests, just
  triggered the dynamic↔static warning across 60+ static importers.
- auth.ts: drop two `await import("./auth/sessions")` calls → static
  imports of `findActiveSession`, `verifyCsrfToken`, `CSRF_HEADER_NAME`.
  csrf-client.ts already imports the same module statically.
- CompanionAppView + CompanionView: drop `lazy(() => import(... CharacterEditor))`
  wrappers; CharacterEditor is statically re-exported by app-core's
  browser entry, so the lazy was eagerly merged anyway.

Build result: 0 warnings (was 11). Real lazy splits now appear as
their own chunks: AppsPageView (73KB), AutomationsView (99KB),
BrowserWorkspaceView (94KB), SettingsView (62KB), MiladyOsAppsView
(25KB), DesktopWorkspaceSection (22KB), StreamView (7KB),
ConnectorsPageView (0.4KB).

fix(electrobun): keep agent runtime + plugins out of the bun bundle

The Electrobun bun process is meant to be a thin native shell — it owns
window creation, RPC dispatch, and either spawns the API runtime as a
child or talks to an external API. It should never bundle the agent
runtime, plugins, database stack, or ML libraries.

A small chain of accidental imports was dragging the whole graph in:

  electrobun/src/native/steward.ts
    → @elizaos/app-steward (barrel)
    → routes/* → @elizaos/app-core
  electrobun/src/* → @elizaos/shared (barrel)
    → eliza-core-roles re-exports → @elizaos/core (logger, createUniqueUuid)
    → typescript/src/** (knowledge service, plugin-sql, drizzle, PGlite,
      transformers, onnxruntime-node, node-llama-cpp)

Result: the bunled bun/index.js was ~957k lines and crashed at startup
trying to initialize PGlite (extension .tar.gz files missing) inside
the Electrobun bun process — which has no business running plugin-sql
in the first place.

Three coordinated cuts:

1. apps/app-steward/src/services/steward-credentials.ts — inline the
   5-line resolveStateDir helper instead of importing it from
   @elizaos/core. The credentials helper is consumed by the Electrobun
   bun side via a deep specifier, so any @elizaos/core edge from here
   pulls the entire core source graph.

2. packages/shared/src/index.ts — stop re-exporting eliza-core-roles
   from the @elizaos/shared barrel. It's the only runtime edge from
   shared into @elizaos/core (logger + createUniqueUuid), and a sweep
   of the workspace + apps shows zero consumers actually using these
   names from the barrel — they all import from
   @elizaos/shared/eliza-core-roles directly, from @elizaos/core, or
   define a local copy. The dedicated subpath in shared's package.json
   exports remains, so existing callers are unaffected.

3. packages/app-core/platforms/electrobun/electrobun.config.ts — add
   build.bun.external for the heavy packages that should never live in
   the Electrobun bun bundle (@elizaos/core, @elizaos/agent,
   @elizaos/app-core, @elizaos/plugin-sql, plugin-knowledge,
   plugin-bootstrap, plugin-local-ai, plugin-local-embedding,
   @electric-sql/pglite, drizzle-orm, pg, node-llama-cpp,
   @huggingface/transformers, onnxruntime-{node,common,web}). This is
   belt-and-braces against future transitive edges sneaking back in.

After all three: bundle drops from ~957k → ~360k lines, the desktop bun
process boots cleanly through WebGPU + RPC + BrowserWorkspaceBridge with
no PGlite / onnxruntime / llama errors.

so dashboard UIs and platform connectors can drive the unified APP
action without going through the chat planner:

    against a synthetic system message; collects callback text so the

      4. On `edit-N`, locate the existing app's source dir and dispatch
         the same way against the existing workdir.

Sweep across the elizaOS/eliza tree to remediate every open CodeQL
finding flagged on `develop`. 188 of 198 open alerts close with this
change; the remainder are documented false positives (Twitter OAuth
1.0a HMAC-SHA1, deterministic SHA-1-derived UUIDs, stale alerts on
already-secure crypto.randomUUID call sites).

Categories addressed:

- request-forgery (2 critical, vertex-tuning.ts): added GCP
  region/projectId/jobName regex validators and a Vertex host
  allowlist before every fetch.
- polynomial-redos / redos (~92): clamped untrusted input length
  before regex match (10k for chat text, 100k for whole files,
  1k for headers, 256 for identifiers) and replaced ambiguous
  quantifiers (\s+\s*, (.*)*, etc.) with bounded non-backtracking
  patterns.
- incomplete-url-substring-sanitization (~18): replaced
  url.includes('host') checks with new URL() + hostname equality
  (or .endsWith('.host') suffix check).
- insecure-randomness (~14): replaced Math.random() session/UUID
  generation with crypto.randomBytes / getRandomValues / randomUUID.
- biased-cryptographic-random (3): replaced randomBytes(n)[i] % m
  with crypto.randomInt(0, m).
- incomplete-sanitization / double-escaping / multi-character (~13):
  reordered escape chains so backslash/ampersand are processed first;
  replaced .replace('x','y') first-occurrence calls with replaceAll;
  fixed XML-entity double-decode order.

- second-order-command-line-injection (5): validated upstream output
  before passing to subsequent commands.
- insufficient-password-hash (5): replaced sha256-of-token wire

feat(actions): self-correcting LLM param extraction in handlers

Per project policy: handlers must NOT use regex / string matching for intent
inference, but planners get params wrong frequently. So when a handler
detects missing required params, it now runs its OWN small LLM call to
extract them from the conversation — never regex.

New `extractActionParamsViaLlm` in
`eliza/packages/agent/src/actions/extract-params.ts`. API:

  extractActionParamsViaLlm<MyParams>({
    runtime, message, state,
    actionName: "OWNER_INBOX",
    actionDescription: "Cross-channel inbox: triage / digest / respond ...",
    paramSchema: ownerInboxAction.parameters ?? [],
    existingParams: rawParams,
    requiredFields: ["subaction"],
  })

The helper:
- Short-circuits when all required fields are present (no model call)
- Builds a focused JSON-extraction prompt with the action's name,
  description, schema, recent conversation, and current message
- Calls TEXT_SMALL with structured output instructions
- Merges extracted values UNDER planner-supplied values (planner wins on
  collisions because it saw the full action surface)
- Returns silently with whatever was extractable; handler decides what to
  do if a field is still missing

Exported from `@elizaos/agent` and `@elizaos/agent/actions/extract-params`.

Lifeops umbrellas + leaf actions:
- OWNER_INBOX, OWNER_CALENDAR, OWNER_WEBSITE_BLOCK, OWNER_APP_BLOCK,
  OWNER_SCREEN_TIME, OWNER_REMOTE_DESKTOP, OWNER_RELATIONSHIP,
  PASSWORD_MANAGER, CALENDLY, INTENT_SYNC, LIFEOPS_COMPUTER_USE,
  LIFEOPS_CONNECTOR, LIFEOPS_MUTATE, PUBLISH_DEVICE_INTENT,
  REQUEST_FIELD_FILL, ADD_AUTOFILL_WHITELIST, TWILIO_VOICE_CALL,
  CALL_EXTERNAL, DOSSIER

Agent-side:
- AGENT_SEND_MESSAGE, SEARCH_CONVERSATIONS, READ_CHANNEL, READ_MESSAGES,
  SEARCH_ENTITY, READ_ENTITY

OWNER_SEND_MESSAGE (cross-channel-send), SUBSCRIPTIONS, BOOK_TRAVEL,
SCHEDULE_X_DM_REPLY, CHAT_THREAD_CONTROL, MANAGE_TASKS, HEALTH, X_READ,
LINK_ENTITY — these already do structured LLM extraction tailored to their
domain. Untouched.

Before: 1 HIGH (LIFEOPS_COMPUTER_USE inferSurface)
After: 0 HIGH / 3 MEDIUM (thin descriptions on a few actions) / 16 LOW
(missing examples on a few new orphan actions). 149 actions scanned (up
from 105 — the user's parallel work added new actions, all clean).

Handlers now self-correct when planner output is incomplete. Pattern:

  const rawParams = (options?.parameters ?? {}) as MyParams;
  const params = await extractActionParamsViaLlm<MyParams>({...});
  // params now has planner values plus LLM-filled missing slots

This formalizes what LINK_ENTITY and OWNER_SEND_MESSAGE were already doing
ad-hoc, and eliminates the temptation to reach for regex when the planner
drops a field.

Add the desktop trust path described in plan §11. On first boot the bun
main process opens a Unix domain socket under <stateDir>/sockets, posts
the path + a 32-byte secret to /api/auth/desktop-bootstrap, waits for the
API to read the secret over the socket (proving filesystem co-location),

already authenticated.

closed: any error → no session, renderer falls through to the standard
login flow. Persisted at <stateDir>/auth/desktop-session.json (mode 0600)
so subsequent boots short-circuit until the session expires.

fix(lifeops): drop `private` from mixin methods to satisfy TS4094

The lifeops payments and sleep mixins both declared `private` async helpers
that were called from public methods on the same class. Once the mixin's
anonymous class is composed into LifeOpsService and re-exported, TypeScript
cannot emit a portable `.d.ts` for the consumer (`service.ts`) without
exposing those private members — `tsc --noCheck` therefore aborted with
TS4094 during declaration emit:

  service.ts(83,7): error TS4094: Property 'collectRegularityEpisodes' …
  service.ts(83,7): error TS4094: Property 'getPaypalManagedClient' …
  service.ts(83,7): error TS4094: Property 'getPlaidManagedClient' …
  service.ts(83,7): error TS4094: Property 'upsertPaypalTransaction' …
  service.ts(83,7): error TS4094: Property 'upsertPlaidTransaction' …

The `@ts-nocheck` already on payments.ts only suppresses source-file
checks; declaration emit at the consumer still trips. Drop `private` and
leave a one-line note explaining why; access semantics inside the
composed service are unchanged because external callers go through the
public `LifeOpsService` surface, not the mixin class itself.

Unblocks the `Build Agent Image` CI job (build:docker-dist).

refactor(actions): strip all handler intent inference, internationalize validate()

Per project policy: ZERO regex / string matching / heuristic helpers in
action handlers. The LLM planner is the only intent classifier. The only
place where string matching is allowed is `validate()`, and only when fully
internationalized + greedy.

## Handler heuristics removed (12 actions)

- intent-sync: looksLikeBroadcastPayload
- twilio-call (CALL_USER, CALL_EXTERNAL, TWILIO_VOICE_CALL):
  looksLikeStandingCallPolicy + buildCallUserPolicyAcknowledgement
- owner-calendar: looksLikeNonRequestPreface, looksLikeRecurringBlockRequest,
  looksLikeSchedulingPreferenceRequest, looksLikeTravelBundleRequest,
  looksLikeBulkRescheduleRequest, looksLikeFlightConflictRequest,
  inferDeterministicOwnerCalendarPlan, resolveOwnerCalendarPlanWithLlm,
  normalizeIntentText, all inferTimeZoneFromLocationText callsites
- remote-desktop: parseLooseParameterString, inferSubactionFromText,
  inferConfirmedFromText
- password-manager: parseLooseParameterString
- calendly: parseLooseParameterString, inferSubactionFromIntent,
  extractEventTypeUri, extractDateRange
- computer-use: inferSurface (replaced with whitelist coercion of params.surface)
- life: extractLifeTimeZoneFromText, resolveAlarmDayOffset,
  parseExplicitLocalDateForLifeRequest, addYearsToLocalDate
- manage-tasks: looksLikeListTaskIntent (in-handler call) +
  hardcoded English TASK_INTENT_TERMS list
- calendar: in-handler "propose N times" regex routing guard

Every handler now trusts planner-provided params directly. Missing required
params return clean MISSING_X errors instead of inferring from text.

## Validate() internationalized

The shared i18n keyword infrastructure
(`@elizaos/shared/i18n/validation-keywords`) is now the only sanctioned
source of validate-time string matching. Two new keyword sets added:

- `validate.codingTaskRequest` — used by LIFE.validate() to decline build-an-
  app / debug-this requests so the orchestrator handles coding work, not
  LifeOps. Translations: en, es, pt, zh-CN, ko, vi, tl.
- `validate.taskIntent` — used by MANAGE_TASKS.validate() to confirm a
  request is task-management before firing. Translations: en, es, pt, zh-CN,
  ko, vi, tl.

English-only `looksLike*` validators that duplicated description-level
guards have been deleted (looksLikeEmailVenting, looksLikeCalendarObservation,
looksLikeGoalAdviceOnly, looksLikeScreenTimeReflection,
looksLikeRelationshipFollowUpRequest). The action descriptions already
carry "DO NOT use for venting / observation / advice" guards; the planner
honors them.

## Audit script hardening

- Resolves `const ACTION_NAME = "X"` referenced as `name: ACTION_NAME`
  (28 actions were previously invisible)
- Detects heuristic helpers at module scope (handler-block check was missing
  helpers that read from `params.intent` rather than message text)
- Tiers violations: HIGH = real intent inference, MEDIUM = format coercion
  (`parseLooseParameterString`)
- Allowlists validate-time helpers that delegate to the i18n loader
  (`getValidationKeywordTerms` + `findKeywordTermMatch`) — string matching
  there is project-policy-compliant.

## Audit deltas

Before this commit: 10 HIGH (real intent inference) / 6 MEDIUM / 16 LOW
After this commit: **0 HIGH** / 2 MEDIUM (thin descriptions) / 16 LOW
(missing examples / parameters on a few orphan actions).

feat(billing): pay-as-you-go container hosting from app earnings

Closes the self-hosting loop for monetized apps deployed on Eliza Cloud
containers. When daily container-billing fires, hosting bills are paid
from the org owner's redeemable_earnings BEFORE falling through to
credit_balance — so apps that earn enough to cover their hosting keep
themselves alive without ever touching cash credits.

how the loop closes:
  user chats with monetized app
    → cloud charges user's org credits + your markup %
    → markup credits your redeemable_earnings (existing flow)
    → container daily-billing pulls earnings first, credits second
    → your container stays alive while profitable

schema (4 migrations):
  0070 — adds the earnings auto-fund settings columns + the
         total_converted_to_credits tracker on redeemable_earnings
  0071 — adds the 'credit_conversion' ledger entry type (separate
         migration so the new value commits before any insert that
         uses it)
  0072 — drops the auto-fund columns; we replaced the original
         opt-in cron with always-on pay-as-you-go in container-billing
  0073 — adds pay_as_you_go_from_earnings boolean (default true) so
         orgs that want earnings preserved purely for cashout can opt
         out at /dashboard/billing

services:
  RedeemableEarningsService.convertToCredits — atomic debit of
  available_balance + increment of total_converted_to_credits + ledger
  entry. uses pg advisory lock + WHERE-clause balance check for
  TOCTOU safety. doesn't touch total_earned/total_redeemed so creator
  stats and token-cashout math stay accurate.

  AppCreditsService.reconcileCredits — debit charges go through
  org credit_balance now (was per-app pool). app-credits is becoming
  vestigial; this is the migration step that lets the messages route
  charge the user's actual org balance.

container-billing cron:
  splits the daily bill: fromEarnings = min(earningsAvailable,
  dailyCost) when pay-as-you-go is on; 0 when off. remaining flows
  to credits via the existing path. credit_transactions metadata
  records the split (paid_from_earnings + paid_from_credits) so
  invoices show exactly where each dollar came from. Promise.allSettled
  wrapping so one bad org doesn't kill the batch.

api surface:
  GET/PUT /api/v1/billing/settings — extended to surface and patch
  the new payAsYouGoFromEarnings flag alongside the existing
  auto-top-up settings
  GET /api/v1/redemptions/balance — surfaces totalConvertedToCredits
  so the earnings page can show "spent on hosting" alongside cashout
  POST /api/v1/messages — sets estimatedBaseCost: 0 so reconcile

fix(message): respect explicit REPLY action in metadata-rescue gate

When the planner returns ['REPLY'], the metadata-overlap rescue at the
end of the action-routing pipeline considered REPLY 'passive' and ran
suggestOwnedActionFromMetadata anyway. If any user message contained
common scheduling/workflow vocabulary ('workflow', 'policy', 'follow
up', 'friday', '2026'), the keyword-overlap scorer would promote the
chitchat to a privileged action like OWNER_INBOX or MANAGE_ISSUES. The
action's role gate then denied the (non-owner) user with messages like
'Permission denied: only the owner or admin may use inbox actions' —
in response to plain conversation.

Concrete repro from a milady deployment today: in a Discord channel,
botdick sent a multi-line monitoring proposal addressed to remilio
nubilio. The planner correctly chose REPLY. The metadata-rescue
overrode it to OWNER_INBOX based on overlap reasons
['overlap:2026,friday', 'workflow']. The bot replied 'Permission
denied: only the owner or admin may use inbox actions' to a guest user
asking for architectural input. Same path also fires REPLY ->
MANAGE_ISSUES on messages mentioning 'issue' / 'll'.

Fix: extract the rescue-eligibility into a tiny, testable predicate
shouldRunMetadataActionRescue. It returns true only when the response
has NO non-passive action AND no explicit REPLY/RESPOND. REPLY is a
deliberate planner signal that the message is conversation; the
keyword-overlap scorer must not override that choice.

Tests cover: empty actions / null / undefined (rescue eligible),
IGNORE/NONE only (eligible), REPLY/RESPOND present (NOT eligible —
even alongside non-string garbage), non-passive action present (NOT
eligible).
fix(message): respect explicit REPLY action in metadata-rescue gate

fix(message): keep explicit-REPLY response when race-discard fires

When a newer message arrives in the same room while we are generating
a response, the race-check at message.ts:3830 blanket-discards the
older response. The intent is to avoid spamming back-to-back replies.

The bug: the discard fires even when the older response was a
deliberate REPLY to a direct \\@-mention. The character contract says
'if a message \\@mentions you, you MUST produce a visible reply.
silence on a direct mention is treated as a bug', so dropping a
ready-to-send REPLY for a tagged message looks broken to the user.

Concrete repro from a milady deployment: in a Discord channel, 1gig
\\@-pinged remilio with a correction. While the bot was generating
the REPLY (~7s LLM call), fishai sent an unrelated message (also in
the same room, addressed to a different bot). The race-check fired
and discarded remilio's reply. From the user's POV: bot went silent
on a direct mention. Bot log line:
  [SERVICE:MESSAGE] Response discarded - newer message being processed
  (roomId=6380f0cf-...).

Fix: skip the discard branch when responseContent has an explicit
REPLY/RESPOND action — that's the planner's deliberate signal that
the message is conversation. The newer message gets its own turn
through the normal pipeline; sending the older REPLY first does not
duplicate either response. Reuses the hasExplicitReplyIntent helper
introduced in elizaOS/eliza#7141 (the metadata-rescue gate); the
helper is already covered by 5 unit tests in that PR's
shouldRunMetadataActionRescue block.

Non-REPLY responses (NONE, IGNORE, action-only) still get discarded
when a newer message arrives — the original race-protection still
fires for the cases it was designed for.

fix(actions): subscriptions trusts mode + multi-step loop breaks on requiresConfirmation

Two related fixes from trajectory analysis:

## subscriptions.ts: trust planner-supplied mode

Trajectory of subscriptions-cancel-* showed Started=SUBSCRIPTIONS,
Completed=(none). The handler was calling its own LLM planner
(resolveSubscriptionsPlanWithLlm) on every invocation, even when the
action planner had already supplied a valid mode (cancel/audit/status).
That second classifier sometimes returned shouldAct=false with a clarification
response, dropping the action result and never emitting ACTION_COMPLETED.

Fix: same pattern as inbox.ts — when params.mode is already a normalized
valid mode, skip the in-handler LLM planner and proceed directly to
the dispatch switch. The umbrella's action planner + the shared LLM param
extractor have already chosen the mode; running a third classifier just
throws away correct hints.

## message.ts: break multi-step loop on requiresConfirmation

Trajectory of remote-desktop-start-session showed 30+ LLM calls in a
single case. The handler returned { requiresConfirmation: true } because
params.confirmed was missing; the multi-step planner read that as
"action incomplete, retry", re-fired OWNER_REMOTE_DESKTOP, and got the
same result. Forever.

Fix: after each action invocation in the multi-step loop, inspect the
ActionResult for requiresConfirmation === true (in either values or data)
or error === "CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED". If present, break the loop. The
confirmation has to come from the next user message — there is nothing
the agent can do to supply it on its own. Logged at info level so the
break is observable.

This applies to every action that returns CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED:
REMOTE_DESKTOP start, OWNER_SEND_MESSAGE confirm-then-dispatch,
BLOCK_WEBSITES, password manager inject, etc. All previously vulnerable
to the same loop.

fix(llama-cpp): swallow UnsatisfiedLinkError in plugin static init

The llama-cpp-capacitor plugin's static initializer re-throws when System.loadLibrary fails, which kills the entire host app on any Android build that doesn't have a matching libllama-cpp-<abi>.so. The plugin currently ships only arm64-v8a, so any x86_64 image (Cuttlefish included) crashes Milady on launch with:

  java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: dlopen failed: library "libllama-cpp-x86_64.so" not found
    at ai.annadata.plugin.capacitor.LlamaCpp.<clinit>(...)
    at com.getcapacitor.PluginHandle.loadInstance(...)
    at com.getcapacitor.Bridge.registerAllPlugins(...)
    -> Milady process killed

Patches the plugin to log the failure but continue. Native API calls will still fail later with their own errors when the JS layer actually tries to use llama-cpp — that's the appropriate failure surface. Crashing the entire host process at startup just because an optional plugin's native lib is missing for the target ABI is wrong.

Verified end-to-end: Cuttlefish boot reaches Milady's MainActivity, the WebView attempts to load (still blocked by other upstream issues but no longer by llama-cpp).

* fix(auth): preempt steward session expiry with eager server+client refresh

Shadow reported being signed out after ~15min, which matches the access
token TTL exactly. Two gaps in our refresh story that made this happen:

1. Server middleware only triggered /auth/refresh when the access token
   was ALREADY expired. If the user's first navigation after a long idle
   coincided with the token expiring milliseconds ago, the refresh
   window was racy. Now we preemptively refresh whenever the token has
   less than 180s remaining on any protected-path request.

2. Client-side interval timer (checkAndRefresh every 60s, triggers when
   <120s left) is unreliable in background tabs. Chrome throttles
   setInterval to roughly 1 call per minute in inactive tabs and can
   suspend them entirely when memory-pressure hits. A user returning to
   an idle-for-15-min tab would find their token gone and the interval
   hadn't fired its check. Added visibilitychange + online event
   handlers that force an immediate check-and-refresh when the tab
   becomes visible or the network reconnects.

Together these close the window in which an expired token reaches any
server request handler. The server-side middleware is the real backstop
since it runs for every protected request regardless of tab state.

* fix(security): set COOP same-origin-allow-popups on /app-auth/* routes

The OAuth popup-callback flow opens a provider popup, polls
window.closed to detect completion or cancellation, and then exchanges
the returned code/token. Default Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy of
'same-origin' (or any CORP-isolated default) makes that closed-check
throw, so the parent window never notices the popup finishing and the
user is stuck in a re-prompt loop.

'same-origin-allow-popups' keeps the page cross-origin-isolated for
its own resources but exempts popups it opened, which is the contract
the Steward + Privy SDKs are coded against.

docs: design spec for the Claude / Codex sub-agent ↔ Milady runtime bridge

Companion to docs/agent-skill-build-monetized-app.md. That doc's footnote
flagged a separate "Claude Code / Codex sub-agent skill for using Milady's
APIs" as a follow-up worth its own design — this is that design doc.

The TL;DR of the gap it captures:

- The Milady orchestrator already injects CLAUDE.md + telemetry hooks into
  every Claude / Codex sub-agent's workspace. Those hooks are one-way: the
  sub-agent emits state events, the parent consumes.
- The sub-agent has no way to READ parent state — character file, memory,
  current room, active workspaces. So coding tasks that depend on parent
  context ("the user mentioned their dad earlier", "use the same markup % as
  the last app") fly blind unless the orchestrator pre-resolves everything
  in its prompt.
- The bridge is a small read-only HTTP surface on the parent (
  `GET /api/coding-agents/<agentId>/parent-context`,
  `GET /api/coding-agents/<agentId>/memory`,
  `GET /api/coding-agents/<agentId>/active-workspaces`)
  that closes the gap without giving the sub-agent any write access to
  parent state.

Design only. Implementation is sequenced as:

1. Wire the bridge endpoints in eliza/packages/app-core/src/api/
2. Extend the orchestrator's CLAUDE.md template to reference them
3. Add the bundled skill at eliza/packages/skills/skills/claude-subagent-milady-bridge/
4. Live-verify by spawning a coding sub-agent and curling the bridge

Each step is shippable on its own; the order matters because the skill body
should reference real endpoints, not aspirational ones.

The doc explicitly rejects two simpler designs that fail (dump full memory
into CLAUDE.md, or share the parent's API key with the sub-agent) and
explains why.

* fix(auth): preempt steward session expiry with eager server+client refresh

Shadow reported being signed out after ~15min, which matches the access
token TTL exactly. Two gaps in our refresh story that made this happen:

1. Server middleware only triggered /auth/refresh when the access token
   was ALREADY expired. If the user's first navigation after a long idle
   coincided with the token expiring milliseconds ago, the refresh
   window was racy. Now we preemptively refresh whenever the token has
   less than 180s remaining on any protected-path request.

2. Client-side interval timer (checkAndRefresh every 60s, triggers when
   <120s left) is unreliable in background tabs. Chrome throttles
   setInterval to roughly 1 call per minute in inactive tabs and can
   suspend them entirely when memory-pressure hits. A user returning to
   an idle-for-15-min tab would find their token gone and the interval
   hadn't fired its check. Added visibilitychange + online event
   handlers that force an immediate check-and-refresh when the tab
   becomes visible or the network reconnects.

Together these close the window in which an expired token reaches any
server request handler. The server-side middleware is the real backstop
since it runs for every protected request regardless of tab state.

* fix(security): set COOP same-origin-allow-popups on /app-auth/* routes

The OAuth popup-callback flow opens a provider popup, polls
window.closed to detect completion or cancellation, and then exchanges
the returned code/token. Default Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy of
'same-origin' (or any CORP-isolated default) makes that closed-check
throw, so the parent window never notices the popup finishing and the
user is stuck in a re-prompt loop.

'same-origin-allow-popups' keeps the page cross-origin-isolated for
its own resources but exempts popups it opened, which is the contract
the Steward + Privy SDKs are coded against.

default. No other change to the existing CSP/security header set.

* fix(auth): recover from expired access token instead of logging out

The silent-logout bug: when an access token sat idle long enough to
fully expire (browsers throttle setInterval in background tabs, so a
15-min idle was enough), the auto-refresh loop had already given up
because it only ran when `secs > 0`. On top of that, syncToken would
delete the server cookie as soon as it saw an expired token, killing
any chance of server-side recovery.

This refactor:
- Drops the `secs > 0` gate in checkAndRefresh so we try to refresh
  even when the access token is fully expired (the refresh token is
  typically still valid for 30 days).
- Moves the "clear server cookie" decision to AFTER refresh fails
  instead of firing on every expired-token observation.
- Adds a visibilitychange listener so we immediately attempt a refresh
  when a tab becomes visible again (covers the 'came back from lunch'
  case where background setInterval was throttled).
- Runs an eager refresh check on mount (covers hard reload after idle).

* fix(auth): preempt steward session expiry with eager server+client refresh

Shadow reported being signed out after ~15min, which matches the access
token TTL exactly. Two gaps in our refresh story that made this happen:

1. Server middleware only triggered /auth/refresh when the access token
   was ALREADY expired. If the user's first navigation after a long idle
   coincided with the token expiring milliseconds ago, the refresh
   window was racy. Now we preemptively refresh whenever the token has
   less than 180s remaining on any protected-path request.

2. Client-side interval timer (checkAndRefresh every 60s, triggers when
   <120s left) is unreliable in background tabs. Chrome throttles
   setInterval to roughly 1 call per minute in inactive tabs and can
   suspend them entirely when memory-pressure hits. A user returning to
   an idle-for-15-min tab would find their token gone and the interval
   hadn't fired its check. Added visibilitychange + online event
   handlers that force an immediate check-and-refresh when the tab
   becomes visible or the network reconnects.

Together these close the window in which an expired token reaches any
server request handler. The server-side middleware is the real backstop
since it runs for every protected request regardless of tab state.

* fix(security): set COOP same-origin-allow-popups on /app-auth/* routes

The OAuth popup-callback flow opens a provider popup, polls
window.closed to detect completion or cancellation, and then exchanges
the returned code/token. Default Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy of
'same-origin' (or any CORP-isolated default) makes that closed-check
throw, so the parent window never notices the popup finishing and the
user is stuck in a re-prompt loop.

'same-origin-allow-popups' keeps the page cross-origin-isolated for
its own resources but exempts popups it opened, which is the contract
the Steward + Privy SDKs are coded against.
