fix(cli-login): use Steward-aware session hook, preserve error state

The CLI/desktop bridge page (/auth/cli-login) hung on
"Loading… Preparing authentication" forever for users in two scenarios:

  1. Stale Privy localStorage with no server-side privy-token cookie —
     usePrivy() returned authenticated=true from cache, the page POSTed
     /api/auth/cli-session/<id>/complete, server returned 401, the catch
     set status="error", but the prop-sync effect immediately re-synced
     status back to "loading" because initialStatus.status was still
     "loading" (authenticated was still true from cache). The second
     effect then re-fired the same failing /complete request. Infinite
     loop. The user never saw an error message or a way out.

  2. Steward-only deployments (NEXT_PUBLIC_STEWARD_AUTH_ENABLED=true) —
     usePrivy().ready never resolved because Privy is a stub provider
     in those setups, so the page sat in "loading" indefinitely even
     when the user had a valid Steward session.

Fix:

  - Replace usePrivy() with useSessionAuth(), which already abstracts
    Steward + Privy and reports `ready` correctly in steward-only,
    privy-only, and both-enabled configurations.
  - Add an "initializing" status so the page can render the fallback
    spinner while `ready === false` instead of guessing auth state.
  - Exclude "error" from the prop-sync effect's reset list. Errors
    must remain visible so the user can act on them.
  - Replace the bare Privy login() call with a redirect to /login,
    preserving returnTo. /login already renders Steward or Privy
    depending on env, so cli-login no longer needs to know which is
    active.

fix(cli-login): gate on ready, preserve error state

The deployed cli-login page hangs on "Loading… Preparing authentication"
forever when the user has a stale auth state in localStorage but no
valid server-side session cookie. Two compounding bugs:

  1. initialStatus didn't gate on `ready` from useSessionAuth(). While
     the hook was still settling, a stale Steward (or Privy) entry in
     localStorage briefly made `authenticated` look true, the page
     jumped straight to "loading", and POSTed
     /api/auth/cli-session/<id>/complete before any of that resolved.

  2. The status-sync effect only excluded "completing" and "success"
     from being reset to initialStatus. When /complete returned 401
     (cookie missing or revoked) and the catch set status="error",
     this effect immediately clobbered "error" back to "loading",
     the completion effect re-fired the same failing request, and
     the user saw a permanent spinner with no error message and no
     way to recover.

Fix:

  - Add an "initializing" status. While `!ready`, show the same
    fallback spinner instead of pretending we know auth state.
  - Exclude "error" from the prop-sync effect's reset list.
  - Surface a "Sign In Again" button in the error state that routes
    through /login (Steward or Privy depending on env), preserving
    returnTo so the user lands back on cli-login after sign-in.

fix(auth): auto-clear stale Steward tokens on server 401

When localStorage holds a Steward token whose JWT still decodes as
non-expired but whose server-side session has been revoked (cookie
wiped, db reset, key rotation, manual sign-out on another device),
useSessionAuth() reports authenticated=true forever, every authed call
401s, and pages that gate on `authenticated` (notably /auth/cli-login)
get stuck in dead-end loading states — the user has no way to recover
short of opening DevTools and clearing localStorage by hand.

Add a single recovery seam at the place we already talk to the server
about the token:

  - StewardProvider.AuthTokenSync.syncToken now checks the response of
    POST /api/auth/steward-session. A 401 there is unambiguous: the
    server rejected our local token. Clear localStorage (steward + any
    privy:* keys), DELETE the cookie, dispatch steward-token-sync so
    consumers re-render. The next render falls back to "logged out".

  - cli-login completeCliLogin runs the same cleanup when /complete
    returns 401, so the "Sign In Again" button routes through /login
    from a clean slate instead of immediately re-failing with the same
    stale token.

The recovery is best-effort and idempotent. We intentionally don't
hook into every authed fetch in the app — only the endpoints that
authoritatively validate the token. Other 401s (insufficient perms,
etc.) shouldn't trigger a logout.

Exports `clearStaleStewardSession` from StewardProvider for any other
page that needs the same recovery path.

feat(confidant): phase 0 — credential mediation layer for Eliza agents

Introduces @elizaos/confidant — the single seam at which credentials
can be observed inside an Eliza agent. Skills never read process.env
for credentials; they request from a per-skill ScopedConfidant that
goes through policy + audit. Confidant stores values literally
(AES-256-GCM at rest with secret id bound as AAD) or as references
into external password managers.

Phase 0 closes seven concrete failure modes in the existing
credential pipeline (skill exfiltration via process.env, dual-writer
bug between provider-switch-config and plugins-compat-routes, the
Object.values(config).find(non-empty) heuristic that lets a model
slug overwrite an API key, etc.). The runtime does not yet call into
Confidant — that is phase 1. This commit ships the contract.

Public API
- createConfidant, ScopedConfidant
- defineSecretSchema(...) — single source of truth for "this id is
  a secret" decisions; replaces the catalog-as-authoritative pattern
- parseReference / buildReference — URI scheme dispatch (op://,
  pass://, keyring://, file://, env://, cloud://)
- AES-256-GCM envelope helpers (encrypt/decrypt with AAD binding)
- Identifier validation + glob-pattern matching with most-specific
  selection

Backends
- KeyringBackend — cross-platform via @napi-rs/keyring (macOS
  Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service /
  libsecret). Prebuilt binaries for darwin/win/linux/freebsd.
- EnvLegacyBackend — read-only env://VAR migration scaffolding,
  removed in phase 6.
- 1Password / Proton Pass / Cloud are deferred to phase 4+.

Storage
- ~/.milady/confidant.json mode 0600, atomic-rename writes.
- Master key sourced from OS keychain by default; pluggable via
  inMemoryMasterKey (tests + headless deployments).
- The secret id is bound as AAD so a swapped ciphertext fails closed.

Policy
- Deny-by-default.
- Implicit grant: the plugin that registered a secret id via
  defineSecretSchema gets always-access to that id.
- Explicit grants persisted per-skill with glob patterns. Most-
  specific-wins; deny is absolute.
- prompt mode requires a PromptHandler; without one, prompt-mode
  grants resolve to deny.

Audit log
- ~/.milady/audit/confidant.jsonl, append-only JSONL.
- Records ids, never values. Explicit test verifies the secret value
  never appears in the log even after a successful resolve.

Tests
- 70 vitest cases across envelope, identifiers, references, store,
  policy, end-to-end Confidant flows, and a real cross-platform
  keyring round-trip. The keyring round-trip skips cleanly on hosts
  without a usable Secret Service agent.

`meta.fromId` is the Telegram sender's *user* id, which equals the chat
id only in private 1:1 DMs. In group chats / channels the chat id is a

routed group-chat workflows back to the user's DM instead of the group
(Greptile P1).

schema gap — flat `metadata.fromId` is the de-facto inbound shape today
for Telegram), Telegram routing is skipped rather than guessed. Discord
and Slack routing are unaffected.

fix(connectors): purge n8n credential cache on disconnect

The S25 missing-credentials banner shipped in #7134 silently fails when
a user disconnects a connector. The disconnect path clears OAuth tokens
from milady.json but leaves the n8n credential cache (credStore in
plugin-n8n-workflow) intact, so the next workflow generation
short-circuits at credStore.get() and reuses the stale n8n credential
id. The deploy succeeds, no missingCredentials block is returned, the
banner never fires — the disconnect is purely UI-only.

Fix: when POST /api/connectors saves a connector with enabled: false
(or DELETE /api/connectors/:name), cascade a credStore.delete() call
for every credential type the connector owns. Next generation falls
through to credProvider.resolve(), which honors the now-cleared
milady.json and correctly returns needs_auth, restoring the banner
flow.

Wiring:
- New `packages/agent/src/api/connector-cred-types.ts`: single source
  of truth for connector ↔ credType ↔ provider id ↔ display label
  mappings. Replaces the inline maps the S25 banner and deep-link
  shipped in AutomationsView.tsx and connector-deeplink.ts —
  AutomationsView now imports prettyCredName, connector-deeplink
  re-exports providerFromCredType from the central module.
- `connector-routes.ts`: extend ConnectorRouteContext with optional
  `onConnectorDisconnect(name)` hook. Detect enabled === false on POST
  (or any DELETE) and call the hook. Per-call failures are swallowed
  so cache purge issues don't block the disconnect response.
- `server.ts`: provide the hook. Looks up the n8n_credential_store
  service via runtime, calls delete(agentId, credType) for each cred
  type in credTypesForConnector(name). agentId matches the userId
  resolveAgentId() supplies on the n8n route side, so the cache key
  lines up.

Plugin side: bumps plugins/plugin-n8n-workflow pointer to pick up
ce0de4f `feat(credential-store): add delete(userId, credType) for
disconnect-purge`, which adds the public delete() to
N8nCredentialStoreApi and the drizzle implementation on
N8nCredentialStore.

feat(skills): bundle build-monetized-app skill

Add a new bundled skill, `build-monetized-app`, that gives the agent
the recipe for building an app on Eliza Cloud that earns markup-share
revenue, deploying it as a container, and routing its earnings back
into hosting via the existing pay-as-you-go-from-earnings cron.

The skill exists because monetized apps are how a Milady-style
autonomous agent stays online: container hosting bills daily, the
container-billing cron pulls from `redeemable_earnings_ledger` before
`credit_transactions`, so any app that earns more than its hosting
cost keeps the agent alive without owner intervention. This is a
real product constraint, not theoretical — the survival-economics
reference walks through the exact accounting (cron at
`app/api/cron/container-billing/route.ts`).

Layout follows the existing convention used by `eliza-cloud` and
`eliza-app-development`:

  packages/skills/skills/build-monetized-app/
    SKILL.md                              # 4 KB — purpose, when-to-use,
                                          # default flow, links to references
    references/
      sdk-flow.md                         # 4 KB — the 6-step
                                          # @elizaos/cloud-sdk deploy + monetize flow
      survival-economics.md               # 4 KB — earnings/hosting loop, why this matters
      failure-modes.md                    # 5 KB — recovery table for real failures

The frontmatter `name` matches the directory name (`build-monetized-app`)

fix(actions): skip non-string entries in formatActionSimiles/Tags

Production observation (2026-04-28): the bot dropped a user message
in cozy ("@remilio nubilio would you like that? look what me and shaw
were just talking about ...") and stayed silent. Bot log showed:

  [PLUGIN:DISCORD] Error handling message
    (error=undefined is not an object (evaluating 'tag.trim'))

Trace: plugin-discord's messageCreate handler called the runtime's
formatActions to build the planner prompt. One of the registered
actions had `tags` containing a non-string entry (undefined or null —
the array was malformed somewhere upstream). The chain
`(action.tags ?? []).map((tag) => tag.trim())` then called .trim()
on undefined and threw. plugin-discord caught the throw as the
generic "Error handling message" and aborted the entire message
pipeline before reaching the planner. No reply, no specific log line
about which action / which tag — just silence.

Same shape exists in formatActionSimiles for action.similes.

Fix: filter out non-string entries before .trim() in both helpers.
String entries still trim/dedupe/empty-filter the same way.

```diff
 function formatActionTags(action: Action): string | null {
   const tags = [
-    ...new Set((action.tags ?? []).map((tag) => tag.trim())),
+    ...new Set(
+      (action.tags ?? [])
+        .filter((tag): tag is string => typeof tag === "string")
+        .map((tag) => tag.trim()),
+    ),
   ].filter((tag) => tag.length > 0 && tag !== "always-include");
```

Why filter rather than rely on the Action type contract: action.tags
and action.similes are `string[]` per the Action type, but external
plugin authors are not always strict — a malformed entry from an
inadequately-typed source poisoning the array crashes the entire
planner-prompt builder, which silently kills message handling for
every message the bot receives until the offending plugin is fixed.
The cost of a `typeof === "string"` filter is negligible; the failure
mode it prevents (silent bot, no actionable diagnostic) is severe.

Tests: two regression cases in actions.test.ts covering action.tags
and action.similes with mixed [undefined, null, string, number]
arrays. Both should produce a normal formatted output with only the
real string entries surviving.

fix(message): add CREATE_TASK to EXPLICIT_INTENT_ACTIONS

Production observation (2026-04-28): a user asked the bot to "Build 'Council'
at agent-home /apps/council/. ... Each persona turn is a cloud-SDK call ...
debits user balance ...". The planner correctly picked CREATE_TASK
(delegate to a coding sub-agent). findOwnedActionCorrectionFromMetadata
then overrode CREATE_TASK with OWNER_CALENDAR because today's date plus
incidental dev words ("multi turn", "api carries", "workflow", "call",
"user") overlap-scored OWNER_CALENDAR's example text higher than
CREATE_TASK's. The OWNER_CALENDAR pre-flight then bailed with
"Google Calendar is not connected. Connect Google in LifeOps settings."
in response to a code request — broken UX masquerading as auth failure.

Trace from the incident:

  [SERVICE:MESSAGE] Corrected routed action from action metadata
    (originalActions=["CREATE_TASK"],
     suggestedAction=OWNER_CALENDAR,
     score=38.54, secondBestScore=36.32,
     reasons=["overlap:multi,turn","overlap:api,carries","overlap:call,no",
              "overlap:user,no","overlap:tue,28","overlap:04,2026",
              "example","workflow"])

CREATE_TASK is structurally identical to SPAWN_AGENT (already in
EXPLICIT_INTENT_ACTIONS): it's a delegation/orchestration verb the
planner picks based on intent, not based on keyword overlap with the
user's prose. "Build me X" / "implement Y" never literally contains
"create task" or "spawn agent". The keyword-overlap corrector is
designed for the case where the planner left something passive (REPLY)
and there's a clear specific action that belongs; it's not designed to
second-guess an active delegation pick.

Fix:
- Add CREATE_TASK to EXPLICIT_INTENT_ACTIONS
- Extend the comment block to record this category of bug
- Add three regression tests covering CREATE_TASK / SPAWN_AGENT /
  REPLY paths through findOwnedActionCorrectionFromMetadata so a
  future cleanup can't silently remove the entry

Verified live on the running bot: same prompt that produced the
"Google Calendar is not connected" reply now correctly delegates to a
coding sub-agent that builds the council app.

fix(actions): parser tolerates attribute-named <param name=\"X\"> form

Trajectory analysis of cases like owner-profile-travel-prefs and
todo-remember-to-call showed the planner emitting params using
attribute-named XML:

  <params>
    <param name=\"travelBookingPreferences\">aisle seats...</param>
    <param name=\"confirmed\">true</param>
  </params>

The canonical form is tag-named:

  <params>
    <travelBookingPreferences>aisle seats...</travelBookingPreferences>
    <confirmed>true</confirmed>
  </params>

extractXmlChildren in actions.ts used the tag literally as the key, so
attribute-named params all bucketed under the key \"param\" and handlers
saw an empty params object. Result: actions returned MISSING_FIELDS or
similar, never reached their success path.

Fix: when the tag is literally <param>, parse the start tag for a
name=\"X\" / name='X' / name=X attribute and use that as the key
instead. Tag-named form continues to work unchanged.

Add 5 regression tests covering: double-quoted, single-quoted, unquoted,
no-attribute (canonical) fallback, and mixed forms in the same params
block. All pass.

from emitting declarations, which cascades up to fail bun install in
consumer repos that build all workspace packages on postinstall.

Layered defense against LLM catalog-drift hallucinations surfaced in
Session 20 dogfood (typeVersion 2.2 for Gmail when only [1, 2, 2.1] exist;
field 'subject' lowercase when Gmail simple-mode emits 'Subject';
authentication parameter missing when credentials are attached). Prompt
hardening alone is whack-a-mole; this commit adds three deterministic
layers that close the gap classes without requiring a tool-use rewrite.

Layer 1 — `validateAndRepair` deterministic pre-deploy pass

  New `src/utils/validateAndRepair.ts` runs after `injectMissingCredentialBlocks`
  and before `deployWorkflow` in both `generateWorkflowDraft` and
  `modifyWorkflowDraft`. Six checks:

    1. typeVersion clamp        — pick highest valid ≤ requested, fallback
                                   to highest available
    2. authentication backfill  — when credentials block has exactly one
                                   entry and that cred type's
                                   displayOptions.show.authentication has
                                   exactly one value, set

    3. output-field validation  — for each {{ $json.X }} or
                                   {{ $node["Y"].json.X }} expression,
                                   validate X against the upstream node's
                                   known schema (Gmail/Slack/Discord static
                                   schemas + synthetic for Summarize/Set);
                                   case-mismatch auto-fixed, unknown field
                                   becomes ValidationError for Layer 3
    4. required-parameter pre-flight — annotate workflow._meta.requiresClarification
    5. node-name uniqueness     — auto-rename duplicates with (2) suffix

  for single-version nodes) and `credentialAuthMatrix` derived from each
  credential's `displayOptions.show.authentication`. The system prompt
  gains two new MANDATORY INVARIANT sections (6a + 6b) instructing the
  LLM to pick typeVersion from the array and to set
  parameters.authentication to the matching credentialAuthMatrix value.

fix(api): merge versions across same-name entries in /types/nodes.json

n8n's /types/nodes.json lists ONE ENTRY PER VERSIONED-NODE CLASS, not
one entry per node type. e.g. Gmail appears twice — once with
`version: [2, 2.1]` (the modern class) and once with `version: 1`
(the legacy class). The previous parser overwrote the map on each
.set(), so the runtime version registry only contained whatever
versions appeared LAST per name.

typeVersion 2.2 to 1 (instead of 2.1) and Discord 2 to 1 (instead
of staying at 2), because the runtime∩catalog intersect was [1] for
both — the modern-class entries were being silently overwritten.

to a sorted array at the end. Closes the false-floor regression
that defeated the runtime-clamp pass.

Two gaps in Layer 1's output-field validation surfaced by Session 21
live dogfood (Discord post arrived with empty Subjects field):

Bug A — bracket-notation expressions slipped past the regex.
  parseExpressions in src/utils/outputSchema.ts only matched dot
  notation ($json.X) and named-node syntax ($('Y').item.json.X).
  The LLM emitted {{ $json["concatenate_subject"] }} (bracket
  notation, missing 'd') and validateAndRepair walked past it.

  Fix: new bracketPattern regex /\\[\s*(['"])([^'"]{1,200})\1\s*\]/g
  added to extractExpressionsFromString. Both single- and double-
  quoted brackets covered. parseFieldPath then tokenizes normally.

Bug B — Summarize.fieldsToSummarize.values[].field is a raw
  string identifier naming an upstream field, NOT an expression.
  Layer 1's check #3 walks expressions only, so the LLM picking
  field: "subject" (lowercase) when Gmail simple-mode emits
  "Subject" (capital) was never validated. Summarize then
  silently concatenated 10 empty strings; the synthetic schema
  for Summarize emitted "concatenated_subject" lowercase
  (derived from the wrong field name); Discord's bracket
  reference compounded by also using the wrong case AND a typo.

  validateAndRepair.ts. For each Summarize node, walks
  fieldsToSummarize.values[], looks up upstream node's known
  output schema, deterministically case-corrects on CI match;
  flags as ValidationError otherwise (kicked to Layer 3 retry).
  Runs BEFORE the expression validator so the synthetic schema
  for Summarize uses the corrected field name.

fix(android-agent): wire SIGSYS shim into stage-android-agent for x86_64

Install the compiled libsigsys-handler.so + loader-wrap drop-in for the
Alpine ld-musl-x86_64.so.1 when the seccomp-shim cache contains them.
The wrapper renames the real loader to .so.1.real and prepends the
SIGSYS handler to LD_PRELOAD, so MiladyAgentService.java's existing
findMuslLoader + ProcessBuilder spawn line transparently picks it up
and bun no longer dies on legacy access/poll/dup2/etc. trapped by the
Android x86_64 seccomp policy.

ARM64 is intentionally skipped — the kernel ABI on aarch64-linux-musl
omits every legacy non-AT syscall the filter could trap on, so musl's
wrappers there never invoke a form the policy can block. The shim's
x86_64 inline asm and REG_RAX greg index would not even compile for
arm64 (sigsys-handler.c #errors on non-x86_64).
fix(android-agent): wire SIGSYS shim into stage-android-agent for x86_64

fix(local-inference): bump LOCAL_INFERENCE_PRIORITY -1 → 0

Cuttlefish smoke surfaced "No handler found for delegate type:
TEXT_SMALL" — the AOSP llama loader registered at priority -1, the
runtime's getModel() returned undefined when no priority-0 cloud
handler was loaded, and inference never reached the router.

The -1 was an attempt to "let cloud win by default" but it conflated
two orthogonal concerns:

  - Handler priority: a registration ordinal the runtime uses to pick
    a default candidate when nothing else exists.
  - Routing policy: the user's per-slot manual / cheapest / fastest /
    prefer-local / round-robin choice, owned by router-handler.ts +
    routing-policy.ts and dispatched from MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.

Bumping to 0 puts local-inference handlers in the same band as cloud
providers; tie-breaks live in routing-policy where they belong. Cloud-
only deployments are unaffected (cloud still registers at 0). AOSP-only
deployments now have a registered priority-0 handler so getModel()
returns it.

    register at priority 0 (regression for the smoke failure).

fix(local-agent-on-android): bun:ffi struct-by-value batch shim + KV chunking

- Wrap llama_batch_get_one + llama_decode behind shim
  (milady_llama_batch_get_one / milady_llama_batch_free /
  milady_llama_decode). bun:ffi cannot round-trip aggregate-by-value
  return/argument structs through the SysV ABI; previous direct
  bindings were reading garbage register values into the batch struct,
  tripping the GGML_ASSERT in llama_context::decode that requires
  exactly one of {token, embd} to be non-null.
- Drop n_batch / n_ubatch off n_ctx defaults (2048 / 512). The
  earlier set-equal-to-n_ctx allocated a 1.85 GiB compute graph and
  wedged the bun event loop long enough for the service watchdog
  to kill us during prompt processing.
- Chunk prompts into n_batch-sized pieces, with awaited setImmediate
  yields between chunks so the /api/health probe gets to run.
- Truncate prompts that exceed (n_ctx - reserve - n_batch)*0.75; drops
  head tokens, preserving the user's most recent turn. Flash-attention's
  sliding KV allocator returns rc=1 on near-full sequences even when
  positions are nominally free, so we leave 25 % headroom.
- Reset KV cache (llama_memory_clear) before each generate / embed
  except on a freshly-loaded ctx (cuttlefish x86_64 segfaults on a
  clear with no decoded positions). Tracked via this.hasDecoded.
- MiladyAgentService: bump HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS 3 s → 120 s. Bun blocks
  on FFI for the duration of one llama_decode call (~60–70 s for an
  n_batch=2048 chunk on cuttlefish CPU); a 3 s read-timeout fires
  mid-decode and racks up strikes. Bumped budget lets the probe sit
  on the socket until bun's setImmediate yield wakes the listener.
- MiladyAgentService: set ELIZA_CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS=1800000
  for AOSP_BUILD. CPU-only inference of a 12k-token planner prompt
  on SmolLM2-360M lands well past the 180 s default; 30 minutes
  covers prompt decode + token generation. Real device hardware
  finishes in seconds; this only matters for cvd smoke runs.

fix(local-agent-android): make Local Agent UX actually work end-to-end

Four discrete fixes that take the cuttlefish image from "Choose your
setup → BACKEND TIMEOUT loop" to a live Milady CompanionShell with the
on-device agent serving the WebView.

1. probe-local-agent accepts the real /api/health shape. The probe used
   to require `body.ok === true`, but the on-device @elizaos/agent
   responds with `{ ready: true, runtime: "ok", database: "ok",
   agentState: "running", ... }` — no `ok` key. Probe was permanently
   false against a healthy agent and the Local Agent tile never
   appeared. Now accepts {ok}, {ready}, or {agentState:"running"}.
   +2 tests pinning both shapes.

2. probe-local-agent split positive/negative cache TTLs. 30 s on a
   negative result kept the tile hidden for half a minute after the
   agent finished booting. Negatives now expire in 3 s; positives stay
   cached the full 30 s for render-cycle stability.

3. RuntimeGate re-polls the probe every 4 s while mounted and the
   agent isn't yet up. Cold boot of the on-device agent takes 30+ s
   (PGlite migration + GGUF model warmup); a one-shot probe at mount
   left the user stuck on Cloud/Remote even when the agent was racing
   toward live. With the polling loop the tile naturally appears as
   soon as /api/health goes green, the existing auto-pick fires, and
   the user lands in chat without ever seeing the "Choose your setup"
   screen — exactly the one-step boot the design wanted.

4. MainActivity sets the WebView's mixed-content mode to
   MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW. The Capacitor WebView renders the page
   at https://localhost; the on-device agent listens at
   http://127.0.0.1:31337. Without this knob Android upgrades the
   loopback fetch to https, the agent (no TLS) refuses, and the UI
   surfaces "Backend Timeout: /api/auth/status - Failed to fetch" even
   though the agent is plainly up.

5. MiladyAgentService no longer sets MILADY_REQUIRE_LOCAL_AUTH=1 by
   default. The bearer token is still generated and written to
   /data/data/<pkg>/files/auth/local-agent-token, and the env var
   ELIZA_API_TOKEN is still injected into the bun child, but the
   server-side gate is off until the WebView wires up a Capacitor
   plugin native binding to read the token file. Without this the
   WebView's first call to /api/auth/status got 401'd and the
   "Initializing agent…" splash never advanced. Re-enabling the gate
   is one line + the future native binding.

End-to-end on cuttlefish_x86_64:
  /api/health → 200 {"ready":true,"agentState":"running",...}
  WebView → /api/auth/status → 200
  RuntimeGate auto-picks Local Agent → CompanionShell renders.

fix(settings): close two structural bugs in the credential save path

These are the two highest-impact user-visible bugs in the existing
credential pipeline. Both are surgical fixes — no new abstractions,
no migrations, just correct the broken flow.

1) usePluginsSkillsState.ts — model-slug-overwrites-API-key

The legacy save path used `Object.values(config).find(non-empty)` to
pick "the API key" before calling switchProvider. This is sensitive
to JS object iteration order: whichever field the user typed FIRST
wins. Typing the model field before the API-key field caused the
model slug (e.g., "tencent/hy3-preview") to be picked up as the
provider's API key and overwrite the actual key.

Replaced with structured field identification using the plugin's
parameter metadata: pick the sensitive parameter whose key matches
an API-key naming pattern (or the first sensitive param as a
fallback). The actual config value is then read by that param's
key, never by value-iteration. Input order can no longer corrupt
the save.

2) server.ts /api/cloud/disconnect — orphan service-routing entries

When a user disconnected Eliza Cloud, the disconnect handler cleared
`cloud.apiKey` and `serviceRouting.llmText` but left the four other
service routes (tts, media, embeddings, rpc) pointing at
`cloud-proxy → elizacloud`. Result: silent 401s for months on every
TTS, image, embedding, and RPC call until the user noticed those
features stopped working.

Extended the disconnect patch to clear all five service routes that
elizacloud had been routing.

These changes don't depend on the new @elizaos/vault package, but
they pair with it cleanly: vault becomes the storage layer the save
path eventually writes through; this commit closes the failures
that exist independent of where the storage lives.

Addresses five review comments from greptile-apps[bot] on #7187.
Three were real bugs; two were design-smell concerns.

Real bugs (P1)
  - vault.list(prefix) prefix-as-substring match (vault.ts:230)
    The filter was `k === prefix || k.startsWith(`${prefix}.`)
    || k.startsWith(prefix)`. The third condition subsumed the
    second AND matched unintended keys: `list("ui")` returned
    `ui_legacy_thing` and `uib`, not just `ui.theme` and

    segment match. Regression test added.

    `!opts.sensitive` guard, so a routing entry like
    `routing: { "ui.theme": "1password" }` would push a
    non-sensitive value through an external password manager —
    contradicting the documented "non-sensitive always in-house"
    invariant. Reordered: sensitivity guard fires first; routing
    only applies for sensitive values. Regression test added.

Real bug (P2)
  - "Saved" button label never reverts (SecretsManagerSection.tsx)
    `Date.now() - savedAt < 2500` was evaluated only at render
    time. Once true, nothing else triggered a re-render at +2.5s,
    so the button stayed "Saved" until the next state change.
    Added a useEffect that clears `savedAt` after 2500ms,
    guaranteeing a re-render. Simplified the label expression
    accordingly: `savedAt !== null ? "Saved" : "Save"`.

    The reviewer's point: needing a `__resetSecretsManagerCacheForTests`

feat(vault/wiring): mirror sensitive plugin saves into @elizaos/vault (write-side)

The vault was a primitive without consumers in the save/load
paths. This adds the write-through mirror: every successful plugin
config save also writes its sensitive fields into the vault.

What this delivers
- Vault becomes populated with the user's actual saved keys
  alongside the legacy `config.env.X` / `config.env.vars.X` storage.
- The Secrets Storage modal's `vault.list()` now reflects what's
  actually saved, not what's hypothetical.
- A future Settings "Reveal" implementation can prefer
  `vault.reveal()` over the legacy `/api/plugins/:id/reveal` route,
  giving consistent treatment regardless of where the value lives.
- When the read-side hydration lands in a follow-up PR, no
  migration is needed: the vault already has the keys.

What this does NOT yet deliver
- Read-side wiring. The runtime still hydrates `process.env` from
  `config.env.X` via the legacy path; plugins read from there. The
  vault is a SHADOW for now. The Secrets Storage modal's "use
  1Password" preference is still decorative until read-side lands.
- Auto-creating items in 1Password / Bitwarden via their CLIs.
  Sensitive saves to in-house only; if the user's preferences say
  "1Password" but no `externalPath` is supplied, vault.set falls
  back to in-house (sensitive: true).

Implementation
- `plugins-compat-routes.ts` PUT handler: after the legacy persist
  + runtime apply succeed, call `mirrorPluginSensitiveToVault`.
- New helper iterates the plugin's `parameters`, finds those marked
  `sensitive`, reads the corresponding values from the request
  body's `config` map, and calls `vault.set(key, value, {
  sensitive: true })` for each.
- Vault key shape = the env-var name itself (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`).
  Matches what the legacy code uses; lets future read-side
  hydration round-trip without a translation layer.

Failure mode
- Any vault.set failure (OS keychain locked, file ENOSPC) is
  logged via `[plugins-compat] vault.set(<key>) failed: ...` and
  swallowed. The save itself is NOT rolled back — legacy storage
  has already succeeded. Users continue to work; the shadow just
  isn't populated for that field.
- Promise floats (caught with `.catch`) so save response isn't
  delayed by the mirror.

Read-side hydration scope
- Looked at the boot path in `eliza.ts setEnvFromConfig` and the
  cloud-managed key allowlist. The right wiring is more invasive
  than this PR should attempt — it touches the credential resolver,
  the eliza.ts boot, and the cloud-managed env allowlist. Filing
  as the next stacked PR after this one lands.

fix(vault): address remaining greptile review issues across the stack

Six issues across the closed-and-folded #7187/#7194 reviews and the
current #7197 review were left unaddressed by the earlier
493074e919 ("list prefix, saved timer, routing order, drop singleton").
"Drop singleton" actually introduced new races by making each HTTP
request build its own VaultImpl pointing at the same disk file.

Round-trip:

- **store.ts: unique per-write tmp filename** (P1). Was `${path}.tmp` —
  a fixed name that two VaultImpl instances racing on the same store
  could collide on. Now `${path}.tmp.${pid}.${randomBytes(8)}` so the
  tmp namespace is per-write, and the rename loser can't clobber a tmp
  the winner is still using.
- **store.ts: cleanup tmp on rename failure** (P1). Previously
  cross-device renames left orphaned `.tmp` files on disk. Now wrapped
  in try/finally with best-effort `fs.rm`.
- **store.ts: drop redundant chmod after rename** (P2 security).
  `fs.writeFile` with `{ mode: 0o600 }` already creates the tmp file
  with the right mode; POSIX rename preserves it. The post-rename
  chmod was a no-op on the happy path with a tiny TOCTOU window
  between rename and chmod where another process could observe the
  file at the umask default.
- **secrets-manager-routes.ts + plugins-compat-routes.ts: per-process
  singleton** (P1). Hoisted both `createManager()` and `createVault()`
  to module scope with a test-only reset hook. Two concurrent PUT
  requests now serialise on the same VaultImpl mutex; previously they
  built independent in-process locks pointing at the same disk file
  and could silently drop entries on the read-modify-write cycle.
  Side-benefit: scryptSync (in `passphraseMasterKey().load()`) now
  runs once at process boot instead of every request when a
  passphrase resolver is in use.
- **vault.ts: state dir convention** (P2). Resolution order was
  `MILADY_STATE_DIR → ELIZA_STATE_DIR → ~/.milady`; now
  `ELIZA_STATE_DIR → MILADY_STATE_DIR → ~/.eliza`. Co-locates the
  vault with `resolveStateDir()`'s default in the agent package so a
  fresh elizaos install doesn't write `~/.milady` next to `~/.eliza`.
- **manager.ts: encrypt preferences at rest** (P2 security). The
  `routing` map can carry password-manager item paths (e.g.
  "Personal/OpenRouter/api-key") which are internal-disclosure-level
  information. `setPreferences` now writes with `sensitive: true` so
  vault.json never contains those paths in clear text.

Plus a new regression test in `vault.test.ts`:

- 50 concurrent `vault.set` calls all round-trip cleanly (would have
  dropped writes under the fixed-tmp-name race)
- Leftover tmp scan walks the parent dir for any per-pid prefix, not
  just the legacy fixed name, so the test catches both old and new
  variants of the failure mode

feat(vault/wiring): mirror sensitive plugin saves into @elizaos/vault (write-side)

The vault was a primitive without consumers in the save/load
paths. This adds the write-through mirror: every successful plugin
config save also writes its sensitive fields into the vault.

What this delivers
- Vault becomes populated with the user's actual saved keys
  alongside the legacy `config.env.X` / `config.env.vars.X` storage.
- The Secrets Storage modal's `vault.list()` now reflects what's
  actually saved, not what's hypothetical.
- A future Settings "Reveal" implementation can prefer
  `vault.reveal()` over the legacy `/api/plugins/:id/reveal` route,
  giving consistent treatment regardless of where the value lives.
- When the read-side hydration lands in a follow-up PR, no
  migration is needed: the vault already has the keys.

What this does NOT yet deliver
- Read-side wiring. The runtime still hydrates `process.env` from
  `config.env.X` via the legacy path; plugins read from there. The
  vault is a SHADOW for now. The Secrets Storage modal's "use
  1Password" preference is still decorative until read-side lands.
- Auto-creating items in 1Password / Bitwarden via their CLIs.
  Sensitive saves to in-house only; if the user's preferences say
  "1Password" but no `externalPath` is supplied, vault.set falls
  back to in-house (sensitive: true).

Implementation
- `plugins-compat-routes.ts` PUT handler: after the legacy persist
  + runtime apply succeed, call `mirrorPluginSensitiveToVault`.
- New helper iterates the plugin's `parameters`, finds those marked
  `sensitive`, reads the corresponding values from the request
  body's `config` map, and calls `vault.set(key, value, {
  sensitive: true })` for each.
- Vault key shape = the env-var name itself (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`).
  Matches what the legacy code uses; lets future read-side
  hydration round-trip without a translation layer.

Failure mode
- Any vault.set failure (OS keychain locked, file ENOSPC) is
  logged via `[plugins-compat] vault.set(<key>) failed: ...` and
  swallowed. The save itself is NOT rolled back — legacy storage
  has already succeeded. Users continue to work; the shadow just
  isn't populated for that field.
- Promise floats (caught with `.catch`) so save response isn't
  delayed by the mirror.

Read-side hydration scope
- Looked at the boot path in `eliza.ts setEnvFromConfig` and the
  cloud-managed key allowlist. The right wiring is more invasive
  than this PR should attempt — it touches the credential resolver,
  the eliza.ts boot, and the cloud-managed env allowlist. Filing
  as the next stacked PR after this one lands.

Builds on PR #7187 (the @elizaos/vault package + Settings UI).

feat(local-agent-android): bun execve + bearer auth + auto-pick

The agent now actually exec's on the cuttlefish image. Successive fixes:

- MiladyAgentService writes a per-boot 32-byte hex token to
  /data/data/<pkg>/files/auth/local-agent-token (mode 0600) and passes
  it via ELIZA_API_TOKEN to the bun child. Server-side, the new
  MILADY_REQUIRE_LOCAL_AUTH=1 env var flips
  isTrustedLocalRequest()'s "loopback is implicitly trusted" heuristic
  off, so every API call from the WebView (or anywhere else) needs a
  bearer token even though it lives on the same loopback. Closes the
  multi-app-on-loopback IPC gap the user surfaced.

- ABI selection in MiladyAgentService.resolveRuntimeAbi() now respects
  Build.SUPPORTED_ABIS[0] order — cuttlefish_x86_64 reports
  ["x86_64","arm64-v8a"] and was previously preferring arm64
  unconditionally, which produced ENOEXEC on the wrong-arch binary.

- Phase A's stage-android-agent.mjs and the spawn site land binaries
  back under assets/agent/{abi}/ instead of jniLibs/{abi}/. The
  earlier jniLibs pivot worked around an SELinux execute denial that
  turned out to be the platform_app vs priv_app domain (we kept the
  platform certificate) — narrower fix is a single vendor sepolicy
  allow rule. The lib*.so renaming + symlink dance disappears with
  it.

- Vendor sepolicy adds milady_agent.te:
    allow platform_app app_data_file:file { execute execute_no_trans };
  AOSP's stock platform_app does not include the equivalent of
  priv_app's `allow priv_app privapp_data_file:file execute`, so
  without this rule the bun execve fails with avc: denied { execute }
  on the loader. validateSepolicy() now pins the rule.

- MiladyAgentService creates a libstdc++.so.6 → libstdc++.so.6.0.33
  symlink in agent/{abi}/ at extraction time so bun's musl loader
  finds the shared object by its soname instead of crashing with
  hundreds of relocation errors.

- run-mobile-build.mjs's isCapacitorPlatformReady() now also requires
  AndroidManifest.xml to exist (was the cause of one round-trip APK
  build failure earlier — a deleted manifest never re-generated).

- RuntimeGate auto-picks Local Agent on Android when the probe
  succeeds and no mode is persisted. User boots cuttlefish → straight
  into chat. Settings ▸ Runtime can re-open the picker for users who
  want cloud/remote later.

- Phase D bundle's externals list adds @elizaos/plugin-browser-bridge
  → null-plugin stub. The eager static import in eliza.ts was
  pulling puppeteer transitively into the mobile bundle.

End state on cuttlefish: bun process executes, MiladyAgentService
keeps it alive via watchdog with exponential backoff, /api/health
responds 200 against the spike-stub bundle. The full @elizaos/agent
bundle exec's but exits with SIGSYS (code 159) — Android's seccomp
filter blocks a syscall bun makes (likely io_uring_setup or one of
the platform-specific futex variants). That's the next yard:
seccomp policy diagnosis + targeted exemption in vendor sepolicy.

feat(confidant): elizaOS integration helpers — schema registry + legacy env bridge

Adds two integration modules so an elizaOS host app can adopt Confidant
in two lines of bootstrap rather than 14 individual schema declarations.
Both are pure data-shape, non-invasive to existing runtime code:

- `registerElizaProviderSchemas()` — registers the canonical schema for
  every AI provider in the elizaOS catalog (anthropic, openai,
  openrouter, google, groq, xai, deepseek, mistral, together, zai,
  elizacloud, ollama) plus the two subscription credential types
  (anthropic-subscription, openai-codex). Each entry carries the
  human label, format-prefix hint (sk-or-v1-..., sk-ant-..., sk-...),
  sensitivity flag, and ownership attribution to the matching plugin
  id (so the implicit-grant rule fires automatically once those
  plugins migrate to Confidant reads).

- `mirrorLegacyEnvCredentials(confidant, credentials)` — bulk-registers
  `env://VAR_NAME` references in Confidant given a list of resolved
  credentials in the shape `@elizaos/app-core`'s `credential-resolver`
  already produces. Returns a structured report of migrated vs.
  skipped entries (unknown-provider / missing-env-var), so callers
  can log adoption progress at boot.

Also exports `isSubscriptionProviderId(providerId)` (used by the future
CloudBackend to refuse syncing device-bound tokens) and
`providerIdForSecretId(id)` (inverse lookup for telemetry).

Why not in `@elizaos/agent` or `@elizaos/typescript`
- The bridge is data-shape-only — `ResolvedCredentialLike` mirrors the
  existing `credential-resolver` shape but the import is structural,
  not a runtime dependency. This avoids forcing `@elizaos/confidant`
  into a dependency cycle with the runtime packages and keeps the
  Confidant package consumable by any host app, not just the elizaOS
  reference runtime.

Tests added (test/integrations.test.ts)
- Coverage of the canonical map, the schema registration, the bridge
  migration paths (success / unknown / missing-env), the subscription
  flag, and the inverse lookup.
- An end-to-end "real-world bootstrap" test that wires schema +
  bridge + scoped resolve through env-legacy and verifies the audit
  log records the granted resolve correctly with `source: env-legacy`.

docs(confidant): seven-phase migration guide for host apps

Adds MIGRATION.md showing step-by-step how an existing Eliza host app
adopts Confidant without breaking the running app at any point. Mirrors
the 7-phase plan from §9 of the architecture design doc but
operationalized for someone reading this package's docs:

Phase 1 — initialize Confidant at app boot (mirror legacy env)
Phase 2 — single canonical writer (Settings saves through confidant.set)
Phase 3 — built-in AI providers migrate to Confidant reads
Phase 4 — password manager backends (1Password, Proton Pass)
Phase 5 — third-party plugins migrate
Phase 6 — close the boundary (process.env.*_API_KEY undefined)
Phase 7 (optional) — E2E-encrypted Cloud sync

Each phase has steps, an exit criterion, and a one-liner test the
migrator can run to verify they actually completed it.

Also documents migration anti-patterns (reading process.env after
phase 6, `*` grants, caching resolved values) and a "When something
breaks" section pointing at the audit log.

feat(confidant): plugin-author entry point — defineSchemaFromRegistry

Adds the scalable answer for the rest of the elizaOS plugin ecosystem
(elizaos-plugins/*, third-party plugins, future plugins). Confidant
doesn't hardcode every plugin in the universe — each plugin self-
registers from its own code in one call.

New API
- `defineSchemaFromRegistry(registryEntry, { domain, subject })` —
  reads the same plugin registry JSON entry the Settings UI already
  uses, finds every `type: "secret"` field, registers each as a
  Confidant SecretId scoped to the plugin's id. Returns a structured
  report (`registered` / `skipped`) so callers can log adoption.

Helpers
- `defaultFieldNameForEnvVar(envVar, subject, domain)` — the default
  env-var → camelCased-field extractor. Strips the subject prefix
  (case-insensitive, dash- or underscore-tolerant), preserves common
  field names (apiKey, apiToken, accessToken, webhookSecret, etc.).
- Per-call overrides: `fieldNameForEnvVar`, `pluginId`, `only`
  (allowlist).

Canonical domains
- `CanonicalDomain` type names the eleven structural namespaces:
  llm, subscription, tts, tool, connector, wallet, rpc, trading,
  music, storage, service. Plugin authors pick the one that matches
  their role; the namespace is shared across the ecosystem so users
  can predict where a plugin's credentials live.

Tests (test/plugin-registry.test.ts)
- Real elizaos-plugins-shaped registry entries — Discord, an LLM
  provider, a wallet plugin with multiple fields.
- The `only` allowlist for plugins with a mix of secret and
  non-secret-but-related fields.
- pluginId override for re-publication scenarios.
- fieldNameForEnvVar override for non-standard env-var shapes.
- Empty / missing registry handling.
- Idempotency (re-registering the same plugin is a no-op).
- Comprehensive coverage of the field-name extractor across normal,
  dashed, and full-camel cases.
- Test count: 91 → 104.

  with one-line adoption example, the canonical domain table, field-
  name conventions, customization patterns, and an explicit list of
  what the plugin gets in return (1Password support, audit log,
  cross-plugin denial, sync semantics, etc.).

Why this matters
- Hardcoding 31 monorepo plugins doesn't scale to the hundreds in
  elizaos-plugins/* and beyond. The right architecture is plugins as
  the source of truth for their own credentials, with Confidant
  providing the structural seam. This commit ships that seam.

feat(confidant): testing harness — createTestConfidant + MockBackend + MockPromptHandler

Adds a framework-agnostic testing surface at the subpath
`@elizaos/confidant/testing` so plugin authors and host-app authors
can test their Confidant integration without an OS keychain, a real
password-manager CLI, or `process.env`.

The harness composes a real Confidant — real encryption, real audit
log, real policy engine — with assertion helpers. No vitest / jest /
mocha imports; works with any test runner.

New API
- `createTestConfidant(opts)` — returns a TestConfidant with a temp
  store, in-memory master key, pre-loaded `secrets` / `references`,
  pre-registered `schemas` (drives implicit grants), and pre-seeded
  cross-skill `grants`. Exposes `getAuditRecords` / `getResolves` /
  `getDenials` / `clearAuditLog`, and `dispose()` for cleanup.
- `MockBackend(source, initial?)` — fully-functional in-memory
  VaultBackend. Records every interaction (`resolve` / `store` /
  `remove`), supports `failNext(error)` for one-shot failure
  injection, and `setValue` / `removeValue` / `resetCalls` for
  runtime mutation between assertion phases.
- `MockPromptHandler(opts)` — for `prompt`-mode grants. `respondWith`
  is either a fixed boolean or a function that decides per-call.
  Records every prompt for inspection via `getCalls()`.
- `resetTestRegistry()` — public name for the schema registry reset
  (the schema registry is process-global; tests sharing a process
  must reset between cases).

Tests added (test/testing.test.ts)
- 16 cases covering the full harness:
  - Pre-loaded secrets via implicit owner grant
  - Ciphertext-on-disk-not-plaintext invariant in test mode
  - Cross-skill denial enforcement
  - Explicit grants (string-pattern AND full Grant-object forms)
  - Audit log filtering (all / resolves / denials)
  - clearAuditLog round-trip
  - dispose() cleanup vs. workDir override (debugging artifacts)
  - MockBackend reference resolution
  - MockBackend.failNext queueing semantics
  - MockBackend.setValue / removeValue runtime mutation
  - MockBackend.resetCalls clears log without mutating values
  - MockPromptHandler respondWith: true / false / function-per-call
- Test count: 104 → 120.

Documentation
- TESTING.md (440 lines) — quick start, options reference, MockBackend
  walkthrough with failure injection, MockPromptHandler patterns,
  audit-log assertions, schema isolation, and worked examples for
  plugin-author tests, cross-plugin denial tests, migration bridge
  tests, and host-app bootstrap tests. Explicit "what you do/don't
  need to mock" section.
- README updated with a brief testing-harness pointer.

Package layout
- New subpath export: `"./testing": "./src/testing.ts"`. Consumers
  import via `import { ... } from "@elizaos/confidant/testing"` to
  keep test-only code out of production bundles.

feat(confidant/testing): MockKeyringBackend + device-keychain testing patterns

Closes a gap in the testing harness around OS-keychain-backed
secrets. Confidant's production code uses @napi-rs/keyring to talk to
macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager / Linux libsecret through
one API; the test harness now has first-class support for mocking
that surface AND clear docs for the three patterns plugin authors
need.

New API
- `MockKeyringBackend` — convenience subclass of `MockBackend`
  specialized for the `keyring` source. Stores values keyed by
  `(service, account)` and produces idiomatic
  `keyring://service/account` references — the same shape the real
  `KeyringBackend` emits. Cross-platform by construction (nothing
  hits the OS keychain).
  - `setEntry(service, account, value)` / `removeEntry(service, account)`
    mirror the real KeyringBackend mental model.
  - `MockKeyringBackend.reference(service, account)` static helper
    builds the canonical URI.
  - Inherits `failNext`, `getResolves`, `resetCalls` from the parent.
- The reference URI shape matches the real `KeyringBackend` exactly
  (split on the LAST `/` to handle service names with slashes like
  `@elizaos/confidant`), so tests written against MockKeyringBackend
  swap to the real backend without code changes.

Tests added (test/testing.test.ts)
- Real round-trip via mocked keychain
- setEntry / removeEntry / static reference helper coverage
- Platform-specific failure simulation via failNext (Linux Secret
  Service unavailable, Windows entry not found, Mac Keychain locked)
- Test count: 120 → 124.

TESTING.md additions
- New "Testing OS-keychain-backed secrets" section covering all three
  patterns plugin authors face:
  1. Plugin / runtime tests — MockKeyringBackend (the typical case;
     no real OS access; works the same on every platform).
  2. Host-app integration tests — register the real KeyringBackend
     against a TEST-ONLY service name; pre-stage entries via
     `@napi-rs/keyring`'s `Entry`; clean up in afterEach.
  3. Cross-platform CI — the Confidant package's own
     `confidant-ci.yaml` already runs the keyring round-trip suite on
     ubuntu/macos/windows. Plugin authors don't need their own matrix
     for keychain coverage; Confidant's CI proves the platform
     contract.
- Explicit table of platform-specific failure modes plugin authors
  may want to simulate (Linux Secret Service unavailable, Mac
  Keychain locked, Windows Credential Manager entry-not-found).
- Reminders about test-only service names + afterEach cleanup so dev
  keychains don't accumulate test droppings.

containers: project-scoped persistent volumes (agent identity layer)

Treat (organization_id, project_name) as the durable agent identity at
the storage layer. Volumes move from per-container paths
(/data/containers/<id>) to per-project paths
(/data/projects/<org_id>/<project_name>). Effects:

- Redeploying an agent under the same project_name reuses the same data
  on disk. Container id changes; agent state survives.
- Sticky scheduling — when a project already has a volume on a node,
  new deploys land on that node. Prior containers' volumes are pinned
  to their host today; no cross-host migration yet.
- Purge guard accepts both /data/projects/ and the legacy
  /data/containers/ prefix; never rm -rf's anything outside those.

This is the smallest version of the agents-identity feature: no new
table, no new model, just the right key for the volume. A future
`agents` resource can sit on top of this without breaking the storage.

fix(workers): restore process.env hydration band-aid

Shaw's d81cbc49a 'Worker env via ALS' commit removed the
Object.assign(process.env, c.env) pattern from bootstrap-app.ts in
favor of getCloudAwareEnv() + AsyncLocalStorage. The ALS pattern is
the correct long-term answer, but the migration is incomplete:
packages/lib/** still has many code paths that read process.env
directly (jwks, service-key, eliza/config, model-tiers, oauth
provider-registry, payout-alerts, etc.). With the band-aid removed,
those readers see undefined and routes silently fail closed.

  configured as Worker secrets

landed, so it still ships the old bootstrap with the band-aid in
place.

Long-term fix is to migrate packages/lib/** readers to
getCloudAwareEnv(). Until then, keep both patterns in parallel.

ci(cf-deploy): bypass wrangler-action, use bunx wrangler directly

cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3 invokes `npm i wrangler@<x>` to ensure
wrangler is available, which fails in this monorepo:

fix(auth): preempt steward session expiry with eager server+client refresh

Shadow reported being signed out after ~15min, which matches the access
token TTL exactly. Two gaps in our refresh story that made this happen:

1. Server middleware only triggered /auth/refresh when the access token
   was ALREADY expired. If the user's first navigation after a long idle
   coincided with the token expiring milliseconds ago, the refresh
   window was racy. Now we preemptively refresh whenever the token has
   less than 180s remaining on any protected-path request.

2. Client-side interval timer (checkAndRefresh every 60s, triggers when
   <120s left) is unreliable in background tabs. Chrome throttles
   setInterval to roughly 1 call per minute in inactive tabs and can
   suspend them entirely when memory-pressure hits. A user returning to
   an idle-for-15-min tab would find their token gone and the interval
   hadn't fired its check. Added visibilitychange + online event
   handlers that force an immediate check-and-refresh when the tab
   becomes visible or the network reconnects.

Together these close the window in which an expired token reaches any
server request handler. The server-side middleware is the real backstop
since it runs for every protected request regardless of tab state.

frontend: green vite build (trim routes + node-builtin shims)

Build now succeeds: 38k modules transformed, dist/ contains index.html
and chunked JS/CSS for the wired routes.

Why the trim:
  Many legacy dashboard pages (and the dashboard layout itself) call
  server-only helpers (requireAuthWithOrg, cookies(), @/db/* schemas,
  @/lib/services/* with pg/nodemailer/posthog-node/auto-top-up). Those
  pull a giant transitive graph through the bundler that the SPA cannot
  execute. Wiring them lazily was not enough — vite still has to walk
  the graph at build time.

Approach:
  - src/App.tsx now wires only SPA-safe routes (/, /login, /auth/*,
    /payment/success, /invite/accept, /blog, /terms-of-service,
    /sandbox-proxy, /app-auth/authorize). All /dashboard/*, /chat/*,
    /docs/* fall through to <UnportedPlaceholder /> with a pointer to
    MIGRATION_NOTES.md.
  - src/shims/empty.ts provides a defensive stub for every node built-in
    a transitive dep might still import (fs, path, os, crypto, stream,
    http, https, url, util, events, EventEmitter class, etc.). Browser
    code never reaches these paths; the stub throws if it does, so we
    fail loud instead of silently shipping broken bytes.
  - vite.config.ts aliases all node:* and bare node built-ins to the
    shim and pre-scopes optimizeDeps.entries to src/main.tsx.
  - frontend/.gitignore added (dist/, node_modules/, *.log).

feat(distro-android): brand-aware AOSP/Cuttlefish toolchain + workflow

Lifts MiladyOS's AOSP/Cuttlefish build toolchain upstream so any brand
(default ElizaOS, downstream MiladyOS) can build a privileged-system-app
distribution by supplying a JSON brand config + vendor tree.

What's new:

  scripts/distro-android/
    brand-config.mjs      Brand resolver: --brand-config <PATH> | $DISTRO_ANDROID_BRAND_CONFIG | brand.eliza.json
    brand.eliza.json      Default ElizaOS brand (ai.elizaos.app, eliza_cf_x86_64_phone, …)
    build-aosp.mjs        Top-level pipeline: libllama → APK → sync → validate → m → cvd start → boot-validate
    sync-to-aosp.mjs      Copy <vendorDir> → <aospRoot>/vendor/<brand>
    validate.mjs          Static vendor + APK validator (xmllint, aapt); class names parameterised on brand.classPrefix
    boot-validate.mjs     adb checks against booted device (roles, intents, package flags, logcat); property prefix from brand.propertyPrefix
    lint-init-rc.mjs      Brand-agnostic Android init.rc syntax checker
    compile-libllama.mjs  Cross-compile musl-linked libllama.so per ABI for the bundled bun runtime
    README.md             Brand contract + downstream call instructions

  os/android/
    vendor/eliza/         Brand-renamed copy of milady's vendor tree (Eliza/eliza/elizaos/ai.elizaos.app)
    README.md             Distro layer overview

  .github/workflows/
    elizaos-cuttlefish.yml   workflow_dispatch + workflow_call; brand-config/vendor-source inputs
    actionlint.yaml          Declares 'kvm' self-hosted runner label

Whitelabel pattern (downstream brand calls eliza's reusable workflow):

    jobs:
      build:
        uses: elizaOS/eliza/.github/workflows/elizaos-cuttlefish.yml@develop
        with:
          brand-config: os/android/brand.mybrand.json
          vendor-source: os/android/vendor/mybrand
          aosp-root: /aosp
          launch: true

Or invoke directly when eliza is checked out as a submodule:

    node eliza/scripts/distro-android/build-aosp.mjs \
      --brand-config os/android/brand.mybrand.json \
      --source-vendor os/android/vendor/mybrand \
      --aosp-root /aosp --launch --boot-validate

capture-screens, sim, build-bootanimation) are not yet ported — they can be

embedding model into the APK at assets/agent/models/ along with a
manifest.json. MiladyAgentService extracts those files into
$MILADY_STATE_DIR/local-inference/models/ on first launch, and the
new bundled-models bootstrap registers each one in the local-inference
registry with source: "milady-download" so the auto-assign pass picks
them up without any download UX.

  every entry, stat's the file on disk, calls upsertMiladyModel. Missing
  files are skipped (broken APK, not broken runtime). Idempotent: the
  registry's id-keyed upsert overwrites cleanly, so re-running on every
  service start is fine.

  0), happy path, missing-file skip, and idempotency.

  so a malformed manifest never breaks the service — worst case is the
  user sees no bundled models and falls back to the existing download

  builds (which don't ship the bundle), so this is a clean no-op there.

feat(local-inference): auto-assign single-model to TEXT_SMALL/TEXT_LARGE

`ensure-local-inference-handler.ts#ensureAssignedModelLoaded` throws
"No local model is active. Assign a model to ${slot} or activate one
in Settings → Local models." whenever a slot has no assignment but a
model is installed. On AOSP all-local first-light, the auto-pick
onboarding lands the user in chat without ever opening Settings, so
the very first turn fails.

Two new functions in `services/local-inference/assignments.ts`:

- `ensureDefaultAssignment(modelId)`: idempotent fill of empty slots.
  Embedding model ids (catalog category/bucket "embedding" or known
  prefix markers like nomic-embed-, bge-, all-minilm-, gte-, e5-)
  only fill TEXT_EMBEDDING; everything else fills TEXT_SMALL +
  TEXT_LARGE. Existing slot assignments are never overwritten.

- `autoAssignAtBoot(installed)`: fills slots only when exactly one
  model is installed and no assignments exist. No-op for the >1 or
  0 cases (cannot guess intent).

Wired in two places:

1. `downloader.ts#runJob` — calls `ensureDefaultAssignment` after
   `upsertMiladyModel`. The just-downloaded model becomes usable
   without a Settings detour. Idempotent across re-downloads.

2. `ensure-local-inference-handler.ts#ensureLocalInferenceHandler`
   — calls `autoAssignAtBoot` right after the available-backend
   pre-flight, so a fresh boot with one externally-discovered or
   pre-downloaded model auto-assigns. The hard `Slot ... assigned ...`
   error in `ensureAssignedModelLoaded` now only fires when the user
   has actively cleared the assignment, which is the intended
   semantic.

Eleven new tests cover ensureDefaultAssignment (generative/embedding
slot routing, no-overwrite, partial-fill) and autoAssignAtBoot
(single-model fill, no-op when assignments present / >1 / 0 / boot
embedding case).

fix(android-agent): SIGSYS / seccomp mitigation via bun feature flags

The on-device bun process was exit-trapping with SIGSYS (signal 31, exit
code 159) at first interpretation of user code on cuttlefish. Root cause
is Android's per-process seccomp-bpf filter installed by the zygote
(bionic/libc/seccomp/{x86_64,arm64}_app_policy.cpp) blocking syscalls
bun makes that aren't on the app domain's allowlist:

  - io_uring_setup / io_uring_enter / io_uring_register (bun's IO pool)
  - pidfd_open (bun's child-process waiter)
  - preadv2 / pwritev2 with RWF_NONBLOCK (bun's async fs path)

SELinux policy in vendor/milady/sepolicy/ is orthogonal — it does not
(and cannot) override seccomp. The filter is inherited and locked via
SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_TSYNC before our process exists, and PR_SET_NO_NEW_-
PRIVS makes the trap final.

Mitigation: pass four BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_* env vars to the spawned bun
child that steer it onto fallback syscalls Android's allowlist already
covers (drop io_uring, drop pidfd_open via waiter-thread, drop
RWF_NONBLOCK from preadv2/pwritev2, drop spawnsync fast path).

Also: add a NOTE block to milady_agent.te making the SELinux/seccomp
distinction explicit, and a "SELinux is NOT seccomp" section to
sepolicy/README.md with the diagnosis playbook (adb logcat / dmesg
incantations + how to map a `audit: type=1326 syscall=N` line to a
syscall name via bionic/libc/kernel/uapi/asm-generic/unistd.h).

This is the "next yard" flagged in 61082accee. Verifies on a fresh
cuttlefish boot: the agent process stays alive and /api/health returns
200 against the full @elizaos/agent bundle (not just the spike stub).

fix(local-inference): MILADY_STATE_DIR fallback in paths.ts

`localInferenceRoot()` only read `ELIZA_STATE_DIR`. On AOSP the agent
process is spawned by `MiladyAgentService.java` with `MILADY_STATE_DIR`
set to `/data/data/<pkg>/files/.milady` and no `ELIZA_STATE_DIR`, so the
fallback hit `os.homedir() + "/.eliza"` and models landed at
`/data/data/<pkg>/files/.eliza/local-inference/models/` instead of the
user-facing `.milady/` state dir. Same divergence for the registry,
downloads staging, and the within-root membership check.

Resolution order is now `MILADY_STATE_DIR` → `ELIZA_STATE_DIR` → `~/.eliza`.
The `.eliza` fallback stays for desktop backward-compat with existing
installs. Added tests for all three precedence paths plus the `~/.eliza`
default.

fix(aosp-build): keep node-llama-cpp stubbed; statically import aosp adapter

The previous build gate at MILADY_AOSP_BUILD=1 un-stubbed node-llama-cpp
and its prebuild aliases under the assumption that the AOSP runtime would
need them. It does not — the AOSP path uses bun:ffi against libllama.so +
libmilady-llama-shim.so directly via runtime/aosp-llama-adapter.ts. Leaving
node-llama-cpp real pulled in unresolvable per-platform prebuild packages
(@node-llama-cpp/win-x64-cuda-ext, etc.) that the agent's transitive
imports reference but the AOSP target cannot install, breaking the build.

Two changes:

1. Drop the AOSP ternary in build-mobile-bundle.mjs. node-llama-cpp and
   the @node-llama-cpp/* aliases are now stubbed unconditionally for every
   mobile target (AOSP and Capacitor).

2. Add a static, named import of registerAospLlamaLoader from bin.ts so
   Bun.build inlines the adapter into agent-bundle.js. A bare side-effect
   import is not enough — empirically, Bun tree-shakes the symbol when
   nothing references the export. The named import is captured to
   globalThis to anchor the reference; the assignment is otherwise inert
   on every non-AOSP platform because the adapter self-gates on
   MILADY_LOCAL_LLAMA=1 at registration time, not at module load.

Verification: MILADY_AOSP_BUILD=1 bun run build:mobile now succeeds,
producing a 33.27 MB agent-bundle.js with multiple registerAospLlamaLoader,
MILADY_LOCAL_LLAMA, and libllama markers (vs. zero before).

feat(aosp-local): bun:ffi struct-by-value via libmilady-llama-shim.so

The bun:ffi adapter previously passed zeroed buffers to llama.cpp's
struct-by-value entry points (llama_model_load_from_file,
llama_init_from_model, llama_sampler_chain_init) because bun:ffi has no
struct-by-value support. That clobbered the canonical defaults — most
importantly model_params.use_mmap = true. With use_mmap forced to false,
the loader read the entire weights file into RAM, which is correctness-
impacting on phones with tight memory budgets.

This commit moves struct-by-value calls through libmilady-llama-shim.so
(built per ABI by scripts/miladyos/compile-libllama.mjs in the parent
repo). The shim runs llama.cpp's *_default_params() helpers under the
hood and returns malloc'd pointers. The adapter dlopens libllama.so first
(populating its symbols globally), then dlopens the shim (NEEDED libllama),
materializes params via the shim's *_params_default() entry points,
optionally calls field-by-field setters to override the few values the
adapter cares about, hands the pointer to the shim's wrapper which
dereferences it once into the real struct-by-value entry point, and
frees the pointer in try/finally so error paths don't leak.

Setters exposed (matched against b4500 llama.h):

docs(aosp-local): clarify TurboQuant fork scope

The apothic/llama.cpp-1bit-turboquant fork's `tbq3_0` / `tbq4_0`
KV-cache types are implemented only in `ggml-cpu` and `ggml-cuda`
(verified against the fork's README and direct inspection of
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/turboquant.cuh` + `fattn-vec-instance-tbq*`
template instances; no `tbq*` references in `ggml-metal`,
`ggml-vulkan`, `ggml-opencl`, `ggml-hexagon`, or `ggml-hip`).

That makes the fork CPU-or-CUDA only. On mobile (Vulkan / GPU-delegate)
and Apple Silicon (Metal), Bonsai 8B 1-bit still loads on stock
llama.cpp at the standard KV-cache footprint — only the TurboQuant
memory win is unavailable. Update the catalog blurb to spell that out
so users can make an informed call.

Decision: do NOT switch the AOSP libllama.so source pin to the apothic
fork. The fork is single-architecture (CPU+CUDA), Milady's AOSP build
is musl-cross-compiled for CPU only on aarch64/x86_64-linux-musl with
no CUDA on those ABIs, and switching would diverge from upstream
release cadence while breaking the b4500 symbol pin the FFI adapter
relies on. Documented in the parent commit's docs update.

feat(android-local): TEXT_EMBEDDING routing through DeviceBridge

End-to-end on-device embeddings on the Capacitor APK path. The
DeviceBridge already shuttled `generate` to a paired device; this
wires the symmetric `embed` flow so the agent's TEXT_EMBEDDING handler
dispatches to whichever device has the model loaded.

DeviceBridge wire protocol (device-bridge.ts):
- New device→agent message: `embedResult` (success | error variants),
  symmetric to `generateResult`. Carries `embedding: number[]` and a
  `tokens` count.
- New agent→device message: `embed` carrying the input string.
- New `pendingEmbeds` map mirrors `pendingGenerates` for routing,
  re-routing on disconnect, and timeout handling.
- Status snapshot counts pending embeds in `pendingRequests` and per-
  device `activeRequests`.
- `DeviceBridge.embed({ input })` picks the best-scoring connected
  device, parks the request when none are connected, times out per
  ELIZA_DEVICE_GENERATE_TIMEOUT_MS (default 60s).
- Both `registerDeviceBridgeLoader` flavours (the one in this file and
  the one in ensure-local-inference-handler.ts) expose `embed` on the
  registered `localInferenceLoader` service.

Capacitor adapter (native-plugins/llama):
- LlamaAdapter contract now exposes `embed(options)` returning
  `{ embedding, tokens }`. The native llama-cpp-capacitor plugin
  exposes `embedding(contextId, text, params)` plus `tokenize` from
  v0.1.5; we feature-detect both at call time so older builds throw
  the explicit "no embedding() on this build" error rather than
  silently miscomputing (Commandment 8).
- `CapacitorLlamaAdapter.embed` calls the native `embedding()` and
  back-fills the token count via `tokenize()` (best-effort; a tokenize
  failure does not block the embedding result).
- `registerCapacitorLlamaLoader` adds `embed` to the registered
  `localInferenceLoader` service so the runtime handler picks it up
  alongside `generate`.

Tests:
- device-bridge.test.ts: new e2e cases — happy-path embed roundtrip,
  reroute when the routed device drops mid-flight, no-device timeout,
  and device-side error propagation.
- native-plugins/llama/src/index.test.ts: embed() invokes the native
  embedding/tokenize methods with the right args, throws when called
  before load(), and the registered loader exposes `embed`. Reset the
  module-level singleton between cases so prior load() state doesn't
  bleed.
- ensure-local-inference-handler.test.ts: device-bridge expectations
  bumped from 2 to 3 registrations (TEXT_SMALL + TEXT_LARGE +
  TEXT_EMBEDDING) now that the bridge loader exposes embed.

implement it on the AOSP bun:ffi adapter, and wire TEXT_EMBEDDING into
`ensureLocalInferenceHandler` so the runtime routes embedding calls
through the loaded model on AOSP builds.

LocalInferenceLoader (active-model.ts):
- Add `embed?(args: { input: string }) => Promise<{ embedding: number[];
  tokens: number }>`. Optional so loaders that can't embed (Capacitor at
  the moment, the desktop fallback engine) leave it undefined and the
  runtime falls through to the operator's configured embedding provider
  rather than serving a silent zero-vector (Commandment 8).

  `llama_get_embeddings`, `llama_model_n_embd`, plus the bun:ffi
  `toArrayBuffer` helper for reading the ctx-owned float buffer.
- Implement `embed(input)`: tokenize → toggle ctx into embeddings mode
  via `llama_set_embeddings(ctx, true)` → decode as one sequence → read
  the pooled per-sequence vector via `llama_get_embeddings_seq(ctx, 0)`.

  model has `pooling_type == NONE`. Restore generation mode in the
  finally block so the next `generate()` doesn't pay a KV-cache reload
  on its first decode.

  memory so the JS array survives the next decode.

  loadModel/unloadModel/currentModelPath/generate.

fix(aosp-local): bump llama.cpp pin to b4500 for sampler chain API

The bun:ffi adapter at packages/agent/src/runtime/aosp-llama-adapter.ts
binds the post-rewrite llama.cpp symbol surface — sampler chain
(`llama_sampler_chain_init`, `llama_sampler_init_greedy`, etc.) plus
the renamed model/vocab API (`llama_model_load_from_file`,
`llama_init_from_model`, `llama_model_get_vocab`, `llama_vocab_eos`,
`llama_vocab_is_eog`). The previous pin (b3490) predates BOTH rewrites:
it ships only the legacy `llama_sample_*` family and the older
`llama_load_model_from_file` / `llama_token_eos` names.

Result: dlopen() succeeded, but `dlsym("llama_sampler_chain_init")` and
every renamed symbol returned NULL. The first call to `generate()`
would throw at runtime — local inference was broken end-to-end on AOSP.

Bump to tag b4500 (commit a133566d34a1dd3693c504786963bf1b7b7d8c0e) —
the first stable tag that exports ALL of the symbols the adapter binds,
including the embedding helpers (`llama_set_embeddings`,
`llama_get_embeddings_seq`, `llama_get_embeddings`, `llama_model_n_embd`)
that the embed() path will use in the follow-up commit.

Researched at https://api.github.com/repos/ggerganov/llama.cpp/contents/include/llama.h?ref=<tag>
across b3490..b4800: b3490 has 0 sampler_chain_init declarations and 5
sample_token declarations; b4500 has 3 sampler_chain_init declarations,
0 sample_token, 2 model_load_from_file, 2 init_from_model, 2 vocab_eos,
2 vocab_is_eog, 1 model_get_vocab, 1 get_embeddings_seq.

Adapter changes:
- Update file header to reflect b4500 / new SHA, with a "why we bumped"
  paragraph and a known-limitation note about struct-by-value (bun:ffi
  has no support for struct-by-value passing; the default-params calls
  pass zeroed buffers; documented for follow-up shim work).
- Add the embedding symbols (`llama_set_embeddings`,
  `llama_get_embeddings_seq`, `llama_get_embeddings`,
  `llama_model_n_embd`) to the dlopen manifest. These will be wired up
  to an `embed()` method in the next commit.
- Add a regression test that intercepts the bun:ffi `dlopen` call and
  asserts the symbol manifest contains every sampler-chain, renamed
  model/vocab, and embedding symbol the adapter relies on. Catches a
  future regression where someone trims the manifest below what
  libllama.so actually exports.

fix(app-control): dedupe verification verdicts + harden bridge unsubscribe

VerificationRoomBridgeService now deduplicates verdict broadcasts keyed
by `${sessionId}:${verdict}` with a 10-minute TTL so a replayed
task_complete or escalation event cannot post a duplicate continuation
message into the originating chat room. Sweep is opportunistic on each
insert.

stop() now reads the stored unsubscribe locally, clears the field
first (so a retry of stop() is a no-op), runtime-checks that the value
is a function, and wraps the call in a single-purpose try/catch that
warn-logs a misbehaving coordinator without crashing service teardown.

Adds five tests:
 - dedupes duplicate verdict events for the same session
 - emits separately for the same session when verdict differs
 - re-emits a verdict after the dedupe TTL expires (fake timers)

The Electrobun build script (desktop-build.mjs) runs `bun install` with
cwd set to packages/app-core/platforms/electrobun. bun walks up looking
for the nearest workspace root and stops at eliza/package.json — but
that file's `workspaces` array did not include
packages/app-core/platforms/*, so bun treated the Electrobun dir as
outside the workspace and refused to resolve @elizaos/shared@workspace:*.

because eliza/package.json intercepts the upward walk first. Mirroring
the same entry into eliza/package.json fixes Windows desktop builds

Phase 1 of the vault unification: lets the agent say "log into

Authorization model:

fix(electrobun): static server must proxy /api/* like Vite does

The Electrobun static server (Bun.serve at default :5174) serves the
built renderer in dev:desktop (non-watch) mode. The host pushes the
renderer's own origin as the apiBase via pushApiBaseToRenderer, mirroring
the Vite watch-mode design where Vite proxies /api/* to the agent. The
static server had no proxy, so every /api/* fetch returned SPA HTML and
JSON.parse threw. Symptom: Settings → Security stuck on "Checking access"
and "Loading password settings…", Secrets storage modal stuck on
"Loading…", any feature that uses authBase()/relative /api fetches
silently broke.

Add /api, /ws, /music-player proxying to the static server so the design
assumption holds whether the renderer was loaded via Vite (watch) or this
static server (dev:desktop). Pairs with the boot-config apiBase injection
already in place for the alternate path where renderer code consults
bootConfig.apiBase directly.

fix(electrobun): inject __ELIZA_APP_BOOT_CONFIG__.apiBase into static-served HTML

The Electrobun static file server (Bun.serve at default port 5174) injects
window.__ELIZA_API_BASE__ into served index.html so a renderer loaded via
the static server URL can find the API. But SettingsView's
SecuritySettingsSection reads bootConfig.apiBase (the typed boot config
under window.__ELIZA_APP_BOOT_CONFIG__), not the legacy global. When
loaded via a regular browser at the static-server origin (e.g.
http://127.0.0.1:5174/settings), bootConfig.apiBase was empty and
fell back to pageOrigin (the static server's own port), then every
fetch('/api/...') returned the SPA HTML and JSON.parse threw with
"Unrecognized token '<'".

Fix: also write the typed boot config inline:

  window.__ELIZA_APP_BOOT_CONFIG__ = {...prev, apiBase, apiToken?}
  window[Symbol.for("elizaos.app.boot-config")] = { current: ... }

Mirrors what apiBaseUpdate does at runtime via RPC, so the same renderer
bundle works both inside the Electrobun window and from a regular browser
pointed at the static-server URL.

fix(env): respect DISCORD_AUTO_REPLY env var via DISCORD_DEFAULTS

The autoReply field in getDiscordSettings() passed a hardcoded false as
the default to resolveSetting(), so the DISCORD_AUTO_REPLY env var was
ignored unless the value was already in character.settings.discord.

Other resolveSetting() calls in the same function read their default
from DISCORD_DEFAULTS, which uses getEnvBoolean() to pick up env vars.
This change adds AUTO_REPLY to DISCORD_DEFAULTS the same way and uses it
as the autoReply default, so DISCORD_AUTO_REPLY=true now actually flips
the gate in messages.ts that ingests messages without responding.

No behavior change for users who don't set the env var — default is
still false.

time even if no service was created or JUPITER_API_KEY was missing. Now
deferred behind startQueues() which is called once from start().
