bundle does `require("@elizaos/core")` at the top level, which throws
"require() async module ... is unsupported" at runtime.

bundle of this plugin. Dropping CJS support entirely:

- delete dist/cjs/

"no \"require\" condition" error instead of a confusing
async-module crash, and should switch to `await import(...)`.

ci: continue-on-error for all anthropics/claude-code-action invocations

When the Anthropic API is unavailable to the action — most commonly low
credit balance, but also rate-limit and transient API outages — the
action exits non-zero. Today that turns the entire workflow run red:
PR checks block, scheduled cron jobs alert, docs CI fails. The Claude
review/maintenance/docs-fix passes are best-effort, not gating.

Add `continue-on-error: true` to every `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1`
invocation across:
  - claude-code-review.yml (PR review)
  - claude.yml (@claude trigger)
  - skill-review.yml (SKILL.md review)
  - weekly-maintenance.yml (cron)
  - docs-ci.yml (link + quality fix passes)

Failed steps still show as red in the run UI for visibility; only the
job-level conclusion is preserved as success when the bot run is the
sole failure. Downstream steps in docs-ci.yml already use the
"Check for Changes" pattern, so they correctly no-op when the fix pass
was skipped.

Repro: run-25252396948/job-74046380246 failed PR #7235's claude review
with `Credit balance is too low` from the agent SDK.

fix(vault): skip OS keychain when host is known to crash @napi-rs/keyring

@napi-rs/keyring's libsecret backend segfaults inside the native
binding (not a catchable JS exception) when no D-Bus session is
available. Headless Linux servers, CI runners, and containers without
a desktop session all hit this. The defensive try/catch around
keychain.load() can't help — the native crash kills the host process
before JS regains control.

Detect the unsafe configuration BEFORE invoking the native code and
fall back to MILADY_VAULT_PASSPHRASE / throw a helpful error:

  1. process.env.MILADY_VAULT_DISABLE_KEYCHAIN === "1"
  2. process.platform === "linux" && !process.env.DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS

Existing desktop / dev-session paths are unchanged. Reproduces with:

  $ unset DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS
  $ bun run dev   # crashed on `new Entry()` in @napi-rs/keyring 1.2.0
fix(vault): skip OS keychain when host is known to crash @napi-rs/key…

fix(confidant): lazy-import @napi-rs/keyring + skip on headless Linux

Both keyring touchpoints in @elizaos/confidant did a top-level static
import of `@napi-rs/keyring`. The native binding initializes at module
eval time, which segfaults the host process on Linux without a D-Bus
session (libsecret backend can't talk to gnome-keyring / kwallet).
Just importing the module from agent runtime startup was enough to
crash the process before any guard could fire.

Fix:
- packages/confidant/src/crypto/master-key.ts: change top-level import
  to type-only; lazy-load Entry inside loadOrCreateKeychainEntry; add
  the same headless-Linux skip as the vault package.
- packages/confidant/src/backends/keyring.ts: same pattern. Add
  loadEntryClass() helper that does the headless check + dynamic
  import; use it in resolve/store/remove.

Effect: importing @elizaos/confidant on a headless host no longer
loads the native binding. Calling into the keyring backend on a
headless host throws BackendNotConfiguredError / MasterKeyUnavailableError
instead of segfaulting the process.
fix(confidant): lazy-import @napi-rs/keyring + skip on headless Linux

fix(vault, confidant): tighten headless-keychain detection + guard public API

Addresses three review findings on the keychain segfault fix:

- P1: detect D-Bus reachability via XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus socket as well
  as DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS. The env-var-only check produces false
  positives on modern systemd desktops (Fedora, Arch, Ubuntu 22+) and
  SSH sessions without env forwarding, where D-Bus is reachable via
  socket activation.
- P2: extend the headless guard to the public osKeychainMasterKey /
  osKeyringMasterKey export so direct callers (plugins, integrations)
  also avoid the native segfault path.
- P2: defaultMasterKey().describe() now reflects the runtime-selected
  resolver — when the keychain is bypassed it reports the passphrase
  path (or "unavailable") instead of misrepresenting the keychain as
  the active source.

Confidant's two callers share a small keychain-host helper module so
the detection rule lives in one place per package. Vault keeps its
own copy since the env var name differs (MILADY_VAULT_DISABLE_KEYCHAIN
vs CONFIDANT_DISABLE_KEYCHAIN).

Also fixes the app-core wiring CI regression: the
secrets-manager-routes route tests were silently relying on
@napi-rs/keyring succeeding on headless Linux runners. They now inject
an in-memory test vault — matching the existing pattern in
secrets-manager-routes-logins.test.ts and the workflow's claim that
these tests "mock the vault at the boundary".

ci(test): switch from --no-frozen-lockfile to --frozen-lockfile

Three CI runs in a row (25243574869, 25243714816, and the rerun) failed
at `bun install --ignore-scripts --no-frozen-lockfile` with:

  error: Workspace dependency "@smithy/service-error-classification" not found
  error: Workspace dependency "@smithy/types" not found
  error: @smithy/types@workspace:^ failed to resolve

Local `bun install --ignore-scripts --no-frozen-lockfile` resolves 4410
packages cleanly with no errors. Exhaustive grep across the workspace
(incl. submodules, cloud worktrees, native plugins, and bun.lock
itself) finds zero `workspace:^` refs anywhere — and certainly none
naming `@smithy/types` or `@smithy/service-error-classification`. The
bun.lock has those packages declared with proper `^4.x.y` ranges.

The trigger appears to be `--no-frozen-lockfile` re-resolving in CI's
Linux runner with bun 1.3.13 in some way that doesn't reproduce on
macOS with the same bun version. Switching to `--frozen-lockfile`
forces bun to obey the lockfile rather than re-derive — and the
lockfile is correct. `--frozen-lockfile` also matches the
setup-bun-workspace action's documented default install-command.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

free-text strings or structured ClarificationRequest objects with
{ kind, platform, scope, question, paramPath }. The structured shape
lets the host render quick-pick pickers (channel, server, recipient)
and patch the draft at the named param path on resolution, instead of
regenerating the whole workflow with the LLM on every clarification.

Adds src/utils/clarification.ts with:
- coerceClarificationRequests() — normalize mixed-shape arrays into
  ClarificationRequest[]; legacy strings become kind: free_text with
  empty paramPath (host falls back to a free-form input).
- isCatalogClarification() / CATALOG_CLARIFICATION_SUFFIX — moved out
  of the service so the suffix-based detection of post-LLM catalog
  warnings works for both shapes.

The service injectCatalogClarifications now uses isCatalogClarification
instead of inline endsWith on strings, so legacy and structured items
both round-trip safely across regeneration cycles.

Action sites that surface clarifications in the chat coerce the array
through coerceClarificationRequests().map(c => c.question) before
formatting, so the user-visible message stays a list of plain strings.

Backward compatible: existing string[] callers are unchanged because
the union type still accepts strings, and the catalog-warning
emission path keeps producing strings.

leading `#` on channel names, and emit the matching id verbatim. A
worked Cozy Devs / #general example anchors the rule. Placeholder
ids, guessed ids, and the display name itself are explicitly
forbidden when a fact resolves the target.

Handling Incomplete Prompts section: documents the structured
ClarificationRequest object (kind, platform, scope, question,
paramPath) as the preferred shape when a specific node parameter is
unresolved. Lists all five `kind` values, requires bracketed-string
syntax in `paramPath` for keys with spaces, instructs the LLM to
leave the unresolved parameter absent so the host can patch it on
quick-pick, and walks through the ambiguous-channel and
missing-server examples with concrete payloads.

target-resolution case: clarify when a target name has no fact-line
match, never clarify when a fact line resolves it.

fix(automations): clarification chained widget remount + busy-state leak

Addresses two P1 bugs Greptile flagged on this PR plus the related P2.

1. ChoiceWidget instance retained across chained clarifications

   The widget tracks its own `selected` state internally and disables all
   buttons after the first click. When the server returned a chained
   `needs_clarification` (e.g. `target_server` → `target_channel`),
   `setClarification` swapped in a new `response` and `choiceId` changed,
   but React identifies component instances by tree position, not by the
   `id` prop. Without an explicit `key`, React reused the same instance,
   so `selected` from the previous pick carried over — the channel-picker
   buttons rendered immediately disabled and the user could not proceed.

   Add `key={choiceId}` to <ChoiceWidget> so React unmounts/remounts it
   for each new clarification.

2. ClarificationFreeTextInput retained text across chained free-text
   clarifications (P2)

   Same root cause. If two consecutive clarifications fall through to
   the free-text path, the input retained the previous step's value.
   Add `key={choiceId}` to the <ClarificationFreeTextInput> element.

3. Busy state leak when draftRecord is unexpectedly falsy

   `setClarification` set busy=true before the try block, but the
   `if (!draftRecord) return` early-exit returned without resetting
   busy. There is no finally, so the panel froze in a perpetual
   loading state with no escape path. Reset busy=false before returning
   on the early-exit path.

Comment update: corrected the misleading comment that said `id` controls
React instance identity — it doesn't, only `key` does. Updated to reflect
the actual reason `choiceId` is computed (key for remount + data id).
fix(automations): clarification chained widget remount + busy-state leak

fix(automations): surface post-deploy refresh failure via pageNotice

Greptile P2 on #7341 round-2: after a successful clarification
resolve+deploy the code calls setClarification(null) and then
awaits ctx.refreshAutomations(). If refreshAutomations rejects,
control falls into the outer catch which calls
setClarification((prev) => prev ? {...} : prev) — but prev is
already null, so the error message is silently swallowed. The
workflow is deployed, but a stale automations list is shown with
no indication that the refresh failed.

Wrap the post-deploy refresh + select in its own inner try block.
On failure, surface a pageNotice describing both the deploy
success and the refresh failure so the user knows their workflow
landed but the UI list may not reflect it yet.

Greptile flagged a second P2 — currentIndex never advancing
within a multi-clarification response — which is deferred. The
chained-server flow (one clarification per round-trip, server
returns next pending one) already works correctly. Local
batching of currentIndex would break the catalog-narrowing
guarantee where the answer to clarification[0] determines
clarification[1]'s catalog (e.g., picking server A means channel
options for server A, not B). The server contract for
multi-clarification-in-one-response is not currently load-bearing
for any real flow.

refactor(cloud): Phase A — Clean Architecture skeleton

First commit in the Clean Architecture migration (~13 phases over 1 PR).
Plan: ~/.claude/plans/met-toi-en-mode-tidy-squirrel.md

Phase A introduces the layer skeleton with no behavior change. Aggregates
migrate one at a time in subsequent commits (Phase B onward).

## Layout

  packages/lib/domain/          — entities + repository interfaces (pure)
    cache/cache.ts               (Cache contract used by decorators)
  packages/lib/application/     — use cases (constructor DI)
  packages/lib/infrastructure/  — concrete adapters
    db/                          (Postgres*Repository delegates to db/repos)
    cache/                       (Cached*Repository decorators)
  apps/api/src/composition/     — composition root (per-request DI)
    build-container.ts           (CompositionContext factory)

## Layering rule

  Transport → Application → Domain
  Infrastructure implements Domain interfaces
  Domain has zero infrastructure imports

## What's wired

  - Cache interface defined (narrow surface: get/set/del/getAndDelete/
    setIfNotExists/wrapNullable/getOrSet/delPattern)
  - CompositionContext type added to AppEnv.Variables

  - Composition middleware mounted in bootstrap-app.ts after the existing
    cloud-bindings + db-cache wrappers — c.var.deps now set per-request
    (empty container until Phase B)

## Why under packages/lib/ for now

  Avoids tsconfig path alias churn during the migration. Phase E promotes
  domain/, application/, infrastructure/ to top-level packages with their
  own tsconfig — at that point file moves are pure config changes.

Typecheck clean. No behavior change. No existing call site touched.

fix(cloud/auth): pass c.env to getAppHost/getAppUrl on Worker

Worker callers of `getAppHost()` / `getAppUrl()` were falling back to the
"http://localhost:3000" default because `process.env` is empty under Cloudflare
Workers (bindings live on `c.env`, not `process.env`). The SIWE nonce response
was returning `domain: "localhost:3000"` and the verify route was checking
against the same wrong value — domain check still passed (both sides agreed)
but the SIWE message presented to the wallet quoted the wrong domain, breaking
phishing-prevention UX.

Changes:
  * `siwe-helpers.ts`: `validateSIWEMessage` and `validateAndConsumeSIWE` now
    take `expectedHost: string` as their last arg. Removed the internal
    `getAppHost()` call (which read `process.env`).
  * `nonce/route.ts`: `getAppHost(c.env)` / `getAppUrl(c.env)`.
  * `verify/route.ts`: resolves `getAppHost(c.env)` and passes it down to
    `validateAndConsumeSIWE`.
  * `app-url.ts`: doc note that Worker callers must pass `c.env` explicitly
    (the `process.env` default is only correct for the browser bundle —
    Vite replaces `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_*` at build time — and Node tests).

Stacked on top of `fix/siwe-cache-bypass`. Once both merge, the SIWE response
domain on staging will read `staging.elizacloud.ai` (and `elizacloud.ai` on
prod) instead of `localhost:3000`.

fix(cloud/auth): unblock SIWE flow by bypassing the disabled cache singleton

The SIWE endpoints `/api/auth/siwe/{nonce,verify}` have been returning 503
in production since `CACHE_ENABLED="false"` was set as a hotfix on 2026-05-02
(commit 3c00f8e62a). The hotfix exists because `CacheClient` is a
module-level singleton whose lazy-opened Redis socket gets bound to the first
request's I/O context on Cloudflare Workers, triggering "Cannot perform I/O
on behalf of a different request" on subsequent requests in the same isolate.
The SIWE routes gate hard on `cache.isAvailable()` and so 503 with the cache
off — breaking the agent → cloud SIWE wallet sign-in flow.

This patch bypasses the singleton in the SIWE routes only and builds a fresh
Redis client per request via `buildRedisClient(c.env)` — the same pattern
already used by `rate-limit-hono-cloudflare.ts` (which works fine in prod,
confirmed live: `X-RateLimit-Policy: redis` with live decrement on hammer).

Changes:
  * `siwe-helpers.ts`: `consumeNonce` and `validateAndConsumeSIWE` now take
    `redis: CompatibleRedis` as their first arg. New `issueNonce(redis)`
    helper that allocates the random hex nonce and `SETEX`-stores it.
  * `nonce/route.ts` + `verify/route.ts`: `buildRedisClient(c.env)` per
    request, replaces the `cache.isAvailable()` 503 gate and the singleton
    `cache.set` / `cache.getAndDelete` calls.

This is a targeted hotfix. The follow-up replaces the module-level singleton
with a per-request `CacheClient` (ALS facade) so we can re-enable
`CACHE_ENABLED=true` globally and remove this bypass.

feat(n8n): clarification roundtrip route + types

Closes the half-built clarification loop on the host side. Previously
the plugin populated _meta.requiresClarification, the LLM was told to
emit it, but the host route ignored it and the UI never rendered it.

POST /api/n8n/workflows/generate now inspects the draft for
clarifications before deploying. When non-empty, the route
short-circuits and returns:
  {
    status: "needs_clarification",
    draft,
    clarifications: ClarificationRequest[],
    catalog: TargetGroup[],
  }
where `catalog` is a snapshot of the connector-target-catalog scoped
to the platforms the clarifications reference. The draft itself is
returned verbatim so the client can post it back unchanged.

POST /api/n8n/workflows/resolve-clarification (new) accepts
{ draft, resolutions: { paramPath, value }[] }. It applies the
resolutions to the draft via a small recursive dot-path setter,
prunes the now-resolved structured clarifications from
_meta.requiresClarification, and either deploys (when the list is
empty) or returns the next pending clarification + updated draft so
the UI can chain a second picker (server-then-channel etc.).

The path setter (n8n-clarification.ts) supports dot identifiers,
bracketed string keys (`nodes["Discord Send"].parameters.channelId`),
and numeric indices (`nodes[0].parameters.guildId`). It rejects
malformed paths and never overwrites a non-object intermediate. The
setter is intentionally tiny — about 30 lines — to avoid pulling
lodash into app-core for one feature.

Folds in P6: client-types-chat.ts adds N8nClarificationRequest,
N8nClarificationTargetGroup, N8nWorkflowNeedsClarificationResponse,
N8nWorkflowResolveClarificationRequest, the type-guard
isNeedsClarificationResponse, and widens
N8nWorkflowGenerateResponse to the three-arm union. The clarification
types mirror the plugin's ClarificationRequest shape but live in the
host so client code does not import from plugin internals.

AutomationsView gets a one-line narrowing branch on
isNeedsClarificationResponse so the wider union typechecks cleanly;
the actual UI render lands in the next PR in the stack (P5).

Tests cover both the helpers and the route handlers:
- n8n-clarification.test.ts: 28 cases for coerceClarifications,
  parseParamPath, setByDotPath, applyResolutions,
  pruneResolvedClarifications, buildCatalogSnapshot.
- n8n-routes.test.ts: appended needs_clarification short-circuit,
  legacy-string clarification coercion, missing-catalog fallback,
  resolve happy path, empty-resolutions rejection, malformed-path
  rejection (with paramPath echo), chained-pending-clarification
  return path, and missing-draft rejection.

Note: the n8n-routes.test.ts file fails to load locally due to a
pre-existing missing package (@elizaos/plugin-browser-bridge) in the

unmodified file. The new route cases run cleanly once that dep is

feat(app-core): connector-target-catalog service (Discord)

Adds a cross-connector target enumeration framework so the n8n
clarification UI can render quick-pick servers/channels/recipients
without making the user paste raw IDs. Discord is the only wired
source in this slice; Slack, Telegram, and Gmail are planned 2.1+
stacks that drop in behind the same `ConnectorTargetCatalog`
interface.

n8n-runtime-context-provider is extracted into a shared
`discord-target-source.ts` exposing two functions:
- fetchDiscordEnumeration(token, opts) returns a structured
  `DiscordEnumerationResult[]` (one entry per guild, with text
  channels or a `channelsError` marker on degraded fetches).
- formatDiscordEnumerationAsFacts(results) renders the same
  human-readable LLM-prompt fact strings the runtime-context
  provider has always emitted, so prompt output is byte-identical
  after the refactor.

unchanged; the existing tests still pass without modification.
A new `discordCache?: DiscordSourceCache` option lets a host wire one
shared cache instance across both services.

connector-target-catalog.ts wraps the same source and exposes:
- TargetGroup { platform, groupId, groupName, targets[] }
- ConnectorTargetCatalog.listGroups({ platform?, groupId? })
- createMiladyConnectorTargetCatalog({ getConfig, fetchImpl?, now?,
    discordCache?, logger? })

The runtime registers it as `connector_target_catalog` in
runtime.services, sharing the same Discord cache as the
runtime-context provider so a "generate" call that primed the cache
incurs zero extra REST cost when the user later picks a channel.

Tests cover: multi-guild enumeration, per-guild groupId narrowing,

fix(android-bundle): inline app-{wifi,contacts,phone} plugins into mobile bundle

The mobile-bundle is a single Bun.build artifact with no node_modules
on-device, so any `await import("@elizaos/app-X/plugin")` against a
runtime-computed specifier fails with "ResolveMessage: Cannot find
module" — which is exactly what cuttlefish was throwing for all three
new plugins after they were added to ANDROID_CORE_PLUGINS.

Static-import the three plugins from a new
`runtime/android-app-plugins.ts` and Object.assign them into
STATIC_ELIZA_PLUGINS so plugin-resolver picks the bundled module up
before falling through to the failing dynamic import. The new file is
imported from `bin.ts` AFTER `aosp-llama-adapter`/`aosp-local-inference-bootstrap`
have already pulled `runtime/eliza.ts` through full evaluation — that
ordering avoids the module-init cycle that prevents this static import
from living inside `eliza.ts` itself (each plugin imports
gatePluginSessionForHostedApp from @elizaos/agent, whose barrel
re-exports eliza.ts).

The `__miladyAndroidAppPlugins` global pin defeats Bun.build's
tree-shaker (mirrors the `__miladyAospLlamaLoader` pattern in
`bin.ts`).

Verified on cuttlefish: agent log now shows
"[eliza] Plugin resolution complete: 4/4 loaded" instead of the prior
3 ResolveMessage failures, and `/api/health` reports ready:true.

fix(cloud): re-apply auth fixes lost in elizaos/cloud → elizaos/eliza migration

The May 3 squash import of elizaos/cloud into this monorepo was taken
from a snapshot before two critical hotfixes landed in elizaos/cloud.
Without re-applying them, the next CF Worker deploy from this repo
will reintroduce two production-impacting bugs that were debugged and
fixed yesterday after a 4+ hour session.

## 1. STEWARD_JWT_SECRET preference order

`@stwd/auth` `getJwtSecret()` treats STEWARD_JWT_SECRET as canonical
and STEWARD_SESSION_SECRET as a deprecated fallback. The worker-side
verifier had the order inverted. When both env vars are set on the
Steward Railway deployment (which they are in production), Steward
signs with STEWARD_JWT_SECRET while the worker verifies with
STEWARD_SESSION_SECRET. No tokens validate. Every authenticated
request returns 401.

Original PR: elizaOS/cloud#501 (merged develop-cf 2026-05-02).

## 2. CACHE_ENABLED on CF Workers

CacheClient is a module-level singleton that lazy-creates a Redis
WebSocket connection on first use. CF Workers reuses isolates across
requests, so the redis I/O streams get bound to the FIRST request's
context. Subsequent requests in the same isolate hit:

  Cannot perform I/O on behalf of a different request. (I/O type: Writable)

The worker hangs (the awaited setex never resolves) and CF kills it
as 'code had hung'. This was the long-standing 'Could not establish a
local Steward session' error since the CF migration. Repro: 1st POST
to /api/auth/steward-session = 200, every subsequent call in same
isolate = 500 until rotation.

Until CacheClient is refactored to scope I/O per-request (proper
follow-up), CACHE_ENABLED="false" is the safest hotfix. The cache
layer detects this and short-circuits all reads/writes. JWT
verification still works (in-memory LRU + jose-local). DB calls go
direct.

Original PR: elizaOS/cloud#502 (merged develop-cf 2026-05-02).

## Verification

After both fixes are re-applied and the next cf-deploy goes out, two
consecutive POSTs to /api/auth/steward-session with the same token
both return 200. Production was last deployed yesterday (already with
both fixes). This PR ensures the next deploy from elizaos/eliza does
not regress.

fix(cloud): address greptile review on PR #7288

Two follow-up fixes from greptile-apps[bot] P2 review:

## REDIS_RATE_LIMITING flipped to false on Workers

rate-limit-redis.ts holds its own module-level SocketRedis singleton
via buildRedisClient(). Today it silently no-ops on Workers because
ENV_PREFIX = process.env.ENVIRONMENT (process.env is empty on
Workers), so getRedisClient() never returns a client and the rate
limiter falls back to the in-memory path.

The trap: once redis-factory or rate-limit-redis is updated to read
from getCloudAwareEnv() (the obvious cleanup), Workers will hit the
exact same cross-request I/O bug that motivated CACHE_ENABLED=false.

Disable on Workers now to prevent re-regression after the
follow-up CacheClient refactor.

## CACHE_DISABLE_REASON env var to silence false-positive critical log

CacheClient.initialize emits logger.error when CACHE_ENABLED!='true'
and NODE_ENV='production'. With this PR every Worker cold start
floods observability dashboards with a CRITICAL alert that is a
false positive.

Add a CACHE_DISABLE_REASON env var that downgrades the message to
warn level when set. Both staging and production wrangler env
sections set it to the documented reason. The CRITICAL log still
fires when production has neither CACHE_ENABLED=true nor
CACHE_DISABLE_REASON set, preserving the original guard rail.

in the framework. Lifting them upstream lets the parent delete the

- packages/agent/scripts/build-mobile-bundle.mjs:

  Add `isRecursivePackageSymlinkTarget()` guard to the symlink filter
  in `shouldCopyPackageEntry()`. Without it, when a workspace package
  symlinks into itself (or into a parent of its own location, e.g. a
  workspace-root → package-dir loop), the recursive copy infinite-
  loops staging the desktop runtime bundle.

- packages/app-core/platforms/electrobun/scripts/stage-macos-release-artifacts.sh:
  Wire `electrobun.config.ts > build.mac.entitlements` through to the
  `.entitlements` plist used by codesign. Previously the config knob

  packages/app-core/scripts/lib/release-check-pack-dry-run.ts:
  Add a tarball-listing fallback for `npm pack --dry-run --json` —
  some npm versions return a JSON envelope claiming the pack succeeded
  while reporting an empty file list, which made `release-check` fail
  on perfectly valid packages. The fallback re-runs `npm pack` for

fix(cloud/auth): unblock SIWE by bypassing the disabled cache singleton (#7324)

* fix(cloud/auth): unblock SIWE flow by bypassing the disabled cache singleton

The SIWE endpoints `/api/auth/siwe/{nonce,verify}` have been returning 503
in production since `CACHE_ENABLED="false"` was set as a hotfix on 2026-05-02
(commit 3c00f8e62a). The hotfix exists because `CacheClient` is a
module-level singleton whose lazy-opened Redis socket gets bound to the first
request's I/O context on Cloudflare Workers, triggering "Cannot perform I/O
on behalf of a different request" on subsequent requests in the same isolate.
The SIWE routes gate hard on `cache.isAvailable()` and so 503 with the cache
off — breaking the agent → cloud SIWE wallet sign-in flow.

This patch bypasses the singleton in the SIWE routes only and builds a fresh
Redis client per request via `buildRedisClient(c.env)` — the same pattern
already used by `rate-limit-hono-cloudflare.ts` (which works fine in prod,
confirmed live: `X-RateLimit-Policy: redis` with live decrement on hammer).

Changes:
  * `siwe-helpers.ts`: `consumeNonce` and `validateAndConsumeSIWE` now take
    `redis: CompatibleRedis` as their first arg. New `issueNonce(redis)`
    helper that allocates the random hex nonce and `SETEX`-stores it.
  * `nonce/route.ts` + `verify/route.ts`: `buildRedisClient(c.env)` per
    request, replaces the `cache.isAvailable()` 503 gate and the singleton
    `cache.set` / `cache.getAndDelete` calls.

This is a targeted hotfix. The follow-up replaces the module-level singleton
with a per-request `CacheClient` (ALS facade) so we can re-enable
`CACHE_ENABLED=true` globally and remove this bypass.

* chore(cloud/auth): clean PR — drop redundant Bindings cast + add unit smoke test

- Routes: `Hono<AppEnv>` already types `c.env` as `Bindings`; the explicit
  `as Bindings` cast was redundant. Dropped along with the now-unused import.
- Add `packages/tests/unit/siwe-helpers-smoke.test.ts` covering `issueNonce`
  and `consumeNonce` against an in-memory Redis mock: nonce shape, single-use
  consume, replay returns false, uniqueness over 50 iterations.

Both /clean and the unit smoke test pass on the diff.

fix(android): track elizaAospBuild as merge-task input + extend bun seccomp envelope + disable on-device training

build.gradle thinning hook
  Track project.findProperty('elizaAospBuild') as a merge*Assets input
  property so switching between -PelizaAospBuild=true and the default
  Capacitor mode forces a re-merge. Without this, gradle short-circuits
  the second invocation as UP-TO-DATE and reuses whatever shape the
  previous build left in merged_assets — observed concretely as an AOSP
  build emitting a 147 MB APK because the prior Capacitor build had
  already deleted assets/agent/ from the cached output dir, and the
  AOSP-mode doLast hook never ran to restore it.

ElizaAgentService bun env
  Add BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_DISABLE_ASYNC_TRANSPILER=1 to the agent spawn
  env. Bun's async-transpiler worker pool uses pthread + futex_waitv
  which Android's app seccomp policy blocks on most pre-API-34 kernels.
  Forces the transpiler onto the main thread; the larger 43 MB
  agent-bundle was tripping a SIGSYS during boot before this flag was
  added. Memfd is intentionally NOT disabled — JSC's JIT uses memfd
  for W^X dual mapping and disabling it forces raw RWX mmap which
  SELinux execmem on platform_app blocks.

  Hard-disable on-device prompt-optimization / training. The runtime's
  trajectory-driven optimizer (MIPRO / GEPA / bootstrap-fewshot)
  spawns coding sub-agents over PTY-backed bash — that pipeline blows
  past the bun seccomp envelope this service builds, churns device
  flash via PGlite, and would mutate prompts mid-smoke. Set both
  ELIZA_DISABLE_AUTO_BOOTSTRAP=1 and ELIZA_DISABLE_TRAJECTORY_LOGGING=1
  (plus the legacy MILADY_DISABLE_AUTO_BOOTSTRAP for older bundles)
  so trajectories are never persisted, the trigger service is never
  notified, and no training round can fire on-device.

fix(startup): MiladyOS-aware policy avoids backend-timeout dead-end on cold boot

Cuttlefish smoke testing showed the splash dead-ending on a "Backend
Timeout: /api/auth/status - Failed to fetch" card before the on-device
agent finished cold-boot (~60–90s of PGlite migration + plugin load +
agent registration). Manual "Retry Startup" tap was required to
proceed.

Root cause: `createMobilePolicy()` ships a 15s `backendTimeoutMs`
designed for cloud-only iOS / Play Store installs, where the backend is
already warm. MiladyOS bundles the agent in-process, so the same
timeout fires before the agent has even bound port 31337.

- createMiladyOSPolicy(): `supportsLocalRuntime: true`, `backendTimeoutMs:
  180_000`, `agentReadyTimeoutMs: 300_000`, `defaultTarget:
  "embedded-local"`. Selected by `useStartupCoordinator` before the
  generic mobile branch — the MiladyOS check sits behind `isMiladyOS()`
  so vanilla Android APK installs keep the original 15s budget.
- `getBackendStartupTimeoutMs()` in `bridge/electrobun-runtime.ts` mirrors
  the same logic for the inner `optDeadline` poll loop in
  `startup-phase-poll.ts`. Without this the second poll (onboarding
  options) would still time out at 30s even with the outer 3-minute
  budget.
- New test file `test/state/milady-os-policy.test.ts` pins the policy
  contract (4 cases) so a regression to the 15s timeout fails CI
  instead of dead-ending real devices.

Also rolls in two rename-alignment edits caught after the eliza-repo
Milady→Eliza chore:
- `__miladyAndroidAppPlugins` → `__elizaAndroidAppPlugins` (mirrors the

- `core-plugins.ts` ANDROID_CORE_PLUGINS comment: `MILADY_PLATFORM` →

   Vite's `util` alias is an empty shim, so the catch path runs —
   but rolldown's CommonJS prebundle for the elliptic graph hoists
   the consumer call sites *before* `require_inherits_browser`'s
   wrapper definition, throwing on first crypto access.
2. The same prebundle hoists `require_inherits` reference for
   nested elliptic submodules before its wrapper is wired up.

Fix:
- Resolve `inherits` directly to a self-contained `inherits.cjs`
  browser shim — bypasses the try/catch entirely so the catch
  path's require chain never enters the prebundle.
- Add the entire crypto graph (elliptic + inherits + hash-base +
  create-hash + create-hmac + browserify-sign + secp256k1) to
  `optimizeDeps.include` so rolldown bundles them as a single
  deterministic chunk with wrappers at top-level.

the plugin populated _meta.requiresClarification, the LLM was told to

POST /api/n8n/workflows/generate now inspects the draft for
clarifications before deploying. When non-empty, the route
short-circuits and returns:
  {
    status: "needs_clarification",
    draft,

to the platforms the clarifications reference. The draft itself is
returned verbatim so the client can post it back unchanged.

POST /api/n8n/workflows/resolve-clarification (new) accepts
{ draft, resolutions: { paramPath, value }[] }. It applies the
resolutions to the draft via a small recursive dot-path setter,
prunes the now-resolved structured clarifications from
_meta.requiresClarification, and either deploys (when the list is
empty) or returns the next pending clarification + updated draft so
the UI can chain a second picker (server-then-channel etc.).

The path setter (n8n-clarification.ts) supports dot identifiers,
bracketed string keys (`nodes["Discord Send"].parameters.channelId`),
and numeric indices (`nodes[0].parameters.guildId`). It rejects
malformed paths and never overwrites a non-object intermediate. The
setter is intentionally tiny — about 30 lines — to avoid pulling
lodash into app-core for one feature.

matches any inner path including the empty string.

fix(cloud/api): make legacy /api/v1/proxy/birdeye redirect public

The legacy birdeye proxy mount returns a 308 redirect to /api/v1/apis/birdeye/*
so old clients can discover the new URL. With the path missing from
publicPathPrefixes, auth middleware ran first and returned 401 before the
redirect could fire, breaking the e2e contract:

    Group H — GET /api/v1/proxy/birdeye/* > legacy mount redirects to
      /api/v1/apis/birdeye (308): Expected 308, Received 401

The redirect target /api/v1/apis/birdeye is still auth-gated (the next test
in the same group covers that), so making the legacy mount public only
exposes the URL rewrite, not the proxy itself.

to the orchestrator+sub-agent for `--provider groq --model openai/gpt-oss-120b`
is now `openai/gpt-oss-120b` (correct Groq ID).

registry.py had stale `cwd_rel` paths pointing at non-existent `benchmarks/
{gaia,tau-bench,terminal-bench}/python` subdirs. Their actual layout is the
top-level benchmark dir. The adapter currently masks this via the
`benchmarks_root / benchmark_dir` fallback, but the wrong primary path is
still misleading and breaks any direct invocation that resolves cwd_rel
literally. Point them at the real dirs.

fix(cloud): address greptile review on PR #7288

Two follow-up fixes from greptile-apps[bot] P2 review:

## REDIS_RATE_LIMITING flipped to false on Workers

rate-limit-redis.ts holds its own module-level SocketRedis singleton
via buildRedisClient(). Today it silently no-ops on Workers because
ENV_PREFIX = process.env.ENVIRONMENT (process.env is empty on
Workers), so getRedisClient() never returns a client and the rate
limiter falls back to the in-memory path.

The trap: once redis-factory or rate-limit-redis is updated to read
from getCloudAwareEnv() (the obvious cleanup), Workers will hit the
exact same cross-request I/O bug that motivated CACHE_ENABLED=false.

Disable on Workers now to prevent re-regression after the
follow-up CacheClient refactor.

## CACHE_DISABLE_REASON env var to silence false-positive critical log

CacheClient.initialize emits logger.error when CACHE_ENABLED!='true'
and NODE_ENV='production'. With this PR every Worker cold start
floods observability dashboards with a CRITICAL alert that is a
false positive.

Add a CACHE_DISABLE_REASON env var that downgrades the message to
warn level when set. Both staging and production wrangler env
sections set it to the documented reason. The CRITICAL log still
fires when production has neither CACHE_ENABLED=true nor
CACHE_DISABLE_REASON set, preserving the original guard rail.

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>

fix(cloud): re-apply auth fixes lost in elizaos/cloud → elizaos/eliza migration

The May 3 squash import of elizaos/cloud into this monorepo was taken
from a snapshot before two critical hotfixes landed in elizaos/cloud.
Without re-applying them, the next CF Worker deploy from this repo
will reintroduce two production-impacting bugs that were debugged and
fixed yesterday after a 4+ hour session.

## 1. STEWARD_JWT_SECRET preference order

`@stwd/auth` `getJwtSecret()` treats STEWARD_JWT_SECRET as canonical
and STEWARD_SESSION_SECRET as a deprecated fallback. The worker-side
verifier had the order inverted. When both env vars are set on the
Steward Railway deployment (which they are in production), Steward
signs with STEWARD_JWT_SECRET while the worker verifies with
STEWARD_SESSION_SECRET. No tokens validate. Every authenticated
request returns 401.

Original PR: elizaOS/cloud#501 (merged develop-cf 2026-05-02).

## 2. CACHE_ENABLED on CF Workers

CacheClient is a module-level singleton that lazy-creates a Redis
WebSocket connection on first use. CF Workers reuses isolates across
requests, so the redis I/O streams get bound to the FIRST request's
context. Subsequent requests in the same isolate hit:

  Cannot perform I/O on behalf of a different request. (I/O type: Writable)

The worker hangs (the awaited setex never resolves) and CF kills it
as 'code had hung'. This was the long-standing 'Could not establish a
local Steward session' error since the CF migration. Repro: 1st POST
to /api/auth/steward-session = 200, every subsequent call in same
isolate = 500 until rotation.

Until CacheClient is refactored to scope I/O per-request (proper
follow-up), CACHE_ENABLED="false" is the safest hotfix. The cache
layer detects this and short-circuits all reads/writes. JWT
verification still works (in-memory LRU + jose-local). DB calls go
direct.

Original PR: elizaOS/cloud#502 (merged develop-cf 2026-05-02).

## Verification

After both fixes are re-applied and the next cf-deploy goes out, two
consecutive POSTs to /api/auth/steward-session with the same token
both return 200. Production was last deployed yesterday (already with
both fixes). This PR ensures the next deploy from elizaos/eliza does
not regress.

fix(agent): preserve agentEntry.settings in buildCharacterFromConfig()

`runtime.getSetting('SOME_KEY')` is the documented way for plugins to read
agent-scoped configuration (see plugin-discord, plugin-twitter, etc.). Until
now the only delivery channel for those values was process.env behind the
hard-coded GETSETTING_ENV_ALLOWLIST in packages/agent/src/runtime/eliza.ts.

This adds a typed `settings?: Record<string, string|number|boolean|null>`
field to `AgentConfig` and merges it into the derived base settings inside
`buildCharacterFromConfig()`. Per-agent values win over derived defaults so
operators can override capability-derived settings from config when needed.

Tests pin the behavior:
  - preserve agent entry settings
  - do not clobber derived base settings when agent entry has none
  - per-agent overrides win
  - undefined-valued keys are opt-outs
  - non-object settings do not throw
  - numeric/boolean values pass through

Field evidence: nyx (self-hosted milady-cloud agent) was previously unable to
deliver DISCORD_AUTO_REPLY through agent config and had to monkey-patch the
runtime allowlist. With this change, the workaround is unnecessary.

fix(automations): support free-form clarifications in resolve flow

The clarification round-trip assumed every clarification has a
non-empty `paramPath` that maps a user-supplied value to a workflow
field. In practice the n8n workflow LLM also emits free-form
clarifications without a paramPath (e.g. "Which Discord channel should
the alerts go to?" presented as a plain string in
`_meta.requiresClarification`). Two contract gaps then break the UI
flow:

1. `applyResolutions` rejects any resolution with empty `paramPath`
   ("resolution missing paramPath" → 400). The Apply button on a
   free-form clarification flashes red and never advances.

2. `pruneResolvedClarifications` only drops object-form items by
   paramPath match. String-form items are always kept, so even if
   resolution succeeded the next round-trip returns the same
   clarifications and the UI loops forever on Step 1.

This PR closes both gaps without inventing a new wire shape:

- `applyResolutions`: when `paramPath` is an empty string, record the
  user's answer under `draft._meta.userNotes` so subsequent LLM
  iterations have the context, but do not mutate the workflow.
- `pruneResolvedClarifications`: take an explicit `freeFormCount` of
  empty-paramPath resolutions in the current request, then prune the
  first N string-form (or empty-paramPath object-form) items
  positionally — matching the order the UI presents them.
- Caller in `n8n-routes.ts` computes `freeFormCount` from the
  resolution shape and passes it through.

The behaviour is additive: existing object-form-with-paramPath flows
are unchanged.

Real LLM output should ideally use structured `kind:'choice'`
clarifications with the connector catalog, but until that's reliable
the free-form path needs to terminate cleanly.

fix(agent): skip vault sentinels in applyConfigEnvToProcessEnv

`loadElizaConfig()` is called by ~30 services (registry-client,
escalation, owner-name, custom-actions, plugin-routes, onboarding-routes,
api/server, runtime/eliza, etc.) — not just at boot. Each call walked
`config.env` and unconditionally wrote every value into `process.env`
via `applyConfigEnvToProcessEnv`.

When a key holds a `vault://KEY` sentinel (because the user's secret was
already migrated to the OS keychain), the literal sentinel string would
overwrite the resolved plaintext that `applyCloudConfigToEnv` had set at
step 2b of `startEliza`. Downstream `runtime.getSetting("KEY")` then
handed the sentinel to consumers like plugin-elizacloud, which sent it
as `Authorization: Bearer vault://KEY` — producing a 401 from elizaOS
Cloud even though the underlying credential in the vault was correct.

Skipping sentinels here keeps the boot-time resolved value intact across
arbitrary later reads. Real plaintext values still propagate; only the
unresolved sentinel placeholder is filtered.

fix(cloud/frontend): consolidate Pages Functions into _middleware.ts

Cloudflare's Pages bundler translates the catch-all directory pattern
[[path]].ts into the route pattern /:path* and registers it with the
Pages router on cold start. The Pages runtime path-to-regexp dependency
was upgraded to v8 between May 2 and May 4, and v8 rejects the legacy
:name* repeating-wildcard syntax with:

  TypeError: Missing parameter name at index 15: /steward/:path*

Because the router is initialised eagerly at boot, a single bad pattern
kills the entire Pages worker. Every request to www.elizacloud.ai/api/*
returns Cloudflare error 1101 (Worker exception), which broke OAuth
login on milady.ai (the GitHub Pages SPA proxies /api/* through
www.elizacloud.ai), the eliza.app homepage, and the eliza-cloud SPA
itself.

Replace functions/api/[[path]].ts and functions/steward/[[path]].ts
with a single functions/_middleware.ts that runs before the SPA
fallback and forwards /api/* and /steward/* to the upstream Workers
API in code. _middleware.ts is a global middleware (no per-route
pattern), so Cloudflare's bundler does not synthesise any route
string. The path-to-regexp parser is never invoked, the worker boots
cleanly, and the same-origin proxy behaviour is preserved end to end.

Behaviour-preserving:
  - Method, headers, body pass through via re-using the original
    Request object (matches the prior implementation).
  - Set-Cookie on the response propagates back unchanged.
  - API_UPSTREAM env var resolution is unchanged (delegates to the
    existing _proxy helpers).
  - Non-/api and non-/steward requests fall through to the SPA via
    context.next().

Verified locally:
  - bunx @biomejs/biome check functions/_middleware.ts: clean.
  - The two pre-existing typecheck errors (entry-server.tsx
    StaticRouter import, cache/client.ts redis SCAN signature) are
    unrelated to this change.

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>

fix(cloud/frontend): StewardProvider syncs steward-session cookie to api.elizacloud.ai (#7360)

* fix(cloud/frontend): use apiFetch for /api/auth/steward-session so cookie sets on api.elizacloud.ai

Follow-up to #7358. setSessionCookie was still calling raw
fetch("/api/auth/steward-session"), which goes same-origin to
www.elizacloud.ai. The Worker sets steward-token + steward-authed
cookies on the host the Set-Cookie response came from, so they
end up host-only on www.elizacloud.ai.

Subsequent apiFetch calls (e.g. /api/auth/cli-session/<id>/complete)
now go cross-origin to api.elizacloud.ai (per #7358 SPA-direct
behaviour). The host-only www cookie does not flow on that
cross-origin request, the request 401s, and the CLI login screen
deadlocks at "Generating API Key" until the 30s client timeout
fires.

Switch setSessionCookie to apiFetch so the cookie-setting POST
also goes to api.elizacloud.ai. The Set-Cookie response is now
scoped to the same host that all subsequent /api/* calls hit.

Production deploy verified: /api/auth/cli-session/<id>/complete
returns 200 with the cookie attached, login flow unblocks past
"Generating API Key".

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>

* fix(cloud/frontend): StewardProvider syncs steward-session cookie to api.elizacloud.ai

Follow-up to #7359. The login form's setSessionCookie was switched to
apiFetch in #7359, but StewardProvider has its own auto-sync useEffect
that POSTs the localStorage token to /api/auth/steward-session via raw
fetch. That request still goes same-origin to www.elizacloud.ai so the
Set-Cookie response is scoped host-only to www. Then when the
/auth/cli-login page's completeCliLogin sends apiFetch to
api.elizacloud.ai, the host-only www cookie does not flow on the
cross-origin request. The CLI login spinner deadlocks at
'Generating API Key' until the 30s client timeout fires.

Same root cause, second seam.

Add a stewardSessionUrl helper that returns the absolute Workers
origin (https://api.elizacloud.ai/api/auth/steward-session) when the
SPA is running on a known elizacloud.ai host, and fall back to the
relative same-origin path everywhere else (dev, preview, ad-hoc
hosts).

All four steward-session calls in StewardProvider (one POST sync,
three DELETE wipes) now go through stewardSessionUrl with explicit
credentials: 'include'. Cookies set on api.elizacloud.ai by the POST
flow with subsequent apiFetch calls.

Verified live on production deploy 60caf2a0:
- www.elizacloud.ai/api/health -> 200 JSON
- www.elizacloud.ai/steward/auth/providers -> 200 JSON
- /auth/cli-login completes the spinner past 'Generating API Key'

fix(cloud/frontend): consolidate Pages Functions into _middleware.ts (#7357)

* fix(cloud/frontend): consolidate Pages Functions into _middleware.ts

Cloudflare's Pages bundler translates the catch-all directory pattern
[[path]].ts into the route pattern /:path* and registers it with the
Pages router on cold start. The Pages runtime path-to-regexp dependency
was upgraded to v8 between May 2 and May 4, and v8 rejects the legacy
:name* repeating-wildcard syntax with:

  TypeError: Missing parameter name at index 15: /steward/:path*

Because the router is initialised eagerly at boot, a single bad pattern
kills the entire Pages worker. Every request to www.elizacloud.ai/api/*
returns Cloudflare error 1101 (Worker exception), which broke OAuth
login on milady.ai (the GitHub Pages SPA proxies /api/* through
www.elizacloud.ai), the eliza.app homepage, and the eliza-cloud SPA
itself.

Replace functions/api/[[path]].ts and functions/steward/[[path]].ts
with a single functions/_middleware.ts that runs before the SPA
fallback and forwards /api/* and /steward/* to the upstream Workers
API in code. _middleware.ts is a global middleware (no per-route
pattern), so Cloudflare's bundler does not synthesise any route
string. The path-to-regexp parser is never invoked, the worker boots
cleanly, and the same-origin proxy behaviour is preserved end to end.

Behaviour-preserving:
  - Method, headers, body pass through via re-using the original
    Request object (matches the prior implementation).
  - Set-Cookie on the response propagates back unchanged.
  - API_UPSTREAM env var resolution is unchanged (delegates to the
    existing _proxy helpers).
  - Non-/api and non-/steward requests fall through to the SPA via
    context.next().

Verified locally:
  - bunx @biomejs/biome check functions/_middleware.ts: clean.
  - The two pre-existing typecheck errors (entry-server.tsx
    StaticRouter import, cache/client.ts redis SCAN signature) are
    unrelated to this change.

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>

* fix(automations): pass triggerName to onDeleteTrigger from detail pane

Greptile P1 on #7317: TriggerAutomationDetailPane called
onDeleteTrigger(trigger.id) but the confirmation dialog read
form.displayName, which reflects the trigger-edit form state
rather than the trigger shown in the pane. When deleting a
trigger that is not currently being edited, the dialog showed
a stale or empty name.

Extend the signature to (triggerId?: string, displayName?: string)
and let the caller pass the target name. Form-driven callers (the
HeartbeatForm onDelete slot) keep working unchanged because both
params are optional and fall back to editingId + form.displayName.

* feat(automations): clarification quick-pick UI

Renders the needs_clarification response from POST
/api/n8n/workflows/generate as an inline panel in AutomationsView,
just below the missing-credentials banner. The user picks from a row
of buttons drawn from the connector-target-catalog snapshot, the
host calls /api/n8n/workflows/resolve-clarification with
{paramPath, value}, and either deploys (clearing the panel and
refreshing the workflow list) or chains a follow-up picker (server
then channel) by surfacing the next pending clarification.

ClarificationPanel renders ChoiceWidget directly. ChoiceWidget's
existing onChoose callback contract was already a clean direct
callback — the chat round-trip via sendActionMessage is layered on
in MessageContent.tsx, not in the widget itself, so the widget did
not need an onChooseDirect prop. The clarification flow simply
instantiates ChoiceWidget with its own callback.

optionsForClarification narrows the catalog snapshot per
clarification:
- target_server lists one button per group.
- target_channel narrows to scope.guildId when set, then lists each
  text channel; if no scope is set and multiple guilds returned, the
  label is prefixed with the guild name to disambiguate same-named
  channels.
- recipient lists each recipient target.
- value / free_text / unmatched-platform fall through to a free-text
  Input bubble (ClarificationFreeTextInput) so the user can still
  answer when no catalog backs the question.

Cancel dismisses the panel locally without touching the server. A
busy spinner suppresses re-clicks while resolve is in flight; an
error string surfaces failed resolves (bad paramPath, validation
rejection) without dropping the panel.

client-n8n.ts gains resolveN8nClarification(request) calling POST
/api/n8n/workflows/resolve-clarification with the same 120s timeout
as generateN8nWorkflow (validateAndRepair + deploy can be slow).

Backend coverage from S28-P4 (route + helper tests) covers the
contract end-to-end. AutomationsView has no existing test harness;
a dedicated snapshot test for this view is left out of this PR
intentionally and tracked for follow-up. The end-to-end dogfood
scenarios in the slice plan are the acceptance check.

* fix(automations): clarification chained widget remount + busy-state leak

Addresses two P1 bugs Greptile flagged on this PR plus the related P2.

1. ChoiceWidget instance retained across chained clarifications

   The widget tracks its own `selected` state internally and disables all
   buttons after the first click. When the server returned a chained
   `needs_clarification` (e.g. `target_server` → `target_channel`),
   `setClarification` swapped in a new `response` and `choiceId` changed,
   but React identifies component instances by tree position, not by the
   `id` prop. Without an explicit `key`, React reused the same instance,
   so `selected` from the previous pick carried over — the channel-picker
   buttons rendered immediately disabled and the user could not proceed.

   Add `key={choiceId}` to <ChoiceWidget> so React unmounts/remounts it
   for each new clarification.

2. ClarificationFreeTextInput retained text across chained free-text
   clarifications (P2)

   Same root cause. If two consecutive clarifications fall through to
   the free-text path, the input retained the previous step's value.
   Add `key={choiceId}` to the <ClarificationFreeTextInput> element.

3. Busy state leak when draftRecord is unexpectedly falsy

   `setClarification` set busy=true before the try block, but the
   `if (!draftRecord) return` early-exit returned without resetting
   busy. There is no finally, so the panel froze in a perpetual
   loading state with no escape path. Reset busy=false before returning
   on the early-exit path.

Comment update: corrected the misleading comment that said `id` controls
React instance identity — it doesn't, only `key` does. Updated to reflect
the actual reason `choiceId` is computed (key for remount + data id).

* fix(automations): surface post-deploy refresh failure via pageNotice

Greptile P2 on #7341 round-2: after a successful clarification
resolve+deploy the code calls setClarification(null) and then
awaits ctx.refreshAutomations(). If refreshAutomations rejects,
control falls into the outer catch which calls
setClarification((prev) => prev ? {...} : prev) — but prev is
already null, so the error message is silently swallowed. The
workflow is deployed, but a stale automations list is shown with
no indication that the refresh failed.

Wrap the post-deploy refresh + select in its own inner try block.
On failure, surface a pageNotice describing both the deploy
success and the refresh failure so the user knows their workflow
landed but the UI list may not reflect it yet.

Greptile flagged a second P2 — currentIndex never advancing
within a multi-clarification response — which is deferred. The
chained-server flow (one clarification per round-trip, server
returns next pending one) already works correctly. Local
batching of currentIndex would break the catalog-narrowing
guarantee where the answer to clarification[0] determines
clarification[1]'s catalog (e.g., picking server A means channel
options for server A, not B). The server contract for
multi-clarification-in-one-response is not currently load-bearing
for any real flow.

fix(lifeops-review-01): never auto-send email replies, always enqueue for approval

The user invariant "NEVER auto-respond to my mails — always asks permission first"
was previously enforced only by the default `autoReply.enabled = false` config, with
no code-level gate. If a config push or migration flipped that flag on, `tryAutoReply`
would dispatch real outbound mail to Gmail with only a soft LLM `reflectOnAutoReply`
check standing between it and the recipient.

This change adds a deterministic, code-enforced gate `requiresApprovalQueue(source)`
that returns true for email sources and forces `tryAutoReply` to enqueue an
approval request via `createApprovalQueue(...).enqueue(...)` instead of sending.
The gate runs BEFORE the confidence / whitelist / rate-limit / reflection checks,
so no LLM hallucination or configuration value can bypass it. Non-email channels
preserve current behaviour (the user's invariant only covers mail).

Adds `apps/app-lifeops/src/actions/inbox.invariant.test.ts`, which stubs the Gmail
send pathway, configures `autoReply.enabled=true`, stubs `reflectOnAutoReply` to
approve, and asserts that for a Gmail message the send spy is never called and
the approval queue is.

fix(docker): break circular symlink for app-core's jose / @node-rs/argon2

The pruner's `link-docker-local-app-packages.mjs` links app-core's owned
root deps in two passes: once into `packages/app-core/node_modules/<dep>`,
once into `/app/node_modules/<dep>`. Each pass resolves the source via
`resolveDependencyPackageDir([packageDir, repoRoot])`.

After the first pass linked `app-core/node_modules/jose →
/app/node_modules/jose`, the second pass's resolver searched packageDir
first, found the freshly-created symlink (its target's package.json
exists, so `fs.existsSync` returns true), and returned the symlink path
verbatim. `linkDependencyPackage`'s equality check
`path.resolve(packageDir) === path.resolve(target)` compared the symlink
path against the target path — different strings, so the function
proceeded to `removePath(target)` (deleting the real npm-installed jose
at /app/node_modules/jose) and then symlinked target → the now-broken
intermediate symlink. End state: a two-hop circular symlink that Node's
ESM resolver can't traverse.

Result in prod: every fresh sandbox provisioned with `:develop` crashed
in agent boot with:

    [eliza-autonomous] Failed to start: Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]:
    Cannot find package 'jose' imported from
    /app/plugins/plugin-elizacloud/dist/node/index.node.js

The container kept running (Node process alive in ep_poll) but never
reached the HTTP listen, so the 180s Docker health check timed out and
the daemon scrubbed the sandbox.

Fix: `resolveDependencyPackageDir` now always returns
`fs.realpathSync(dir)` instead of the raw join path. The realpath
collapses any prior symlink, so when the second-pass call resolves jose
it returns /app/node_modules/jose (the actual install) — and
`linkDependencyPackage`'s equality check correctly detects target ===
packageDir and skips the link, preserving the real npm install at root.

Tested locally on a stable build of `:develop` by manually fixing the
symlink in the container and re-launching — the same boot path that was
crashing now progresses past the jose import.

   keep their current main-surface fallback.

3) Deny-by-default on ⚠️ error events: only user-action failure kinds

plain stdio), every emitProgress would otherwise spam a fresh message per
narration chunk + heartbeat tick. Suppress mid-task narration on those
surfaces and only let the spawn ack + terminal summary through.

- emitProgress: when state exists and !thread && !canEdit, update lastText
  in-memory and return without posting. The 🚀 spawn ack already happened
  on first emit (state-init path keeps that send).
- markTaskComplete: when !canEdit, post the final ✅ as a fresh message
  (the 🚀 ack can't be edited to carry the outcome on these surfaces).
- markTaskFailed: when no reaction support AND no edit, post a fresh ❌
  message so the user sees the terminal status.

Net effect by surface:
- Discord/Slack (threads + edit + react): rich UX, narration in thread,
  🚀 → ✅/❌ reactions + edit on spawn ack.
- Telegram (edit, sometimes threads): rich UX or edit-in-place.
- WhatsApp (edit, no threads): edit-in-place on spawn ack, no thread.
- Twitter DM / SMS / plain stdio (no edit, no threads): 🚀 ack →
  silent → ✅/❌ summary. Two messages per task, no spam.
fix(orchestrator): silent narration on capability-poor surfaces

The moltbot `shouldRecord` equivalent for elizaOS. Cross-platform fix for
the recurring planner-hallucination loop:

   `metadata.transient: true` via the new `transientContent(text, source)`
   helper. Persisted Memory carries the flag through the connector chain
   regardless of which surface delivered the post (thread, edit-in-place,
   or fresh send) — so the LLM cannot resurface past status text as
   "facts" to paraphrase on future turns.

post status as plain messages, those messages get marked transient, the
LLM never reads them. Same outcome as Discord-with-threads in terms of
memory hygiene, just a different visual surface.

feat(planner-loop): honor `data.suppressPlannerReply` to mute hallucinated user-facing text on spawn turns

Defensive flag at the planner-loop's `continueChain: false` exit. When a
terminal action sets `data.suppressPlannerReply: true`, finalMessage is
forced to "" regardless of the planner's `messageToUser`. Used by
TASKS_SPAWN_AGENT so an LLM that hallucinates a "Can't spawn..." text
on the same turn it calls the spawn tool cannot leak that text to the
channel via callers reading the trajectory.

sub-agent's narration is the user-facing voice; the planner's
hallucinated chatter never reaches the surface.

fix(image.yaml): mirror build-agent-image.yml pre-build so release builds publish

Dockerfile.ci is a pruner-style image that expects pre-built node_modules + per-package dist/ to already be on the host. build-agent-image.yml (continuous publication of :develop / :stable / :latest) does that prelude — image.yaml (release-triggered publication of versioned tags) did not, so every workflow_dispatch run was failing on the first RUN inside the docker pruner stage:

    Error: Missing package manifest:
      packages/app-core/node_modules/@node-rs/argon2/package.json
      or node_modules/@node-rs/argon2/package.json
        at resolveDependencyPackageDir (link-docker-local-app-packages.mjs:213)

Two coupled problems:

1. No `bun install` step on the host, so `node_modules/.bun/` (the bun virtual store the link script falls back to) never existed in the build context.

2. The repo's root `.dockerignore` excludes `**/node_modules` — even if bun install had run, root node_modules would have been pruned from the Docker context. build-agent-image.yml works around this by `cp packages/app-core/deploy/.dockerignore.ci .dockerignore` right before the docker build; image.yaml never did that swap.

This commit copies the full pre-build sequence from build-agent-image.yml verbatim:
  - jq + Bun setup + cache
  - bun install --no-frozen-lockfile
  - postinstall patches (patch-tsup-dts, ensure-type-package-aliases)
  - build contracts, core (node-only), shared, cloud-sdk, cloud-routing, skills, ui
  - per-plugin build loop (plugin-sql, plugin-video, etc.)
  - bun run build:client (UI)
  - packages/agent build:docker-dist
  - packages/app build:web
  - cp packages/app-core/deploy/.dockerignore.ci .dockerignore

After this, image.yaml workflow_dispatch on develop builds and publishes a release-tagged image with the same artifacts the develop continuous build produces.

Follow-up: extract the shared pre-build into a reusable workflow / composite action so the two files don't duplicate ~120 lines of YAML. Out of scope here — first make image.yaml work.

fix(docker): bake standalone tsx loader into :develop / :stable images

The Dockerfile.ci entry point is `node --import tsx packages/agent/dist/bin.js start`. tsx must be resolvable from /app/. bun's workspace install on GHA produces it under `node_modules/.bun/tsx@<version>/` but doesn't always materialize a `node_modules/tsx/` symlink — and `.dockerignore.ci` prunes per-package node_modules, so even if the symlink lands, transitive resolution can break.

Confirmed regression on `:develop` (sha-06dc596): running the image with the default CMD crashes immediately with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package 'tsx' imported from /app/`. `:stable` (May 13 p14-test3) had tsx present and worked.

Mirror Dockerfile.cloud's pattern:
- Add a dedicated `tsx` stage: `npm install --prefix /opt/tsx --no-save tsx@4.21.0`.
- COPY /opt/tsx into the final image.
- Switch the default APP_CMD_START + CMD fallback to `--import /opt/tsx/node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs` so the import path doesn't depend on workspace resolution at all.

Idempotent + version-pinned. Adds ~30MB to the image (tsx + esbuild + get-tsconfig) — negligible vs. the ~3GB total.

How this manifested in prod: every fresh sandbox provisioned with the default agent flavor (which resolves to `:develop` via `ELIZA_AGENT_IMAGE` env var on the provisioning daemon) failed health check inside 180s with "Sandbox health check timed out". The container started but the Node process never reached the listen call because of the tsx import error.
fix(docker): bake standalone tsx loader into :develop / :stable images

feat(provisioning-worker): own the three SSH-bound cron paths instead of forwarding to the control-plane

After PR #7775 folded node health checks into this daemon, three more cron
paths in CRON_FANOUT still forwarded from CF Workers to the
container-control-plane (a Node service whose host we no longer reliably
track) for SSH-bound work that races against the daemon's writes:

  - agent-hot-pool: syncAllocatedCounts + prePullAgentImageOnAvailableNodes
  - node-autoscale: evaluateCapacity + provisionNode / drainNode
  - pool-drain-idle: WarmPoolManager.drainIdle

When the control-plane runs without CONTAINERS_SSH_KEY (verified in prod
2026-05-17), its writes flip every milady-core back to 'offline' five
minutes after the daemon writes them 'healthy'. The fix is the same as
PR #7775: rapatrier the cycle into the orchestrator host that already
has the SSH key + Neon access, and stop fanning out to a separate
service that drifts.

What this commit does:

- Folds the three cycles into the provisioning-worker daemon's
  pollCycle, gated by the same nodeHealthIntervalMs (default 5 min,
  matches the legacy CRON_FANOUT cadence). Each cycle has its own
  try/catch so a single failure (e.g. HCLOUD_TOKEN missing) doesn't
  starve the others.
- Adds processSyncAllocatedCountsCycle, processPrePullImagesCycle,
  processNodeAutoscaleCycle, processPoolDrainIdleCycle to the daemon.
- Loads getNodeAutoscaler, WarmPoolManager, getHetznerPoolContainerCreator,
  containersEnv lazily through the existing loadDeps singleton.
- Caches a single WarmPoolManager instance per daemon process (same
  pattern container-control-plane used).
- Removes the three paths from CRON_FANOUT so the CF Worker stops
  fanning out at all — the daemon is now the only writer.

What this commit deliberately does NOT do:

- The container-control-plane service keeps these route handlers wired
  for backwards compatibility (and for any direct admin invocation),
  but they won't be reached from the CF Worker cron anymore.
- The control-plane still serves the user-facing endpoints (containers
  CRUD, agent bridge, stream). Moving those is a separate, larger PR
  that adds an HTTP server to the daemon.
- The deployment-monitor and other warm-pool crons stay on the
  control-plane for now; they tick at different cadences and don't
  contest docker_nodes truth.

Ops note: scale-up only succeeds when both HCLOUD_TOKEN and
CONTAINERS_AUTOSCALE_PUBLIC_SSH_KEY are present on the daemon host.
Today the worker host doesn't have HCLOUD_TOKEN, so scale-up reports
'scale_up_skipped' until those secrets are added — same posture as the
control-plane was in. Adding them on /opt/eliza/cloud/.env.local on the
orchestrator unlocks autoscale without any further code change.

fix(image.yaml): pre-build packages/agent/dist before Docker build

Dockerfile.ci is a pruner image (see line 3: "Pre-built artifacts come
from GHA") whose first RUN expects `packages/agent/dist/package.json` to
exist on the host before Buildx kicks in. The image.yaml workflow has
been missing that pre-build forever; it shows up the moment we trigger
it manually because nothing else in the repo runs this workflow path
besides releases (which historically came with a pre-built tree).

  #13 0.536 Error: Missing compiled package manifest for @elizaos/agent:
            packages/agent/dist/package.json
  process "/bin/sh -c node \"${APP_CORE_DIR}/scripts/relink-workspace-packages-to-dist.mjs\"
            @elizaos/agent" did not complete successfully: exit code: 1

Fix: add a minimal three-step pre-build before the Buildx step:

  1. setup-bun (1.3.13, the version the repo standardizes on)
  2. bun install --frozen-lockfile (workspaces resolved, lockfile honored)
  3. bun run --cwd packages/agent build:docker-dist
       → rm -rf dist
       → tsc --noCheck -p tsconfig.build.json
       → node ../scripts/prepare-package-dist.mjs packages/agent
         (this is what writes packages/agent/dist/package.json)

We don't replicate the full docker-ci-smoke.sh pre-build chain
(build:client, build:web, root tsdown) because Dockerfile.ci only
needs the agent dist for its workspace-relink step. The web bundle and
the rest are produced inside the Docker stages.

feat(provisioning-worker): fold node health checks into the daemon so the orchestrator owns them

Today docker_nodes status is driven by container-control-plane, a separate
Node service that the CF Worker cron `agent-hot-pool` forwards to every
5 minutes. That service is deployed somewhere we no longer reliably know,
and verified in prod 2026-05-17 it cannot SSH the cores (its
CONTAINERS_SSH_KEY is missing) — every milady-core-* sat `offline` for days
even though SSH + `docker info` succeed instantly from this very daemon's
host using the key we just configured here for provision/stop.

Folding the loop into the provisioning worker daemon is the smaller-blast-
radius fix: this host already has

  - the CONTAINERS_SSH_KEY load-bearing for provision and stop (PR #7746)
  - direct Neon write access via DATABASE_URL
  - a 30s poll cycle that's a perfect carrier for a 5-min cadence

so we just call `dockerNodeManager.healthCheckAll()` from `pollCycle`,
gated by `lastNodeHealthCheckAt + nodeHealthIntervalMs <= now`. The CF
Worker cron route can stay as a no-op for now (`forwardCronToContainerControlPlane`
returns 503 when no URL is configured) and be removed in a follow-up; this
PR is the source-of-truth flip, not the cleanup.

Defaults / env:
  - `WORKER_NODE_HEALTH_INTERVAL` (ms) — defaults to 5 min, mirroring the
    legacy CRON_FANOUT cadence for agent-hot-pool.
  - Logs each tick at INFO with total/healthy/unhealthy so ops can spot
    regressions without grepping CF tail.

Concurrency: `healthCheckAll` already iterates with `Promise.allSettled`
and has its own MAX_RETRIES timeout, so a slow node never starves the
heartbeat or job-pickup cycle.

refactor(container-control-plane): drop node healthCheckAll() — owned by provisioning-worker daemon now

The daemon (PR's previous commits) now health-checks every enabled
docker_nodes row on its own poll loop, using the load-bearing
CONTAINERS_SSH_KEY that lives on the orchestrator host. Keeping the same
call here too would race with the daemon: with a different (likely empty)

fails, the agent-hot-pool cron tick writes 'offline' to every row, and the
daemon flips them back to 'healthy' two minutes later. The status visible
to the rest of the system would depend on which 5-min cron landed last.

— syncAllocatedCounts, prePullAgentImageOnAvailableNodes, and the
capacity report still ride on the same CF Worker cron forward and still
need this Node service. Only the contested write goes away.

fix(shell): final-review fixes — global mount, canSend, z-index, stories format

Addresses the five issues called out in the final code review of the
shell-foundation v1 implementation:

- (Critical) `<ShellFoundationMount />` only rendered inside the pre-agent
  cloud-shell branch of App.tsx. Steady-state shell users (everyone past
  onboarding) saw no pill. Mount also at the steady-state shell return
  site so the pill is truly always present.

- (Critical) `canSend = "summoned" || "responding"` invited the user to
  type while the agent was streaming, but the reducer's SEND guard
  rejects from `responding` — silent input drop. Fix to
  `"summoned" || "listening"` matching the reducer contract. Add a
  shell-state unit test pinning the no-op so a future regression is
  caught at unit level rather than in the live app.

- (Important) HomePill + AssistantOverlay hardcoded `z-[10000]` /
  `z-[10001]` Tailwind classes. The project convention (per
  `lib/floating-layers.ts`) is to derive z-index from the exported
  constants. Tailwind's JIT can't statically follow template-interpolated
  arbitrary values, so use inline `style={{ zIndex: Z_SHELL_OVERLAY }}`
  (and `Z_SHELL_OVERLAY + 1` for the drawer that should cover the pill).

- (Important) `shell-foundation.stories.tsx` was authored in Storybook CSF
  format, but `packages/ui-stories` is a custom Vite catalog that consumes
  `StoryDefinition[]` arrays, not CSF default+named exports. The stories
  were also not wired into `ui-stories/App.tsx` so they never rendered.
  Rewrite as `shellFoundationStories: StoryDefinition[]` and add the
  group to the catalog's `App.tsx`.

- (Important) Offline visual (`isOnline` → pill tint + input placeholder
  swap) was spec'd but never reached any component. State is plumbed
  correctly; UI work is purely additive. Document this as a Known v1
  deviation in the design spec so future implementers see the gap.

  Re-exported from src/platform/index.ts so the rest of the package gets a
  single source of truth for the darwin predicate.

  non-darwin (its only working data source is the native activity tracker).
- src/actions/connector.ts: short-circuit dispatchIMessage with

runVaultBootstrap) was gated only by `!isMobilePlatform()`. In a cloud
Docker sandbox (`ELIZA_CLOUD_PROVISIONED=1`) it's both pointless and
actively harmful:

- The daemon already injects every secret as a real env var

  are no plaintext secrets to migrate.
- libsecret isn't installed in the slim Docker image.
- The vault opens a second PGlite worker at `<stateDir>/.vault-pglite/`,
  parallel to plugin-sql's primary PGlite/Neon. In `:develop` builds the
  second PGlite init was hanging silently — the HTTP listen never fired,
  every fresh sandbox tripped the 180s docker health check, and the
  daemon scrubbed the container with "Sandbox health check timed out".

mobile guard. The daemon already sets this flag at container create time
(`docker-sandbox-provider.ts:464`, `local-docker-sandbox-provider.ts:249`).

the vault path — the cloud sandbox just needed the equivalent opt-out.

image) in a Docker container. Before this commit: container stalls
forever after `[eliza] DATABASE_URL detected: using Postgres database`
log line, Node process alive in ep_poll, never reaches
"[eliza-api] Listening on http://0.0.0.0:2138". After this commit (with
ELIZA_CLOUD_PROVISIONED=1 set): boot continues past vault, plugin
loading proceeds, server binds the agent port.

fix was discovered and shipped while diagnosing exactly this sandbox-

verification.

fix(boot): skip account-pool bootstrap in cloud containers (circular import deadlock)

The account-pool block at startEliza step 2f calls
`await importAppCoreRuntime()`, which loads `@elizaos/app-core/agent-bridge`,
which transitively loads `app-core/services/account-pool`, which statically
imports from `@elizaos/agent` — the same module we're currently inside.

In desktop / Android boot paths this circular import resolves because the
agent module's top-level evaluation has already partially completed by the
time account-pool needs its bindings. In a cloud Docker container with
`ELIZA_CLOUD_PROVISIONED=1` and the vault paths already skipped (commits
1a4f226 + e10eb89), the `await importAppCoreRuntime()` at line 3061 is the
FIRST call to load app-core's bridge — and Node ESM module evaluation
deadlocks waiting for the cycle to resolve. PID 1 sits in `ep_poll`, no
listen, 180s health timeout.

Cloud sandboxes don't need the multi-account pool anyway: the daemon
injects exactly one set of provider credentials per sandbox as env vars
(ELIZA_API_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, …). The pool is a
desktop feature for users juggling work / personal / throwaway accounts
per provider; cloud has nothing to multiplex.

Gating with `process.env.ELIZA_CLOUD_PROVISIONED !== "1"` keeps the path
intact for every non-cloud target and only short-circuits in the one
environment where (a) it isn't useful and (b) it deadlocks.

Validated in tracing: with vault hydration + vault-profile-resolver +
agent-wallets skipped (commits 1a4f226 + e10eb89), boot still hung at this
account-pool block. Adding this guard expected to unblock plugin
auto-enable + the rest of startEliza. Will test the rebuilt image in the
next cycle.

fix(ui): inline z-index arbitrary classes so Tailwind v4 emits them

Tailwind v4's source scanner only sees classes as literal substrings of
the source text. Several UI primitives shipped with template-literal
interpolation of floating-layer constants, e.g.:

    className={`fixed inset-0 z-[${Z_DIALOG_OVERLAY}] ...`}

The scanner cannot resolve `z-[${Z_DIALOG_OVERLAY}]` at build time, so
the matching utility is never emitted to the CSS bundle. At runtime the
template renders the expected class name, but no rule exists in the
stylesheet — the dialog overlay and content lose `position: fixed`,
`inset-0`, and their stacking context, the overlay backdrop disappears,
and underlying page chrome bleeds through the modal.

Symptom in production (reported in #eliza-cloud):
the "New Agent" modal on the Instances page rendered with no overlay
and a transparent body, exposing the pricing table, balance, and the
"+ New Agent" button behind it.

Replace the broken interpolations with literal arbitrary values
mirrored from packages/ui/src/lib/floating-layers.ts:

  Z_DIALOG_OVERLAY (160)  → z-[160]
  Z_DIALOG         (170)  → z-[170]
  Z_OVERLAY        (200)  → z-[200]
  Z_SYSTEM_BANNER  (9998) → z-[9998]
  Z_SYSTEM_CRITICAL(9999) → z-[9999]
  Z_SHELL_OVERLAY  (10000)→ z-[10000]

Affected primitives:
  - components/ui/dialog.tsx
  - components/ui/drawer-sheet.tsx
  - components/ui/tooltip-extended.tsx
  - components/composites/chat/chat-conversation-item.tsx
  - components/shell/SystemWarningBanner.tsx
  - components/shell/ConnectionFailedBanner.tsx
  - components/shell/RestartBanner.tsx
  - components/shell/ShellOverlays.tsx

Each file gets a short comment pinning the literal to the constant in
floating-layers.ts so future edits stay in sync. No behavior changes
beyond restoring the missing CSS.
