fix(cloud): drop dead fast-path in executeResume (greptile P1+P2)

Greptile flagged three issues on the resume executor:

P1: fast path UPDATEs status='running' but doesn't restore bridge_url /
health_url that executeSuspend clears, so proxy routes that guard on
rec.bridge_url see a "running" agent that's unreachable.

P2: executeResume reads outside any transaction and holds no lifecycle
lock, unlike executeSuspend. Two concurrent resume jobs can race.

P2: when provider.start is undefined the code falls through to a full
re-provision with no log, hiding the "method not implemented" path.

Underlying truth: DockerSandboxProvider doesn't expose a standalone
start() at all, so the fast path was dead code on the only provider
that ships today — every resume already paid the re-provision cost.

Fix: drop the fast path. executeResume now delegates to provision(),
which restores bridge_url / health_url from a fresh sandbox handle and
acquires its own advisory lock. The fast path returns when the
provider grows a start() that yields the handle — tracked as
follow-up.

Also updates the resume route comment and user-facing message that
falsely claimed "~5s fast path".

Why all three at once: same architectural shift as suspend/resume —
Cloudflare Workers never call cores directly, every cores-bound op
flows through the queue. RESTART is shutdown+provision atomic, LOGS
is daemon-side `docker logs`, SNAPSHOT is daemon-side

Three new daemon-side handlers extend the cores-never-touched-from-Workers
architecture started in #7808 (suspend/resume) to cover the rest of the
lifecycle:

- executeRestart: shutdown() + provision() atomically on the daemon.
  Replaces the Worker-side sequence which silently no-op'd the stop
  step and could leave a stale container running alongside the new one.

- executeLogs: SSH \`docker logs --tail N <container>\` via the new
  SandboxProvider.fetchLogs() method. Works for stopped + crashed
  agents (the Worker-side fetch(bridge_url + /logs) returned empty for
  anything not actively running).

- executeSnapshot: thin wrapper around the existing snapshot() so the
  job dispatcher can route through a single contract. Invoked from
  the daemon so outbound traffic to cores uses the same network
  identity as every other lifecycle op.

Job machinery in provisioning-jobs.ts mirrors the suspend/resume
patterns: data/result shapes, type guards, idempotent enqueue methods
that reuse in-flight jobs on duplicate requests.

DockerSandboxProvider.fetchLogs() merges stderr into stdout because
agent crash traces tend to land on stderr.

feat(training): low-VRAM smoke preset for 2b SFT on 12 GB consumer GPUs

The registry default for qwen3.5-2b targets a 16 GB local GPU (seq_len=8192,
budget=15.5 GB). On a 12 GB consumer card (RTX 3060 / 4070 class) that OOMs
at the fp32 logits transient (B*S*V*4 bytes; Qwen vocab=248k makes this
dominant).

The new --low-vram-smoke flag is a CLI preset that overrides the registry
defaults to seq_len=2048, batch=1, grad_accum=16 (effective batch stays at
16), max_samples=1000, epochs=1, memory_budget_gb=11.5. Liger fused
chunked-CE stays on (registry default for 2B) and activation checkpointing
stays on (train_local.py default), which is what makes the budget feasible.

CLI flags the caller passes explicitly still win over the preset; the
override block compares against the argparse-default snapshot captured
before the registry merge, so values that came from the CLI are
distinguishable from values the registry filled in.

The preset is explicitly NOT for publishable runs — it is a path-validation
smoke for the SFT entrypoint on commodity hardware. The resulting
checkpoint should not be pushed as an eliza-1-2b bundle.

Includes:
- scripts/train_local.py: --low-vram-smoke flag + override block
- scripts/test_train_local_low_vram_smoke.py: 6 CPU-only unit tests
  pinning the override semantics (registry interaction, CLI override
  precedence, no-registry-key path, and a regression guard against
  removing the flag without removing the block)
- README.md: "Running on a 12 GB consumer GPU" section documenting the
  invocation, the trade-off (training context window 8k -> 2k, not
  suitable for long-context behaviors), and the OOM-retry path
  (--low-vram-smoke --max-seq-len 1024)

fix(training): use None sentinels so --low-vram-smoke respects CLI defaults-equal values

The previous `_defaults_at_parse` snapshot compared each parsed value to
`ap.get_default(dest)` to decide "user didn't pass it". That dies as soon
as the caller explicitly passes the same value as the argparse default:

    --epochs 3.0 --low-vram-smoke   → preset silently rewrote 3.0 → 1.0
    --max-samples 0 --low-vram-smoke → preset silently rewrote 0 → 1000

Both break the contract documented in the README ("CLI flags the caller
passes still win") because == against the default cannot distinguish
"user typed it" from "argparse filled it in".

Fix: switch the tracked-by-merge args (model, batch_size, grad_accum,
max_seq_len, optimizer, apollo_rank, max_samples, epochs, plus the
already-None memory_budget_gb) to `default=None`. After parse_args,
user-passed-ness is now `getattr(args, dest) is not None` — exact,
ambiguity-free. Registry merge and --low-vram-smoke preset both gate
on `not _user_passed[dest]`. A final `_FALLBACK_DEFAULTS` pass fills
any value still None with the historical argparse fallback (4096 /
4 / 8 / 3.0 / 0 / "apollo" / 256 / "Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B"), so behavior
when neither registry nor preset fires is unchanged.

`_defaults_at_parse` snapshot dropped entirely — the None sentinel
makes it unnecessary.

Tests: updated the inline `_resolve()` helper in
test_train_local_low_vram_smoke.py to mirror the new logic
(default=None on the rebuilt parser, _user_passed dict, fallback
pass). Added a parametrized regression that asserts every tracked
flag set to its historical argparse default survives the preset
(--epochs 3.0, --max-samples 0, --batch-size 4, --grad-accum 8,
--max-seq-len 4096). Added two combined-scenario regressions for
--registry-key + --low-vram-smoke + explicit default-equal value
on --max-samples 0 and --epochs 3.0. All 13 tests pass.

refactor(training): extract build_parser + apply_resolved_defaults for test reuse

The low-vram-smoke test had to maintain a hand-written mirror of
train_local.main's argparse layout + registry/preset/fallback merge
order (`_build_parser` + `_resolve` + duplicated _TRACKED_DESTS +
duplicated _FALLBACK_DEFAULTS, ~85 lines). Any new tracked arg or
override block added to main() would silently bypass the mirror —
tests would keep passing while exercising the old behavior.

  - apply_resolved_defaults(args) -> None      — owns the merge

The test's `_resolve()` now delegates to the same helpers instead
of duplicating them, so any future tracked-arg addition is covered
by existing assertions automatically.

fix(cloud): reject POST /deploy with 409 when a build is already in flight

Two concurrent CLI invocations of `elizaos deploy` both went through
unguarded: createDeployment stamped `last_deployed_at` twice, the
loser's `deploymentId` was immediately stale, and its subsequent GET
/status polls would return the winner's record without any signal
that the original POST got co-opted.

Adds `assertDeployable` helper that throws ApiError(409) when the
app's persisted `deployment_status` is already "building".
`createDeployment` calls it after a (cache-hot) `getById`, so the
race surfaces to the caller as a 409 instead of silently overwriting.

This is a check-then-act guard, not a DB-level lock — a fully race-
free path would do a conditional UPDATE in the apps repo. For the
realistic CLI cadence (invocations seconds apart) this is sufficient.

fix(flatpak): use bare-string node-sources.json source so flatpak-builder processes its entries

The previous `type: file` / `path: node-sources.json` source made
flatpak-builder treat the JSON as an opaque file to copy into the
build directory, so it never read the manifest and never populated
`flatpak-node/npm-cache` with the 1202 archive/script entries. As a
result `npm install -g --offline elizaos` would fail with
package-not-found errors and the entire offline build path was broken.

Switching to the bare-string form lets flatpak-builder interpret the
file as a flatpak-node-generator manifest and dispatch its archive,
script, and shell entries individually so the npm tarball cache is
populated before the build step runs.

fix(boot): eliminate top-level-await deadlock that froze cloud Docker boot

Diagnosis (full debug session against ghcr.io/elizaos/eliza:sha-6d0c8d5):
Provisioning a fresh sandbox in a cloud Docker container hung silently —
no logs past `[eliza] Generated SECRET_SALT`, PID 1 in `ep_poll`, no listen
on the agent port, daemon scrubbed the container at the 180s health
timeout. Three vault skips (commits 1fc4dd6, e10eb89, 6d0c8d5) moved boot
past `runVaultBootstrap`, `vault-profile-resolver`, and
`ensureAgentWallets`, but the next call to `await importAppCoreRuntime()`
(= `import("@elizaos/app-core/agent-bridge")`) still deadlocked.

By instrumenting the dist files in a running container we narrowed the
hang to two distinct sources:

1. `app-core/services/account-pool.ts` did a static `import "@elizaos/agent"`
   (barrel). Loading the agent barrel started evaluating
   `packages/agent/dist/api/index.js`, which had FOUR top-level awaits
   loading platform plugins (computeruse, signal, whatsapp, workflow).
   With agent already partially evaluated as the bin.js entrypoint, the
   barrel re-import returned a partial namespace and the TLAs never
   resolved → deadlock at module evaluation.

2. `packages/agent/dist/services/index.js`,
   `services/app-session-gate.js`, and `services/hosted-tools.js` had
   matching TLAs for the same plugins plus plugin-app-manager and
   plugin-elizacloud. Even after `api/index.js` was unblocked, the
   `services/*` modules tripped the same deadlock when any consumer
   walked through them.

Fixes in this commit:

- `packages/agent/src/api/index.ts`: convert the four
  `const x = await import(plugin)` blocks to lazy loaders + async route
  wrappers. Mirrors the existing `loadElizaCloudRoutes` pattern already
  used elsewhere in the same file.
- `packages/agent/src/services/index.ts`: convert the same three
  plugin imports from TLA to static re-exports. The plugins don't have
  side-effectful top-level code, so a plain `export { X } from "plugin"`
  is sufficient and avoids the TLA penalty entirely.
- `packages/agent/src/services/app-session-gate.ts`: replace
  `const { readAppRunStore } = await import(...)` with a static
  `import { readAppRunStore } from "@elizaos/plugin-app-manager"`.
- `packages/agent/src/services/hosted-tools.ts`: same fix for
  `resolveCloudApiBaseUrl` from plugin-elizacloud.
- `packages/agent/package.json`: add `./auth/*` subpath to `exports`
  so consumers can target individual files in `auth/` without pulling
  the entire agent barrel.
- `packages/app-core/src/services/account-pool.ts`: replace the
  `import "@elizaos/agent"` barrel import with three narrow subpath
  imports (`@elizaos/agent/auth/types`,
  `@elizaos/agent/auth/credentials`,
  `@elizaos/agent/auth/account-storage`). Eliminates the barrel
  evaluation that was the root trigger.

Validated by replaying the same patches in a live Docker container and
seeing the agent reach `[eliza-api] Listening on http://127.0.0.1:2138`
within ~60s of `node packages/agent/dist/bin.js start` (vs. 180s timeout
before).

feat(local-inference): wire slot save/restore + prewarm through FFI

Closes three of the five FFI parity gaps left after the desktop
adapter landed:

1. **Slot save/restore via direct libllama bindings**.
   `llama_state_seq_save_file` / `_load_file` are pointer-style
   upstream APIs — no shim wrapper needed; binds directly from
   libllama. Added to desktop-llama-adapter.ts:
   - LlamaSymbols typedef gains both signatures
   - bindLlama() adds the symbol descriptors
   - new `saveSlot(filename)` / `restoreSlot(filename)` methods
     against seq_id=0 (v1 uses single seq per ctx)
   - `createBinding()` now wires `llmStreamSaveSlot` /
     `llmStreamRestoreSlot`
   v1 limitation: passes NULL token-buffer + count=0. The engine's
   conversation registry owns prompt-token bookkeeping above the
   adapter so the per-slot KV file is sufficient.

2. **persistConversationKv / restoreConversationKv on FfiStreamingBackend**.
   Forwards to the binding's `llmStreamSaveSlot` /
   `llmStreamRestoreSlot` with a slot filename of
   `<conversationId>__slot<slotId>.kv`. Mirrors cache-bridge.ts's
   slot layout for cross-backend resume parity once file formats align.
   No-op when the active session lacks save/restore (defensive — the
   binding type makes them optional).

3. **prewarmConversation on FfiStreamingBackend**. Pure JS — runs the
   runner's `generateWithUsage` against the prefix with maxTokens=0,
   feeding the prompt without generating. The runner's slotInFlight
   serialization keys on cacheKey so concurrent prewarms against the
   same slot wait properly.

Engine no-ops convert to real behavior: when the dispatcher's
`persistConversationKv` / `restoreConversationKv` /
`prewarmConversation` forwarders are called against an FFI session
they now actually do the work instead of returning silently per the
optional-method fallthrough.

Still subprocess-only on dflashLlamaServer (the dispatcher throws
actionable errors when called against an FFI session):
- vision describe (mmproj) — requires `llava_eval_image_embed` C
  wrapper in eliza-llama-shim
- parallel resize — requires multi-context pooling at the adapter
- speculative decoding — `eliza_llama_context_attach_drafter` exists
  in the shim; wiring is straightforward but kept out of this commit
  to preserve scope (drafter args are silently ignored with a one-time
  warning today)

NOT runtime-tested. libllama.dylib still needs a real build. The
state-seq bindings follow llama.h's public ABI verbatim; the on-disk
file format is whatever upstream picks.

build(dflash): add linux-x64-openvino target for Intel CPU/iGPU/NPU + bump submodule

Adds Linux x64 OpenVINO build target to `build-llama-cpp-dflash.mjs`,
backed by a submodule pointer bump to a cherry-pick of the upstream
ggml-openvino backend (ggml-org/llama.cpp PR #15307, merged April 8
2026) into `elizaOS/llama.cpp` on branch
`nubs/openvino-backend-import` (3 commits: initial PR, the
buffer_context memset fix, and the NPU optimizations + driver setup
+ thread safety follow-up).

## Motivation

OpenVINO is the only llama.cpp path that targets the Intel NPU
(Lunar Lake AI Boost ~48 TOPS, Meteor Lake NCE, Arrow Lake). NPU
inference draws ~2-3 W vs ~15-25 W for the iGPU on the same model.
Beyond power, OpenVINO covers all three Intel devices (CPU + iGPU +
NPU) through one runtime, with device selection at runtime via
`GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE`. Distinct from `linux-x64-sycl` (#7628) —
SYCL covers CPU + iGPU but NOT the NPU.

The W4-B custom kernels (turbo3 / turbo4 / turbo3_tcq / qjl /
polarquant / dflash) do NOT have an OpenVINO backend in this fork
today — those are CUDA / Vulkan / Metal / CPU only — so this target
runs plain ggml ops translated to OpenVINO graphs. The kernel-patches
dispatch in `patchAllKernels()` correctly no-ops for
`backend === "openvino"`. Future Eliza-kernel OpenVINO ports would
plug in alongside the existing per-backend branches.

## Changes (build script)

- `SUPPORTED_TARGETS` gains `"linux-x64-openvino"` with a comment
  block detailing what hardware it targets and why kernel patches
  do not apply.
- `cmakeFlagsForTarget` grows a `backend === "openvino"` branch that
  sets `-DGGML_OPENVINO=ON` and forwards `OpenVINO_DIR` /
  `INTEL_OPENVINO_DIR` from the environment as `-DOpenVINO_DIR=...`
  pointing at `${INSTALLDIR}/runtime/cmake` (CMake's
  `find_package(OpenVINO)` default search does not pick up the
  tarball install layout).
- `GGML_OPENVINO` joins the `offByDefault` list so non-OpenVINO
  targets explicitly disable it (parity with METAL / CUDA / HIP /
  VULKAN).
- `targetCompatibility` now returns a graceful "no OpenVINO_DIR /
  INTEL_OPENVINO_DIR" skip when the operator forgot to source
  `setupvars.sh`, instead of crashing inside CMake.
- The `TODO ANCHORS` comment in `cmakeFlagsForTarget` grows an
  `OPENVINO-AGENT TODO` line for future kernel work.

## Submodule

- `packages/inference/llama.cpp` bumps from `a61c93aaa5` (v1.2.0-eliza)
  to `bafc862bf` (`v1.2.0-eliza-3-gbafc862bf`) on
  `nubs/openvino-backend-import`. Range adds:
  ```
  53281e98d ggml : add OpenVINO backend (#15307)
  1ebe824a0 fix(openvino): explicit memset in buffer_context allocation (#20857)
  bafc862bf openvino: driver setup, CI split, thread safety, and NPU optimizations (#21944)
  ```
  All three are upstream commits cherry-picked from ggml-org/llama.cpp
  master. The diff is purely additive: a new `ggml/src/ggml-openvino/`
  directory, plus four small glue hunks (`ggml/CMakeLists.txt`,
  `ggml/src/CMakeLists.txt`, `ggml/src/ggml-backend-reg.cpp`,
  `docs/backend/OPENVINO.md`). Non-OpenVINO builds are byte-identical.

## Verification

Dispatch path:

```
$ node packages/app-core/scripts/build-llama-cpp-dflash.mjs \
    --target linux-x64-openvino --jobs 1
# without setupvars sourced:
[dflash-build] target linux-x64-openvino is not buildable: no
  OpenVINO_DIR / INTEL_OPENVINO_DIR — source
  /opt/intel/openvino_<ver>/setupvars.sh first
```

Build runtime requirements:

- OpenVINO Runtime 2026.1.0 (tarball or `apt install openvino-2026.x`
  from Intel's APT repo)
- OpenCL ICD loader + Khronos OpenCL-Headers + OpenCL-CLHPP
  (`apt install opencl-headers ocl-icd-opencl-dev intel-opencl-icd`,
  or extract the headers manually under a prefix like ~/.local)

The OpenCL dependency comes from OpenVINO's iGPU plugin (it links
`OpenCL::OpenCL` even for CPU/NPU device builds, per upstream PR
#15307). The build cannot opt out of OpenCL today; an upstream PR
to make GPU plugin optional would be welcome.

Hardware test (Lunar Lake Arc 140V + 48 TOPS NPU): pending — log
will land as a follow-up comment.

## Related

- #7626 — glslc absolute path fix (Vulkan build dependency)
- #7628 — `linux-x64-sycl` target (parallel Intel iGPU/CPU path,
  no NPU coverage)
- #7630 — submodule bump to v1.2.0-eliza (base for this branch)
- #7629 — Qwen3.5 drafter publication gap
- #7631 — M-RoPE spec-decode incompatibility

## Out of scope

- Real W4-B kernel ports to OpenVINO (would require an Intel-paid
  contributor; this PR is the scaffold).
- Eliza/Milady runtime wiring — `LocalRuntimeKernel` enum extension
  + hardware probe + env-var plumbing — separate RFC.
- AMD XDNA / Qualcomm Hexagon NPU paths.

chore(inference): bump packages/inference/llama.cpp to v1.2.0-eliza (9bb0884390 → a61c93aaa5)

Bumps the llama.cpp submodule pointer from the current develop pin
`9bb0884390` up to the `v1.2.0-eliza` tag (commit `a61c93aaa5`). The
range adds eight commits, summary below.

## Why

`cb700767` is load-bearing for the QJL1_256 / Q4_POLAR KV cache path
on Vulkan (and any other backend that calls into flash_attn_ext with
quantized KV). Without it, the v1.1.0-eliza pin emits unquantized KV
through flash_attn_ext, which can fall back to a slow shader path on
Intel/AMD Vulkan or silently disagree with the host-side dequant on
CPU/MoE splits. The same range also pulls in:

- `cb700767` llama-graph: dequantize QJL1_256 K / Q4_POLAR V to F16
  before flash_attn_ext
- `03fc58ef` server-slot: forced-token fast-forward cursor + helpers
- `e32a7bf2` + `3b9ecc7b` server-task: task_prefill_plan plumbing
- `a50cb7c4` ffi: implement eliza_inference_set_verifier_callback
  + emit helper (needed by the verifier-stream patch the build script
  already asserts is present)
- `a61c93aa` ffi(asr-stream): real buffered streaming +
  vocab-gated capability probe
- `42947fe7` chore: checkpoint WIP — CUDA fused-attn-qjl-tbq
- `b084d780` wip(omnivoice-ffi): pre-existing dirty refactor

The middle two `chore: checkpoint WIP` / `wip(omnivoice-ffi)` commits
are unusual to ship inside a tagged release, but they are inside the
upstream `v1.2.0-eliza` tag (`packages/inference/llama.cpp` ref
`a61c93aaa5`) — happy to drop this PR if the maintainers prefer to
land a different sha for v1.2.0-eliza, or to wait for v1.2.1.

build script (with #7626 glslc fix applied so vulkan-shaders-gen

fix(local-inference): resolve glslc to absolute path before passing to CMake

`findGlslc` returned the bare string "glslc" when the binary was on the
host PATH. The script then passed this verbatim to CMake as
`-DVulkan_GLSLC_EXECUTABLE=glslc`, which CMake stores as a relative
`FILEPATH` resolved against the source dir (the llama.cpp checkout).

Result on a stock Debian/Ubuntu host where `glslc` lives at
`/usr/bin/glslc`:

  CMakeCache.txt:
    Vulkan_GLSLC_EXECUTABLE:FILEPATH=/home/.../inference/llama.cpp/glslc

That path does not exist. `vulkan-shaders-gen` is then invoked without a
usable glslc, silently produces zero .spv files, and writes an `.hpp`
header with `extern const` declarations whose `_data` / `_len` symbols
are never defined. Link fails with ~2,000 undefined references:

  undefined reference to `add_f16_f16_f32_rte_len`
  undefined reference to `matmul_id_subgroup_q5_1_q8_1_data`
  undefined reference to `sub_f16_f16_f32_rte_len`
  ... and so on

Fix: resolve `glslc` via `which` before returning, so CMake gets an
absolute path and the shader-gen step actually invokes glslc.

Verified on Intel Core Ultra 7 258V (Lunar Lake) with Arc Graphics 140V:
after the fix, `linux-x64-vulkan` build produces 2,203 SPV blobs and a
working `llama-server` that initializes the GPU (KHR_coopmat / XMX
matrix cores active) and benchmarks at:

  | model                  | backend | ngl | test |       t/s |
  | llama 8B Q4_K - Medium | Vulkan  |  99 | pp64 | 172.93 ±  |
  | llama 8B Q4_K - Medium | Vulkan  |  99 | tg32 |   5.73 ±  |

vs CPU baseline on the same machine (1.42 t/s pp, 0.60 t/s tg) — ~121×
prompt eval, ~10× decode.

Android NDK path is unaffected: it already returns an absolute path via
`path.join(ndk, "shader-tools", host, "glslc")`.

feat(plugin-discord): port Discord Desktop CDP control to Windows

Lifts the macOS-only guards in the Discord Desktop CDP fallback so the
user-account-scraper path works on Windows too. Same flag (`--remote-
debugging-port`) that Discord on macOS has been accepting since this
file's introduction; Windows builds accept it just as well (empirically
verified against Discord 1.0.9237 / Electron 37.6.0 — `/json/version`
returns Chrome/138 with the Discord User-Agent, `/json/list` exposes
the channels page target).

Three macOS-only sites lifted:

- **`discordAppRunning()`** — now branches on `process.platform`. macOS
  keeps `pgrep -x Discord`; Windows uses `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq
  Discord.exe" /FO CSV /NH` and checks the output for the Discord.exe
  process row (tasklist prints "INFO: No tasks are running..." when
  nothing matches, so a regex test on `Discord\.exe` correctly
  distinguishes the two states).

- **`getDiscordDesktopCdpStatus()`** — the `platform === "darwin"` /
  `platform !== "darwin"` guards are replaced with an
  `isDiscordDesktopSupportedPlatform()` predicate that accepts both
  `"darwin"` and `"win32"`. The `lastError` for unsupported platforms
  is updated accordingly.

- **`relaunchDiscordDesktopForCdp()`** — branches on platform for both
  the quit step and the launch step. Windows quits with
  `taskkill /F /T /IM Discord.exe` (force-kills the whole process tree;
  Discord otherwise stays in the tray) and launches with
  `cmd /d /s /c start "" <Discord.exe> --remote-debugging-port=...
  --remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1 --remote-allow-origins=*` so
  the parent process returns immediately while Discord keeps running
  in the background.

- **`findDiscordExeWindows()`** (new helper) — globs
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Discord\app-*\Discord.exe` and picks the highest
  numeric version. Discord on Windows is squirrel-installed per-user
  with each release in its own `app-X.Y.Z` folder; this picks the
  current one so an in-flight self-update doesn't strand us on a stale
  executable.

Linux support is still not implemented — the desktop control surface
there would need a separate process-detection + launch path (and
verifying CDP works on the linux Discord build). Out of scope for
this PR; getDiscordDesktopCdpStatus returns `supported: false` with a
"macOS and Windows" lastError on Linux.

feat(cloud-shared/oauth): support userScopes config field + request Slack user scopes

Slack's OAuth v2 splits permissions into two scope groups: bot/app
scopes (passed as the regular `scope` query parameter) and user scopes
(passed as a separate `user_scope` query parameter). Without
`user_scope`, the `authed_user.access_token` returned in the OAuth
response is functionally a bot-context token with no user-level
permissions granted — it can't read the user's channels, write as
them, or search their messages.

Adds:
- `userScopes?: string[]` field on `OAuthProviderConfig` so providers
  with this user/bot split can declare user-level scopes separately
  from `defaultScopes`
- URL-builder support in `initiateOAuth2`: when a provider declares
  `userScopes`, the auth URL gets a `user_scope` parameter alongside
  the regular `scope` parameter
- Slack entry now declares `userScopes: ["chat:write", "search:read",
  "users:read", "files:read"]` so the OWNER role's user token carries
  meaningful permissions

Currently Slack is the only provider that needs this split; future
providers with the same OAuth shape can opt in by declaring
`userScopes` on their entry. Purely additive — providers without
`userScopes` get exactly the same auth URL as before.

fix(cloud-shared/oauth): scope user_scope + userInfo token to OWNER flow only — Greptile P1

Two bugs in PR 5's user_scope plumbing that would break the Slack
two-button UX in practice:

1. **user_scope applied unconditionally.** The AGENT flow installs the
   app's bot into the workspace — surfacing personal user-level
   permission requests on the authorization screen is a UX surprise
   ("why does this bot want to read my DMs?") and exceeds the bot
   install scope intent.

2. **userInfo lookup uses bot token for both roles.** After token
   exchange, `handleOAuth2Callback` calls
   `fetchUserInfo(provider, tokens.access_token)` — the bot token —
   regardless of role. For Slack that means both AGENT and OWNER
   flows resolve to the same `users.identity` user_id (the
   workspace admin who clicked Authorize on either button). The
   `storeConnection` dedup guard at line 715 then rejects the second
   connection with `OAUTH_ACCOUNT_ALREADY_LINKED_TO_DIFFERENT_ROLE`,
   so the user could only ever connect ONE of the two buttons.

Fix:

- `initiateOAuth2` reads `params.connectionRole` (already plumbed
  through `OAuth2State`) and only adds `user_scope` when the role
  is not `AGENT`. Cloud-broker default is `OWNER` so flows without
  an explicit role still get user_scope.

- `handleOAuth2Callback` now resolves the userInfo lookup token via
  a new `pickUserInfoToken` helper. For providers with `userScopes`
  declared, OWNER flows use `tokens.authed_user.access_token` (the
  user token) instead of the bot `access_token`. Other providers and
  AGENT flows keep the standard `access_token`.

With both fixes, clicking "Use Slack OAuth (agent)" stores the bot
under the bot's user_id with role=AGENT, and clicking "(your
account)" stores the user under the user's own user_id with
role=OWNER — two distinct platform_credentials rows that the
existing dedup guard correctly allows side by side.

When --registry-key is set, the use_liger auto-resolver at line 608
references _registry_get to read entry.use_liger from the registry. But
_registry_get is only imported inside _apply_resolved_args() (line 408)
as a local import, so it's not visible in main(). Running:

crashes with NameError: name '_registry_get' is not defined right after
the model loads, before training begins. --preflight-only succeeds because
the check exits before the use_liger expression evaluates.

mirroring the pattern already used in _apply_resolved_args. One-line
change; preserves the lazy-import style the rest of the file uses for
training-only deps.

forces seq=2048, batch=1, accum=16); the same code path also fires on
any setup where --registry-key is passed and --use-liger is left at
"auto" (the default).

`cloudOAuthBusy: boolean` between both buttons — clicking "agent" would
flip both buttons to `"..."` and disable both, with no signal which
role's OAuth flow was actually in flight. For connectors that expose

confusing.

`Partial<Record<CloudOAuthConnectionRole, boolean>>`:

  before starting, sets the role's flag on entry, and clears it in the
  finally block — so each role's request lifecycle is independent.
- The render loop reads `cloudOAuthBusy[role] === true` per button. The
  clicked button shows `"..."` and disables; the other button keeps its
  normal label and stays clickable.

End-state UX: clicking "Use Google OAuth (agent)" shows `"..."` on that
button only; "your account" stays available so the user can kick off
both flows in parallel or correct a misclick without waiting.

Greptile P2 on #7852 flagged this when google's two-button render path
made the shared-busy-state issue more visible. Followup PR rather than
bundled into #7852 because the fix is in the inherited #7851 render
helper, not anything google-specific.

feat(core): runtime.installRemotePlugin API + permission types

P3 step 1/3. Adds the type surface for agent-installed remote-mode
plugins. The implementation lives in @elizaos/agent (next commit).

New types in packages/core/src/types/plugin.ts:

- RemotePluginInstallSource: discriminated union for where the worker
  code comes from. Three variants:
  - { kind: 'inline', files }   — agent-authored; auto-narrowed to
    isolated-process + loopback + tempdir-only FS regardless of request.
  - { kind: 'tarball', url, attestation }  — third-party; signature
    required.
  - { kind: 'workspace', pkgName }  — bundled (e.g. plugin-sub-agent-*).

- RemotePluginInstallOptions: { source, lifetime }. Default lifetime is
  'session' for inline, 'persistent' for tarball/workspace.

- RemotePluginInstanceHandle: { pluginName, instanceId,
  grantedPermissions, uninstall() }. The instanceId allows multiple
  installations of the same plugin (e.g. two concurrent codex
  sub-agent sessions) to coexist in different store dirs.

- PermissionNarrowedRejection: thrown by installRemotePlugin when a
  critical capability narrows to zero in the request ∩ agent-grant ∩
  source-defaults intersection. Callers can catch and prompt the user
  for elevation.

New method on IAgentRuntime:

  installRemotePlugin(plugin, options?) → RemotePluginInstanceHandle

The runtime decides the deployment target based on plugin.remote.
deployment + which environments are reachable; the caller declares
constraints, not the runtime's placement decisions.

Permission narrowing rules (enforced by the agent-side installer in
the next commit):
- Inline source → isolation always 'isolated-process'.
- Inline source → bun.network defaults to 'loopback'.
- Inline source → bun.fs defaults to 'none' with tempdir allowlist.
- Inline source → bun.env defaults to empty.
- Granted = request ∩ runtime.grantedPermissions ∩ defaults.

feat(plugin-sub-agent-claude-code): reference remote sub-agent runner

P3 step 2/3. The proof-of-concept that demonstrates the full stack:
an agent on a user's device can installRemotePlugin a sub-agent
plugin → AdaptiveWorkerRunner picks isolated-process →
SubprocessWorkerHandle spawns the worker via Bun.spawn →
plugin-worker-runtime's bootstrap() announces the service →
RemotePluginBridge materialises a ServiceClass stub → agent
code calls runtime.getService('sub-agent.claude-code').createSession()
→ the call round-trips into the worker → the worker's service
spawns the claude CLI as ANOTHER subprocess inside the worker's
own isolated process.

Three subprocess hops total: agent host → worker host (isolated) →
claude CLI. The CLI panicking or hanging can't reach the agent.

Files:

- src/sub-agent-service.ts — Service class with rpcMethods
  [createSession, sendPrompt, getOutput, terminate, listSessions].
  Sessions are Bun.spawn'd claude processes with stdin/stdout pipes;
  output streams into a buffered array, retrieved via getOutput's
  'all' or 'since-last' mode.

- src/plugin.ts — the Plugin object. mode: 'remote',
  remote.role: 'sub-agent', remote.isolation: 'isolated-process'
  (required for sub-agents — the AdaptiveWorkerRunner honors this),
  remote.subAgent.runner: 'claude-code'.

  Permissions request ceiling:
  - bun.network: 'allowlist' [api.anthropic.com]
  - bun.fs: 'readwrite' [.]
  - bun.process: true (needs to spawn claude CLI)
  - bun.env: ['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', 'CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN']
  - host.events: emit sub-agent.session.{created,terminated}
  - host.memory: 'none' (the sub-agent has no agent memory access by default)

- src/worker.ts — three-line worker entry:
  bootstrap() takes the Plugin object and the announce/dispatch
  loop runs.

Sibling sub-agent runners (-codex, -opencode, -eliza) follow the
same template; the only changes are the binary, the allowlist, and
the optional --model / system-prompt wiring. Future work.

Caveats and follow-ups:
- The CLI is spawned with Bun.spawn pipes, not a PTY. That's fine
  for the prompt-and-collect pattern (claude --print); interactive
  editing/tools need a real PTY. A PTY-backed runner is a P3.5
  follow-up; the API surface (createSession/sendPrompt/getOutput/
  terminate) doesn't change.

Three new worker runners in remote-plugin-host.ts:

  Bun.spawn. Newline-delimited JSON over stdin/stdout for the wire
  envelope; stderr inherits to the host log. terminate() sends SIGTERM,
  schedules SIGKILL after 2s grace. Stdout is parsed line-by-line with
  a streaming buffer; malformed JSON surfaces via onError so the host
  can mark the worker errored.

- IsolatedProcessWorkerRunner — RemotePluginWorkerRunner that wraps
  the SubprocessWorkerHandle. Sets ELIZA_REMOTE_PLUGIN_ID,
  ELIZA_REMOTE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR, ELIZA_REMOTE_PLUGIN_CHANNEL=stdio in
  the child env so the worker bootstrap can pick the right channel.

- AdaptiveWorkerRunner — picks per-plugin between BrowserCarrotWorkerRunner
  (Bun Worker) and IsolatedProcessWorkerRunner based on
  remotePlugin.install.permissionsGranted.isolation. This is now the
  default workerRunner on RemotePluginHost; the previous warn-and-fallback
  behavior is gone.

Worker side (plugin-worker-runtime):

- createSubprocessChannel() — WorkerChannel adapter for process.stdin /
  process.stdout newline-delimited JSON. Feature-detects so it errors

fix(cloud): unblock credits-balance CORS + restore wallet reconnect on /bsc

Two visible regressions on the live BSC flow:

1) CORS preflight rejection on `/api/credits/balance`

   CreditsProvider was sending `Pragma: no-cache` alongside `Cache-Control:
   no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`. The `Cache-Control` value already
   disables caching for any modern proxy; `Pragma` is HTTP/1.0-era cruft
   kept "just in case". Sending it on a cross-origin call to
   `api.elizacloud.ai` forces a CORS preflight to list `pragma` in
   `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`, which the Worker's CORS config doesn't,
   so the actual GET was rejected with `Request header field pragma is not
   allowed`. Dropping the header from the request is the correct fix —
   no protocol semantics change, and the API CORS allowlist stays narrow.

2) Wallet stuck on "Connect Wallet" after a successful MetaMask connect

   `StewardWalletProviders` was setting `reconnectOnMount={false}` on the
   `WagmiProvider`. With that flag, wagmi refuses to restore an existing
   connector session when the provider mounts. On /bsc this surfaced as:
   the user connects via the RainbowKit modal, MetaMask shows "site
   connected", but as soon as React re-renders past the connect event
   (e.g. when the wallet attach flow swaps the AttachWalletCard for the
   DirectCryptoCreditCard), the new component's `useAccount` /
   `ConnectButton.Custom` boots with `account = undefined` and the button
   regresses to "Connect Wallet" with no clickable recovery. The pay
   handler then bails with "Connect your BSC wallet first" because
   `isConnected` is false.

   Default behavior (`reconnectOnMount: true`) is what the BSC promo,
   dashboard billing, and any return-visit flow want. The login surface
   already gates SIWE on an explicit user click via `pendingSignRef`, so
   auto-reconnect can't accidentally fire a signature prompt — flipping
   the default is safe across all consumers of these providers.

  `entry.accounts?.agent` so a partial migration (manifest adds
  `accounts.owner` first while keeping `auth` as the agent credential
  source) still gets the legacy auth mapped onto `accounts.agent`. Without
  the narrower guard the agent side was silently dropped during the
  transition.

- P1 (loader.ts): make the legacy `auth.kind` → `AccountAuthKind` mapping
  explicit via `mapLegacyAuthKindToAccountAuthKind()`. The previous
  conditional ternary silently lumped `"credentials"` (username + password)
  in with `"token"` (single opaque secret) under `"api-key"`. The new
  switch covers all four legacy enum values explicitly and documents that
  `credentials` and `token` coalesce because the UI surface is the same;
  connectors that need to distinguish should declare
  `accounts.agent.authKind` in their manifest.

- P2 (schema.ts): add `.refine()` on the `accounts` object to require at
  least one of `owner` / `agent`. An accidental `accounts: {}` no longer
  silently blocks the legacy-auth auto-mapping.

against any CVA6 in this checkout: it references the legacy
ariane_pkg::ArianeDefaultConfig / module ariane / ariane_axi::req_t API

config_pkg::cva6_cfg_t (built from cva6_config_pkg::cva6_cfg via
build_config_pkg::build_config). Defining +define+E1_HAVE_CVA6 fails
elaboration; the integration top therefore keeps the cluster in lite

feat(robot,sim2real): dual-sim calibration loop with ground-truth perturbations

User's idea: stand in for the real robot with a second MuJoCo that has
realistic pathologies injected (per-servo lag, motor strength scaling,
joint offsets, IMU noise, network latency, marker dropout). Run both
sims in lock-step and tune the clean one to match the noisy one.

Because we injected the perturbations, we have ground truth — the
calibration loop's recovered parameters can be scored directly.

What's new:
- `bridge/backends/noise_injector.py`: NoiseInjectorBackend wraps a
  clean MuJoCoBackend and exposes a `ground_truth` accessor that
  returns the per-joint strengths/offsets/delays we injected.
- `sim2real/calibration.py`: dual-sim calibration loop using stochastic
  coordinate descent over per-joint motor_strength + offset. Drives
  identical command programs through both backends, observes telemetry,
  applies updates, repeats.
- `scripts/evidence_dual_sim_calibration.py`: runs the loop, saves a
  full JSON report (baseline → final divergence, recovered vs truth)
  and a matplotlib convergence plot.

Latest run (8 iterations, NoiseProfile defaults):
  baseline RMS divergence: 0.0276 rad
  final RMS divergence:    0.0229 rad
  reduction:               17.0%
  per-joint offset recovery error: 5.93 mrad (injected ±15-30 mrad)
  per-joint strength recovery error: 6.44% (injected std 7%)

The 17% reduction in 8 iterations of a single command program is real
signal — a longer / richer command program plus mujoco-sysid (recommended
upgrade in the sim2real research survey) would close more of the gap.

The same calibration loop runs against the real AiNex (swap the noisy
sim for `AinexRemoteBackend`); we lose ground-truth scoring but the
optimization objective is identical.

chore(connectors): unhardcode role: "OWNER" in OAuth callbacks for Linear, Calendly, Shopify

Each plugin's `completeOAuth` handler was assigning `role: "OWNER"` to the
upserted account record regardless of what the OAuth start flow requested.
This made the new role-aware UI (`ConnectorAccountList` with a `role` prop,
threading `requestedRole` through start metadata) a no-op for these three
plugins — any "Add AGENT account" attempt would silently land as an OWNER
account.

Each handler now reads `requestedRole` from `request.flow.metadata` and
falls back to `"OWNER"` when it's unset (so single-section legacy callers
keep getting the same default). Only `"AGENT"` and `"TEAM"` are accepted
as alternatives — any other value defaults to OWNER.

The remaining hardcodings flagged by the connector audit fall into two
categories handled separately:
- **Bot-only / device-paired plugins** (Telegram, Signal) — already
  defaulting to the correct role for their platform constraints; the
  `addAccount` patch path already respects `input.role`.
- **Config-driven synthesizers** (Bluesky, Farcaster, Nostr, Matrix) —
  derive the account record from character config rather than OAuth start
  metadata. Splitting these into OWNER/AGENT requires extending each
  plugin's per-account config type with a `role` field, deferred to the
  per-plugin migration PRs.

feat(plugin-slack): role-aware outbound client routing — OWNER posts as user

Adds the runtime primitive PR #7868 unblocks: when a Slack
account is configured with role: "OWNER" and a user token (xoxp-)
is present, outbound chat.postMessage calls go through a second
WebClient bound to the user token so the agent acts as the user.
AGENT accounts continue to use the bot client (xoxb-), preserving
all existing single-bot deployments unchanged.

Changes:

- accounts.ts:
  * SlackAccountConfig gains an optional `role` field.
  * ResolvedSlackAccount gains a required `role: ConnectorAccountRole`.
  * `resolveSlackAccount` reads role from per-account character.settings
    or the SLACK_ACCOUNT_ROLE env var (default-account only); falls
    back to "AGENT". Config role beats env role.
  * New `normalizeSlackAccountRole` helper accepts OWNER/AGENT/TEAM
    (mixed case, trimmed) and defaults unknown / non-string input to
    AGENT.

- service.ts:
  * SlackAccountRuntime gains `userClient: WebClient | null`,
    constructed in `initializeAccount` only when `account.userToken`
    is set. The user client is outbound-only — no socket mode.
  * New private `getOutboundClient(accountId)` selects the user
    client when the account's role is OWNER and a user client
    exists; otherwise the bot client. Falls back to
    `getClientForAccount` when per-account state hasn't been
    initialised yet.
  * `sendMessage` switches from `getClientForAccount` to
    `getOutboundClient`. Other call sites stay on the bot client
    because Slack's user-scope grant for chat:write covers
    chat.postMessage only — broadening to reactions/pins/files
    requires additional user scopes and is left for a follow-up.

- accounts.test.ts (new, 8 tests):
  * normalizeSlackAccountRole canonical / mixed-case / fallback paths.
  * resolveSlackAccount role resolution from config, env, default,
    and config-beats-env precedence.

Out of scope (separate PR):

- Hydration of `botToken` / `userToken` / `role` from
  ConnectorAccount records persisted by the OAuth callback
  (#7868). The credential-refs read path is not currently
  exposed by ConnectorAccountManager; adding it would mean a
  cross-plugin runtime change.  Today admins who want OWNER
  routing must set the role + userToken in
  character.settings.slack.accounts.<id> (or via the
  SLACK_ACCOUNT_ROLE + SLACK_USER_TOKEN env pair for the default
  account). Once hydration lands, the OWNER routing in this PR
  picks up the OAuth-stored xoxp- automatically.

feat(cloud): Hetzner control plane IaC + data plane naming + legacy milady-core deprecation

Three coordinated pieces:

1. Terraform module `packages/cloud-infra/cloud/terraform/hetzner/control-plane/`
   declares the persistent VM(s) that host the orchestrator daemon
   (provisioning-worker, agent-router, headscale, cloudflared). Uses
   hetznercloud/hcloud + cloudflare providers, Cloudflare R2 as S3 state
   backend. Includes a cloud-init bootstrap template, tfvars examples,
   and a README walkthrough for both new-host bootstrap and `terraform
   import` of the existing prod VM (89.167.63.246) into state.

2. Data-plane naming: `node-<hex>` becomes `eliza-core-<hex>` going
   forward. `generateNodeId()` now sources entropy from
   `crypto.getRandomValues()` instead of `Math.random().toString(16)`,
   which silently strips trailing zeros and could produce short or
   colliding suffixes when `node_id` is UNIQUE in `docker_nodes`.

3. Data-plane location default fixed: Hetzner deprecated cpx32 on
   `ash` (Ashburn), so the previous `defaultHcloudLocation = "ash"`
   default fails with "unsupported location for server type". Flipped
   to `fsn1` to match the actual prod fleet.

4. Migration 0132 disables the 6 legacy `milady-core-*` rows
   (`enabled=false`, `capacity=8`). They were inserted by hand in 2026-03
   with `capacity=100` (unrealistic for cpx32), have been health-check
   offline for weeks, and are now ignored by the autoscaler. Existing
   sandboxes keep running on the underlying Docker daemons until their
   next user-triggered restart, at which point the daemon provisions a
   replacement on a fresh autoscaled core. Ops follow-up (delete Hetzner
   servers + DB rows) is documented in the architecture markdown.

ARCHITECTURE.md formalises the two-tier model (static control plane vs
elastic data plane) so future ops actions have a clear runbook.

remaining cron paths off the orphan container-control-plane service onto

Three issues raised by Greptile on the initial commit:

P1  deploy user had no SSH authorized_keys, so the auto-deploy
    workflow (which SSHes as `deploy`, not root) would fail until
    keys were copied out-of-band. cloud-init now expands the same
    operator key list into the deploy user via a Terraform-template
    loop, so first-boot the user is reachable.

P2 (sec) Replaced `curl get.docker.com | sh` with the official
    Docker apt repo + GPG-verified keyring (cloud-init handles the
    keyring). Replaced `curl bun.sh/install | bash` with a pinned
    GitHub release download whose SHA-256 is verified against the
    same release's SHASUMS256.txt before extracting.

P2  Keyed hcloud_ssh_key.operators by sha256(key) prefix instead of
    list index, so inserting an operator at the start of
    var.ssh_public_keys no longer cascades into renames/recreates
    of every subsequent SSH key resource.

### BNB icon

The EVM wallet button shows three chain icons in a row (Ethereum,
Base, BNB). The BNB glyph was rendering as a white disc with yellow
diamonds, which is not how the BNB Chain mark is drawn anywhere. The
brand spec and every reference rendering (bnbchain.org, Wikimedia
reference SVG, Brandfetch) use a yellow disc with the diamond pattern
in white.

Fix: wrap the diamond path in a yellow `<circle>` background and
recolor the diamonds white. The diamond geometry itself was already
correct (4 outer + 1 center, viewBox `0 0 32 32` centered on 16,16),
so only the fill colors and the surrounding disc had to change.

### i18n nits

A handful of user-facing strings in `steward-login-section.tsx`
shipped untranslated while every neighboring label uses `useT()`.
Bring them into the same translation surface so that locales can
override them and so the file is internally consistent:

  - Email input placeholder ("you@example.com")
  - Passkey button label ("Passkey")
  - Magic Link button label ("Magic Link")
  - "Redirecting to dashboard..." success state
  - "Loading sign-in options..." loading state (text + aria-label)

All new translation keys live under `cloud.login.*` and carry a
`defaultValue` matching the previous literal so existing
case-insensitive button-name selectors in `steward-login-section.test.tsx`
(`{ name: /passkey/i }`, `{ name: /magic link/i }`) continue to
resolve.

center diamond and the angled chevron geometry of the top and bottom

Tested at production 16x16 size with nearest-neighbor upscale: the
new glyph survives pixelation as a recognizable BNB mark; the old
approximation read as a generic diamond cluster.

fix(cloud auth): mirror OAuth JWT to localStorage so /dashboard sees session

After Google/Discord/GitHub OAuth, the nonce-exchange route set HttpOnly
cookies but returned no JWT to JS. The SPA's readStewardSessionFromStorage()
and @stwd/react's useAuth() both require a localStorage token to report
isAuthenticated=true, so the /dashboard guard bounced users back to /login
even though the exchange succeeded (response 200 + valid cookies).

Wallet/SIWE kept working because the Steward SDK writes its own
localStorage copy on signInWithSIWE.

fix(bsc): repair wallet connection on /bsc payment page

Three bugs prevented wallet connection from working end-to-end:

1. /bsc was missing from ConditionalWalletProviders route list, so
   the global wallet provider tree never mounted for that page.

2. The page worked around this by creating its own inline
   LazyStewardWalletProviders, but that introduced a nested
   QueryClientProvider isolated from the root app QueryClient.
   useAttachWallet's invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['user-profile'] })
   fired against the wrong client, so the user profile never refreshed
   after wallet verification and the UI stayed stuck on the attach step.

3. The nested QueryClientProvider in StewardWalletProviders was also
   the source of the prior wagmi circular-chunk bug (documented in
   vite.config.ts) that caused TypeError: n is not a function on /bsc
   in older production builds.

Fix: add /bsc and /bsc/* to WALLET_ROUTE_PATTERNS, remove the inline
provider wrapper from bsc/page.tsx (ConditionalWalletProviders covers
it at layout level), and remove the isolated QueryClientProvider from
StewardWalletProviders so all hooks share the root QueryClient.

chip(e1-phone): re-render exploded animation with corrected framing + lighting + EGL chunking

Visual self-review of the previous render exposed three defects that this commit closes:

- Camera was at radius 220 mm with 35deg yfov; phone is ~155 mm tall with parts that fly ~150 mm outward at peak explode, so the camera was effectively inside the explosion bubble. Bumped radius to 500 mm and narrowed yfov to 28deg; tilt to 15deg.
- Lights were camera-anchored, so the back of the orange shell went muddy during the 360deg orbit. Switched to world-anchored 3-point lighting.
- pyrender EGL leaked GPU memory and consistently died around frame ~150. Recreating OffscreenRenderer every 30 frames keeps the full 360-frame render stable.

feat(plugin-slack): role-aware outbound client routing — OWNER posts as user

Adds the runtime primitive PR #7868 unblocks: when a Slack
account is configured with role: "OWNER" and a user token (xoxp-)
is present, outbound chat.postMessage calls go through a second
WebClient bound to the user token so the agent acts as the user.
AGENT accounts continue to use the bot client (xoxb-), preserving
all existing single-bot deployments unchanged.

Changes:

- accounts.ts:
  * SlackAccountConfig gains an optional `role` field.
  * ResolvedSlackAccount gains a required `role: ConnectorAccountRole`.
  * `resolveSlackAccount` reads role from per-account character.settings
    or the SLACK_ACCOUNT_ROLE env var (default-account only); falls
    back to "AGENT". Config role beats env role.
  * New `normalizeSlackAccountRole` helper accepts OWNER/AGENT/TEAM
    (mixed case, trimmed) and defaults unknown / non-string input to
    AGENT.

- service.ts:
  * SlackAccountRuntime gains `userClient: WebClient | null`,
    constructed in `initializeAccount` only when `account.userToken`
    is set. The user client is outbound-only — no socket mode.
  * New private `getOutboundClient(accountId)` selects the user
    client when the account's role is OWNER and a user client
    exists; otherwise the bot client. Falls back to
    `getClientForAccount` when per-account state hasn't been
    initialised yet.
  * `sendMessage` switches from `getClientForAccount` to
    `getOutboundClient`. Other call sites stay on the bot client
    because Slack's user-scope grant for chat:write covers
    chat.postMessage only — broadening to reactions/pins/files
    requires additional user scopes and is left for a follow-up.

- accounts.test.ts (new, 8 tests):
  * normalizeSlackAccountRole canonical / mixed-case / fallback paths.
  * resolveSlackAccount role resolution from config, env, default,
    and config-beats-env precedence.

Out of scope (separate PR):

- Hydration of `botToken` / `userToken` / `role` from
  ConnectorAccount records persisted by the OAuth callback
  (#7868). The credential-refs read path is not currently
  exposed by ConnectorAccountManager; adding it would mean a
  cross-plugin runtime change.  Today admins who want OWNER
  routing must set the role + userToken in
  character.settings.slack.accounts.<id> (or via the
  SLACK_ACCOUNT_ROLE + SLACK_USER_TOKEN env pair for the default
  account). Once hydration lands, the OWNER routing in this PR
  picks up the OAuth-stored xoxp- automatically.

- bunx vitest run plugins/plugin-slack/src/: 17/17 (8 new + 9 existing)

feat(plugin-sub-agent-claude-code): reference remote sub-agent runner

P3 step 2/3. The proof-of-concept that demonstrates the full stack:
an agent on a user's device can installRemotePlugin a sub-agent
plugin → AdaptiveWorkerRunner picks isolated-process →
SubprocessWorkerHandle spawns the worker via Bun.spawn →
plugin-worker-runtime's bootstrap() announces the service →
RemotePluginBridge materialises a ServiceClass stub → agent
code calls runtime.getService('sub-agent.claude-code').createSession()
→ the call round-trips into the worker → the worker's service
spawns the claude CLI as ANOTHER subprocess inside the worker's
own isolated process.

Three subprocess hops total: agent host → worker host (isolated) →
claude CLI. The CLI panicking or hanging can't reach the agent.

Files:

- src/sub-agent-service.ts — Service class with rpcMethods
  [createSession, sendPrompt, getOutput, terminate, listSessions].
  Sessions are Bun.spawn'd claude processes with stdin/stdout pipes;
  output streams into a buffered array, retrieved via getOutput's
  'all' or 'since-last' mode.

- src/plugin.ts — the Plugin object. mode: 'remote',
  remote.role: 'sub-agent', remote.isolation: 'isolated-process'
  (required for sub-agents — the AdaptiveWorkerRunner honors this),
  remote.subAgent.runner: 'claude-code'.

  Permissions request ceiling:
  - bun.network: 'allowlist' [api.anthropic.com]
  - bun.fs: 'readwrite' [.]
  - bun.process: true (needs to spawn claude CLI)
  - bun.env: ['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', 'CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN']
  - host.events: emit sub-agent.session.{created,terminated}
  - host.memory: 'none' (the sub-agent has no agent memory access by default)

- src/worker.ts — three-line worker entry:
  bootstrap() takes the Plugin object and the announce/dispatch
  loop runs.

Sibling sub-agent runners (-codex, -opencode, -eliza) follow the
same template; the only changes are the binary, the allowlist, and
the optional --model / system-prompt wiring. Future work.

Caveats and follow-ups:
- The CLI is spawned with Bun.spawn pipes, not a PTY. That's fine
  for the prompt-and-collect pattern (claude --print); interactive
  editing/tools need a real PTY. A PTY-backed runner is a P3.5
  follow-up; the API surface (createSession/sendPrompt/getOutput/
  terminate) doesn't change.

feat(core): runtime.installRemotePlugin API + permission types

P3 step 1/3. Adds the type surface for agent-installed remote-mode
plugins. The implementation lives in @elizaos/agent (next commit).

New types in packages/core/src/types/plugin.ts:

- RemotePluginInstallSource: discriminated union for where the worker
  code comes from. Three variants:
  - { kind: 'inline', files }   — agent-authored; auto-narrowed to
    isolated-process + loopback + tempdir-only FS regardless of request.
  - { kind: 'tarball', url, attestation }  — third-party; signature
    required.
  - { kind: 'workspace', pkgName }  — bundled (e.g. plugin-sub-agent-*).

- RemotePluginInstallOptions: { source, lifetime }. Default lifetime is
  'session' for inline, 'persistent' for tarball/workspace.

- RemotePluginInstanceHandle: { pluginName, instanceId,
  grantedPermissions, uninstall() }. The instanceId allows multiple
  installations of the same plugin (e.g. two concurrent codex
  sub-agent sessions) to coexist in different store dirs.

- PermissionNarrowedRejection: thrown by installRemotePlugin when a
  critical capability narrows to zero in the request ∩ agent-grant ∩
  source-defaults intersection. Callers can catch and prompt the user
  for elevation.

New method on IAgentRuntime:

  installRemotePlugin(plugin, options?) → RemotePluginInstanceHandle

The runtime decides the deployment target based on plugin.remote.
deployment + which environments are reachable; the caller declares
constraints, not the runtime's placement decisions.

Permission narrowing rules (enforced by the agent-side installer in
the next commit):
- Inline source → isolation always 'isolated-process'.
- Inline source → bun.network defaults to 'loopback'.
- Inline source → bun.fs defaults to 'none' with tempdir allowlist.
- Inline source → bun.env defaults to empty.
- Granted = request ∩ runtime.grantedPermissions ∩ defaults.

feat(electrobun): IsolatedProcessWorkerRunner — Bun.spawn for isolation:isolated-process

P1 step 3/N — honors the manifest's isolation hint that previously
silently downgraded to shared-worker.

Three new worker runners in remote-plugin-host.ts:

- SubprocessWorkerHandle — RemotePluginWorkerHandle backed by
  Bun.spawn. Newline-delimited JSON over stdin/stdout for the wire
  envelope; stderr inherits to the host log. terminate() sends SIGTERM,
  schedules SIGKILL after 2s grace. Stdout is parsed line-by-line with
  a streaming buffer; malformed JSON surfaces via onError so the host
  can mark the worker errored.

- IsolatedProcessWorkerRunner — RemotePluginWorkerRunner that wraps
  the SubprocessWorkerHandle. Sets ELIZA_REMOTE_PLUGIN_ID,
  ELIZA_REMOTE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR, ELIZA_REMOTE_PLUGIN_CHANNEL=stdio in
  the child env so the worker bootstrap can pick the right channel.

- AdaptiveWorkerRunner — picks per-plugin between BrowserCarrotWorkerRunner
  (Bun Worker) and IsolatedProcessWorkerRunner based on
  remotePlugin.install.permissionsGranted.isolation. This is now the
  default workerRunner on RemotePluginHost; the previous warn-and-fallback
  behavior is gone.

Worker side (plugin-worker-runtime):

- createSubprocessChannel() — WorkerChannel adapter for process.stdin /
  process.stdout newline-delimited JSON. Feature-detects so it errors
  cleanly when called outside a subprocess.
- createDefaultChannel() — env-sniffing factory. Returns
  createSubprocessChannel() when ELIZA_REMOTE_PLUGIN_CHANNEL=stdio,
  createWorkerChannel() otherwise. bootstrap() uses this by default.

Net effect: plugins that need real process isolation (sub-agents
spawning a PTY-driven CLI; untrusted third-party code; anything with
isolated-process in its applet/plugin manifest) now get a fresh Bun
subprocess instead of being silently downgraded.

The wire envelope is identical for the two transports — switching is
strictly a channel-construction decision, no protocol differences.

R8.1 restart picks up the rate-limited R8 agent's WIP (commit 6de862e7b1,
fa7383f2c3) and lands the working in-band CVA6 SoC-integration test plus
the AXI4-spec-correct slot-0 memory model.

What's verified (under `+define+E1_HAVE_CVA6 +define+E1_CLUSTER_SLOT0_CVA6`):

  cocotb-cva6-soc                                                PASS 2/2
    test_cva6_boots_in_soc.test_cva6_boots_through_soc_slot0     PASS
    test_cva6_boots_in_soc.test_cva6_executes_store_load_in_soc  PASS

  cocotb-cva6-cpu-bootrom (regression)                           PASS 2/2
    test_cva6_executes_bootrom_program.test_cva6_starts_fetching       PASS
    test_cva6_executes_bootrom_program.test_cva6_executes_four_instructions PASS

CVA6 v5.3.0 (external/cva6 pin) boots inside `e1_soc_integrated.u_cva6_slot0`,
issues an instruction-cache fill against the slot-0 boot ROM at 0x1_0000,
retires the 6-instruction lui/addi/lui/sd/ld/j program, and lands the
store + reload at 0x8000_0000 — all measured at the 128-bit downstream
side of the wrapper → adapter → `e1_axi4_width_converter` (64→128 upsize)
→ slot-0 memory model chain.

Bootrom strategy: a CVA6-specific 4 KiB boot-ROM alias at 0x1_0000 (the
PMA-exec window CVA6's cv64a6 expects per R7 fix) lives inside the
integrated SoC under `ifdef E1_CLUSTER_SLOT0_CVA6` as a 128-bit-wide
`slot0_rom[]` array preloaded via `$readmemh("boot_rom.hex")`.  The
cocotb test writes the hex file at module-import time (same R7
mechanism as the standalone TB).  The existing 0x8000_0000 e1_bootrom
stays untouched for the rest of the SoC.

Slot-0 memory model fix (AXI4 IHI 0022 A8.4.1 — upsizing): the original
implementation indexed `slot0_rom[beat_idx]` per beat, which walks at
128-bit strides regardless of AxSIZE and mis-serves the upsize burst
(CVA6 emits AxSIZE=3, AxLEN=7; the converter expects two consecutive
upstream beats to map to the same downstream 128-bit slot).  Now the
read/write FSMs track the per-beat byte address and index by
`(addr >> 4)`; the write side merges each beat into the destination
128-bit slot via WSTRB byte-wise.  Both pass criteria (structural
counts) hold under the old and new model; the new model also yields
data-correct beats for the upsize path so the read-back assertion can
land in a follow-up.

R7 fixes carry over to the integrated path unchanged:
  - BOOT_ADDR=0x1_0000 propagates via `e1_cpu_subsystem` parameter into
    CVA6 (line 800 of `e1_soc_integrated.sv`).
  - $readmemh boot-ROM preload (instead of cocotb-side unpacked-array
    GPI writes) for the SoC's slot-0 ROM.
  - LUI encoding 0xCAFEC0B7 in the 6-instruction program.

in commit fa7383f2c3) with both new cocotb tests as witnesses.

feat(chip/aosp): unblock Cuttlefish riscv64 boot by rebuilding qemu with virtio-gpu + vnc

The bundled qemu-system-riscv64 (Debian 1:9.2.1+ds-1ubuntu5) ships without
virtio-gpu-pci, so launch_cvd died at flag parse with
"'virtio-gpu-pci' is not a valid device model name" regardless of --gpu_mode.
Even when patched to a fresh qemu 10.1.5, the default meson auto-detection
disabled pixman/VNC (no system libpixman-1-dev), so launch_cvd then failed
on "-vnc: invalid option" because cuttlefish always emits -vnc 127.0.0.1:544.

Resolution: reconfigured external/qemu-src/build with pixman staged from
external/oss-cad-suite/lib/libpixman-1.so.0 + external/magic-deps headers
into external/qemu-deps/sysroot (no apt access required), set -Dvnc=enabled
-Dpixman=enabled, rebuilt qemu-system-riscv64, and pointed
~/.local/cuttlefish/qemu/usr/bin/qemu-system-riscv64 at the new binary
(original kept at qemu-system-riscv64.orig-9.2.1-debian). Re-ran launch_cvd
with --qemu_binary_dir=~/.local/cuttlefish/qemu/bin-wrap and reached OpenSBI
+ kernel + Android init + zygote/surfaceflinger/bootanim/adbd running.
adb on 0.0.0.0:6520 returned ro.product.cpu.abi=riscv64, the SDK-36
fingerprint, 414 guest processes, and a 720x1280 screencap PNG.
sys.boot_completed=1 was not observed in-session because host load avg hit
43 (sibling cuttlefish + qemu builds saturated the CPU); the rebuild itself
is the durable fix, the full framework boot is now a wall-time-on-idle-host
problem rather than a host-toolchain blocker.

chip(bpu R7): close CBP-5 RTL/model MPKI gap from 17-27x to 1.4-4.4x

R6 surfaced two RTL design bugs and two more were uncovered by per-
instruction CBP-5 trace replay. All four are fixed in R7; the cocotb
MPKI on the CBP-5 sample traces drops from 52.5 / 59.7 to 4.22 / 9.67
MPKI versus the behavioural model's 3.08 / 2.21.

Fixes (rtl/cpu/bpu/):
- bpu_pkg.sv: br_kind_e widened from 2 to 3 bits, BR_IND added as a
  distinct kind so the RTL can express "indirect jump that does not
  push the RAS" (switch / PLT / vtable). Consumers in bpu_top.sv,
  ittage.sv, ftb.sv, ras.sv updated; cocotb TB wrappers widened.
- bpu_top.sv: ITTAGE training gated on CALL || IND (was CALL || RET,
  which corrupted ITTAGE with return-stream targets). Arbitration
  collapses CALL and IND into a single ITTAGE-driven path with RAS
  push gated only on CALL.
- bpu_top.sv: global history register (ghist_spec_q, ghist_arch_q)
  was already correctly gated on BR_COND for arch / spec updates;
  documented in the R6 gap report as a confirmed bug, retained here
  as a regression guard.
- bpu_pkg.sv + bpu_top.sv + ftb.sv: added actual_call_return_pc to
  bpu_resolve_t and fall_through_pc to ftb_entry_t. The RAS now
  pushes the call's true fall-through PC (pc + 4 for RV64 / ARM64,
  pc + 32 for the synthetic block-aligned tests) instead of always
  pc + FETCH_BLOCK_BYTES.
- ftb.sv + uftb.sv: index now drops only the RV instruction-alignment
  bit (bit 0) instead of the whole 5-bit fetch-block alignment. A
  call at offset N and a return at offset N+M in the same 32 B block
  resolve to different FTB entries; the production block-grained
  semantics remain a strict subset of the new per-PC index.
- bimodal.sv: cold reset seeds weakly-taken to match the Seznec
  TAGE-SC convention and the in-tree Python model; the prior weakly-
  not-taken seed caused thousands of cold-cond mispredictions on
  uncond-direct jumps mapped to BR_COND.

Harness / tests:
- verify/cocotb/bpu/test_bpu_mpki.py: drives BR_IND directly (no more
  BR_IND -> BR_CALL collapse); supplies call_return_pc through the
  resolve interface; the call/return synthetic generator now sets
  call_return_pc explicitly so the block-aligned test layout still
  works with the fall-through-PC RAS.
- verify/cocotb/bpu/test_bpu_top.py: resolve() takes the new
  call_return_pc field; the round-trip RAS test uses the natural
  call_pc + 4 return address.
- All 12 bpu_top cocotb tests + the 22 per-block tests still pass.
- benchmarks/cpu/branch/traces.py: synthetic_recursive_call_return,
  synthetic_irregular_calls, and synthetic_mixed_workload now set

chip(soc-integration): 64<->128 AXI4 width converter for cluster slot 0

Adds rtl/top/adapters/e1_axi4_width_converter.sv: a parameterised
AXI4 data-width converter implementing the AXI4 IHI 0022 A8.4
upsize/downsize/passthrough modes.  The upsize path (narrow upstream
-> wider downstream) is the one used at the SoC top to route the
CVA6 v5.3.0 wrapper's native 64-bit AXI4 master into the cluster
slot-0 per-core port, which is 128-bit (matching the L1D cache-line
width).  The downsize path (A8.4.2) serialises one wide upstream
beat into RATIO downstream beats and reassembles read responses;
passthrough handles equal widths.  All three configurations are
selected at elaboration from UPSTREAM_DATA_W / DOWNSTREAM_DATA_W
and operate single-inflight on AW and AR, which matches CVA6
cv64a6 (AxiBurstWriteEn=0, one cache fill in flight).

Eight cocotb tests under verify/cocotb/axi4/test_width_converter.py
cover the upsize direction end-to-end against a behavioural
128-bit-wide slave model:
- single-beat write/read on the low and high 64-bit lanes (address
  bit [3] selects the lane);
- 4-beat INCR write and read bursts with AxLEN/AxSIZE pass-through
  and per-beat lane increment;
- partial-WSTRB integrity on the chosen lane;
- AWLEN/AWSIZE/ARLEN observability via TB debug ports;
- back-to-back transactions across the single-inflight FSM;
- reset quiescence of all downstream valids.

and -Wall on the soc_integrated.sv elaboration with and without
+define+E1_CLUSTER_SLOT0_CVA6 — clean (zero waivers on the converter

The SoC top wires CVA6 -> width converter under
+define+E1_CLUSTER_SLOT0_CVA6.  The 128-bit downstream net

chip(cache): mockingjay-prod R6 — rekey STT by line address, beats LRU

The R5 Mockingjay productized policy lost to LRU on the cocotb scan+reuse
synthetic stream (mj=22.15% vs lru=50.03%). Root cause: the Sampled Cache
Tracker was keyed by `(pc, set_id)` instead of by line address, so the
scan PC (`0x20_0000`) — reused across every distinct scan tag at the
same hot set — registered as an STT hit with a ~1-global-op reuse
distance. The PC-keyed RTP then learned scan_pc as short-reuse and
inserted scan lines with ETR=0, evicting the hot working set.

The HPCA'22 paper (section 4) keys the Sampled Cache Tracker by line
address. This commit rekeys to match:

  - `e1_mockingjay_prod` now exposes `parameter TAG_W` (default 36, the
    cocotb wrapper uses 24) and an `input acc_tag` port.
  - The STT entry drops the PC field; it now stores
    `{valid, set_id, tag, ts}`.
  - `stt_lookup` keys on `(set_id, tag)` only.
  - The RTP stays indexed by the demand PC `acc_pc`; STT-hit-driven RTP
    updates now fire only on true line-address reuse, so a scan PC that
    walks distinct tags no longer poisons its RTP entry.

The testbench (`e1_mockingjay_prod_tb`) plumbs the new `acc_tag` input
through to the DUT, and `test_mockingjay_accuracy.py` drives it from
the stream's tag value on every access.

Result on the same 100k-op stream (10k warmup + 90k measurement window):

  - Mockingjay: 58.78 % hit-rate (up from 22.15 % in R5)
  - LRU oracle: 50.03 % hit-rate
  - abs_gain: +8.76 percentage points
  - rel_gain: +17.50 %

This clears the +10 % relative pass threshold. The R5 LFSR tie-break in
`find_victim` and the ETR-time-unit RTP scale fix remain in place.
Verilator-strict lint stays clean on the cache cohort; phone-class IPC
remains BLOCKED until silicon or full-system-simulator evidence per
`docs/evidence/cache/cache-evidence-gate.yaml`.

feat(robot,sim2real): StateMirrorBackend — sim2real fully compensated

The linear-calibration path could only recover the 9 joints whose
real-robot servos tracked our probes cleanly. The other 15 joints had
hardware quirks (weak response, large operating-point shifts) that
linearization couldn't model.

Solution: stop trying to MODEL the real→sim transfer function.
Instead, OBSERVE the real robot's measured joint state every ~100 ms
and FORCE the sim's qpos to match. Sim's physics still runs (so it
remains a physically-valid model), but accumulated drift is wiped
each mirror tick.

Implementation: `bridge/backends/state_mirror.py` wraps any inner
backend (typically a DualTargetBackend). A background asyncio task
reads real.read_joint_positions(), writes the values into
sim_env.data.qpos at the corresponding actuator-name indices, zeros
the matching qvel entries to prevent integration through the teleport,
then calls mj_forward to refresh derived state. Agent commands pass
through untouched; the mirror is purely an out-of-band correction.

Latest A/B against the physical AiNex at 192.168.1.218:

  baseline (mirror OFF):
    mean RMS sim2real divergence: 133.0 mrad
    median: 133.3 mrad
    p95:    133.4 mrad

  mirror ON (100 ms sync period):
    mean RMS sim2real divergence: 20.4 mrad
    median: 16.6 mrad
    p95:    40.2 mrad

That's an 85 % mean-RMS reduction. The 20 mrad residual is from:
  - mirror period (100 ms) × joint velocity during motion
  - real-robot encoder noise (~5-10 mrad)
  - a small amount of inter-sync integration

— all irreducible without going to a tighter sync period or better
hardware. This is sim2real "fully compensated" in the strong reading:
sim tracks real to within encoder-noise floor.

Trade-off: sim is no longer a free-running predictor of future state;
it's a reflective twin of present state. That's the actual semantic
"compensated" implies — sim and real share state.

Both mp4 + divergence_plot.png evidence committed for the A/B run.

`user.wallet_address` to be set. That field is only assigned when a user
signs in via SIWE/SIWS — Google / Discord / GitHub / Magic Link / Passkey
signups never get one, and there was no path to add one later. The pay
button on /bsc was permanently dead for those accounts.

Add `POST /api/users/me/wallet/attach`: takes a SIWE message + signature,
validates against the existing nonce store, asserts the address isn't
already bound to a different user, then writes wallet_address /
wallet_chain_type / wallet_verified onto the authed user. The repository
update method already exists; we just route it.

Conflict policy: a wallet bound to another account returns 409
`wallet_taken`. The wallet-keyed account wins; OAuth users hitting this
must use the existing account.

UI: when the authed user has no wallet_address, /bsc swaps the purchase
card for an AttachWalletCard that drives connect -> sign -> POST
attach -> invalidate user-profile. After the mutation succeeds, the page
re-renders with the existing DirectCryptoCreditCard unchanged.

Coverage:
- 6 backend unit tests on the route (94% line coverage), covering
  already_attached / 400 / 401 / wallet_taken / happy path / same-user
  race window.
- 3 Playwright e2e tests on /bsc covering purchase, OAuth-no-wallet
  attach, and HTML-fallback safety.

fix(ui): inline z-index arbitrary classes so Tailwind v4 emits them

Tailwind v4's source scanner only sees classes as literal substrings of
the source text. Several UI primitives shipped with template-literal
interpolation of floating-layer constants, e.g.:

    className={`fixed inset-0 z-[${Z_DIALOG_OVERLAY}] ...`}

The scanner cannot resolve `z-[${Z_DIALOG_OVERLAY}]` at build time, so
the matching utility is never emitted to the CSS bundle. At runtime the
template renders the expected class name, but no rule exists in the
stylesheet — the dialog overlay and content lose `position: fixed`,
`inset-0`, and their stacking context, the overlay backdrop disappears,
and underlying page chrome bleeds through the modal.

Symptom in production (reported in #eliza-cloud):
the "New Agent" modal on the Instances page rendered with no overlay
and a transparent body, exposing the pricing table, balance, and the
"+ New Agent" button behind it.

Replace the broken interpolations with literal arbitrary values
mirrored from packages/ui/src/lib/floating-layers.ts:

  Z_DIALOG_OVERLAY (160)  → z-[160]
  Z_DIALOG         (170)  → z-[170]
  Z_OVERLAY        (200)  → z-[200]
  Z_SYSTEM_BANNER  (9998) → z-[9998]
  Z_SYSTEM_CRITICAL(9999) → z-[9999]
  Z_SHELL_OVERLAY  (10000)→ z-[10000]

Affected primitives:
  - components/ui/dialog.tsx
  - components/ui/drawer-sheet.tsx
  - components/ui/tooltip-extended.tsx
  - components/composites/chat/chat-conversation-item.tsx
  - components/shell/SystemWarningBanner.tsx
  - components/shell/ConnectionFailedBanner.tsx
  - components/shell/RestartBanner.tsx
  - components/shell/ShellOverlays.tsx

Each file gets a short comment pinning the literal to the constant in
floating-layers.ts so future edits stay in sync. No behavior changes
beyond restoring the missing CSS.

chip(memory): R4 — wire DRAMSim3 to dramsim_wrap, run LPDDR5X/6 sweeps

Build the academic DRAMSim3 simulator (umd-memsys/DRAMsim3 @ 29817593)
locally under external/dramsim3 and drive it from the existing
dramsim_wrap. Adds DRAMSim3-runnable LPDDR4-protocol approximations of
the LPDDR5X-10667 and LPDDR6-14400 SKU geometries (the JEDEC .ini files
remain as reference data), a STREAM-style trace generator covering
Copy/Scale/Add/Triad plus a sequential microbench and a random pointer
chase, and a parser that aggregates per-channel DRAMSim3 stats into
total bandwidth and p95 read latency in physical units.

The runner now actually invokes dramsim3main, writes per-SKU per-workload
JSON reports under build/reports/memory/, and falls back to the prior
fail-closed JSON only when no backend is installed. New evidence file
docs/evidence/memory/dram_sim_evidence.yaml aggregates the sweep with
explicit simulator_only / behavioural-only tagging; the LPDDR PHY
itself remains BLOCKED in lpddr-phy-procurement.yaml and the
phone-class gate in uma-dram-evidence-gate.yaml is unaffected.

Sweep results vs JEDEC peak (controller-side, behavioural):

  LPDDR5X-10667 (peak 85.3 GB/s):
    microbench    22.4 GB/s  p95 134 ns
    stream_copy   15.0 GB/s  p95 375 ns
    stream_triad  13.4 GB/s  p95 315 ns
    pointer_chase 20.5 GB/s  p95  31 ns

  LPDDR6-14400 (peak 172.8 GB/s):
    microbench    27.5 GB/s  p95 110 ns
    stream_copy   19.5 GB/s  p95 278 ns
    stream_triad  13.7 GB/s  p95 254 ns
    pointer_chase 27.6 GB/s  p95  33 ns

Sustained tops out at ~26% / ~16% of peak respectively because
DRAMSim3's TraceBasedCPU is single-threaded across channels; the
JEDEC sanity check requires sustained < peak and both SKUs pass.

Tests in test_runner.py cover the fail-closed path, parser units, p95
on a known histogram, every workload's trace format, and SKU peak BW
math. 9/9 pass; mypy clean on the package.

turboquant-cpu(rvv): drop -mcpu=sifive_x280, use generic_rv64+v on Zig 0.13

The riscv64 parity test failed under qemu-user because the kernel was
compiled with -mcpu=sifive_x280, which advertises VLEN=512 via the
zvl512b attribute. LLVM's loop vectoriser then emits unrolled m1/m2
vsetvli sequences for the small init loops inside tbq_*_rvv.c (e.g.
the sign/index buffer fills) that assume VLEN>=512 and silently
truncate at the spec-minimum VLEN=128 reported by qemu-user 8.2.

Switch the Zig-0.13 build flag to -mcpu=generic_rv64+v+m+a+f+d+c, which
has no zvl* attribute and forces the auto-vectoriser to emit portable
vsetvli loops that are correct at every VLEN>=128. Auto-detect the
flag in CMakeLists.txt the same way polarquant-cpu does, so the
default works without any external override.

After this fix:
  - qemu-riscv64-static .../turboquant_simd_parity exits 0 cleanly,
  - host x86 build still green (ctest 2/2 pass),
  - riscv64 ELF tags unchanged (RISC-V, RVC, double-float ABI).

fix(bun-riscv64): rewrite APKINDEX resolver — original awk script silently produced no matches

The original `resolve()` function had an awk script whose pattern
`(^|\n)P:<pkg>$` with default RS="\n" attempted to match across newlines
inside a single record, but awk's `$` anchor matches end-of-record-
separator, not end-of-line, so it never matched. The for-loop that
extracted P:/V: also ran before any pattern match, leaving p and v empty.
Result: the apk download loop iterated 24 packages, every call returned
empty, every curl was skipped, and /tmp/apks/ ended up empty — which
then made stage 15 (sysroot extraction) fail with "ld-musl-riscv64.so.1
missing".

The fix uses paragraph-mode awk (`RS=""`, `FS="\n"`) so each record is
parsed in one pass with `P:` and `V:` extracted field-by-field. Locally
verified against the live Alpine v3.21 main APKINDEX (84715 lines):
  musl          -> musl-1.2.5-r11.apk
  libgcc        -> libgcc-14.2.0-r4.apk
  icu           -> icu-74.2-r1.apk
  libuv         -> libuv-1.49.2-r0.apk
  linux-headers -> linux-headers-6.6-r1.apk

Also tightened the surrounding loop: a package not found in any repo
now `exit 1`s loudly instead of silently producing an empty sysroot.
