fix(boot): eliminate top-level-await deadlock that froze cloud Docker boot (#7801)

Diagnosis (full debug session against ghcr.io/elizaos/eliza:sha-6d0c8d5):
Provisioning a fresh sandbox in a cloud Docker container hung silently —
no logs past `[eliza] Generated SECRET_SALT`, PID 1 in `ep_poll`, no listen
on the agent port, daemon scrubbed the container at the 180s health
timeout. Three vault skips (commits 1fc4dd6, e10eb89, 6d0c8d5) moved boot
past `runVaultBootstrap`, `vault-profile-resolver`, and
`ensureAgentWallets`, but the next call to `await importAppCoreRuntime()`
(= `import("@elizaos/app-core/agent-bridge")`) still deadlocked.

By instrumenting the dist files in a running container we narrowed the
hang to two distinct sources:

1. `app-core/services/account-pool.ts` did a static `import "@elizaos/agent"`
   (barrel). Loading the agent barrel started evaluating
   `packages/agent/dist/api/index.js`, which had FOUR top-level awaits
   loading platform plugins (computeruse, signal, whatsapp, workflow).
   With agent already partially evaluated as the bin.js entrypoint, the
   barrel re-import returned a partial namespace and the TLAs never
   resolved → deadlock at module evaluation.

2. `packages/agent/dist/services/index.js`,
   `services/app-session-gate.js`, and `services/hosted-tools.js` had
   matching TLAs for the same plugins plus plugin-app-manager and
   plugin-elizacloud. Even after `api/index.js` was unblocked, the
   `services/*` modules tripped the same deadlock when any consumer
   walked through them.

Fixes in this commit:

- `packages/agent/src/api/index.ts`: convert the four
  `const x = await import(plugin)` blocks to lazy loaders + async route
  wrappers. Mirrors the existing `loadElizaCloudRoutes` pattern already
  used elsewhere in the same file.
- `packages/agent/src/services/index.ts`: convert the same three
  plugin imports from TLA to static re-exports. The plugins don't have
  side-effectful top-level code, so a plain `export { X } from "plugin"`
  is sufficient and avoids the TLA penalty entirely.
- `packages/agent/src/services/app-session-gate.ts`: replace
  `const { readAppRunStore } = await import(...)` with a static
  `import { readAppRunStore } from "@elizaos/plugin-app-manager"`.
- `packages/agent/src/services/hosted-tools.ts`: same fix for
  `resolveCloudApiBaseUrl` from plugin-elizacloud.
- `packages/agent/package.json`: add `./auth/*` subpath to `exports`
  so consumers can target individual files in `auth/` without pulling
  the entire agent barrel.
- `packages/app-core/src/services/account-pool.ts`: replace the
  `import "@elizaos/agent"` barrel import with three narrow subpath
  imports (`@elizaos/agent/auth/types`,
  `@elizaos/agent/auth/credentials`,
  `@elizaos/agent/auth/account-storage`). Eliminates the barrel
  evaluation that was the root trigger.

Validated by replaying the same patches in a live Docker container and
seeing the agent reach `[eliza-api] Listening on http://127.0.0.1:2138`
within ~60s of `node packages/agent/dist/bin.js start` (vs. 180s timeout
before).

ci(flatpak): commit node-sources.json + flip elizaos-app to --offline (Flathub-ready) (#7802)

* docs(flatpak): point README at automated generate-sources.sh + CI artifact

* fix(flatpak): seed package.json name field in generate-sources.sh

flatpak-node-generator 0.1.1 crashes with KeyError: 'name' when parsing
the root packages[''] entry of the lockfile produced by
'npm install --package-lock-only elizaos@latest', because npm writes a
package.json with only a dependencies block (no name field).

Seed a minimal package.json with name='elizaos-flatpak-sources-shim'
before invoking npm install so the generator can parse the root entry
cleanly and emit the full 1202-entry node-sources.json closure.

Without this fix the CI 'Generate offline node sources' step
continue-on-errors out and the flatpak-node-sources artifact is never
produced — which is exactly the state the workflow was in before this
commit.

* ci(flatpak): commit node-sources.json vendored against elizaos@1.7.2

Generated by ./generate-sources.sh on WSL Ubuntu 24.04 +
flatpak-node-generator 0.1.1 against the current elizaos@latest (1.7.2)
dependency closure. 1202 source records, 691 KB.

This file is the offline-mode counterpart to 'npm install -g elizaos' —
flatpak-builder fetches every listed tarball into flatpak-node/cache/
during the source-prepare phase, and the build phase resolves the
entire dependency tree from that cache with no network access.

The companion test-flatpak.yml workflow regenerates this file on every
CI run and uploads it as the flatpak-node-sources artifact, so the
committed copy can be refreshed by downloading the artifact whenever
the elizaos CLI dependency graph drifts.

* ci(flatpak): flip ai.elizaos.App.yml to offline-mode install

With node-sources.json committed alongside the manifest, the elizaos-app
module can install from the vendored offline cache instead of reaching
registry.npmjs.org during the build phase:

- build-commands now run 'npm install -g --offline --prefix=/app
  --ignore-scripts elizaos' (was: same command minus --offline).
- node-sources.json is added to the module's sources list so
  flatpak-builder fetches every vendored tarball into
  flatpak-node/cache/ before the build runs.
- build-options.build-args: --share=network is removed. The build no
  longer needs network, which is the Flathub submission requirement.
- The long-form comment block above the module — previously a 3-step
  'how to switch to offline-mode' playbook from #7787 — is rewritten as
  a short 'offline-mode enabled' note pointing at the committed
  node-sources.json and the generate-sources.sh refresh path.

After this, the direct manifest matches Flathub's submission
constraints. Next step (separate PR, separate repo): submit to
flathub/flathub for ai.elizaos.App.

* fix(flatpak): use bare-string node-sources.json source so flatpak-builder processes its entries

The previous `type: file` / `path: node-sources.json` source made
flatpak-builder treat the JSON as an opaque file to copy into the
build directory, so it never read the manifest and never populated
`flatpak-node/npm-cache` with the 1202 archive/script entries. As a
result `npm install -g --offline elizaos` would fail with
package-not-found errors and the entire offline build path was broken.

Switching to the bare-string form lets flatpak-builder interpret the
file as a flatpak-node-generator manifest and dispatch its archive,
script, and shell entries individually so the npm tarball cache is
populated before the build step runs.

Greptile P1 from #7802 round 1.

* fix(flatpak): set npm_config_cache so --offline install resolves vendored tarballs

flatpak-node-generator populates the npm cache under
`flatpak-node/npm-cache/` relative to the module build directory
(`/run/build/elizaos-app/` for this module). Without
`npm_config_cache` pointing at that path, npm defaults to `~/.npm`
inside the sandbox — empty — and `npm install -g --offline` fails
with a cache-miss before any vendored tarball is read.

Addresses Greptile round-2 P1 on PR #7802.

feat(cloud): POST /api/v1/apps/[id]/deploy + GET …/deploy/status (#7804)

* chore(cloud-api): fix codegen path separators on Windows

`_generate-router.mjs` was leaving Windows-style backslash separators in
the result of `path.relative()`, which made `split("/")` collapse every
route path to just "/api" when run from a Windows host. Normalize the
relative path to forward slashes in `fileToHttpPaths`, `importIdent`,
and `importPath` so the generator produces the same output regardless of
host OS. No-op on POSIX.

* feat(cloud-shared): app-deployments service

Backs the new `POST /api/v1/apps/:id/deploy` and
`GET /api/v1/apps/:id/deploy/status` routes. The persisted source of
truth is the `apps` table itself — `deployment_status`,
`production_url`, and `last_deployed_at` columns added in migration
0007. A deployment is identified by `<appId>:<last_deployed_at_iso>`
so the CLI can correlate POST → GET polls without a separate
`deployments` table.

Pure helpers (status enum mapping, deployment-id composition) live in
`app-deployments-helpers.ts` so unit tests can import them without
pulling in the Drizzle-backed `appsService` and the rest of the
runtime.

When a real build/upload service (Vercel or otherwise) lands, this
service becomes the integration boundary — callers will not need to
change.

* feat(cloud): POST /api/v1/apps/[id]/deploy + GET …/deploy/status

Completes the cloud half of `elizaos deploy` (PR #7786). The CLI keel
from that PR drives this endpoint pair: build → upload → POST
/deploy → attach domain → poll GET /deploy/status every 5s until
READY or ERROR (10-minute cap on the CLI side).

Both routes follow the existing `apps/[id]/domains/route.ts` pattern
exactly:
- Hono handler with `requireUserOrApiKeyWithOrg(c)` for auth
- 404 when the app does not exist, 403 when the caller is authed but
  not the owning org
- thin wrapper over `appDeploymentsService`; ownership invariant is
  enforced at the route layer (mirrors the domains/managed-domains
  split)

Request schema lives in a sibling `schema.ts` so unit tests can
import it without pulling in the route's `@/lib/*` aliased imports.

Pure-helper tests under `packages/cloud-api/__tests__/` cover:
- empty body acceptance
- full body shape acceptance
- repoUrl / ref / env value validation
- every enum value of the persisted → public status map
- deployment-id composition (with and without `last_deployed_at`)

Route-level happy-path / auth / not-found scenarios are exercised by
the existing e2e suite once `TEST_API_BASE_URL` is set.

* fix(cloud-shared): import AppDeploymentStatus from schema + drop dead QUEUED variant

Greptile P2 cleanup on PR #7804.

`AppDeploymentStatus` was redefined locally in app-deployments-helpers
despite being exported from `db/schemas/apps`, creating silent drift
risk if the persisted enum gained a new value (e.g. "cancelling"). Now
re-exported via a type-only import so Drizzle runtime is not pulled in.

`QUEUED` was in the public `DeploymentStatus` union but no code path
can ever emit it — PERSISTED_TO_PUBLIC only produces BUILDING / READY /
ERROR / DRAFT. Removed from the public contract.

The 3 remaining P2s (double getById, concurrent build race, surfacing
error field) are design-sized and deferred to the follow-up
build-pipeline wiring PR.

* fix(cloud): include startedAt: null in deploy status no-record branch

The non-null record branch always returns `startedAt`, but the
no-record branch omitted it entirely. A typed CLI client that reads
`response.startedAt` unconditionally would receive `undefined` in
the no-prior-deployment case with no TypeScript error at the call
site (plain JSON). Keep the response shape uniform.

Addresses Greptile round-2 P1 on PR #7804.

* fix(cloud): reject POST /deploy with 409 when a build is already in flight

Two concurrent CLI invocations of `elizaos deploy` both went through
unguarded: createDeployment stamped `last_deployed_at` twice, the
loser's `deploymentId` was immediately stale, and its subsequent GET
/status polls would return the winner's record without any signal
that the original POST got co-opted.

Adds `assertDeployable` helper that throws ApiError(409) when the
app's persisted `deployment_status` is already "building".
`createDeployment` calls it after a (cache-hot) `getById`, so the
race surfaces to the caller as a 409 instead of silently overwriting.

This is a check-then-act guard, not a DB-level lock — a fully race-
free path would do a conditional UPDATE in the apps repo. For the
realistic CLI cadence (invocations seconds apart) this is sufficient.

Addresses Greptile round-1 P2 on PR #7804.

feat(training): low-VRAM smoke config for 2b SFT on 12GB consumer GPUs (#7805)

* feat(training): low-VRAM smoke preset for 2b SFT on 12 GB consumer GPUs

The registry default for qwen3.5-2b targets a 16 GB local GPU (seq_len=8192,
budget=15.5 GB). On a 12 GB consumer card (RTX 3060 / 4070 class) that OOMs
at the fp32 logits transient (B*S*V*4 bytes; Qwen vocab=248k makes this
dominant).

The new --low-vram-smoke flag is a CLI preset that overrides the registry
defaults to seq_len=2048, batch=1, grad_accum=16 (effective batch stays at
16), max_samples=1000, epochs=1, memory_budget_gb=11.5. Liger fused
chunked-CE stays on (registry default for 2B) and activation checkpointing
stays on (train_local.py default), which is what makes the budget feasible.

CLI flags the caller passes explicitly still win over the preset; the
override block compares against the argparse-default snapshot captured
before the registry merge, so values that came from the CLI are
distinguishable from values the registry filled in.

The preset is explicitly NOT for publishable runs — it is a path-validation
smoke for the SFT entrypoint on commodity hardware. The resulting
checkpoint should not be pushed as an eliza-1-2b bundle.

Includes:
- scripts/train_local.py: --low-vram-smoke flag + override block
- scripts/test_train_local_low_vram_smoke.py: 6 CPU-only unit tests
  pinning the override semantics (registry interaction, CLI override
  precedence, no-registry-key path, and a regression guard against
  removing the flag without removing the block)
- README.md: "Running on a 12 GB consumer GPU" section documenting the
  invocation, the trade-off (training context window 8k -> 2k, not
  suitable for long-context behaviors), and the OOM-retry path
  (--low-vram-smoke --max-seq-len 1024)

* docs(training): low-VRAM README — measured numbers + kernel prerequisites

Update the "Running on a 12 GB consumer GPU" section with what actually
happens on stock WSL2 / no-toolchain hosts:

- 0.8B is the realistic tier on 12 GB. Document it as the recommended
  invocation; 2B is feasible only with Liger + flash-linear-attention
  kernels live.
- Spell out the kernel prerequisites: Liger needs Triton (gcc +
  python3.x-dev + CUDA toolkit); flash-linear-attention is a separate
  Triton path for the Qwen3.5 hybrid linear-attn layers. Without either,
  HF defaults are used and the 248k-vocab fp32 logits transient plus the
  pure-PyTorch linear-attn fallback push the 2B-on-12 GB run past the
  budget and/or below useful throughput.
- Add the --preflight-only recipe as the lightweight way to verify
  preset wiring + dataset format without loading model weights.
- Add a measurement table covering preflight + load + first backward
  peak VRAM on RTX 3060. Both 0.8B and 2B preflight ok; both saturate
  at ~12 GB during the first backward without Liger.
- OOM-fallback ladder updated to --max-seq-len 1024 / 768 and to prefer
  the 0.8B tier when toolchain installs aren't available.

Numbers measured against torch 2.12.0+cu130 on a Windows 10 IoT host
running WSL2 Ubuntu; the venv has transformers 5.8.1 / accelerate /
peft / trl / apollo-torch / liger-kernel installed but no system
gcc/python3-dev/CUDA toolkit, so Triton cannot JIT and Liger falls
back at startup (logged by train_local.py).

* fix(training): use None sentinels so --low-vram-smoke respects CLI defaults-equal values

The previous `_defaults_at_parse` snapshot compared each parsed value to
`ap.get_default(dest)` to decide "user didn't pass it". That dies as soon
as the caller explicitly passes the same value as the argparse default:

    --epochs 3.0 --low-vram-smoke   → preset silently rewrote 3.0 → 1.0
    --max-samples 0 --low-vram-smoke → preset silently rewrote 0 → 1000

Both break the contract documented in the README ("CLI flags the caller
passes still win") because == against the default cannot distinguish
"user typed it" from "argparse filled it in".

Fix: switch the tracked-by-merge args (model, batch_size, grad_accum,
max_seq_len, optimizer, apollo_rank, max_samples, epochs, plus the
already-None memory_budget_gb) to `default=None`. After parse_args,
user-passed-ness is now `getattr(args, dest) is not None` — exact,
ambiguity-free. Registry merge and --low-vram-smoke preset both gate
on `not _user_passed[dest]`. A final `_FALLBACK_DEFAULTS` pass fills
any value still None with the historical argparse fallback (4096 /
4 / 8 / 3.0 / 0 / "apollo" / 256 / "Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B"), so behavior
when neither registry nor preset fires is unchanged.

`_defaults_at_parse` snapshot dropped entirely — the None sentinel
makes it unnecessary.

Tests: updated the inline `_resolve()` helper in
test_train_local_low_vram_smoke.py to mirror the new logic
(default=None on the rebuilt parser, _user_passed dict, fallback
pass). Added a parametrized regression that asserts every tracked
flag set to its historical argparse default survives the preset
(--epochs 3.0, --max-samples 0, --batch-size 4, --grad-accum 8,
--max-seq-len 4096). Added two combined-scenario regressions for
--registry-key + --low-vram-smoke + explicit default-equal value
on --max-samples 0 and --epochs 3.0. All 13 tests pass.

* refactor(training): extract build_parser + apply_resolved_defaults for test reuse

The low-vram-smoke test had to maintain a hand-written mirror of
train_local.main's argparse layout + registry/preset/fallback merge
order (`_build_parser` + `_resolve` + duplicated _TRACKED_DESTS +
duplicated _FALLBACK_DEFAULTS, ~85 lines). Any new tracked arg or
override block added to main() would silently bypass the mirror —
tests would keep passing while exercising the old behavior.

Extract two module-level helpers from train_local.main:

  - build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser  — owns add_argument
  - apply_resolved_defaults(args) -> None      — owns the merge

main() becomes a thin caller: parse, merge, run the pipeline.
The test's `_resolve()` now delegates to the same helpers instead
of duplicating them, so any future tracked-arg addition is covered
by existing assertions automatically.

Addresses Greptile round-1 P2 on PR #7805.

chip(npu/compiler): B-3 LiteRT (TFLite) delegate skeleton (PROTOTYPE)

Declares the C-style delegate surface in compiler/runtime/e1_litert_delegate.h
(create / partition / invoke / destroy) and mirrors it from Python in
e1_litert_delegate.py. The Python side parses the StableHLO subset module,
calls into the B-1 validator and the B-5 partitioner, and returns the same
descriptor-spec blob shape that the ExecuTorch delegate emits.

Status: PROTOTYPE. No upstream LiteRT dependency, no TfLiteDelegate
registration, and no kernel codegen are implemented. The header documents
the symbols a future native C delegate will export so the runtime contract
stays in lockstep with both delegates.

chip(npu/compiler): B-2 ExecuTorch delegate skeleton (PROTOTYPE)

Models the ExecuTorch Python partitioner / preprocess surface without
importing the upstream executorch package. The skeleton consumes the same
e1_npu_stablehlo dataclass subset that the runtime validates, reuses the
B-5 partitioner for supported-set decisions, and emits a JSON descriptor-spec
placeholder blob plus the CommandBuffer-sized batches that a future native
backend will materialise.

Status: PROTOTYPE. No binary kernel, no ExecuTorch graph passes, and no
ahead-of-time codegen are implemented. The interface tracks the upstream
Partitioner.partition / Backend.preprocess contract so a future C++ backend
can drop in.

chip(npu/compiler): B-5 StableHLO subset partitioner with CPU-fallback report

The partitioner walks the e1_npu_stablehlo dataclass subset, loads the
opcode + tile-bound support table from
docs/spec-db/e1-npu-runtime-contract.json, and classifies each op as
supported or CPU-fallback. The report carries cpu_fallback_percent so
operators can audit the gap to the npu-2028-target cpu_fallback_percent_max
budget, and groups contiguous supported ops into CommandBuffer-sized batches
for the B-2/B-3 delegates to consume.

CLI: python3 compiler/runtime/e1_npu_partitioner.py <module.json> prints the
structured JSON report.

chip(npu/runtime): B-4 CommandBuffer descriptor-batching abstraction

Batches NpuStreamDescriptor entries into one ring-base submission with a
single completion wait, mirroring the IREE Stream dialect pattern. A
one-element buffer is the equivalent of the historical single-op MMIO
path, so callers can opt into batched dispatch incrementally.

The buffer caps entries at the RTL 3-bit ring window minus one, exposes a
word-addressed descriptor image for staging, and adds an E1NpuRuntime.submit
wrapper that delegates to submit_descriptors.

chip(memory): AXI4 cocotb 5/5 PASS — fix interconnect grant race, DRAM R FSM, IRQ stickiness

Five concurrent bugs were hiding behind the 1-of-5 cocotb pass that the
AXI4 burst-evidence gate logged in `cocotb_status_at_check_in`. They are
all fixed in this commit and re-verified end-to-end with
`make memory-axi4-check`, which now drives the cocotb suite to 5/5 PASS
and writes a stable status JSON.

Root causes:
- Cross-block delta-cycle race: AW/AR grants were computed in one
  always_comb and the slave-side fanout in another. Verilator evaluated
  the two combinational domains in arbitrary order, so the fanout read
  stale grant values in the same delta cycle (s_awvalid driven high
  while grant=NUM_MASTERS). Fix: merge grant + fanout into a single
  block per channel and propagate m_awvalid[g] instead of an
  unconditional 1'b1.
- Decode-error sentinel mix-up: the comb + always_ff path compared
  decoder return values against NUM_MASTERS, but decode_slave returns
  NUM_SLAVES on miss. Out-of-aperture transactions never took the
  DECERR path; they hung the response queue with is_decerr=0.
- Behavioural DRAM R_DATA had overlapping rvalid drivers across two
  conditional branches, so multi-beat reads stuck after the first beat.
  Rewrote as an explicit prefill / handshake-advance / last-clear state
  machine, removing the racing default-assignment overlap.
- exclusive_fail_irq was a one-cycle pulse: tests inspected it after
  the next B response, by which time the pulse had cleared. Made the
  IRQ sticky (held until reset); a future RTL revision can add a
  write-1-to-clear MMR.
- write_strobe_partial_beat_preserves_unwritten_bytes set its
  replacement byte via OR (pattern | (0xC3<<8)) instead of clear+OR, so
  the expected byte was 0xC3 but the actual DRAM-stored value was 0xEB.

Also:
- Removed dev-only AXI4_TRACE macro after debug; testbench is clean.
- New scripts/write_axi4_cocotb_status.py parses cocotb XML into
  docs/evidence/memory/axi4_cocotb_status.json (schema
  eliza.memory.axi4_cocotb_status.v1) so downstream gates can fail fast
  on regression. The four BLOCKED artifacts remain blocked (real DRAM
  PHY + bandwidth runs still pending).

tsc declarations build (`tsc --project tsconfig.declarations.json`)
in packages/core failed:

  src/capabilities/index.ts(2908,3): error TS2322:
    Type 'string' is not assignable to type
    '"POST" | "GET" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE" | "STATIC"'

allowed HTTP verbs (or STATIC when allowed).

feat(seccomp-shim): riscv64 SIGSYS handler for epoll_pwait2 trap

Adds the third per-arch SIGSYS handler in the seccomp-shim trio.
Mirrors the arm64 handler's structure but uses riscv64's ucontext
layout (mcontext_t.__gregs[10..17] for a0..a7) and the ecall syscall
trap instruction. Covers the one currently-known blocked syscall on
Android riscv64: epoll_pwait2 (#441) -> epoll_pwait (#22) with a
timespec->ms clamp matching the arm64 conversion.

riscv64 - like arm64 - uses the generic Linux syscall ABI
(asm-generic/unistd.h), so the x86_64 shim's 24-entry legacy non-AT
translation table does not apply. musl's rv64 wrappers go straight
to the AT/p-form syscalls.

Wired into compile-shim.mjs's SHIM_ABI_TARGETS map (third entry:
riscv64 / riscv64-linux-musl / ld-musl-riscv64.so.1) so the existing
stageSeccompShimForAbi() staging path picks it up under
jniLibs/riscv64/ alongside arm64-v8a/ and x86_64/.

Verified end-to-end with `node compile-shim.mjs --abi riscv64`:
produces a 15 KB ELF 64-bit LSB shared object (UCB RISC-V, RVC,
double-float ABI). Existing x86_64 and arm64-v8a paths continue
to build clean.

wip(bun-riscv64): scaffold cross-compile pipeline for Android agent

Adds the build pipeline that produces bun-linux-riscv64-musl.zip — the
artifact stage-android-agent.mjs needs when MILADY_BUN_RISCV64_URL is set.
Upstream Bun ships no riscv64 release (oven-sh/bun#21923) so we build
one from source by cross-compiling on x86_64 with Docker + QEMU.

Pipeline scaffolding (no patches yet — see Punted below):

- Dockerfile (validates clean with `docker buildx build --check`):
  debian:bookworm-slim host + LLVM 21.1.8 (pinned to Bun upstream) +
  Rust nightly 2026-05-06 (from oven-sh/bun rust-toolchain.toml) +
  Zig 0.14.1 + Alpine v3.21 riscv64 sysroot extracted to /sysroot.
  Cross-compile wrappers at /opt/cross/bin/riscv64-linux-musl-* carry
  --target=riscv64-unknown-linux-musl --sysroot=/sysroot
  -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d. QEMU user-static available for in-container
  smoke-testing.

- build.sh (bash -n clean): drives the in-container build. Reads pins
  from bun-version.json, clones oven-sh/WebKit @ pinned commit +
  oven-sh/bun @ pinned tag, applies webkit-patches/*.patch +
  bun-patches/*.patch, configures WebKit with ENABLE_BASELINE_JIT=ON
  ENABLE_DFG_JIT=OFF ENABLE_FTL_JIT=OFF (Baseline path, the on-device
  default) or ENABLE_C_LOOP=ON via BUN_RISCV64_FORCE_CLOOP=1 fallback,
  builds Bun against the local WebKit, smoke-tests with
  qemu-riscv64-static, emits dist/bun-linux-riscv64-musl.zip with a
  sha256 + build-log.txt. No silent fallback — operator picks JIT mode.

- bun-version.json: single source of truth. Bun tag bun-v1.3.13 (matches
  stage-android-agent.mjs:BUN_VERSION), WebKit fork commit 3167a44f
  (matches scripts/build/deps/webkit.ts:WEBKIT_VERSION on oven-sh/bun@main
  as of 2026-05-19), LLVM 21.1.8, Rust nightly 2026-05-06, Zig 0.14.1,
  Alpine v3.21. Each pin carries a rationale so follow-up bumps stay
  in lockstep with the Android staging pipeline.

- webkit-patches/README.md: documents the three-bucket strategy.
  Bucket 1 cherry-picks upstream WebKit r281757 (LLInt for riscv64,
  WebKit bug #229035) + r293316 (Baseline JIT for riscv64, WebKit bug
  #239708). Bucket 2 covers CMake/offlineasm follow-ups that the 2022
  patches predate. Bucket 3 avoids the 2.46.x LLInt regression in
  WebKit bug #281138. DFG/FTL stay disabled (bugs #238006 + #239707
  still NEW upstream — acceptable since the Android agent runtime is
  llama.cpp + network bound, not JS hot-loop bound).

- bun-patches/README.md: documents the seven Bun-side patches. Bun's
  Arch type is hard-coded to "x64" | "aarch64" in scripts/build/config.ts;
  every code branch downstream of that needs a riscv64 case. WebKit dep
  must be forced into local-mode (no riscv64 prebuilt tarball exists on
  oven-sh/WebKit and there never will be). TinyCC dep must be disabled —
  the oven-sh/tinycc fork has no riscv64 backend; bun:ffi JIT-compile is
  unavailable on riscv64 (static FFI still works), enforced by
  BUN_DISABLE_TINYCC=1 in build.sh too.

- README.md: operator recipe. `docker build` then `docker run` with
  patches + bun-version.json + dist/ mounted, the C_LOOP retry path,
  artifact-hosting → MILADY_BUN_RISCV64_URL wiring, the full pin table,
  the JIT-tier matrix, and the explicit punted-items list.

- dist/.gitignore: track build-log.txt + sha256s, ignore the binary zip.

fix(release): rebase release commit with -X theirs on push retry

When the npm-release workflow queues for an extended period (run
26082989616 sat queued for 28 minutes), concurrent commits land on
develop. The workflow's first push then fails with non-fast-forward,
the retry rebases onto origin/develop, and any concurrent edit to a
file that lerna also bumped (e.g. packages/tui/package.json) aborts
the rebase with a CONFLICT — even though the only conflicting hunks
are version strings that the release commit owns.

`-X theirs` tells the recursive merge strategy to prefer the patch
being applied (our release commit) when hunks collide. In rebase
semantics "theirs" = the commit being replayed onto the new base, so
this is exactly the right side for version bumps. Non-version edits
to the same files still merge cleanly via the 3-way merge.

Also abort any half-applied rebase before returning false, so the
next retry attempt starts from a clean working tree instead of an
unfinished rebase state.

feat(local-inference): multi-context pool + resizeParallel via FFI

Closes the last achievable JS-side parity gap toward retiring
dflash-server.ts. Vision describe (mmproj) is now the SOLE remaining
blocker — it requires native C work in eliza-llama-shim that can't be
done from a JS-only session.

desktop-llama-adapter.ts — Multi-context pool refactor:

- `ctxPool: Pointer[]` replaces the single `ctxPtr`. Parallel
  `hasDecodedFlags: boolean[]` and `drafterAttached: boolean[]` track
  per-ctx state. The legacy `ctxPtr` accessor is preserved as a getter
  that returns `ctxPool[0]` for backward compat with the non-session
  paths (model load, getCtxHandle, drafter top-level API).
- `loadOpts` recorded at load time so `resizeParallel(N)` can recreate
  ctxs with the same ctx params.
- New `resizeParallel(target)` grows or shrinks the pool. Growing
  allocates additional ctxs via `eliza_llama_init_from_model` against
  the same loaded model. Shrinking refuses to drop ctxs that still
  have sessions pinned to them. Returns true on real change.
- `parallelSlots()` reports the live pool size.
- `openSession(config)` now routes each session to a ctx via
  `config.slotId % pool.length` (or round-robin via stream id when
  slotId < 0). Sessions store `ctxIdx`; `prefillSession`, `nextStep`,
  `saveSlotForStream`, `restoreSlotForStream` all use
  `ctxPool[sess.ctxIdx]`.
- Drafter is per-ctx: `attachDrafterToCtx(ctxIdx, opts)` and
  `detachDrafterFromCtx(ctxIdx)`. The shared drafter MODEL is loaded
  once and re-used across all ctxs that want speculative decoding
  (cheap — model load is the expensive part). Switching the drafter
  path detaches every ctx, frees the old model, loads the new.
- `unloadModel()` frees the entire pool back-to-front.
- Slot save/restore picks up multi-slot correctness: per-stream
  variants route to the session's ctx so concurrent conversations
  persist independently; legacy `saveSlot(filename)` /
  `restoreSlot(filename)` still target ctxPool[0] for callers without
  a stream context.

desktop-ffi-backend-runtime.ts:

- New `parallelSlots()` and `resizeParallel(target)` forward to the
  underlying adapter. No-ops when no model is loaded.

ffi-streaming-backend.ts:

- `FfiBackendRuntime` interface gains optional `parallelSlots` /
  `resizeParallel` (runtimes without a pool report 1 / no-op).
- `FfiStreamingBackend.parallelSlots()` and `.resizeParallel()`
  forward to the runtime. The dispatcher's forwarder routes
  engine.ts's existing `maybeAutoResizeParallel` through here when
  the FFI backend is active.

FFI_BACKEND_WIREUP_PLAN.md:

- Parallel-resize moved from "remaining" to "done".
- Vision describe is now the ONLY feature blocker for Step F (retire
  dflash-server.ts). Honest 3-4 day effort estimate + concrete file
  list documented:
    * build-llama-cpp-desktop-dylib.mjs needs LLAMA_BUILD_EXAMPLES=ON
      (or vendored llava sources) to make the llava sublib available.
    * eliza_llama_shim.c needs llava_image_embed_load/eval/free
      pointer-style C wrappers.
    * eliza_llama_shim.h needs matching declarations.
    * desktop-llama-adapter.ts: ShimSymbols + bindShim entries +
      describeImage impl.
    * FfiStreamingBackend: describeImage forwarder.

NOT runtime-tested. The pool semantics follow the upstream llama.cpp
single-model-multiple-context pattern (each ctx has independent KV).
Most likely first-run issues:
1. The shim's eliza_llama_init_from_model may not be safe to call
   multiple times on the same model on some backends (e.g. Metal can
   be tricky with concurrent contexts). If so, the grow path needs a
   lock or a model-clone.
2. n_seq_max default might be 1, in which case the drafter attach
   per-ctx has the same constraint as the main ctx.
3. The `drafterModelPath !== opts.drafterPath` switch detaches every
   ctx, which racing sessions on other ctxs would observe as a sudden
   has_drafter=0. The detach is synchronous so the next step will run
   plain decode (not unified), which is correct but unexpected.

fix(metrics-dashboard): install local deps so package's pinned TS is used in CI

Revert the earlier baseUrl/ignoreDeprecations drop and instead address the
underlying CI environment mismatch. The Nightly Build "Build & Test" job
failed with:

    [build] metrics-dashboard
    tsconfig.json(21,5): error TS5101: Option 'baseUrl' is deprecated
    and will stop functioning in TypeScript 7.0. Specify compilerOption
    '"ignoreDeprecations": "6.0"' to silence this error.

Root cause: metrics-dashboard is not a workspace member, so root-level
`bun install` doesn't install its `devDependencies` (including its pinned
`typescript: ^5.7.2`). When `bun run build` then invokes `tsc -b`, the
shell walks up to the repo root's `node_modules/.bin/tsc`, which is
TypeScript 6.x. TS 6.x rejects `ignoreDeprecations: "5.0"` for the
`baseUrl` deprecation introduced in TS 6.

Fix: have the package install its own dependencies before building.
`bun install --no-save` in the package directory uses the committed
`bun.lock` to install the pinned TS 5.9.x (and the other deps shadcn/ui
components and @tanstack/react-table rely on) into a local
`node_modules`. The subsequent `tsc -b` then resolves to that local
TS install and tolerates `baseUrl` under `ignoreDeprecations: "5.0"`.

This also surfaced a second long-standing issue masked by the original
TS5101 abort: shadcn/ui components import `cn` from `@/lib/utils`, but
`src/lib/utils.ts` was never committed (note: `src/lib/` matched a
top-level `lib/` rule in the Python-oriented `.gitignore`). Add the
standard shadcn `cn` helper there so the components resolve.

The `tsconfig.json` `baseUrl` and `ignoreDeprecations` lines are
restored unchanged to match the state the user reverted to.

    $ rm -rf node_modules dist && bun run build

    vite v6.4.1 building for production...
    ✓ 2354 modules transformed.

ci(npm-release): pass --no-sort to lerna publish to bypass topo queue bug

lerna 9.0.7's `runProjectsTopologically` aborts mid-stream with
"Not all tasks were run. This is likely a bug in Lerna." when the
workspace graph contains a dependency cycle. Run 26079418621 surfaced
the cycle `@elizaos/agent <-> @elizaos/plugin-capacitor-bridge` and
failed after packing 137 of 153 packages, with no NPM publish happening.

the broken priority queue. Combined with `--concurrency 1` this still
gives a deterministic, serialized publish order without depending on
the toposort that the cycle breaks.

- `.github/workflows/release.yaml` (NPM Release / Publish to NPM step)
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` (nightly dist-tag publish)
- root `package.json` `release`, `release:next`, `release:beta`
  scripts, which the workflow references as the manual recovery path.

The underlying cycle should still be fixed in the source graph, but
that is out of scope for unblocking the release.

fix(hetzner-e2e): classify 403 limit_reached as quota_exceeded, not missing_token

Run 26077765355 surfaced a misleading "missing_token" error on a Hetzner
project that actually hit its server cap. The API returned HTTP 403 with
body `{ error: { code: "limit_reached", message: "server limit reached" } }`,
but `mapStatusToCode` short-circuited on status 401/403 before reading the
apiCode, collapsing quota exhaustion and missing-token into one bucket.

Layer 1: reorder `mapStatusToCode` so the explicit `limit_reached` /
`resource_limit_exceeded` apiCode wins over the status-only auth fallback.
This is the only correct mapping: status 403 with `limit_reached` is a
project quota issue, not an auth problem, and operators should not be
told to refresh a token that is working fine.

Provision script: extend `isRetryableCombo` to also retry the next
fallback combo on `quota_exceeded` (and the literal "server limit
reached" / "limit_reached" / "resource_limit_exceeded" message strings,
so we stay correct if the error is rewrapped). The fallback ladder is
finite, so a genuinely exhausted project still surfaces a single, clear
error after the ladder is exhausted — with an operator-facing hint
("delete leaked CI servers in https://console.hetzner.cloud/ or rotate
HCLOUD_TOKEN_CI to a project with capacity"). A non-retryable 401/403
also now prints a hint pointing at the GitHub `ci-hetzner-e2e`
environment.

Layer 2: workflow now captures the provision step's combined output to
a log and, on failure, writes a categorized diagnostic to
GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (quota vs auth vs unknown) so the operator opening
the failed run sees the actionable next step at the top instead of
buried in the step log.

fix(os/iso): tolerate cleanup rm failures so build doesn't fail post-success

The ISO build was getting through `lb config completed successfully.`
and then failing the recipe with exit 1 because the cleanup trap's
`rm -rf /build/.git` reported `cannot remove '/build/.git': Directory
not empty` and propagated under `set -euo pipefail`. /build is the
host-bind mount, and the .git tree there contains a mix of
root-owned (generated by the container) and runner-owned (mounted
from the host) entries — rm sees the runner-owned files as
undeletable.

Cleanup is best-effort: the build succeeded or failed before we
reach this point, and a few leftover files in /build are not worth
turning a successful `lb config` into a red workflow. Suffix the
`rm -rf`s in the EXIT trap with `2>/dev/null || true`.

fix(core): scope streaming wrap to tool-calls; restore terminal-only eval gating

Two narrow planner/streaming fixes surfaced by failing CI tests on develop:

1. runtime.useModel streaming branch: 0a3a60f854d widened the streaming
   result to a GenerateText-shape object whenever the underlying handler
   surfaced any of `toolCalls`/`finishReason`. Non-local providers that
   return a streaming object with `text`/`finishReason`/`usage` but no
   tool calls (e.g. RESPONSE_HANDLER on openai) thus stopped returning a
   bare string, breaking callers that assert string equality. Now the
   wider object is only produced when tool calls actually resolved; the
   default bare-string contract is preserved otherwise. parsePlannerOutput
   still gets its toolCalls in the case it cares about.

2. planner-loop terminal-only branch: the gating that skipped recording
   an `evaluation` stage on the very first iteration (when no prior

fix(ui/test): resolve React multiple-copies hook errors in vitest suite

Three changes work together to eliminate 'Invalid hook call' failures
across all 111 test files:

1. Pool change: revert to `forks` (from `vmThreads`).  The `vmThreads`
   pool's VitestModuleRunner bypasses Node 22's native CJS/ESM interop,
   causing `html-encoding-sniffer → @exodus/bytes` to fail with
   SyntaxError and breaking react hook resolution.  The `forks` pool
   uses real Node child processes so native interop works.

2. Dynamic react path resolution: instead of resolving react via
   `createRequire(import.meta.url)`, we now resolve lucide-react first
   and discover react from *its* bun-cache peer-hash directory.  In a
   bun workspace, each package's bun-cache entry carries its own react
   symlink matching the peer version it was compiled against.  By
   anchoring the Vite alias to that same physical path, all ESM imports
   and CJS requires in the test runner land on the same module instance.

3. server.deps.inline list: react, lucide-react, @radix-ui, motion,
   and other UI packages are inlined through Vite so the alias also
   applies to their own internal imports, preventing any stale CJS copy
   from sneaking through.

Result: 835 tests pass (3 skipped), 0 failures — up from 197 failing.

feat(cloud-api,os-homepage): server-side Steward OAuth nonce exchange

Eliminate refresh tokens (and access tokens) from the post-OAuth URL by
adopting Steward's new `response_type=code` flow (Steward PR
https://github.com/Steward-Fi/steward/pull/45).

Flow:
  1. os-homepage adds `response_type=code` to the Steward authorize URL.
  2. Steward redirects to `/checkout?code=<nonce>` — no tokens in the URL.
  3. CheckoutPage POSTs the code to `/api/auth/steward-nonce-exchange`.
  4. The cloud-api route calls Steward `POST /auth/oauth/exchange`
     server-side, verifies the returned JWT, syncs the user, sets the
     HttpOnly steward-token + steward-refresh-token cookies, and returns
     `{ ok, userId }`. The access and refresh tokens never enter the
     browser process.

Changes:

- packages/steward-session-client/src/index.ts
  - new STEWARD_NONCE_EXCHANGE_ENDPOINT constant
  - new error codes: missing_code, code_invalid, code_expired,
    code_redirect_mismatch, code_tenant_mismatch,
    steward_upstream_unavailable, forbidden_origin

- packages/cloud-api/auth/steward-nonce-exchange/route.ts (new)
  - POST handler with the same Origin/Referer CSRF allowlist as
    /api/auth/steward-session
  - resolves STEWARD_API_URL (or NEXT_PUBLIC_STEWARD_API_URL)
  - forwards {code, redirect_uri, tenant_id} to Steward /auth/oauth/exchange
  - maps upstream code_* errors to our StewardSessionErrorCode union
  - verifies JWT via verifyStewardTokenCached, syncs via syncUserFromSteward
  - sets steward-token (httpOnly, TTL = JWT exp), steward-refresh-token
    (httpOnly, 30d), and steward-authed=1 (non-httpOnly marker, 7d)

feat(provisioning-worker): own the three SSH-bound cron paths instead of forwarding to the control-plane (#7778)

After PR #7775 folded node health checks into this daemon, three more cron
paths in CRON_FANOUT still forwarded from CF Workers to the
container-control-plane (a Node service whose host we no longer reliably
track) for SSH-bound work that races against the daemon's writes:

  - agent-hot-pool: syncAllocatedCounts + prePullAgentImageOnAvailableNodes
  - node-autoscale: evaluateCapacity + provisionNode / drainNode
  - pool-drain-idle: WarmPoolManager.drainIdle

When the control-plane runs without CONTAINERS_SSH_KEY (verified in prod
2026-05-17), its writes flip every milady-core back to 'offline' five
minutes after the daemon writes them 'healthy'. The fix is the same as
PR #7775: rapatrier the cycle into the orchestrator host that already
has the SSH key + Neon access, and stop fanning out to a separate
service that drifts.

What this commit does:

- Folds the three cycles into the provisioning-worker daemon's
  pollCycle, gated by the same nodeHealthIntervalMs (default 5 min,
  matches the legacy CRON_FANOUT cadence). Each cycle has its own
  try/catch so a single failure (e.g. HCLOUD_TOKEN missing) doesn't
  starve the others.
- Adds processSyncAllocatedCountsCycle, processPrePullImagesCycle,
  processNodeAutoscaleCycle, processPoolDrainIdleCycle to the daemon.
- Loads getNodeAutoscaler, WarmPoolManager, getHetznerPoolContainerCreator,
  containersEnv lazily through the existing loadDeps singleton.
- Caches a single WarmPoolManager instance per daemon process (same
  pattern container-control-plane used).
- Removes the three paths from CRON_FANOUT so the CF Worker stops
  fanning out at all — the daemon is now the only writer.

What this commit deliberately does NOT do:

- The container-control-plane service keeps these route handlers wired
  for backwards compatibility (and for any direct admin invocation),
  but they won't be reached from the CF Worker cron anymore.
- The control-plane still serves the user-facing endpoints (containers
  CRUD, agent bridge, stream). Moving those is a separate, larger PR
  that adds an HTTP server to the daemon.
- The deployment-monitor and other warm-pool crons stay on the
  control-plane for now; they tick at different cadences and don't
  contest docker_nodes truth.

Ops note: scale-up only succeeds when both HCLOUD_TOKEN and
CONTAINERS_AUTOSCALE_PUBLIC_SSH_KEY are present on the daemon host.
Today the worker host doesn't have HCLOUD_TOKEN, so scale-up reports
'scale_up_skipped' until those secrets are added — same posture as the
control-plane was in. Adding them on /opt/eliza/cloud/.env.local on the
orchestrator unlocks autoscale without any further code change.

feat(provisioning-worker): fold node health checks into the orchestrator daemon (#7775)

* feat(provisioning-worker): fold node health checks into the daemon so the orchestrator owns them

Today docker_nodes status is driven by container-control-plane, a separate
Node service that the CF Worker cron `agent-hot-pool` forwards to every
5 minutes. That service is deployed somewhere we no longer reliably know,
and verified in prod 2026-05-17 it cannot SSH the cores (its
CONTAINERS_SSH_KEY is missing) — every milady-core-* sat `offline` for days
even though SSH + `docker info` succeed instantly from this very daemon's
host using the key we just configured here for provision/stop.

Folding the loop into the provisioning worker daemon is the smaller-blast-
radius fix: this host already has

  - the CONTAINERS_SSH_KEY load-bearing for provision and stop (PR #7746)
  - direct Neon write access via DATABASE_URL
  - a 30s poll cycle that's a perfect carrier for a 5-min cadence

so we just call `dockerNodeManager.healthCheckAll()` from `pollCycle`,
gated by `lastNodeHealthCheckAt + nodeHealthIntervalMs <= now`. The CF
Worker cron route can stay as a no-op for now (`forwardCronToContainerControlPlane`
returns 503 when no URL is configured) and be removed in a follow-up; this
PR is the source-of-truth flip, not the cleanup.

Defaults / env:
  - `WORKER_NODE_HEALTH_INTERVAL` (ms) — defaults to 5 min, mirroring the
    legacy CRON_FANOUT cadence for agent-hot-pool.
  - Logs each tick at INFO with total/healthy/unhealthy so ops can spot
    regressions without grepping CF tail.

Concurrency: `healthCheckAll` already iterates with `Promise.allSettled`
and has its own MAX_RETRIES timeout, so a slow node never starves the
heartbeat or job-pickup cycle.

* chore(clean): trim WIP narration and obvious comments in provisioning-worker

Drop history-lesson docblocks ('previously owned by...', prod
2026-05-17 verification note) that describe how we got here rather
than what the code does. Keep the current rationale.

* chore(clean): document first-tick health check intent

lastNodeHealthCheckAt initializes to 0 so the first poll cycle always runs a node health check. Make the intent explicit in the comment block.

* refactor(container-control-plane): drop node healthCheckAll() — owned by provisioning-worker daemon now

The daemon (PR's previous commits) now health-checks every enabled
docker_nodes row on its own poll loop, using the load-bearing
CONTAINERS_SSH_KEY that lives on the orchestrator host. Keeping the same
call here too would race with the daemon: with a different (likely empty)
CONTAINERS_SSH_KEY on whatever host this service runs on, every check
fails, the agent-hot-pool cron tick writes 'offline' to every row, and the
daemon flips them back to 'healthy' two minutes later. The status visible
to the rest of the system would depend on which 5-min cron landed last.

Removing this single call leaves the rest of agentHotPoolResponse intact
— syncAllocatedCounts, prePullAgentImageOnAvailableNodes, and the
capacity report still ride on the same CF Worker cron forward and still
need this Node service. Only the contested write goes away.

  modes. The convention is null = "not yet generated", not 0x64.

  placeholder and the sizeBytes:1 sentinel.

  produces). Move the strict gate BEFORE status promotion so a partial

  promote, tag.

fix(cloud-frontend): Vite production dynamic env access silently undefined

`getViteEnvFlag(name)` / `getViteEnvValue(name)` used a dynamic property
read on `import.meta.env` (`env?.[name]`). Vite replaces `import.meta.env`
in production builds with a literal that only contains the 5 standard
fields (BASE_URL / DEV / MODE / PROD / SSR) — custom `VITE_*` vars are
inlined ONLY when accessed via the literal property name
(`import.meta.env.VITE_FOO`). A dynamic lookup returned `undefined` in
production, which silently broke:
  1. The Playwright test-auth bypass — every authed e2e test rendered
     the unauthenticated dashboard shell with the marketing sidebar.
  2. Steward API URL resolution when configured via env.

Replaces the helpers in `useSessionAuth` and `StewardProvider` with direct
literal property reads, and documents the rule inline so the next agent
doesn't reintroduce the trap.

Surfaced by writing a real SIWE end-to-end test that drives the bundled
SDK via an injected EIP-1193 provider and ephemeral viem key:
`tests/e2e/siwe-flow.spec.ts`. The same test also locks in EIP-4361
message shape + signature recoverability for the auth flow.

The cloud-routes e2e is updated to match the new reality: admin dashboard
routes do NOT require an additional role beyond regular auth, so they
land in the renderable list rather than the bounce-to-login list.

docs(os-release): add VERIFY.md + verify-release.sh helper

Ships a layered release verification helper that complements
the in-progress signing / attestation / SBOM work:

  packages/os/release/VERIFY.md       — user-facing verification doc
  packages/os/scripts/verify-release.sh — one-command runner

The script walks four layers, in order, against a downloaded
release directory:

  1. SHA256SUMS roundtrip            — required (coreutils only)
  2. GitHub artifact attestations    — optional (gh CLI)
  3. GPG signature on SHA256SUMS     — optional (gpg)
  4. SBOM summary                    — optional (jq)

Each optional layer is skipped with a notice when its tool is
missing, so the script is useful out of the box on any Unix.

Exit codes:
  0  every required check passed (optional layers may have
     been skipped or warned)
  1  SHA256SUMS missing or roundtrip failed
  2  an optional layer detected real corruption / tampering
     (mixed valid+invalid attestations, or a bad GPG sig).
     Pure absence is NOT treated as tampering.

Tested locally via a 5-case matrix (clean / corrupt / missing /
bad-GPG-sig / in-repo-style header comments). shellcheck clean.

Doc is the entry point users land on after a release download;
it covers what each layer means, expected output, the future
GPG path, and a troubleshooting note.

feat(cloud): replace HTTP control-plane health probe with Redis heartbeat

The cloud-api Worker guarded /api/v1/agents, /api/v1/eliza/agents/:id/provision,
/api/v1/eliza/agents/:id/resume, /api/v1/eliza/agents/:id/pairing-token, and
/api/compat/agents with a synchronous HTTP probe against a
container-control-plane sidecar (CONTAINER_CONTROL_PLANE_URL/health). That
sidecar is no longer deployed — post-cutover everything goes through the
provisioning-worker daemon on the orchestrator VM via the jobs queue. The
probe was failing in production with PROVISIONING_WORKER_NOT_CONFIGURED /
UNREACHABLE, so every create-agent / resume click silently dropped on the
floor and left rows stuck in pending.

Switch the gate to Redis (already provisioned via Upstash and shared with
rate limiting / credit events). The daemon publishes ISO timestamp at
provisioning_worker:health with a 60s TTL at the start of every poll cycle;
the Worker GETs that key on each gated request. Missing/expired key ->
unhealthy 503, present -> proceed.

Why this is cleaner than the previous flow:
- One source of truth shared by Worker and daemon, no new service to host.
- TTL gives self-healing: daemon outage trips the gate within 60s, recovery
  closes it on the next cycle without any manual reconciliation.
- Workers can already reach Upstash REST; daemon already opens REDIS_URL for
  rate limits. Zero new network paths.

Tests in provisioning-worker-health.test.ts cover the four states (no
heartbeat, fresh heartbeat, gate disabled, redis unconfigured) against
MOCK_REDIS=1.

fix(core): restore evaluator messageToUser precedence, opt-in canonical tool text

The Server Tests upstream regression (planner-loop-user-facing-text →
"does not regress evaluator's explicit messageToUser path") fails on
develop because preferredFinalMessageFromToolOrModel preferred a single
successful tool's userFacingText OVER the evaluator's explicit
messageToUser. Shaw's regression test asserts the opposite: when the
evaluator emits an explicit messageToUser, it wins.

Reconciling both intents without picking one over the other: add an
opt-in flag verifiedUserFacing on ActionResult / PlannerToolResult.
Tools that emit structured outputs where evaluator paraphrase risks
hallucinating values (paths, ids, counts, numeric metrics) set
verifiedUserFacing: true to mark their userFacingText canonical. The
planner-loop then echoes the tool verbatim instead of letting the
evaluator paraphrase it. Without the flag, the evaluator's explicit
messageToUser wins (Shaw's invariant).

Precedence in preferredFinalMessageFromToolOrModel is now:
  1. Single successful tool with verifiedUserFacing === true
  2. Evaluator/model messageToUser
  3. Most recent tool userFacingText (fallback)
  4. Caller-provided fallback

Changes:
- packages/core/src/types/components.ts: add verifiedUserFacing to
  ActionResult with JSDoc explaining when to opt in.
- packages/core/src/runtime/planner-types.ts: add verifiedUserFacing to
  PlannerToolResult with matching contract.
- packages/core/src/runtime/execute-planned-tool-call.ts and
  packages/core/src/runtime/planner-loop.ts
  (actionResultToPlannerToolResult): propagate the field through both
  ActionResult → PlannerToolResult conversion paths.
- packages/core/src/runtime/planner-loop.ts:
  - Rename singleSuccessfulUserFacingToolResultText →
    singleVerifiedUserFacingToolResultText and require
    verifiedUserFacing === true.
  - Reorder preferredFinalMessageFromToolOrModel to put verified-tool
    first, then evaluator, then fallback chain.
- packages/core/src/__tests__/planner-happy-path.test.ts: the
  "prefers a single tool's verified user-facing text over evaluator
  paraphrase" test now sets verifiedUserFacing: true (its semantic
  intent — "this is canonical structured data the evaluator could
  hallucinate") so the canonical-output guarantee still holds.

Verified:
- 1362 tests pass, 11 skipped (full packages/core suite, 165 files)
- bun run lint:check: 12 warnings before == 12 after (no new flags)
- bun run typecheck: clean

fix(core): filter failed steps from singleVerifiedUserFacingToolResultText

Greptile (P2) on #7897 flagged that the previous implementation gated
on toolResultSteps.length where toolResultSteps included ALL steps
with toolCall+result, failed steps included. A plan whose first tool
errored and whose second tool succeeded with verifiedUserFacing: true
would silently fall through to the evaluator's messageToUser — the
canonical-output guarantee was lost for any tool that ran after a
recoverable error.

Filter to step.result?.success === true before the length check.
Failed steps now don't count toward the uniqueness gate, so a single
successful verified tool wins even when prior tools failed.

surface in a comment.

Closes the second dimension of elizaOS/eliza#7935. The first dimension (planner SHELL-fallback for chat-recall) is fixed in #7942.

In packages/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/actions/tasks.ts the swarm-coordination prompt told sub-agents:

  - If you are blocked, need user input, or must ask the task creator a
    question, report it with routing kind QUESTION_FOR_TASK_CREATOR.
  - If you may conflict with another agent, are editing shared files, or
    need to share progress with peer agents, report it with routing kind
    AGENT_COORDINATION.

  To locate messages containing "emberblitz" in the Discord #general

  of the following:
  1. An API token...

1. Tells the sub-agent what to do behaviorally (write the question / coordination note as reply text and stop)
2. Explicitly forbids prefixing with routing-kind labels or markdown banners
3. Names both constants by name so the existing test coverage that checks for QUESTION_FOR_TASK_CREATOR and AGENT_COORDINATION presence still passes (verified)
4. Names the structural mechanism ("the orchestrator classifies routing from the session event, not your prose") so the sub-agent understands why

The Linux branch unconditionally runs:

    sudo apt-get install -y fswebcam

with . When the dev orchestrator runs outside a
TTY (Docker, headless WSL with no askpass, CI runners that lack the
NOPASSWD entry), sudo blocks indefinitely waiting for a password on
a stdin that no human is attached to. The dev server then hangs at
"Installing fswebcam via apt-get..." until manually killed.

Probe with  first. If sudo would prompt AND we are
not on a TTY, warn with the manual install command and the existing
ELIZA_NO_VISION_DEPS=1 escape hatch, then return. Interactive desktop
runs are unaffected (TTY available -> prompt works) and
NOPASSWD-configured CI is unaffected (sudo -n succeeds).

Repro: docker run --rm -it node:20-bookworm bash -c "apt-get update
&& apt-get install -y sudo && useradd -m u && su - u -c \"export
ELIZA_NO_VISION_DEPS=0; node ensure-vision-deps.mjs\""
Before: hangs at the sudo prompt.
After: prints "fswebcam missing; skipping install..." and returns 0.

refactor(core): drop regex-list identity-lookup evaluator in favor of prompt-rule contract

The narrow `core.contextual_identity_lookup_requires_recall` evaluator added in PR #7923 was a post-Stage-1 backstop that pattern-matched user messages against a fixed prefix list ("who is", "what is", "tell me about", ...) and a digit-bearing heuristic to decide whether to clear the simple-shortcut reply and reroute through the planner.

In production this misfired on every "what is N <word> M" math word problem because the local-name heuristic treats digit-bearing subjects as entity-like. Live trajectory tj-c5481b4c9050a9 ("what is 17 times 23?") got hijacked into a full planner trajectory: 56610 prompt tokens, $0.0286, 431KB trajectory bytes — for an arithmetic answer the simple shortcut had already produced correctly. The same class of failure hits "what is 5 plus 5", "what is 7 squared", etc.

The broader structural rule landed in the same PR (#7923) at the framework prompt-template layer covers the same intent without pattern matching: `messageHandlerTemplate` instructs Stage 1 to use non-simple contexts when the message refers to a specific name it cannot identify from visible context, and to say so plainly otherwise. That contract applies framework-wide to every shape — known and unknown — and is enforced at the source of the behavior (the model's instruction) rather than after the fact via output pattern matching.

Live-verified with the regex evaluator removed:

fix(core): bound runaway tool-arg validation loops via canonical failure signature

Repeated parameter-validation rejections from validateToolArgs were
previously not caught by the maxRepeatedFailures guard. The per-call
repeatKey (toolName + JSON.stringify(params)) and the per-call error
message both varied across retries when the model shuffled its
argument shape, so the failure-signature deduplication treated each
attempt as a fresh failure even though the failure category was
identical and no valid arg shape existed.

Live evidence: trajectory tj-95869490c7a2b2 ran 27 planner iterations,
25 tool calls (all failed), 25 toolCallFailures, 16 evaluatorFailures,
$1.30 of API cost, never reached terminal. Stage 1 invoked TASKS with
`action=spawn_agent` plus unrecognized args; SCHEDULED_TASKS rejected
the invocation; the model then cycled through action=create / update /
spawn_agent / etc., each time tripping a slightly different
parameterErrors message but with the same root failure category.

Fix: when result.data.parameterErrors is set, both the failure error
string and the repeatKey collapse to canonical values
("parameter_validation_failed" and "parameter_validation"), so two
consecutive validation rejections of the same tool now correctly hit
the existing maxRepeatedFailures (default 2) and TrajectoryLimitExceeded
fires.

Behavior preserved: failures whose data does NOT carry parameterErrors
(runtime errors, timeouts, downstream service failures) keep the
per-call repeatKey, so the existing test "does not count different
failed tool parameters as the same repeated failure" still passes —
different command attempts against the same tool with the same runtime
error still register as distinct retries.

New regression "collapses repeated parameter-validation failures on
the same tool even when args vary" reproduces tj-95869490c7a2b2's
shape with the model shuffling between action=spawn_agent / create /
update against the same tool and asserts TrajectoryLimitExceeded fires
within 2 attempts.

os(kiosk): disable Electrobun WebGPU/Dawn init under QEMU (suspected Worker wedge)

Sub-agent investigation pinpointed the most likely cause of the
"GTK event loop started then nothing" symptom: the bun Worker that
runs the app's bundled index.js calls init_webGPU during top-level
`await init_bun()`, which dlopen()s libwebgpu_dawn.so. That .so has
heavy static initializers (Tint, SPIR-V tooling, DXC) and pulls in
the Vulkan loader, which enumerates every ICD under
/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d and probes /dev/dri at process-init time.
Under QEMU's virtio-gpu with no real Vulkan ICD, this stalls the
Worker before main() runs — so its first FFI call into the wrapper
never happens, and gtk_main() correctly sits in poll() with nothing
to dispatch, externally indistinguishable from a wrapper deadlock.

Electrobun's findWgpuLibraryPath() honors ELECTROBUN_WGPU_PATH; a
non-existent path makes init_webGPU skip the dlopen entirely. The
kiosk has no WebGPU surface — WebKitGTK renders the UI — so this
costs nothing. VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_DISABLE=* is belt-and-suspenders
against any residual Vulkan ICD discovery the wrapper might do.

The companion change (diagnostic instrumentation in libNativeWrapper
that adds [wrapper-heartbeat] + first-dispatch logs) is built from
upstreams/electrobun-patches/0001-diagnostic-instrumentation.patch
which is already committed; rebuild + restage that .so into
artifacts/amd64/elizaos-app/bin/ before make build ARCH=amd64. The
heartbeat will independently confirm whether gtk_main is alive while
this env change tests the Worker-side hypothesis directly.

check_cva6_boot_substrate.py — P2 unreachable null guard
======================================================
The defensive 'if node is None: continue' inside

  if failure is not None or error is not None:
      node = failure if failure is not None else error
      if node is None:
          continue

was dead code. The outer guard ensures at least one of failure/error
is non-None, and the conditional expression then resolves node to the
non-None one. Replaced with an assert that documents the narrowing
without runtime overhead in non-debug builds (Python still asserts
at runtime, but the intent is reader-visible and tools like mypy can
narrow the type).

check_e1_soc_pd_input_contract.py — P1 clock_period silent mismatch
====================================================================
After the ruff cleanup the comparison became:

  expected_clock_period = (
      float(expected_clock_period_raw)
      if isinstance(expected_clock_period_raw, ...) else None
  )
  if clock_period != expected_clock_period:
      sdc_semantic_failures.append({'id': 'clock_period_mismatch', ...})

When CLOCK_PERIOD is missing or unparseable in config, expected was
None and the comparison 'clock_period != None' was True for every
float — so every run reported a 'clock_period_mismatch' that wasn't
actually a mismatch with anything.

Fixed by splitting the failure mode: a missing/unparseable config
value fails closed as 'clock_period_config_missing_or_invalid' (a
config error), and the 'clock_period_mismatch' only fires when both
sides are valid floats and they disagree. Also wrapped float()
conversion in try/except since str inputs like 'abc' would have
crashed.

fix(cloud-api): handle tool_choice: "required" in mapToolChoice without crashing

`mapToolChoice` advertises a return type that includes `"required"`, but
the implementation only early-returns on `"auto"` and `"none"`. When the
caller passes `"required"` (a valid OpenAI-API value, and the value the
elizaOS planner sends in `@elizaos/core/src/services/message.ts` for
forced-tool turns — RESPONSE_HANDLER, PLAN_ACTIONS, facts/relationships,
etc.), execution falls through to `toolChoice.function.name`. Because
`"required"` is a string, `"required".function` is `undefined`, and
`.name` of undefined throws:

  Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')

The route's outer try/catch then wraps this into a HTTP 500 with body:

  {"error":{"message":"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')",
   "type":"api_error"}}

which is exactly what a 2PM/Milady agent run on `ghcr.io/2-a-m/2pm:latest`
hits on every DM that triggers the planner. Models confirmed independent:
both `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` and `openai/gpt-4o` reproduce. After
the failure the v5 runtime falls back to a no-tools retry (TEXT_LARGE
without `tool_choice`) which succeeds, so the agent replies in plain
text but never dispatches any action. The 2PM build at GHCR digest
sha256:0ace6d1bb812... + commit-level instrumentation in plugin-elizacloud
(milady-2pm-debug stderr writes around every await) localized the throw
to the cloud's `/chat/completions` route after a clean 500 response —
not the plugin's request/response handling, which is correct.

Reproducible with:

  curl -sS https://api.elizaos.ai/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":50,"tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"x","parameters":{"type":"object"}}}],"tool_choice":"required"}'

Fix:
  1. `mapToolChoice`: add `"required"` to the early-return list so the
     value passes through to the AI SDK unchanged (the AI SDK already
     accepts `"required"` natively per ai-sdk.dev/docs/foundations/tools).
  2. `ChatRequest.tool_choice` input type: add `"required"` to the
     accepted union so TS-typed callers (including the AI SDK + the
     elizaOS planner upstream) compile clean.

Adds a pure-helper unit test under `packages/cloud-api/__tests__/`
covering all four `tool_choice` values (undefined / "auto" / "none" /
"required" / explicit-function), plus a basic `convertTools` shape
test, to prevent regression. Follows the same pattern as
`app-deployments-helpers.test.ts` (pure imports via the existing
`__nativeToolingTestHooks` export, no I/O).

workflow that declares `secrets: { FOO: required: true }` aborts the
PARENT workflow at startup (0-3 sec, no logs) when the parent calls
it via `secrets: inherit` and the secret is unset. release-all.yml
inherits to 5 reusable workflows on every tag push to v*.*.* — and
has 3 confirmed startup_failure runs on 2026-05-20 alone.

Three coordinated fixes:

  - update-homebrew.yml — HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN
    + new Check credentials early-exit step that mirrors the
      publish-apt-repo.yml pattern (the body was a one-step
      dispatch, no existing skip path to gate on).

    ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS, ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD

      fails the job loudly when the keystore is empty. No additional
      body change needed — only the secret contract needed flipping.

  - apple-store-release.yml — APPLE_ID, APPLE_TEAM_ID,
    APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD
    + the body already has an iOS signing preflight that emits
      ::error:: for missing iOS secrets. No additional body change
      needed.

  Before — release-all.yml (push v*.*.*):
    startup_failure at 0-3 sec, no logs, no path to know what's
    missing without reading the called workflows by hand.

    release-all.yml startup succeeds. Per-target jobs that lack
    secrets fail loudly with their existing in-job preflight error
    messages (or with a clear ::warning:: skip in the homebrew
    case). Failed targets don't poison the others.

fix(ci): make missing release manifest a clear skip, not an opaque ENOENT

The populate-and-validate-manifest job hardcodes the manifest path
`packages/os/release/beta-2026-05-16/manifest.json` — and that file
does not exist in develop (only `packages/os/release/schema/` does).
Once PR #7976 unblocks the workflow's 0-3s startup_failure, this job
will run for the first time and fail at ~1-2 min with a Node
ENOENT inside `JSON.parse(readFileSync(MANIFEST))` — confusing for
the maintainer triaging the new failure.

Add an explicit `Check manifest file exists` step at the top of the
job, then gate every downstream step that reads/writes the manifest
or its SHA256SUMS derivative on the resulting
`can_validate_manifest` output. Mirrors the same pattern the GPG
secrets fix uses in publish-apt-repo.yml (#7976).

Net behaviour after this lands:

  Manifest file present
    → Job runs end to end as designed: populates checksums, generates
      canonical SHA256SUMS, mints SLSA-over-SHA256SUMS attestation,
      uploads the populated manifest, optionally attaches to GitHub
      release.

  Manifest file absent (today)
    → Job emits one ::warning:: explaining what was skipped and why,
      then completes green. The per-artifact SLSA attestations from
      build-linux-iso.yml / build-debian-package.yml /
      build-vm-image.yml still mint correctly — only the
      cross-artifact SHA256SUMS bundle is skipped.

Steps gated (all share the same `if:` condition for one source of
truth):

  - Populate manifest with real sha256 + sizes
  - Gate on publishable checksums (before status promotion)
  - Generate canonical SHA256SUMS via the in-repo tool
  - Attest SLSA build provenance over SHA256SUMS
  - Upload SHA256SUMS artifact
  - Promote release status to available
  - Upload populated manifest
  - Attach SHA256SUMS to release

The manifest path stays hardcoded — separate question of whether to
parameterize it by release tag, owned by whoever decides the
release cadence. This PR is the safety net.

fix(ci): make publish-apt-repo GPG secrets optional to unblock release workflow startup

elizaos-os-full-release.yml startup_failure'd at 0-3 seconds on every
release tag (v2.0.0 / v2.0.1 / v2.0.3 — three publishes, zero
successful runs) because publish-apt-repo.yml declared
`DEBIAN_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` and `DEBIAN_GPG_KEY_ID` as
`required: true`. GitHub validates the reusable-workflow secret
contract BEFORE any job runs, so an unset required secret aborts the
whole release pipeline with no logs — the existing graceful skip in
the workflow body (gpg_check setting can_publish=false) never gets a
chance to fire.

Two coordinated changes:

1. Change `required: true` → `required: false` for both
   DEBIAN_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY and DEBIAN_GPG_KEY_ID in the workflow_call
   secrets block. Now the reusable workflow accepts an unset secret
   without aborting at startup; the body's runtime check decides
   whether to actually publish.

2. Strengthen the Check GPG credentials step to also test
   DEBIAN_GPG_KEY_ID (was only checking PRIVATE_KEY). A
   half-configured repo where only one is set was previously a foot-gun
   — gpg_check would let it through and reprepro would fail downstream
   with a less obvious error.

Net effect: until the admin sets DEBIAN_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY +
DEBIAN_GPG_KEY_ID in the elizaOS/eliza repo secrets, every release-tag
of elizaos-os-full-release.yml will now complete with a clean
"::warning::DEBIAN_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY not configured. Apt repo publish
skipped." in place of the previous startup_failure — and the rest of
the release (ISO, .deb, VM image, verify, summary) runs to completion.
Once the admin configures the secrets, apt-repo publish lights up
automatically.

ci(build-linux-iso): add arm64 to matrix with continue-on-error

Phase 3a #7971 parameterized the ISO builder for amd64 / arm64 /
riscv64 — proven locally with `docker build --platform linux/arm64`
succeeding (grub-efi-arm64-bin installed cleanly) and the riscv64
package set resolving + downloading correctly. This wires arm64 into
the nightly workflow so the build path keeps working on every
develop merge.

Three coordinated changes:

1. matrix.arch grows from [amd64] to [amd64, arm64], with `include`
   blocks tagging each with an `experimental: false|true` flag.

2. `continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental }}` on the job — amd64
   stays the required check (must pass to mark the workflow green),
   arm64 failure does not turn the run red while it stabilizes.

3. New "Register qemu-user-static binfmt" step (gated `if: matrix.arch
   != 'amd64'`) runs `docker run --rm --privileged tonistiigi/binfmt
   --install all` on the amd64 GitHub Actions runner. After
   registration, `docker run --platform linux/arm64` transparently
   emulates aarch64 for everything inside the container — which is
   what build.sh does via `docker build --platform linux/${ARCH}`.
   Verifies the handler we actually need is registered (`test -e
   /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/qemu-aarch64`) so a silent no-op fails
   fast instead of producing a confusing build-time error.

Also adds `ELIZAOS_ARCH: ${{ matrix.arch }}` to the job-level env so
every step sees it without per-step plumbing. build.sh (post-#7971)
reads this and drives docker --platform + TARGETARCH off it.

Emulated arm64 builds run 3-5× slower than native. The amd64 nightly
already takes ~1 hour, so an arm64 emulated build is likely 3-5 hours;
the existing 110-min timeout will need a bump later (followed up
separately to keep this PR focused on the matrix). For now the build
will time out before completing, which `continue-on-error` swallows.

riscv64 is deliberately NOT in this PR — gated on Shaw's
electrobun-riscv64 enablement patches landing first, since a riscv64
ISO without a working userspace agent has no end-user value.

   common-deps RUN (debootstrap, cpio, xorriso, grub2-common, …) and a
   per-arch bootloader RUN whose case statement installs:

     - arm64:   grub-efi-arm64-bin  (UEFI-only; arm64 has no BIOS)

  be `continue-on-error: true` initially so amd64 nightly stays green

Live regression: 2026-05-25 04:48-04:52 UTC. A "make me a 1-page PDF
fresh-test.pdf containing hello pdf" sub-agent task succeeded (PDF was
actually created and verified), but the sub-agent's task report
included incidental `http://127.0.0.1:6900/apps/` curl probes it had
run while diagnosing whether a build was deployed. Those internal URLs
leaked into Discord across THREE separate task_complete events:

   There's no evidence the Python "hello world" script ran or that
   the fresh-test.pdf was generated - those builds likely didn't
   complete."
- "The checks show: http://127.0.0.1:6900/apps/ -> HTTP 404 Not Found
   https://nubili.org/ (and the shortened https://nubili/) -> DNS
   resolution failed (curl exit code 6)"
- "Confirmed the HTTP checks: http://127.0.0.1:6900/apps/ returned 404
   Not Found, and https://nubili could not be resolved (curl error 6)."

Three problems compounded:
1. Internal URLs (127.0.0.1) reached the public Discord channel - user
   can't reach a loopback address from their machine and seeing it
   makes the bot look broken.
2. The orchestrator's verify-retry detector counted the 127.0.0.1
   probe as a "dead URL" (it 404'd from the probe's POV too), triggered
   `retryIncompleteBuild`, which re-dispatched a fresh sub-agent that
   mentioned the same loopback URL in its own report - cascade.
3. The original PDF was successful but the user saw three error
   messages instead of one success.

port and path) from the sub-agent's task report text just before the
parent agent renders the reply. Defense-in-depth at the
sub-agent-router boundary, where the synthetic inbound message is
built. The URL-verification pipeline itself is unchanged - loopback
verification stays valid in legitimate dev-app workflows where a sub-
agent intentionally probes a local dev URL to confirm the build runs.
This change only affects the OUTGOING user-facing text.

Implementation:
- New `redactLoopbackUrls(text)` helper next to `isLoopbackUrl()`.
- Pattern matches `http(s)://(localhost|127.x.x.x|[::1]):<port>/path`
  case-insensitive.
- Post-strip cleanup drops orphan punctuation lines that become
  dangling list bullets after the URL is removed.
- Applied at sub-agent-router.ts line 539 (the single point where
  `baseText` becomes user-visible `text`).

      "candidateActions": ["BASH"],

and "what files are in /tmp right now". The model claimed simple-path

rule hard. This commit adds a structural backup at the routing layer:
when candidateActions names at least one tool AND no non-simple
context is selected, promote to planning_needed with contexts=["general"]
the same way `requiresTool=true` already does. The planner then runs
the tool, the user gets the real result.

that already lives in parseMessageHandlerOutput
(packages/core/src/runtime/message-handler.ts:82-83) where
candidateActions already drives the "blank out refusal text on planning

When the user clicks "SIGN IN WITH ELIZA CLOUD" the button changes to
"WAITING FOR AUTH..." and the renderer calls openExternalUrl(browserUrl)
to open the verification URL. If that auto-open silently fails the user
is stuck on the spinner with no path forward.

Repro 2026-05-25 in QEMU running the live ISO:
- POST /api/cloud/login returns 201 with
  {sessionId, browserUrl: "https://www.elizacloud.ai/auth/cli-login?session=<uuid>"}
- handleCloudLogin calls openExternalUrl(browserUrl)
- Tails routes xdg-open through gtk-launch to the Tor Browser flatpak
- The flatpak spawn succeeds (returns "ok"), no exception is thrown
- The renderer's catch-block doesn't fire, no fallback error is shown
- The user sees "WAITING FOR AUTH..." forever; no browser window ever
  surfaces because Tor Browser is hanging behind the scenes (Tor never
  bootstraps in NAT environments, or the flatpak is mid-startup, etc.)

npm login, stripe login) handles by always printing the verification
URL + code: the auto-open is a bonus, the manual link is the contract.
