fix(os/linux): self-recover from stuck persistence-maintenance flag

The user-visible symptom is "I click the elizaOS app and nothing
happens". Reproduced 2026-05-25 in QEMU after a session restart: the
gate at /run/elizaos/persistence-maintenance stays set forever, so
elizaos-{agent,renderer,pill,milady}.service all skip start (their
unit files have `ConditionPathExists=!/run/elizaos/persistence-maintenance`).
Only recovery was `sudo /usr/local/lib/elizaos/persistence-maintenance
leave` from a terminal.

Root cause (two cooperating bugs):

1. /etc/gdm3/PostLogin/Default sets the flag with
   `persistence-maintenance enter || true` whenever the greeter's
   create-persistent-storage box is checked, and relies on the
   downstream create-persistent-storage-session (which has a proper
   `trap cleanup EXIT` calling `leave`) to clear it. If that downstream
   never runs (wizard crash, user cancels at greeter without unchecking
   the persist box, GDM restart mid-wizard, SIGKILL of the session) the
   flag stays forever.

2. The PostLogin "else" branch (greeter create-persistence NOT checked)
   does a raw `rm -f /run/elizaos/persistence-maintenance` to clear any
   leftover flag from a prior boot. That clears the gate but leaves the
   elizaos units in whatever stopped state the prior boot's `enter` had
   killed them into — `leave` would `reset-failed` and `start --no-block`
   the four units, raw `rm` does not.

Fix has two parts:

A. elizaos-keeper gains an auto-leave watchdog. Every tick (default
   5s), if maintenance_flag is held AND no user-session persistence
   wizard is active (user_persistence_flag absent) AND the flag's mtime
   is older than `ELIZAOS_KEEPER_STALE_FLAG_SECONDS` (default 120s),
   call `persistence-maintenance leave` to recover. 120s covers GDM
   login + user-session startup + wizard autostart with plenty of slack;
   a flag still held past that with no wizard active is by definition
   abandoned. The watchdog deliberately does not touch the
   user_persistence_flag — that's the wizard's own enter/leave dance and
   racing it would break clean persistence creation. Threshold and
   interval are env-overridable for debugging.

B. /etc/gdm3/PostLogin/Default's else branch now calls
   `persistence-maintenance leave` (with a `[ -x ... ]` guard and
   `|| true` so login never blocks on it) instead of raw `rm`. This
   makes the "user did not check create-persistence" path also restart
   any units the prior boot left stopped, not just clear the gate.

Watching this in journal:
    journalctl -t elizaos-keeper

fix(os/linux): route docs launcher file:// URIs around Tor Browser flatpak sandbox

The "elizaOS Documentation" launcher (`tails-documentation.desktop` →
`/usr/local/bin/tails-documentation doc`) opens
`file:///usr/share/doc/elizaos/website/doc.en.html` via
`gtk-abspath-launch` → `org.boum.tails.TorBrowser.desktop`. The desktop
file falls back to `tails-run-tor-browser-in-flatpak`, so the URI gets
loaded in Tor Browser running inside a flatpak sandbox. The sandbox has
no read access to /usr/share/doc/, so Tor Browser renders a
"Problem loading page — Access to the file was denied — The file at
/usr/share/doc/elizaos/website/doc.en.html is not readable" error page.

Reproduced 2026-05-25 in QEMU with screenshot proof:
- Window list (gnome-shell D-Bus): `Tor Browser` titled `Problem loading
  page — Tor Browser`
- Journal: `gtk-abspath-launch: Call failed: The name
  org.boum.tails.TorBrowser was not provided by any .service files`,
  then `sudo[]: amnesia : COMMAND=/usr/local/lib/tails-run-tor-browser-in-flatpak`
- The error page is "Access to the file was denied — The file at
  /usr/share/doc/elizaos/website/doc.en.html is not readable. It may
  have been removed, moved, or file permissions may be preventing
  access." Plus the system notification "System was put in unsafe mode
  — Apps now have unrestricted access" (the flatpak portal's downgrade
  path is unrelated and does not grant /usr/share/doc/).

The file IS present and readable (root:root 0644, 3417 bytes). The
sandbox is the problem.

Fix: in `tails-documentation`, route `file://` URIs to
`/usr/local/lib/elizaos/elizaos-webkit-shell` instead. That shell is
the same WebKit2GTK widget the main Milady app uses, runs as the
amnesia user, and has full file:// access — no sandbox restrictions.
Remote https:// URIs continue to use Tor Browser so external
documentation links keep their privacy guarantee.

This is the minimum-blast-radius fix: it does not weaken the Tor
Browser sandbox, does not add a new browser dependency (the shell is
already installed and the same WebKit version powers the main app),
and leaves the online-docs codepath unchanged.

fix(app-core,plugin-elizacloud): break Bun strict-ESM circular-import TDZ cascade

elizaOS Live USB symptom: Electrobun shell showed "Backend Timeout" and
/api/auth/status never came up. Root cause was a TDZ cascade triggered by
the agent → app-core → agent import cycle on Bun's strict ESM evaluator.

Each fix in this commit is documented at the patch site with the same
explanatory block, since they're all instances of the same pattern.

1. services/vault-bootstrap.ts — primary fix
   Was: `import { ... } from "@elizaos/agent"` (closes a cycle agent →
        app-core/vault-bootstrap → agent at module-top time)
   Now: types-only import + lazy `agentBridge()` getter using dynamic
        `import("@elizaos/agent")` resolved once and cached. The dynamic
        import defers the cycle closure until after both modules have
        fully evaluated, breaking the partial-eval re-entry path.

2. services/vault-mirror.ts — defensive
   Was: `let cachedManager: SecretsManager | null = null`
        TDZ-prone: any future caller during partial-eval would throw
        "Cannot access 'cachedManager' before initialization".
   Now: module-top `var state = { manager: null }` + a self-heal guard
        in sharedSecretsManager(). var hoists the slot to undefined
        before any executable line runs; the self-heal initializes the
        container if a future cycle re-enters before the assignment.

3. registry/index.ts — same pattern
   Was: `let cache: LoadedRegistry | null = null` (same TDZ pattern)
   Now: `var cacheSlot: { value: LoadedRegistry | null } = ...` +
        self-heal. Symptom path: vault-bootstrap → sensitiveKeysFromRegistry
        → loadRegistry hit TDZ on `cache`.

4. security/hydrate-wallet-keys-from-platform-store.ts — same pattern
   Was: module-top `const WALLET_VAULT_KEYS = [...]` and
        `const STEWARD_OS_PAIRS = [...]` referenced by async functions
        called on the boot path. TDZ via the same circular path.
   Now: function getters that build the literal at call time. Same
        idiom used elsewhere in this codebase (see existing
        isEnvVarKey() in vault-bootstrap.ts:55 with comment block
        explaining the Bun.build __esm wrapper variant of this bug).

5. plugins/plugin-elizacloud/src/routes/cloud-provisioning.ts — local def
   Was: `export { isCloudProvisionedContainer } from "@elizaos/shared"` —
        but @elizaos/shared/dist/ has no such export. Bun's strict ESM
        linker rejected the chain at startup with
        "SyntaxError: export 'isCloudProvisionedContainer' not found
        in '@elizaos/shared'".
   Now: local function definition with the same shape (ELIZA_CLOUD_PROVISIONED
        gate + steward/api-token/cloud-api-key fallback). Consumers
        (agent/src/api/{auth,health,server,server-auth,server-helpers-auth,
        onboarding,static-file-server}.ts) already import from
        @elizaos/plugin-elizacloud, so no consumer changes needed.

Smoke evidence (ISO #8, amd64 milady-tails build):
- Agent process binds 127.0.0.1:31337 cleanly
- /api/auth/status → 200, /api/health → 200 (ready=true, plugins.loaded=20,
  failed=0), /api/runtime → 200 (160 actions, 58 providers, 29 services),
  /api/agents → 200 (Eliza running)
- Zero "Fatal error", "ReferenceError", "Cannot access ... before
  initialization", or "SyntaxError" in 18 minutes of journal
- Renderer (port 5174) → agent (31337) proxy works end-to-end
- Milady Electrobun onboarding wizard renders and advances

fix(plugin-sql): emit USING clause for character-varying→uuid migrations

The runtime migrator's checkIfNeedsUsingClause matched only the "varchar"
spelling, but Postgres introspection reports the canonical "character
varying". So an existing varchar/character-varying column migrated to uuid
produced `ALTER COLUMN id SET DATA TYPE uuid` with no USING clause, which
Postgres rejects ("cannot be cast automatically") — failing the migration
on every boot against a database that predates the uuid id schema.

Normalize "character varying" → "varchar" before the conversion-pair
lookup so the existing varchar→uuid (and varchar→integer/numeric/boolean/
jsonb) pairs match the introspected type, emitting
`ALTER COLUMN id TYPE uuid USING "id"::text::uuid`.

Adds a regression test (varchar→uuid with UUID-string data) to
03-type-changes-with-data.real.test.ts.

fix(core): expose actionStateProvider in every context, not just general

actionStateProvider surfaces previous action results to the planner so
the LLM can see what just ran and advance to the next step in a multi-
step chain. It was contextGated on 'general' only.

When a turn engages a non-'general' context like 'code' or 'tasks'
(e.g. orchestrator TASKS: provision_workspace -> spawn_agent ->
submit_workspace), the provider stops firing. Each subsequent planner
turn has zero memory of the just-executed step and keeps re-picking
the first op until the repeated-failure limit hits and the run times
out.

Drop the context gate. Previous results are context-agnostic - every
planner turn following a tool call needs them regardless of which
context is engaged.

fix(core): drop unknown top-level planner args before strict validation

PLAN_ACTIONS exposes wrapper-only protocol fields (notably `subaction`
for router-style actions). The unwrap layer in planner-loop.ts forwards
them through alongside the action's real parameters, so a PLAN_ACTIONS
call shaped like:

  { action: "TASKS", subaction: "provision_workspace",
    parameters: { op: "provision_workspace", repo: "..." } }

arrives at executePlannedToolCall with `subaction` in the args bag.
Actions whose schemas do not declare `subaction` (e.g. TASKS uses
`action`/`op`) crash strict validation with "Unexpected argument
'subaction'" on every dispatch, and the planner runtime retries until
the repeated-failure limit fires.

Filter unknown top-level args against the action's parameter schema
before handing off to validateToolArgs. Action invariants stay strict
for known fields; unknown wrapper fields are dropped with a debug log
naming them. Same guard absorbs any future LLM-hallucinated extra field
without polluting per-action schemas.

fix(orch): forward GITHUB_TOKEN to git-workspace-service when caller omits userCredentials

CodingWorkspaceService.provisionWorkspace only forwards credentials to
git-workspace-service when the caller passes them in options.userCredentials.
Every dispatch from the orchestrator planner arrives without that field
(TASKS.handler does not synthesize one), so the underlying clone fires
unauthenticated against private or yet-to-be-created repos and throws:

fix(roles): re-fire ensureOwnerRole on WORLD_JOINED/WORLD_CONNECTED

rolesPlugin.init() runs before any connector (Discord/Telegram/etc.) has
populated runtime.worlds. ensureOwnerRole then sees an empty worlds set,
returns true (the for-loop is empty - no error, no role applied), and the
scheduled retry tail fires three times within ~10s. On a slow connector
boot the worlds still are not present at the final retry, so the owner
role never lands in world metadata.

resolveStage1SenderRole then falls back to USER (rank 2) for the owner
forever. Every ADMIN-gated context (tasks, code, automation, connectors,
agent_internal) is hidden from the Stage 1 planner. Higher-tier actions
like the orchestrator's TASKS surface stay invisible to the LLM, so the
planner can never dispatch them.

Hook WORLD_JOINED + WORLD_CONNECTED so the bootstrap re-fires the moment
the first connector world appears, regardless of how the initial retry
timing lined up. The fix is idempotent - ensureOwnerRole rewrites world
metadata in-place under updateWorldMetadata, which short-circuits when
nothing changes.

fix(cloud-api): handle tool_choice: "required" in mapToolChoice without crashing (#7992)

* fix(cloud-api): handle tool_choice: "required" in mapToolChoice without crashing

`mapToolChoice` advertises a return type that includes `"required"`, but
the implementation only early-returns on `"auto"` and `"none"`. When the
caller passes `"required"` (a valid OpenAI-API value, and the value the
elizaOS planner sends in `@elizaos/core/src/services/message.ts` for
forced-tool turns — RESPONSE_HANDLER, PLAN_ACTIONS, facts/relationships,
etc.), execution falls through to `toolChoice.function.name`. Because
`"required"` is a string, `"required".function` is `undefined`, and
`.name` of undefined throws:

  Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')

The route's outer try/catch then wraps this into a HTTP 500 with body:

  {"error":{"message":"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')",
   "type":"api_error"}}

which is exactly what a 2PM/Milady agent run on `ghcr.io/2-a-m/2pm:latest`
hits on every DM that triggers the planner. Models confirmed independent:
both `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` and `openai/gpt-4o` reproduce. After
the failure the v5 runtime falls back to a no-tools retry (TEXT_LARGE
without `tool_choice`) which succeeds, so the agent replies in plain
text but never dispatches any action. The 2PM build at GHCR digest
sha256:0ace6d1bb812... + commit-level instrumentation in plugin-elizacloud
(milady-2pm-debug stderr writes around every await) localized the throw
to the cloud's `/chat/completions` route after a clean 500 response —
not the plugin's request/response handling, which is correct.

Reproducible with:

  curl -sS https://api.elizaos.ai/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":50,"tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"x","parameters":{"type":"object"}}}],"tool_choice":"required"}'

Fix:
  1. `mapToolChoice`: add `"required"` to the early-return list so the
     value passes through to the AI SDK unchanged (the AI SDK already
     accepts `"required"` natively per ai-sdk.dev/docs/foundations/tools).
  2. `ChatRequest.tool_choice` input type: add `"required"` to the
     accepted union so TS-typed callers (including the AI SDK + the
     elizaOS planner upstream) compile clean.

tj-c227b5bbff288a / tj-d5e298b2542aa0). Stage 1 produced the
self-contradictory envelope:

    {
      "contexts": ["simple"],
      "requiresTool": false,
      "candidateActions": ["BASH"],
      "replyText": "On it."
    }

for prompts like "find files in /etc that contain the word hostname"
and "what files are in /tmp right now". The model claimed simple-path
(no planner needed) while ALSO naming a specific exposed tool (BASH)
that would fulfill the request. Both flags cannot be true at the same
time - candidateActions is a concrete reference to a tool, not a
suggestion. routeMessageHandlerOutput honored the simple-path flag,
delivered "On it." as the final reply, and the user got a bare ack
with no follow-up - the planner never ran.

The Stage-1 prompt rule that bans bare-ack on simple-path
(packages/prompts/src/index.ts, "simple-path replyText must be
non-empty, must directly answer the question, and must not be a
bare acknowledgement that promises work without doing it") is a soft
contract the model occasionally violates - we can't make a prompt
rule hard. This commit adds a structural backup at the routing layer:
when candidateActions names at least one tool AND no non-simple
context is selected, promote to planning_needed with contexts=["general"]
the same way `requiresTool=true` already does. The planner then runs
the tool, the user gets the real result.

This is the routing analogue of the parser-side `planningPath` heuristic
that already lives in parseMessageHandlerOutput
(packages/core/src/runtime/message-handler.ts:82-83) where
candidateActions already drives the "blank out refusal text on planning
path" decision. The two places now agree.

- "The checks show: http://127.0.0.1:6900/apps/ -> HTTP 404 Not Found

- "Confirmed the HTTP checks: http://127.0.0.1:6900/apps/ returned 404

- Pattern matches `http(s)://(localhost|127.x.x.x|[::1]):<port>/path`

fix(prompts): forbid empty + bare-ack replyText on simple-path; clarify interim-ack contract

Live deepscan of 50 probes on 2026-05-25 surfaced four trajectory shapes
where Stage 1 produced a non-answer reply text on simple-path
(simple=true, requiresTool=false), with no planner iteration to follow
up. The user saw a phantom acknowledgement and the bot did nothing.

- Probe 20 ("what directory are you running in") -> simple=true, reply
  "On it." -> iters=0 tools=0 -> user got nothing real.
- Probe 21 ("how many cpu cores does this machine have") -> simple=true,
  reply "On it." -> iters=0 tools=0 -> same.
- Probe 22 ("list the top-level dirs in /home/milady") -> simple=true,
  reply="" (empty string) -> bot posted literally nothing.
  trajectory tj-f61e23c88bdcbc.json.
- Probe 50 ("make me a pdf with 3 pages about elizaOS history") ->
  simple=true, reply "Spawning the sub-agent now." -> iters=0 tools=0 ->
  user waited forever for a non-existent sub-agent.

The fix is structural: tighten the simple-path replyText contract so the
model treats simple=true as "this reply IS the complete answer," not "I
will get back to you." Bare acknowledgements like "On it.", "Sure.",
"Got it, working on that.", "Spawning the sub-agent now.", "One sec.",
"Let me handle that." are not answers - they are promises of in-flight
action that never arrives, because simple=true means no planner
iteration will run.

Crucially: interim acks are perfectly fine on the NON-simple path. The
contract is now stated explicitly in the rule body:
- simple=true => "this reply is the complete answer"
- simple=false + requiresTool=true => "this reply is the interim ack,
  the planner will deliver the real result."

feat(cloud-billing): wire signed waifu webhook emit for the credit money path

Eliza Cloud is the metered billing rail under a hosted waifu agent. Waifu
already exposed signed receivers for credit and inference events, but the emit
side was missing: nothing actually POSTed the credit signals back, and the one
existing provision-complete callback was unsigned so waifu rejected it with a
401.

This adds the emit side in the monorepo cloud package and closes the seam:

- new packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services/waifu-webhook.ts: a signed emitter
  that matches waifu's receiver contract exactly. It computes an HMAC-SHA256
  over the timestamp and raw body, sends it in the X-Waifu-Webhook-Signature
  header, includes a stable idempotencyKey for replay protection, and routes
  per event kind to the credits or inference receiver. It resolves its target
  from the environment and no-ops cleanly when unconfigured, so non-waifu orgs
  and local or CI environments are unaffected. It never throws, so a webhook
  delivery problem can never block the billing path.
- credits.ts: after a successful deduction crosses the low or depleted
  threshold, emit credits.low or credits.depleted to waifu so a hosted agent
  can downgrade its model tier or pause itself. Fire-and-forget alongside the
  existing low-credits email.
- provisioning-jobs.ts: sign the provision-complete callback with the waifu
  envelope so the receiver accepts it instead of returning 401.
- classifyCreditBalance: pure threshold mapping shared by the billing path so
  the money-path decision is unit-testable without a database.

Tests: packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services/waifu-webhook.test.ts (13 tests,
all passing) lock the signing contract recomputed byte-for-byte against waifu's
own scheme, per-kind receiver routing, idempotency key presence, clean no-op
when unconfigured, never-throw on delivery error, the credit-status threshold
mapping, and the credit and inference payload shapes.

Scope note: this wires the credit-state money-path emit (low and depleted) and
the signed provision callback. The high-volume per-call inference.spent emit
helper is provided and tested but left unwired by design, since per-inference
metering is the separate metering workstream.

Re-homed from the wrong repo (RemilioNubilio/cloud PR #1, an old Next.js
app/api layout) into the correct monorepo cloud package
(packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services). The code was adapted from the
@/lib/* alias to the relative imports used by this package; the HMAC contract
is unchanged and still matches waifu's receiver byte-for-byte.

feat(plugin-elizacloud): forward per-inference spend to waifu burn meter

Hosted waifu agents run as sandboxed containers whose model inference is
routed through the Eliza Cloud metered inference gateway. The gateway is the
honest meter: it owns the per-model pricing table and platform markup and
debits the organization credit balance on every call. That debit already
happens server side and is authoritative.

What was missing was the signal back to waifu. The waifu burn rollup reads
inference.spent agent events to compute daily burn and runway, but fell back
to a 5 USD per day placeholder when no such events existed because nothing
emitted them.

This adds a waifu metering bridge that listens for the runtime MODEL_USED
event (emitted by the cloud model handlers after each inference) and POSTs a
signed inference.spent webhook to waifu. It is a no-op unless the container is
provisioned with the waifu metering env knobs, so it never fires for local or
standalone agents.

Token counts are exact (reported by the gateway). USD is the authoritative
post markup cost when the gateway surfaces it (usage.cost_usd or the
X-Eliza-Cost-Usd response header); otherwise a conservative, configurable
token based estimate is used. The credit debit itself remains the cloud
authoritative number; the estimate only affects waifu burn display until the
cloud cost is wired through.

- events.ts: carry resolved model id and optional gateway cost on MODEL_USED
- text.ts: pass model name and parse gateway cost from inference responses
- waifu-metering.ts: config resolution, HMAC signing, payload build, POST
- index.ts: register the MODEL_USED handler
- unit tests cover config gating, signing, estimate vs gateway cost, idempotency

   as cloud burn, billing free inference as paid. The handler now meters only

   safely derives the sibling /inference path from a known /credits URL, and
   never reuses a non-inference URL.

fix(orchestrator): allow read-only webfetch in opencode spawn config

opencode's webfetch permission defaults to "ask". Under the acpx "standard"
approval preset (which answers non-interactive permission prompts with "deny"),
a spawned sub-agent's web fetch is silently denied, so the model — unable to
reach the network — tends to confabulate an answer instead of fetching live
data. Allow the read-only webfetch GET (opencode caps the body at 5MB and never
mutates the workspace) so sub-agents can retrieve real live data on any
provider, without granting write/exec (bash, edit) permissions, which stay
gated by the approval preset.

screen.

crash. Unit tests cover allowLoopback and the loopback recovery path.

fix(agent-image): add zod + eager-boot externals to Dockerfile.ci runtime deps

The CI agent image crashes on boot with:
  Cannot find package 'zod' imported from
  /app/packages/core/dist/node/index.node.js
(exit 1, before any agent code runs). This affects the :develop image
and every new build; it is a pre-existing packaging regression.

Root cause: packages/app-core/deploy/Dockerfile.ci installs a hardcoded
allowlist of runtime deps into /app/node_modules. .dockerignore excludes
**/node_modules, so the ONLY runtime deps in the final image are this
allowlist plus relinked workspace packages plus whatever the dist bundles
inline. packages/core/dist/node/index.node.js third-partyises zod
(build.ts nodeExternals) and imports it eagerly (35 static top-level
imports). zod was missing from the allowlist, so it never landed in the
image and the container crashed on the very first module load.

Fix part 1: add zod@4.4.3 (matches packages/core/package.json ^4.4.3,
provides the ./v3 and ./v4 subpath exports core imports).

Fix part 2 (audit, so the next boot does not hit a different missing
dep): packages/agent/dist is transpiled with tsc (NOT bundled), so every
bare import stays third-party. Traced the eager boot path
(runtime/eliza.js dynamically imports api/server.js, whose static import
graph loads eagerly at module-eval). Beyond zod, that graph pulls in
non-allowlist third-partys that would each be the next hard crash:
  hono           <- api/hono-adapter (HTTP server)
  json5          <- config/config
  @noble/curves  <- api/wallet (secp256k1)
  ethers         <- api/wallet
  esbuild        <- services/plugin-compiler (via workbench routes)
  isomorphic-git <- services/vfs-git
Added all of these (plus @noble/hashes, a curves dep, for safety) to
both the npm install list and the rm -rf pre-clean list. Versions track
the declarations in packages/agent/package.json. Verified the set
installs together cleanly and each entry imports without error
(zod/v3, zod/v4 and @noble/curves/secp256k1.js subpaths resolve).

The allowlist is hand-maintained and brittle; documented the boot-path
reasoning in the Dockerfile and flagged deriving it from the workspace
dist third-partys as follow-up.

Does not touch the entrypoint or agent logic; dependency packaging only.

fix(agent-image): derive runtime deps closure instead of hand-maintaining

The agent CI image links a fixed set of workspace packages into
/app/node_modules. Several of those packages are transpiled (tsc, not
bundled), so their bare third-party imports stay third-party and must resolve from
node_modules at runtime. The image used to install a hand-maintained
allowlist of those third-partys, which had to be extended by hand every time a
newly-linked package introduced a new dependency. Each omission was a hard
boot crash ("Cannot find package '<dep>' imported from
/app/packages/<pkg>/dist/..."), and we hit a string of them (zod, then
@elizaos/core, then chalk).

Replace the hand-maintained list with a derived one. A new script,
collect-docker-runtime-deps.mjs, reads the declared dependencies of every
workspace package that gets linked into the image, drops the @elizaos/*
workspace entries (those are linked, not installed), and emits the union
pinned to the versions the workspace lockfile resolves. npm install then
pulls the full transitive closure automatically. This ends the whole class
of one-dep-at-a-time boot-crash loops: every dependency a linked package
declares is present, so the image boots and any character config can load
any bundled plugin without a missing-module crash.

Details:
- Versions are pinned from bun.lock for reproducibility, falling back to the
  declared range when a package is not in the lockfile.
- Pure browser/UI packages (notably @elizaos/ui and its radix/three/recharts
  tree) are excluded in the script: they are linked for module-resolution
  integrity but never imported by the headless server runtime, so installing
  their frontend deps would only bloat the image.
- --legacy-peer-deps is added to the npm install: the broad closure includes
  packages with conflicting optional peer ranges (e.g. the discord.js voice
  stack's opusscript peer), which a flat registry install would otherwise
  reject. This matches how the workspace install hoists/resolves them.

Verified locally that npm install resolves the full closure cleanly
(1055 packages) with --legacy-peer-deps.

feat(agent): accept X-Server-Token on inbound auth so cloud gateways can route messages

The cloud Discord and webhook gateways forward inbound platform messages to a
provisioned container's POST /agents/:id/message endpoint and attach the shared
service secret as an X-Server-Token header (only when AGENT_SERVER_SHARED_SECRET
is configured). The container runtime in packages/agent previously authorized
that endpoint only via a trusted-loopback request or a Bearer token matching the
per-agent inbound API token, so a real gateway-routed message returned 401.

Teach the agent server's isAuthorized path to also accept a request whose
X-Server-Token header matches AGENT_SERVER_SHARED_SECRET, mirroring the existing
Kubernetes agent-server contract. The shared-secret check runs after the
trusted-local short-circuit and before the Bearer check, using a constant-time
comparison. When AGENT_SERVER_SHARED_SECRET is unset the header carries no
authority and existing Bearer and loopback auth are unchanged, so there is no
regression for deployments that never configure it.

Inject AGENT_SERVER_SHARED_SECRET into the provisioned container's base
environment so the container can validate the header. The value is sourced from
an explicit per-deployment entry in the sandbox environment vars when present,
otherwise from the daemon's own AGENT_SERVER_SHARED_SECRET (the same value the
gateways read), so both ends share one secret without extra configuration. When
neither is set the variable is omitted and the X-Server-Token path stays
disabled.

Add X-Server-Token to the CORS allowed-headers list and cover the new auth path
with unit tests: a matching token authorizes, a wrong or missing token is
rejected, an unset or whitespace secret disables the path, and existing Bearer
auth continues to work alongside it.

fix(core): decide complete-direct-reply preference structurally, not by user-intent regex

`shouldPreferCompleteDirectReply` decided whether a finished model reply should
win over force-injected planning by scanning the user's message with five intent
regexes (looksLikeCodingWork / WebSearch / LocalShell / ActionExplanation /
CreativeWriting). `looksLikeCodingWorkRequest` matches any "app" near "build", so
a complete one-sentence answer to a question like "what are your app-build
routing rules? ... do not build anything" was force-planned into a redundant
sub-agent spawn.

Decide on structure instead, using signals the function already computes: a
complete substantive reply (not ack / progress / refusal / empty, via
`looksLikeCompleteDirectReply`) plus only weak/injectable planning signals
(simple|general context + search/shell/spawn-class candidates, via
`hasOnlyWeakDirectReplyPlanningSignals`) wins directly. The Stage-1 inference
backstop still plans genuine web/shell/build turns, because those return an
ack/empty/refusal reply that fails `looksLikeCompleteDirectReply` — so no
behavior is lost, only the substring false-positive is removed.

The five `looksLikeX` predicates remain in use by the inference/recovery paths;
this only removes their misuse as a user-intent classifier in the direct-reply
decision. Adds regression tests: a complete reply answers directly even when a
coding-class candidate is force-injected; an ack-only build ask still plans.

`bridgeUrl` as a raw container address (http://<ip>:<port>) that the browser

server-provided web UI URL when present (future-proof); otherwise derive the
apex from the cloud control-plane host the client provisioned against; fall back
to the raw bridgeUrl only for local-dev clouds that have no public gateway.

`resolveCloudAgentApiBase` is a pure exported function with a unit regression
matrix (derivation from www./api./apex bases, server-URL preference,
never-pin-raw-IP, local-dev fallback).

feat(cloud): fleet-upgrade reconciler — blue/green swap onto the deployed image

Today a new agent image only reaches the fleet when an individual agent
crashes or is manually restarted, so the cluster runs a mix of image
versions until everyone naturally cycles. This wires up a real fleet
rollout: when the registry-side digest of the configured agent tag
moves, the daemon enqueues a blue/green `agent_upgrade` job per running
agent still on the old digest, capped at 3 in flight.

Each upgrade is cross-node blue/green:

  1. Probe `containersEnv.defaultAgentImage()` against ghcr.io and read
     the manifest digest. Null (non-ghcr image, registry down) means
     skip the cycle — the agent stays on its current image.
  2. Pick a target node != current via `excludeNodeId` (container names
     are deterministic `agent-${id}` per docker daemon, so blue must
     live on a different host than old). The autoscaler-on-demand path
     fires automatically if no other node has capacity.
  3. Provision blue, health-check it. If it doesn't come up, tear it
     down — the agent keeps running on the old container with the old
     image. Auto-rollback, no operator intervention.
  4. Atomic UPDATE on `agent_sandboxes`: swap bridge_url, health_url,
     node_id, container_name, ports, docker_image, image_digest. New
     HTTP requests hit blue from this point on. UPDATE failure tears
     down blue so the swap doesn't leak ports + allocated_count.
  5. `docker stop -t 30` on old (SIGTERM drain for in-flight requests
     and websockets), then `docker rm -f`. Allocated_count decremented
     on the old node.

The autoscaler's existing idle-node drain cleans up nodes that empty
out as agents rebalance — no new cleanup loop needed.

Reconciler runs on the 30s `pollCycle` (alongside heartbeat), not the
5-min infra-maintenance cycle, so a push reaches the fleet within ~30s
of `docker pull`-ability.

Schema: new `image_digest text` column on `agent_sandboxes`. Stamped at
provision time via `resolveImageDigest()` on the provisioner metadata
path. NULL on rows that predate this PR is treated as "differs from
target" — the first rollout after this ships sweeps the existing fleet
onto the current digest, after which the registry-vs-stored compare is
exact.

boundaries, URL escaping for tags/repos with special characters, 404 /
5xx / network-error handling, only-ghcr policy, negative caching, cache
lifecycle across heterogeneous refs) and a smoke test on the job-type
registry.

fix(desktop): stop the renderer diagnostic mirror warning on 404

The Electrobun renderer log mirror reported every non-OK fetch/XHR — including

application-handled status (e.g. probing a runtime-plugin route like

optional-resource check), so warning on it is false-positive noise that
pollutes an otherwise clean startup log.

app's own error handling is unchanged.

in diagnostic-format.ts (which exists specifically so these helpers can be
unit-tested without pulling in Electrobun native bindings), removing the
duplicated status logic across the two wrappers. Add diagnostic-format.test.ts
asserting 404 is the ONLY suppressed status — 5xx still errors, every other 4xx
(401/403/410/429) still warns — so the behavior is reviewer-checkable without a
GUI boot. Regenerated preload.js from source.

* feat(cloud): container self-registers + boots as its character (Path A fix #1)

Provisioned Hetzner containers were orphaned compute: the published image
entrypoint runs packages/agent/dist/bin.js, whose runtime has zero
sandbox-registry code, so the 5 injected SANDBOX_REGISTRY_* env vars were
never consumed and the container never wrote agent:<id>:server /
server:<name>:url to Upstash. It also booted as the generic "Eliza" preset
because the assigned character was never loaded.

This wires the container self-registration + character load into the agent
runtime (the actual entrypoint), feature-flagged by env presence:

- New packages/agent/src/runtime/sandbox-registry.ts: a dependency-free
  (Upstash REST via fetch, no @upstash/redis SDK) backport of app-core's
  SandboxRegistry. agent cannot import app-core without an agent->app-core
  ->agent workspace cycle, so the app-core copy never runs in a container.
  buildSandboxRegistryFromEnv() returns null unless all 5 SANDBOX_REGISTRY_*
  vars are present, so it is inert for every non-provisioned runtime.

- startEliza server-only mode now registers + heartbeats (30s) and
  unregisters on graceful shutdown.

- New packages/agent/src/runtime/sandbox-character.ts: reads
  ELIZA_AGENT_CHARACTER_JSON and merges the injected character onto
  config.agents.list[0] before buildCharacterFromConfig, so the container
  boots AS its character (e.g. "Nyx"). No-op when the var is absent.

- Provisioner side: docker-sandbox-provider injects ELIZA_AGENT_CHARACTER_JSON
  from the agent_sandboxes.agent_config row (passed through the new optional
  SandboxCreateConfig.agentConfig field by eliza-sandbox). JSON.stringify
  output contains no control chars, so it passes validateEnvValue.

Feature-flag/blast-radius: both paths are gated on env presence, so the
working in-worker agent and every non-provisioned runtime are unaffected.

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>

* feat(cloud): gateway routes to container via registry + kill K8s wakeServer (Path A fix #2/#3)

Routing-id correctness (prerequisite): the gateways resolve and address an
agent by its platform character_id (agent:<characterId>:server +
/agents/<characterId>/message), but the container registered under, and ran
as, the sandbox id. Fixed end to end:
- New SANDBOX_ROUTE_AGENT_ID env (= agent_sandboxes.character_id), injected by
  the provisioner via the new SandboxCreateConfig.routeAgentId field.
- sandbox-registry keys on SANDBOX_ROUTE_AGENT_ID (falls back to SANDBOX_AGENT_ID).
- sandbox-character pins the runtime character.id to the route id, so the
  container's /agents/:id/message identity check passes.

container when resolveAgentServer returns a route, and FALLS BACK to the
in-worker CF path (forwardEvent -> /api/internal/discord/events) when no key
exists. Previously a missing route silently dropped the message. This is the
feature flag for container routing: only agents whose container has
self-registered are routed to the container; every other agent (incl. the
working in-worker agent that never registers) keeps the proven in-worker path.
Removing the registry key reverts an agent to in-worker with no redeploy.

Fix #3 (kill K8s wakeServer landmine): wakeServer now no-ops for direct
host:port server URLs (the Hetzner container model) before touching the K8s
service-account token / Deployment scale PATCH. The gateways run on Railway,
not K8s; Hetzner containers are already up under the provisioning daemon.
getHashTargets already short-circuits direct (non-.svc) URLs to a single
target, so the K8s EndpointSlice/hash-ring path is bypassed for Hetzner too.

* feat(agent): accept X-Server-Token on inbound auth so cloud gateways can route messages

The cloud Discord and webhook gateways forward inbound platform messages to a
provisioned container's POST /agents/:id/message endpoint and attach the shared
service secret as an X-Server-Token header (only when AGENT_SERVER_SHARED_SECRET
is configured). The container runtime in packages/agent previously authorized
that endpoint only via a trusted-loopback request or a Bearer token matching the
per-agent inbound API token, so a real gateway-routed message returned 401.

Teach the agent server's isAuthorized path to also accept a request whose
X-Server-Token header matches AGENT_SERVER_SHARED_SECRET, mirroring the existing
Kubernetes agent-server contract. The shared-secret check runs after the
trusted-local short-circuit and before the Bearer check, using a constant-time
comparison. When AGENT_SERVER_SHARED_SECRET is unset the header carries no
authority and existing Bearer and loopback auth are unchanged, so there is no
regression for deployments that never configure it.

Inject AGENT_SERVER_SHARED_SECRET into the provisioned container's base
environment so the container can validate the header. The value is sourced from
an explicit per-deployment entry in the sandbox environment vars when present,
otherwise from the daemon's own AGENT_SERVER_SHARED_SECRET (the same value the
gateways read), so both ends share one secret without extra configuration. When
neither is set the variable is omitted and the X-Server-Token path stays
disabled.

Add X-Server-Token to the CORS allowed-headers list and cover the new auth path
with unit tests: a matching token authorizes, a wrong or missing token is
rejected, an unset or whitespace secret disables the path, and existing Bearer
auth continues to work alongside it.

feat(cloud-shared): wire signed waifu webhook emit for the credit money path (#8094)

* feat(cloud-billing): wire signed waifu webhook emit for the credit money path

Eliza Cloud is the metered billing rail under a hosted waifu agent. Waifu
already exposed signed receivers for credit and inference events, but the emit
side was missing: nothing actually POSTed the credit signals back, and the one
existing provision-complete callback was unsigned so waifu rejected it with a
401.

This adds the emit side in the monorepo cloud package and closes the seam:

- new packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services/waifu-webhook.ts: a signed emitter
  that matches waifu's receiver contract exactly. It computes an HMAC-SHA256
  over the timestamp and raw body, sends it in the X-Waifu-Webhook-Signature
  header, includes a stable idempotencyKey for replay protection, and routes
  per event kind to the credits or inference receiver. It resolves its target
  from the environment and no-ops cleanly when unconfigured, so non-waifu orgs
  and local or CI environments are unaffected. It never throws, so a webhook
  delivery problem can never block the billing path.
- credits.ts: after a successful deduction crosses the low or depleted
  threshold, emit credits.low or credits.depleted to waifu so a hosted agent
  can downgrade its model tier or pause itself. Fire-and-forget alongside the
  existing low-credits email.
- provisioning-jobs.ts: sign the provision-complete callback with the waifu
  envelope so the receiver accepts it instead of returning 401.
- classifyCreditBalance: pure threshold mapping shared by the billing path so
  the money-path decision is unit-testable without a database.

Tests: packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services/waifu-webhook.test.ts (13 tests,
all passing) lock the signing contract recomputed byte-for-byte against waifu's
own scheme, per-kind receiver routing, idempotency key presence, clean no-op
when unconfigured, never-throw on delivery error, the credit-status threshold
mapping, and the credit and inference payload shapes.

Scope note: this wires the credit-state money-path emit (low and depleted) and
the signed provision callback. The high-volume per-call inference.spent emit
helper is provided and tested but left unwired by design, since per-inference
metering is the separate metering workstream.

Re-homed from the wrong repo (RemilioNubilio/cloud PR #1, an old Next.js
app/api layout) into the correct monorepo cloud package
(packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services). The code was adapted from the
@/lib/* alias to the relative imports used by this package; the HMAC contract
is unchanged and still matches waifu's receiver byte-for-byte.

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>

* fix(cloud-shared): route waifu webhooks by kind to stop money-path misroute

receiverPath() trusted any WAIFU_WEBHOOK_URL that already contained
/v2/webhooks/ regardless of the requested kind, so a credits receiver URL
plus kind: "inference" would POST inference payloads to the /credits
receiver (and vice versa). The credits mapper defaults unknown payloads to
credits.topped_up, so this corrupted credit state on the money path.

Routing is now driven by kind: a bare origin gets the canonical
/v2/webhooks/eliza-cloud/{credits|inference} path, and a full receiver path
re-derives the sibling path for the requested kind by swapping the trailing
/credits <-> /inference segment. Mirrors the deliberate safe derivation in
plugins/plugin-elizacloud/src/utils/waifu-metering.ts.

Also tighten isWaifuWebhookTargetUrl() to gate the signed envelope on the
/v2/webhooks/ path prefix AND origin, not origin alone, so a same-origin
non-webhook callback (e.g. /internal/job-done) never gets the signed waifu
shape or the shared HMAC signature.

Adds regression tests: credits-path target + inference kind -> /inference
(and the reverse), preserved same-kind routing, and the tightened gating.

feat(plugin-elizacloud): forward per-inference spend to the waifu burn meter (#8089)

* feat(plugin-elizacloud): forward per-inference spend to waifu burn meter

Hosted waifu agents run as sandboxed containers whose model inference is
routed through the Eliza Cloud metered inference gateway. The gateway is the
honest meter: it owns the per-model pricing table and platform markup and
debits the organization credit balance on every call. That debit already
happens server side and is authoritative.

What was missing was the signal back to waifu. The waifu burn rollup reads
inference.spent agent events to compute daily burn and runway, but fell back
to a 5 USD per day placeholder when no such events existed because nothing
emitted them.

This adds a waifu metering bridge that listens for the runtime MODEL_USED
event (emitted by the cloud model handlers after each inference) and POSTs a
signed inference.spent webhook to waifu. It is a no-op unless the container is
provisioned with the waifu metering env knobs, so it never fires for local or
standalone agents.

Token counts are exact (reported by the gateway). USD is the authoritative
post markup cost when the gateway surfaces it (usage.cost_usd or the
X-Eliza-Cost-Usd response header); otherwise a conservative, configurable
token based estimate is used. The credit debit itself remains the cloud
authoritative number; the estimate only affects waifu burn display until the
cloud cost is wired through.

- events.ts: carry resolved model id and optional gateway cost on MODEL_USED
- text.ts: pass model name and parse gateway cost from inference responses
- waifu-metering.ts: config resolution, HMAC signing, payload build, POST
- index.ts: register the MODEL_USED handler
- unit tests cover config gating, signing, estimate vs gateway cost, idempotency

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>

* fix(plugin-elizacloud): meter only cloud inference and never post to the credits webhook

Two metering correctness fixes for the waifu inference bridge.

1. Filter MODEL_USED events by source. ElizaOS dispatches MODEL_USED globally,
   so the bridge also received events from other model providers, including
   plugin-local-inference (source "local-ai", free CPU inference with no real
   credit debit). It built an estimated inference.spent for those and posted it
   as cloud burn, billing free inference as paid. The handler now meters only
   events whose source is the cloud metered gateway ("elizacloud").

2. Never reuse the credits webhook URL for inference. The config previously fell
   back from WAIFU_INFERENCE_WEBHOOK_URL to WAIFU_WEBHOOK_URL, which is the
   credits receiver. Posting an inference payload there is misclassified as a
   credit event (the credits mapper defaults unknown status to credits.topped_up
   and corrupts credit state). The resolver now requires an inference URL, or
   safely derives the sibling /inference path from a known /credits URL, and
   never reuses a non-inference URL.

Tests: local-ai and openrouter events are not metered while an elizacloud event
is; a credits-only URL derives /inference and is never reused as-is; a
non-derivable URL yields no metering.

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>

Add a 10s AbortSignal.timeout to the inference.spent webhook POST so a stuck
receiver can no longer leave a background fetch hanging. Timeouts are caught and
logged with the agent id and never rethrown, keeping metering best-effort.

Send only the canonical X-Waifu-Webhook-Signature header. The receiver reads

X-Waifu-Signature header was redundant. Adjust the test to assert the canonical
header is the only signature header sent and add coverage for the timeout path.

ci(agent-image): gate the push on a real boot verification (#8081)

The build-agent-image workflow built and pushed the cloud-agent image with
no boot verification, and docker-ci-smoke.sh booted a stub health server
instead of the real entrypoint. Net result: an image that crashes on boot
(missing zod / @elizaos/core / chalk and similar runtime-dep gaps) built
green and shipped to ghcr, which is the recurring breakage Stan keeps
hand-fixing after merges.

Changes:
- docker-ci-smoke.sh now boots the image with its real default command
  (APP_CMD_START = node --import tsx packages/agent/dist/bin.js start)
  instead of substituting a fake http.createServer health server. It adds
  a boot-verify-only mode (--boot-verify-only / BOOT_VERIFY_ONLY) that skips
  the build and verifies a pre-built image, scans container logs for known
  startup-crash signatures (Cannot find package/module, ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND,
  Failed to start, crashed during init, ...) to fail fast, detects non-zero
  container exit, and retries the health probe to avoid flakiness.
  --skip-smoke is kept as an escape hatch.
- build-agent-image.yml now builds the image into the local daemon (load,
  no push), runs the real boot verification against it, and only pushes if
  the verification passes. A non-bootable image never reaches ghcr.

Verified the gate goes GREEN on a bootable image (exit 0, health served)
and RED on a broken image (exit 1) via both crash-signature detection
(missing module) and the health timeout (server never listens).

fix(core): decide complete-direct-reply preference structurally, not by user-intent regex (#8071)

`shouldPreferCompleteDirectReply` decided whether a finished model reply should
win over force-injected planning by scanning the user's message with five intent
regexes (looksLikeCodingWork / WebSearch / LocalShell / ActionExplanation /
CreativeWriting). `looksLikeCodingWorkRequest` matches any "app" near "build", so
a complete one-sentence answer to a question like "what are your app-build
routing rules? ... do not build anything" was force-planned into a redundant
sub-agent spawn.

Decide on structure instead, using signals the function already computes: a
complete substantive reply (not ack / progress / refusal / empty, via
`looksLikeCompleteDirectReply`) plus only weak/injectable planning signals
(simple|general context + search/shell/spawn-class candidates, via
`hasOnlyWeakDirectReplyPlanningSignals`) wins directly. The Stage-1 inference
backstop still plans genuine web/shell/build turns, because those return an
ack/empty/refusal reply that fails `looksLikeCompleteDirectReply` — so no
behavior is lost, only the substring false-positive is removed.

The five `looksLikeX` predicates remain in use by the inference/recovery paths;
this only removes their misuse as a user-intent classifier in the direct-reply
decision. Adds regression tests: a complete reply answers directly even when a
coding-class candidate is force-injected; an ack-only build ask still plans.

* fix(agent-image): add zod + eager-boot externals to Dockerfile.ci runtime deps

The CI agent image crashes on boot with:
  Cannot find package 'zod' imported from
  /app/packages/core/dist/node/index.node.js
(exit 1, before any agent code runs). This affects the :develop image
and every new build; it is a pre-existing packaging regression.

Root cause: packages/app-core/deploy/Dockerfile.ci installs a hardcoded
allowlist of runtime deps into /app/node_modules. .dockerignore excludes
**/node_modules, so the ONLY runtime deps in the final image are this
allowlist plus relinked workspace packages plus whatever the dist bundles
inline. packages/core/dist/node/index.node.js third-partyises zod
(build.ts nodeExternals) and imports it eagerly (35 static top-level
imports). zod was missing from the allowlist, so it never landed in the
image and the container crashed on the very first module load.

Fix part 1: add zod@4.4.3 (matches packages/core/package.json ^4.4.3,
provides the ./v3 and ./v4 subpath exports core imports).

Fix part 2 (audit, so the next boot does not hit a different missing
dep): packages/agent/dist is transpiled with tsc (NOT bundled), so every
bare import stays third-party. Traced the eager boot path
(runtime/eliza.js dynamically imports api/server.js, whose static import
graph loads eagerly at module-eval). Beyond zod, that graph pulls in
non-allowlist third-partys that would each be the next hard crash:
  hono           <- api/hono-adapter (HTTP server)
  json5          <- config/config
  @noble/curves  <- api/wallet (secp256k1)
  ethers         <- api/wallet
  esbuild        <- services/plugin-compiler (via workbench routes)
  isomorphic-git <- services/vfs-git
Added all of these (plus @noble/hashes, a curves dep, for safety) to
both the npm install list and the rm -rf pre-clean list. Versions track
the declarations in packages/agent/package.json. Verified the set
installs together cleanly and each entry imports without error
(zod/v3, zod/v4 and @noble/curves/secp256k1.js subpaths resolve).

The allowlist is hand-maintained and brittle; documented the boot-path
reasoning in the Dockerfile and flagged deriving it from the workspace
dist third-partys as follow-up.

Does not touch the entrypoint or agent logic; dependency packaging only.

* fix(agent-image): derive runtime deps closure instead of hand-maintaining

The agent CI image links a fixed set of workspace packages into
/app/node_modules. Several of those packages are transpiled (tsc, not
bundled), so their bare third-party imports stay third-party and must resolve from
node_modules at runtime. The image used to install a hand-maintained
allowlist of those third-partys, which had to be extended by hand every time a
newly-linked package introduced a new dependency. Each omission was a hard
boot crash ("Cannot find package '<dep>' imported from
/app/packages/<pkg>/dist/..."), and we hit a string of them (zod, then
@elizaos/core, then chalk).

Replace the hand-maintained list with a derived one. A new script,
collect-docker-runtime-deps.mjs, reads the declared dependencies of every
workspace package that gets linked into the image, drops the @elizaos/*
workspace entries (those are linked, not installed), and emits the union
pinned to the versions the workspace lockfile resolves. npm install then
pulls the full transitive closure automatically. This ends the whole class
of one-dep-at-a-time boot-crash loops: every dependency a linked package
declares is present, so the image boots and any character config can load
any bundled plugin without a missing-module crash.

Details:
- Versions are pinned from bun.lock for reproducibility, falling back to the
  declared range when a package is not in the lockfile.
- Pure browser/UI packages (notably @elizaos/ui and its radix/three/recharts
  tree) are excluded in the script: they are linked for module-resolution
  integrity but never imported by the headless server runtime, so installing
  their frontend deps would only bloat the image.
- --legacy-peer-deps is added to the npm install: the broad closure includes
  packages with conflicting optional peer ranges (e.g. the discord.js voice
  stack's opusscript peer), which a flat registry install would otherwise
  reject. This matches how the workspace install hoists/resolves them.

Verified locally that npm install resolves the full closure cleanly
(1055 packages) with --legacy-peer-deps.

fix(orchestrator): harden SSRF, credential-bridge, session-limit, round-trip cap

Four confirmed orchestrator findings in plugin-agent-orchestrator:

- SSRF (#16): the completion-URL verifier GET-probes URLs extracted from
  untrusted sub-agent narration with redirect:follow and no host filtering,
  letting a compromised sub-agent steer the parent into private/link-local/
  cloud-metadata endpoints. Add src/services/ssrf-guard.ts: resolve the host
  and reject non-public addresses (RFC1918, link-local incl. 169.254.169.254,
  ULA, CGNAT, multicast/reserved) while allowing loopback (local build
  verification depends on it), and follow redirects manually, re-validating
  each hop. Route both verifier fetch sites (probeOnce, detectCachedMiss)
  through safeFetch. Resolver is injectable for tests.

- Credential bridge (#17): the POST issued the owner REQUEST_SECRET flow and
  minted a scopedToken for any path-supplied sessionId, gated only on loopback.
  Add an ownership gate mirroring the read-only parent-context bridge: reject
  (410) when the session is unknown or terminal in this parent runtime.

- Session-limit race (#18): enforceSessionLimit (list) and store.create were
  separate awaited ops, so concurrent spawns could each pass the check before
  any inserted and overshoot ELIZA_ACP_MAX_SESSIONS. Wrap check+insert in a
  per-service promise-chain mutex (reserveSessionSlot) so the reservation is
  atomic.

- Round-trip cap miscount (#19): the per-session counter incremented before the
  three task_complete suppression returns (verify-retry handoff, stale
  continuation, cross-session dedupe), so suppressed events counted against the
  runaway-loop cap. Roll the increment back on those paths.

Tests: ssrf-guard unit suite; bridge-routes ownership-gate rejections;

fix(local-inference): correct Windows FFI backend, switch rollback, unload ordering, and token decoding

Four local-inference defects in plugin-local-inference:

- #8 desktop-llama-adapter.ts: the runtime default backend for Windows was
  "cpu" but the build script (build-llama-cpp-desktop-dylib.mjs) stages the
  Windows dylibs under "windows-x86_64-vulkan". The runtime probed
  "windows-x86_64-cpu", never found them, and silently skipped the in-process
  FFI fast-path. Default Windows to "vulkan" to match the build target.

- #13 active-model.ts: switchTo() unloads the active model before loading the
  new one with no rollback, so a load failure mid-switch left the host with
  zero models loaded while reporting status "error" against the requested id.
  Snapshot the previously-ready model and restore it on failure; only when
  there is no prior model (or the restore also fails) report error with
  modelId null, so a failed switch never silently drops a working model and
  the state never claims a phantom id.

- #14 ffi-streaming-backend.ts / desktop-ffi-backend-runtime.ts: unload()/
  release() nulled the session refs before awaiting the native release, so a
  throwing bun:ffi free left the backend wedged (next acquire() hit the
  live-session guard forever). Await release first and clear refs in a
  finally at both runtime levels.

- #11 desktop-llama-adapter.ts: llama_token_to_piece's negative return (buffer
  too small) was dropped by the `wrote > 0` guard, and per-piece TextDecoder
  mangled UTF-8 codepoints split across token boundaries (CJK/emoji/accented
  text) into U+FFFD. Add tokenToText(): resize+retry on a negative return and
  decode through a persistent per-session streaming TextDecoder.

Adds focused tests for all four (loader-path rollback, split-UTF-8 +
resize/retry, FFI unload ordering / no-wedge).

fix(scenario-eval): close training-integrity and honesty gaps in scenario/reward path

Five confirmed findings in the scenario-runner / training corpus path that
let failed or reward-hacked behavior leak into training data or test passes.

#48 reward fn ignored extra/spurious tool calls. _score_tool_calls only
iterated over expected_calls, so a predicted call past the expected length was
never inspected and full content credit was granted. A response of
[SEND_EMAIL, DELETE_ALL_FILES] scored 0.798 — HIGHER than the clean single
call. Now require an exact-length match for content credit, add a
"too_many_tool_calls" note, and zero content_ok on extras. The destructive
extra now scores 0.397 vs 0.790 clean.

#49 the executor synthesized a REPLY with result.success=true when the LLM
emitted text but selected no action, masking real selection failures as
passing REPLYs. Stop claiming success on the fabricated entry and exclude
synthesized-reply captures from the actionCalled / selectedAction final
checks, so REPLY-targeting assertions only pass on a genuine LLM selection.

#47 native export stamped every scenario trajectory as gold-weight training
data regardless of assertion outcome (the only outcome marker was the recorder
lifecycle, which the scorer never reads). Thread each scenario's pass/fail into
exportScenarioNativeJsonl and emit a top-level `status`, so a failed scenario's
rows carry status="failed" and route to rating="repair"/weight=0 in
native_success_and_score instead of gold. Manifest now records per-outcome row
counts.

#51 fuzzy action matcher treated a generic action as satisfying a specific
expectation: separator-stripped includ() made SEND match SEND_EMAIL's
expectation and LIFE↔LIFEOPS, MESSAGE↔READ_MESSAGES all match. Restore a
bounded token-boundary rule (leading-token prefix in either direction, plus a
provider-prefix suffix for the candidate) and drop the unbounded
includes/token-subset over-match.

#50 connector dispatch `delivered` defaulted to true when no boolean success
field was present, letting messageDelivered pass on a handler that never
reported success. Default to false, matching the safe action-result default.

Tests: reward fn extra/exact-call cases; action-family parent-vs-generic
matching; connector delivered default; native-export scenario-outcome
stamping.

fix(orchestrator): don't false-flag a served-200 build as stale

a static app that exists, is non-empty, and serves http 200 was marked
"dead" purely because its local file mtime predated session.createdAt-5s.
deploy steps that copy a build into place preserve the source file's
mtime, so the wall-clock freshness gate in verifyLocalTarget
false-positived on a healthy served app. that false-dead triggered a
spurious verify-retry, suppressed round-1 task_complete, and the in-flight
retry tripped newerTaskSince in coding-session-changes — so the real diff
was withheld and "what did you change?" wrongly reported no captured diff.

the live http 200 probe is authoritative for a served url, so it must not
be overridden by the mtime comparison. thread a servedLive flag from the
healthy-probe call sites in annotateUnverifiedUrls through
verifyMappedLocalUrl into verifyLocalTarget; when the url is confirmed
served, skip the freshness gate. the missing-file and empty-file checks
stay unconditional, and the gate still applies when the url is not served
(the file is then the only liveness signal).

tests: add verify-served-200-freshness covering both a served-200 old-mtime
app (not flagged) and the negative control where the url 404s (still
flagged); update the existing router test that encoded the old behavior.

Issues found while bringing eliza-staging-1 up for the first time —
3 manual fixes were needed to get the daemon running, and each one is
a gap in either the cloud-init template or the deploy workflow.

Cloud-init template (one-shot at first boot):
- Install Node 24 via NodeSource. The systemd unit calls tsx which is a
  Node process; without node, the daemon fatals with
  '/usr/bin/env: node: No such file or directory'.

  'turbo run build --filter=@elizaos/...' on 19 packages; swap pushes
  the build through without resizing the VM.
- Add bunx symlink. The canary bun.sh/install tarball stopped shipping
  bunx as a separate binary at some point; build scripts that call
  'bunx tsc' then fail. The symlink is enough since bunx is just bun
  reading argv[0].

Deploy workflow (idempotent safety net for existing hosts):
- New 'Ensure host prereqs' step that does the same Node/swap/bunx
  setup if missing. Catches hosts provisioned before this cloud-init
  template (eliza-1 and eliza-staging-1 today).
- Post-bun-install: defensive symlink for @elizaos/cloud-shared in
  node_modules. The daemon imports it but lives in packages/scripts/
  (no package.json), so bun's workspace graph never adds it to the
  global node_modules. Recreate after every deploy.

seeded them into the default deferred load set (isCore=true, fatal on import
failure). But collect-docker-runtime-deps.mjs deliberately excludes their

deps either), on the assumption these plugins are never loaded by default.
That assumption was false once they were in CORE_PLUGINS.

LifeOps enablement) and platform deps, so move them out of CORE_PLUGINS into
OPTIONAL_CORE_PLUGINS. Now they only load when explicitly enabled, the default
hosted-agent image boots clean, and any later missing-package failure is
treated as a benign optional-plugin skip rather than a fatal core failure.
Also drop the eager deferred static registration for plugin-google in eliza.ts
so boot no longer attempts to import it (and emit googleapis warnings) by
default; explicit enablement still resolves it via the normal optional path.

The lifeops to google boot dependency hint and the runtime-app subpath /
dynamic-import references (permissions-routes, binance-skill-helpers,
plugin-resolver) are unaffected: they are config/runtime-gated, not part of
the default boot load set.

fix(desktop): stop infinite fetch recursion in local-agent IPC bridge

index.html installs an inline window.fetch override that rewrites loopback
http://127.0.0.1:31337/* requests into native Agent.request() calls. That
rewrite is only correct on a native Capacitor platform (iOS/Android), where the
in-process local agent has no directly-reachable TCP port and Agent.request
resolves to a native plugin.

On any non-native host (Electrobun desktop, plain web) there is no native Agent
plugin, so Capacitor resolves Agent.request to the web fallback
(AgentWeb.request), which fetches `${apiBase}${path}` — the same
http://127.0.0.1:31337 URL — through the bridged window.fetch, re-entering the
bridge and recursing with no delay. This hammered the local agent (observed:
/api/vincent/status fetched hundreds of thousands of times per run), allocating
Promise/Response objects on the renderer's main thread until the WebKitGTK web
process climbed ~140MB/s to OOM; it starved paint/rAF so the splash appeared
frozen.

Gate the loopback->IPC rewrite behind a positive isNativeCapacitorAgentHost()
check (Capacitor.getPlatform() in {ios, android}) so the rewrite happens only
where a native Agent plugin exists. Non-native hosts fetch the real backend
directly. This closes the whole recursion class, not just the desktop host, and
is behaviourally identical for mobile (rewrite stays on) and desktop (rewrite
off). The eliza-local-agent:// protocol branch is unchanged (loop-safe:
AgentWeb returns 503 for it).

perf(app): serve @elizaos/core browser BUNDLE in renderer, not source graph

The renderer was resolving @elizaos/core to its browser SOURCE entry
(packages/core/src/index.browser.ts), which transitively pulled ~435 individual
core source modules. In dev that meant ~435 HTTP round-trips + on-demand TS
transforms, AND the browser tried to evaluate core's node:async_hooks / node:fs
imports — producing minute-long cold loads on /home that frequently never
mounted ("loading every TS file, 120MB, totally broken").

resolveElizaCoreBundlePath() deliberately preferred the source entry to "avoid
parsing the huge bundled artifact." That reasoning is backwards: one pre-built,
browser-safe 3.3MB bundle (single request, single parse, node: builtins already
stripped) is far cheaper than 435 source round-trips. Flip the preference to the
dist/browser bundle; keep the source entry only as a last-resort fallback for a
fresh linked checkout that has no build yet.

Verified on an isolated eliza-source dev server (HMR port matched):
  before: core source files = 435, load never mounted, node: import errors
  after:  core source files = 0  (served as 1 dist bundle), 0 console/page
          errors, /home mounts. (Remaining cost is now @elizaos/ui source —
          ~893 files — tracked separately.)

fix(agent): move plugin-google and plugin-lifeops to optional so the default image boots (#8105)

The Docker boot smoke (the #8081 boot gate) crashed during the post-health
window: the agent loaded 10/12 plugins, then failed core plugins
@elizaos/plugin-google and @elizaos/plugin-lifeops with
"Cannot find package 'googleapis'" and "Cannot find package '@capacitor/core'",
which marked the image NOT bootable and blocked every fresh image build.

Root cause: both plugins were listed in CORE_PLUGINS, so collectPluginNames()
seeded them into the default deferred load set (isCore=true, fatal on import
failure). But collect-docker-runtime-deps.mjs deliberately excludes their
heavy native deps (@capacitor/core; googleapis is not in any linked package's
deps either), on the assumption these plugins are never loaded by default.
That assumption was false once they were in CORE_PLUGINS.

Fix (Option A, surgical): they need explicit configuration (Google OAuth,
LifeOps enablement) and platform deps, so move them out of CORE_PLUGINS into
OPTIONAL_CORE_PLUGINS. Now they only load when explicitly enabled, the default
hosted-agent image boots clean, and any later missing-package failure is
treated as a benign optional-plugin skip rather than a fatal core failure.
Also drop the eager deferred static registration for plugin-google in eliza.ts
so boot no longer attempts to import it (and emit googleapis warnings) by
default; explicit enablement still resolves it via the normal optional path.

The lifeops to google boot dependency hint and the runtime-app subpath /
dynamic-import references (permissions-routes, binance-skill-helpers,
plugin-resolver) are unaffected: they are config/runtime-gated, not part of
the default boot load set.

Verification:
- Updated core-plugins.test.ts to assert plugin-google/plugin-lifeops are
  OPTIONAL (and absent from CORE_PLUGINS and DEFERRED_CORE_PLUGINS); 2/2 pass.
- biome 2.4.15 clean on all changed files.
- tsgo typecheck of packages/agent surfaces no errors from the changed lines
  (only pre-existing unbuilt-workspace module-resolution noise).

fix(orchestrator): allow read-only webfetch in opencode spawn config

opencode's webfetch permission defaults to "ask". Under the acpx "standard"
approval preset (which answers non-interactive permission prompts with "deny"),
a spawned sub-agent's web fetch is silently denied, so the model — unable to
reach the network — tends to confabulate an answer instead of fetching live
data. Allow the read-only webfetch GET (opencode caps the body at 5MB and never
mutates the workspace) so sub-agents can retrieve real live data on any
provider, without granting write/exec (bash, edit) permissions, which stay
gated by the approval preset.

permission.webfetch while leaving bash/edit ungranted.

fix(agent): strip ESM-incompatible shebang from mobile bundle

output, ABOVE the entry's #!/usr/bin/env node, so the shebang lands on ~line 4.

module (compileSourceTextModule) — which crash-looped the riscv64 OS agent at

so /api/health never came up). The bundle is always launched via an explicit
`node <bundle>` (run-agent.sh), never executed directly, so the shebang is dead
weight. Strip the first shebang line after reading the Bun.build output.

line 4 and passes (exit 0) once stripped.

fix(app): resolve es-toolkit/compat/* to ESM (fixes recharts blank screen)

recharts (via es-toolkit@1.47) default-imports 11 `es-toolkit/compat/<name>`
subpaths (get, omit, sortBy, throttle, ...). es-toolkit's `./compat/*` export
map exposes ONLY a CJS condition (no `import`/ESM), and that CJS impl declares a
local `require_isUnsafeProperty` that collides with the Vite/Rolldown dep
optimizer's CJS-interop helper of the same name. Both serve paths blank the app:

  - pre-bundled: the optimizer emits a self-shadowing
    `var require_isUnsafeProperty = require_isUnsafeProperty()` (TDZ ->
    "require_isUnsafeProperty is not a function" at recharts.js)
  - served raw: `import get from "es-toolkit/compat/get"` resolves to the CJS
    `compat/<name>.js`, which Vite can't surface a `default` export for ->
    "does not provide an export named 'default'"

Add a resolver on BOTH the raw-serve `plugins` path and the
`optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions.plugins` optimizer path that rewrites each
`es-toolkit/compat/<name>` to its real ESM `dist/compat/**/<name>.mjs` (resolved
relative to the importer, so the es-toolkit version recharts actually depends on
is used) and re-exports the named binding as default — matching how recharts
consumes it. Covering both paths keeps the fix correct whether or not Vite
decides to pre-bundle recharts on a given boot.

Root cause is an es-toolkit packaging issue (`./compat/*` should also offer an
`import` condition); this is a consumer-side workaround until that lands
upstream.

fix(cloud): guarantee response-token budget for all reasoning models

Reasoning models (OpenAI o-series, DeepSeek R, MiniMax M, Qwen think, GLM/
Kimi/Nemotron/OLMo think tiers, etc.) spend output tokens on hidden
chain-of-thought before emitting a visible answer. When max_tokens only
covered the reasoning, the model truncated mid-thought and the route returned
content:null while still billing the consumed tokens.

The fix existed but was Anthropic-only: computeEffectiveMaxTokens reserved
MIN_RESPONSE_TOKENS beyond the thinking budget, but the budget was computed
solely via resolveAnthropicThinkingBudgetTokens. Every other reasoning model
fell through with the raw (often tiny) request max_tokens.

Changes:
- Add modelUsesReasoningTokens() in cloud-shared/pricing.ts: a broad detector
  for models that consume output tokens on hidden reasoning. Kept separate from
  the narrow isReasoningModel() (which only governs temperature stripping and
  must stay narrow).
- computeEffectiveMaxTokens now floors effective max_tokens at
  MIN_RESPONSE_TOKENS for any reasoning model, not just Anthropic CoT.
- Non-streaming response: if a completion is empty but tokens were billed
  (truncated mid-reasoning), report finish_reason "length" instead of a
  misleading "stop", and log a warning, so OpenAI-compatible clients retry
  with a higher max_tokens instead of silently paying for nothing.
- Tests for the detector (29) and the budget logic (7), exported
  computeEffectiveMaxTokens via __nativeToolingTestHooks.

Verified live: minimax/minimax-m3 returned content:null + billed 10-16 tokens
at low max_tokens; returns a real answer at higher budgets. Catalog itself is
healthy (336 text models, 311 priced + 25 free, in sync with OpenRouter), so
this token-budget gap is the systemic cause of reasoning-model failures.

fix(discord): carry recent unaddressed messages into a following addressed batch

a question typed without an @-mention, then an "@bot ^^" pointer a few seconds
later, landed in separate channel-debounce batches. the pointer flushed alone
with an empty "[recent channel context]", so the model saw a content-light
current message and replied with a generic greeting instead of answering the
question — while the same question answered fine when it shared the debounce
window with the pointer.

- debouncer: keep a short recency-based per-channel buffer of recent unaddressed
  messages (strict/mention-only mode, skipped when coalescing) and fold them into
  the next addressed batch so the existing bundler renders them as "[recent
  channel context]". cleared on markResponded and destroy.
- events: arm the response cooldown only when the bot actually engages with a
  batch, so purely-unaddressed chatter no longer starts the cooldown that would
  otherwise drop the next unaddressed message before it is even recorded.

structural (recency/addressing only, no content inspection); strict-mode only,
so respond-to-all, dm, and coalesce paths are unchanged. adds debouncer unit tests.

fix(discord): only fold recent context into pointer messages; keep buffering during cooldown

follow-up hardening on the recent-unaddressed buffer, after adversarial review
and live testing surfaced two residuals:

- the response cooldown gate dropped unaddressed messages before they could be
  buffered. in strict / mention-only mode those messages never trigger a reply,
  so dropping them only discarded context a following "@bot ^^" pointer needs.
  skip the cooldown drop when we are buffering (respond-to-all is unchanged).
- fold the buffer only into a pointer message — an addressed message that, once
  mentions are stripped, has no word characters (e.g. "^^", "👆", "?"). a
  self-contained question carries its own content; folding unrelated recent
  chatter into it can derail its routing, so it now stands on its own.
- dedupe by id when draining, since an unaddressed message briefly lives in both
  the rolling buffer and the pending debounce batch.

cooldown then pointed at answers 3/3; a substantive question with recent chatter
