fix(cloud-api/steward): pin tenant id via X-Steward-Tenant header

PR #8176 set NEXT_PUBLIC_STEWARD_TENANT_ID at Pages build env but Vite
isn't inlining it into the bundle, so the staging SPA still initialises
the Steward SDK with `tenantId=undefined` and Steward falls back to the
"default" tenant (which has no `magicLinkBaseUrl` override → magic-link
redirects to www.elizacloud.ai instead of staging).

Fix it at the proxy layer: the cloud-api Worker already has
`STEWARD_TENANT_ID=elizacloud-staging` in `[env.staging.vars]`, so use
that to set the `X-Steward-Tenant` header on every forwarded Steward
request. Steward's auth routes resolve tenant from
`X-Steward-Tenant || body.tenantId || STEWARD_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`, so the
header pins the tenant regardless of what the SPA sends.

Prod path unchanged — `STEWARD_TENANT_ID` is unset in
`[env.production.vars]` so the conditional skips the header injection
and the upstream falls through to its existing default tenant.
fix(cloud-api/steward): pin tenant id via X-Steward-Tenant header

fix(cloud-frontend): wire NEXT_PUBLIC_STEWARD_TENANT_ID into Pages preview build

Per Shaw's review on #8179: the Pages preview build reads its env from
wrangler.toml `[env.preview.vars]`, not the GHA workflow `env:` block on
the build step (that scope only applies to the GHA shell, not the
downstream Vite process spawned by `wrangler pages deploy`).

Without this entry the Vite allowlist at vite.config.ts:63 has nothing
to inline, so `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_STEWARD_TENANT_ID` resolves to
`undefined` in the bundle and the SPA initialises the Steward SDK
without a tenant id. Magic-link goes through the proxy header pin from
the previous commit, but OAuth resolves tenant from the
`tenant_id` query param (steward auth.ts:2293) — which depends on the
SPA building the URL with the right id — so OAuth users registered on
staging end up under the prod `elizacloud` tenant without this fix.

Prod build is unaffected: `[vars]` (production block) doesn't set this,
so the prod SPA keeps falling back to the SDK's own default (which the
prod Steward instance already routes correctly).
fix(cloud-frontend): wire NEXT_PUBLIC_STEWARD_TENANT_ID into Pages pr…

fix(cloud-api/steward): close two bypass routes that skip tenant pinning

The /steward/* proxy header injection (previous commits on this PR) only
covers requests that flow through the embedded handler. Two sibling
routes in auth/ make direct upstream fetches and were leaking to the
default tenant:

- steward-refresh/route.ts → POST baseUrl/auth/refresh
- steward-nonce-exchange/route.ts → POST baseUrl/auth/oauth/exchange

Both now forward `X-Steward-Tenant` from c.env.STEWARD_TENANT_ID when
set. Additionally, steward-nonce-exchange now falls back to the env
tenant when the SPA omits tenant_id in the body — without this, Steward
resolves `body.tenant_id=null` to STEWARD_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID and a
staging OAuth exchange would mint a session against the prod tenant.

Also corrected the misleading comment in embedded.ts: it claimed Steward
"auth routes" all honor X-Steward-Tenant, but OAuth /authorize reads
tenant only from the query param. The comment now distinguishes the two
paths and points at the wrangler.toml fix that handles OAuth.

Gap was surfaced by adversarial verification of Shaw's PR review.

feat(plugin-agent-orchestrator): add LLM goal verifier service

On `task_complete` an orchestrator task advances to status `validating`
and waits for a caller to invoke `OrchestratorTaskService.validateTask`
with a pass/fail judgment. The existing validators are a human pressing
a button in the orchestrator UI and the pattern-based
`sub-agent-completion` response evaluator (which only routes back through
TASKS when completion text contains explicit failure markers — it does
not judge whether the work satisfies the goal).

Add a third validator: a small-model judge that reads the task's
`acceptanceCriteria` and the sub-agent's completion evidence and returns
a structured `{ passed, summary, missing }` verdict. Callers (HTTP route
in a follow-up commit, orchestrator UI button, future automatic hook)
forward the verdict to `validateTask` under
`verifier: "llm-goal-verifier"`.

Design constraints:

- No automatic firing — verifier runs only when an explicit caller invokes
  it, so an LLM-billed judgment never fires without consent. Surprises
  users about model spend would be a bad first impression.
- `ModelType.TEXT_SMALL` is sufficient for a yes/no judgment against a
  short criteria list and keeps the per-task cost bounded.
- Defensive parse — a malformed model response always resolves to
  `passed: false` with an explanatory summary, never crashes the route.
- Empty criteria short-circuit to pass; empty evidence short-circuits to
  fail; both paths skip the model call entirely.

Tests cover the prompt builder, the response parser (clean JSON, prose
preamble, nested braces, malformed JSON, non-object root, schema-invariant
enforcement, summary clamp, whitespace trim), and the orchestration paths
that bypass the model (empty criteria, empty evidence, model throw, pass,
fail). The model call itself is mocked via a minimal runtime stub so the
suite never reaches a real provider.

Refs: elizaOS/eliza#8124

feat(plugin-agent-orchestrator): expose POST /tasks/:id/auto-validate

Wire the LLM goal verifier service into the orchestrator HTTP surface so
the orchestrator UI, a TASKS sub-action, or a future automatic hook on
`validating` transitions can request a model-judged validation in one
round-trip without reimplementing the prompt/parse contract.

Behavior:

- Validates the task exists and is in `validating` status (409 on mismatch
  with the current status echoed back, matching the existing 409 the
  `/validate` route returns when status is stale).
- Reads `goal` + `acceptanceCriteria` directly from the task record. The
  caller supplies `completionEvidence` in the body (the sub-agent's final
  reply text, recent task events, test output — whatever the caller has
  the best view of). Empty evidence is permitted and short-circuits to a
  fail verdict server-side; that path is covered in the verifier unit
  tests.
- Calls `verifyGoalCompletion` once, forwards the verdict to the existing
  `validateTask` with `verifier: "llm-goal-verifier"` so audit-log
  consumers can distinguish LLM judgments from human approvals.
- Returns `{ task, verdict }` so the caller can render both the updated
  task DTO and the verifier's `missing` list (used to compose a corrective
  follow-up prompt on fail).

No automatic firing — wiring an event-driven trigger is deliberately a
follow-up so an LLM-billed judgment never runs without an explicit caller.

sandbox. It was disabled by default in managed-eliza-config because the

fix(android): apply Kotlin plugin to native Capacitor libs so release dex includes their classes

AGP 8.13's built-in Kotlin compile path (build/intermediates/built_in_kotlinc)
compiled the plugins' .kt sources but did NOT bundle the resulting .class files
into the *release* library jar — the release classes.jar came out empty except
for R.class. The app's :app:assembleRelease therefore linked plugin AARs with
zero classes, so every @elizaos/capacitor-* native plugin's Kotlin code was
absent from the final release dex.

The user-visible symptom: ai.elizaos.app crash-looped at boot on the
eliza_cf_riscv64_phone AOSP image with

  java.lang.ClassNotFoundException:
    ai.eliza.plugins.websiteblocker.WebsiteBlockerBootReceiver

because the websiteblocker Capacitor manifest is merged into the APK (declaring
a BOOT_COMPLETED receiver + VPN service by name) but the receiver class was
stripped along with all other plugin Kotlin classes. websiteblocker was the
only plugin to crash because it is the only one with a manifest-instantiated
component; the others were silently non-functional.

Explicitly applying org.jetbrains.kotlin.android (already on the root
buildscript classpath) wires Kotlin compilation into both the debug and release
jar-bundling tasks. Align compileOptions + kotlinOptions.jvmTarget to 21 to
match the root subprojects JavaCompile toolchain (the explicit Kotlin plugin
enforces JVM-target parity that the built-in path skipped).

Verified: the rebuilt release APK's classes.dex now contains
WebsiteBlockerBootReceiver/VpnService and 149 ai.eliza.plugins.* classes
(previously 0), R8 keeps them, and the merged manifest references resolve.

fix(cloud): guarantee response-token budget for all reasoning models (#8189)

* fix(cloud): guarantee response-token budget for all reasoning models

Reasoning models (OpenAI o-series, DeepSeek R, MiniMax M, Qwen think, GLM/
Kimi/Nemotron/OLMo think tiers, etc.) spend output tokens on hidden
chain-of-thought before emitting a visible answer. When max_tokens only
covered the reasoning, the model truncated mid-thought and the route returned
content:null while still billing the consumed tokens.

The fix existed but was Anthropic-only: computeEffectiveMaxTokens reserved
MIN_RESPONSE_TOKENS beyond the thinking budget, but the budget was computed
solely via resolveAnthropicThinkingBudgetTokens. Every other reasoning model
fell through with the raw (often tiny) request max_tokens.

Changes:
- Add modelUsesReasoningTokens() in cloud-shared/pricing.ts: a broad detector
  for models that consume output tokens on hidden reasoning. Kept separate from
  the narrow isReasoningModel() (which only governs temperature stripping and
  must stay narrow).
- computeEffectiveMaxTokens now floors effective max_tokens at
  MIN_RESPONSE_TOKENS for any reasoning model, not just Anthropic CoT.
- Non-streaming response: if a completion is empty but tokens were billed
  (truncated mid-reasoning), report finish_reason "length" instead of a
  misleading "stop", and log a warning, so OpenAI-compatible clients retry
  with a higher max_tokens instead of silently paying for nothing.
- Tests for the detector (29) and the budget logic (7), exported
  computeEffectiveMaxTokens via __nativeToolingTestHooks.

Verified live: minimax/minimax-m3 returned content:null + billed 10-16 tokens
at low max_tokens; returns a real answer at higher budgets. Catalog itself is
healthy (336 text models, 311 priced + 25 free, in sync with OpenRouter), so
this token-budget gap is the systemic cause of reasoning-model failures.

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>

* fix(cloud): detect reasoning models via catalog supported_parameters

Follow-up to the name-pattern detector: the production-reported models
(kimi-k2.6, glm-5.1, deepseek-v4-pro) are reasoning models but carry NO
'think'/'reasoning' token in their id, so name patterns missed them. They DO
advertise 'reasoning'/'include_reasoning' in the OpenRouter catalog's
supported_parameters.

- modelUsesReasoningTokens(model, supportedParameters?) now prefers the
  authoritative catalog signal, falling back to id name patterns when catalog
  metadata is unavailable.
- Added supported_parameters to CatalogModel + OpenAIModel (populated verbatim
  from the OpenRouter catalog the cloud already fetches).
- The chat-completions route does a best-effort getCachedGatewayModelById lookup
  and passes supported_parameters into computeEffectiveMaxTokens; on lookup
  failure it falls back to name patterns (no added hard dependency).

Verified live: glm-5.1 at max_tokens=50 returned content:null + billed 50
tokens (the exact production failure); kimi-k2.6, glm-5.1, deepseek-v4-pro all
return real answers at normal budgets. Tests now cover the catalog signal for
all three (38 detector + 18 budget tests, green).

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>

fix(cloud-api): pin Steward tenant via X-Steward-Tenant header (#8179)

* fix(cloud-api/steward): pin tenant id via X-Steward-Tenant header

PR #8176 set NEXT_PUBLIC_STEWARD_TENANT_ID at Pages build env but Vite
isn't inlining it into the bundle, so the staging SPA still initialises
the Steward SDK with `tenantId=undefined` and Steward falls back to the
"default" tenant (which has no `magicLinkBaseUrl` override → magic-link
redirects to www.elizacloud.ai instead of staging).

Fix it at the proxy layer: the cloud-api Worker already has
`STEWARD_TENANT_ID=elizacloud-staging` in `[env.staging.vars]`, so use
that to set the `X-Steward-Tenant` header on every forwarded Steward
request. Steward's auth routes resolve tenant from
`X-Steward-Tenant || body.tenantId || STEWARD_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`, so the
header pins the tenant regardless of what the SPA sends.

Prod path unchanged — `STEWARD_TENANT_ID` is unset in
`[env.production.vars]` so the conditional skips the header injection
and the upstream falls through to its existing default tenant.

* fix(cloud-frontend): wire NEXT_PUBLIC_STEWARD_TENANT_ID into Pages preview build

Per Shaw's review on #8179: the Pages preview build reads its env from
wrangler.toml `[env.preview.vars]`, not the GHA workflow `env:` block on
the build step (that scope only applies to the GHA shell, not the
downstream Vite process spawned by `wrangler pages deploy`).

Without this entry the Vite allowlist at vite.config.ts:63 has nothing
to inline, so `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_STEWARD_TENANT_ID` resolves to
`undefined` in the bundle and the SPA initialises the Steward SDK
without a tenant id. Magic-link goes through the proxy header pin from
the previous commit, but OAuth resolves tenant from the
`tenant_id` query param (steward auth.ts:2293) — which depends on the
SPA building the URL with the right id — so OAuth users registered on
staging end up under the prod `elizacloud` tenant without this fix.

Prod build is unaffected: `[vars]` (production block) doesn't set this,
so the prod SPA keeps falling back to the SDK's own default (which the
prod Steward instance already routes correctly).

* fix(cloud-api/steward): close two bypass routes that skip tenant pinning

The /steward/* proxy header injection (previous commits on this PR) only
covers requests that flow through the embedded handler. Two sibling
routes in auth/ make direct upstream fetches and were leaking to the
default tenant:

- steward-refresh/route.ts → POST baseUrl/auth/refresh
- steward-nonce-exchange/route.ts → POST baseUrl/auth/oauth/exchange

Both now forward `X-Steward-Tenant` from c.env.STEWARD_TENANT_ID when
set. Additionally, steward-nonce-exchange now falls back to the env
tenant when the SPA omits tenant_id in the body — without this, Steward
resolves `body.tenant_id=null` to STEWARD_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID and a
staging OAuth exchange would mint a session against the prod tenant.

Also corrected the misleading comment in embedded.ts: it claimed Steward
"auth routes" all honor X-Steward-Tenant, but OAuth /authorize reads
tenant only from the query param. The comment now distinguishes the two
paths and points at the wrangler.toml fix that handles OAuth.

Gap was surfaced by adversarial verification of Shaw's PR review.

fix(orchestrator): close completion-dedup TOCTOU race (duplicate replies) (#8161)

The cross-session completion-dedup guard (added for eliza#7967) read the
"first poster" slot before the awaited delivery loop but only wrote it after,
so two same-lineage retry sessions completing in the same event-loop window
both passed the check and double-posted to the user. Replace the split
check-then-mark with a synchronous compare-and-set (tryClaimCompletion) claimed
BEFORE the loop, with no await between the get and the set. A verify-retry
handoff returns earlier (before the claim), so an incomplete-build session never
claims its slot and its retry still posts; same-session progressive completes
still post (the claim is keyed by sessionId).

feat(cloud): enable agent web UI by default (ELIZA_UI_ENABLE=true) (#8167)

The per-agent web UI is the natural way users interact with a provisioned
sandbox. It was disabled by default in managed-eliza-config because the
original concern was that a public web UI exposed without auth would leak
agent state to anyone who guessed the agent subdomain.

That gate already exists: the agent-router (Hetzner control plane) checks
the per-agent ELIZA_API_TOKEN on every request before proxying to the
container's web port. A client that doesn't present a valid token gets
401 at the agent-router and never reaches the container. The web UI
itself is therefore safe to enable by default — it's not publicly
reachable, only reachable through the authenticated agent-router path.

Operators who want to disable UI per-agent can still set
ELIZA_UI_ENABLE=false in the sandbox's existingEnv at provision time.

Also update agent-flavors description to reflect the new default.

then copied caller-supplied customCredentials verbatim, with no deny-list check.
customCredentials arrive with the spawn request, so a caller could inject a key
the deny-list exists to keep out of sub-agents — a connector bot token
(DISCORD/TELEGRAM/SLACK/BOT *TOKEN) or ELIZA_VAULT_PASSPHRASE — defeating the
forwarding guard for exactly the secrets it protects.

process.env loop and the customCredentials loop through it; reject + warn on a
denied customCredential. Legit caller keys (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY,
etc.) are not in the deny-list, so this is non-breaking. Adds a unit test.

Cold start was ~36s, almost entirely timeout-waiting on cloud/Discord/
Anthropic endpoints that are slow or unreachable. The boot work itself
is sub-second; the stalls were missing or 10s fetch timeouts on the
gated critical path.

Quick wins:
- anthropic-login.ts: add AbortSignal.timeout(5s) to both OAuth fetches
  (refresh + token exchange) — refresh had no timeout and hung on the OS
  TCP timeout (~10s pre-resolve-setup pole).
- eliza.ts: lower Discord/cloud-GitHub probe timeouts 10s -> 3s.
- cloud-auth.ts: lower key-validation timeout 10s -> 2.5s.
- registry-client-network.ts: run the generated + index registry fetches
  concurrently instead of sequentially (offline path ~5s -> ~2.5s).

Structural:
- eliza.ts: move the Discord/cloud-GitHub Promise.all join off the
  blocking path into the deferred phase (verified no blocking-phase
  plugin reads DISCORD_APPLICATION_ID/GITHUB_TOKEN at resolve time).
- credentials.ts/eliza.ts: split applySubscriptionCredentials into a
  local-only synchronous part (model.primary derivation, kept blocking)
  and a deferred OAuth-import part (logging-only, no config/env mutation),
  so the network probe no longer blocks plugin resolution.
- shared/elizacloud/is-cloud-reachable.ts: new per-boot-memoized
  isCloudReachable() probe (1s timeout); cloud-auth and registry-client
  short-circuit to the offline path when unreachable.
- bin.ts: enable Node 24 module.enableCompileCache() (defensive) so 2nd+
  cold boots skip recompiling transpiled plugin source.

the server replayed state.eventBuffer.slice(-120), re-flooding the client with

biggest lever on the statesync KPI (reconnectMs + broadcast skew under load).

  slice(-120) behavior — existing clients send no cursor and are unaffected.

  suffix, so events pushed via the /api/agent-event REST mirror (which lacks
  bufferSeq) still filter/sort correctly.

onReconnect/RESYNC reconciliation remains the source of truth, so replay is a

feat(app-core): cloud SSO /pair handler for the dashboard popup flow

The dashboard "Open Web UI" popup navigates to `<agent>/pair?token=<X>` and
expects the agent to exchange the token for an API key, then sign the
browser in to the SPA. We had everything wired EXCEPT the agent-side
handler — the popup landed on a 404 fallback (login screen), the SPA tried
`POST /api/auth/login/password` / `POST /api/auth/pair`, both refused, and
the user saw "Reconnecting…" loops.

This handler closes that gap. `GET /pair?token=X` on the agent runtime:

1. Calls cloud-api `POST /api/auth/pair` server-side (the existing endpoint
   that consumes the pairing token, verifies origin, returns the agent's
   ELIZA_API_TOKEN — already in publicPathPrefixes and rate-limited
   STRICT).
2. Serves an HTML page with an inline script that pins the returned key on
   `window.__ELIZAOS_API_TOKEN__` (the global the SPA's ElizaClient reads
   on hydrate — see packages/ui/src/api/client-base.ts:388) and redirects
   to `/`.
3. On any failure (missing token, expired token, cloud-api 5xx, timeout,
   rate-limit) returns a styled error page with a back link to
   elizacloud.ai/dashboard/agents so the user can retry.

Why server-side relay: the agent web UI lives on the docker node's public
IP, which is NOT in cloud-api's CORS allowlist. A direct browser fetch
to api.elizacloud.ai would fail preflight. Doing the exchange from the
agent's Node process sidesteps CORS entirely.

Security:
- The token is single-use, 60s TTL, triple-bound to (user, org, agent) +
  origin at generate time. Cloud-api enforces all of those at exchange.
- Inline-script escaping uses `JSON.stringify(...).replace(/</g,
  "\\u003c")` so a malicious key with `</script>` cannot break out.
- Rate limit via `getSensitiveLimiter("cloud.pair.relay")` — 5/min/IP,
  same bucket model as bootstrap exchange.
- Cache-Control: no-store; X-Frame-Options: DENY; Referrer-Policy:
  no-referrer.

Known limitations:
- Pairing token is consumed atomically on the cloud-api side. If the
  agent's HTML send fails after the token is consumed, the user must
  click "Open Web UI" again from the dashboard. The 60s TTL caps the
  damage. Documented; idempotent preview is a follow-up if real users
  hit it.
- Existing agents on the old image will 404 `/pair` — same as today, no
  regression. Pickup requires the image rebuild + sandbox restart.

feat(app-core): cloud SSO /pair handler for the dashboard popup flow

The dashboard "Open Web UI" popup navigates to `<agent>/pair?token=<X>` and
expects the agent to exchange the token for an API key, then sign the
browser in to the SPA. We had everything wired EXCEPT the agent-side
handler — the popup landed on a 404 fallback (login screen), the SPA tried
`POST /api/auth/login/password` / `POST /api/auth/pair`, both refused, and
the user saw "Reconnecting…" loops.

This handler closes that gap. `GET /pair?token=X` on the agent runtime:

1. Calls cloud-api `POST /api/auth/pair` server-side (the existing endpoint
   that consumes the pairing token, verifies origin, returns the agent's
   ELIZA_API_TOKEN — already in publicPathPrefixes and rate-limited
   STRICT).
2. Serves an HTML page with an inline script that pins the returned key on
   `window.__ELIZAOS_API_TOKEN__` (the global the SPA's ElizaClient reads
   on hydrate — see packages/ui/src/api/client-base.ts:388) and redirects
   to `/`.
3. On any failure (missing token, expired token, cloud-api 5xx, timeout,
   rate-limit) returns a styled error page with a back link to
   elizacloud.ai/dashboard/agents so the user can retry.

Why server-side relay: the agent web UI lives on the docker node's public
IP, which is NOT in cloud-api's CORS allowlist. A direct browser fetch
to api.elizacloud.ai would fail preflight. Doing the exchange from the
agent's Node process sidesteps CORS entirely.

Security:
- The token is single-use, 60s TTL, triple-bound to (user, org, agent) +
  origin at generate time. Cloud-api enforces all of those at exchange.
- Inline-script escaping uses `JSON.stringify(...).replace(/</g,
  "\\u003c")` so a malicious key with `</script>` cannot break out.
- Rate limit via `getSensitiveLimiter("cloud.pair.relay")` — 5/min/IP,
  same bucket model as bootstrap exchange.
- Cache-Control: no-store; X-Frame-Options: DENY; Referrer-Policy:
  no-referrer.

Known limitations:
- Pairing token is consumed atomically on the cloud-api side. If the
  agent's HTML send fails after the token is consumed, the user must
  click "Open Web UI" again from the dashboard. The 60s TTL caps the
  damage. Documented; idempotent preview is a follow-up if real users
  hit it.
- Existing agents on the old image will 404 `/pair` — same as today, no
  regression. Pickup requires the image rebuild + sandbox restart.

fix(cloud): send PKCE on Steward OAuth + sign the nonce-exchange call

require a PKCE code_challenge and made mutating /auth/* require an HMAC
request signature. The Eliza Cloud client never sent either, so Google
login 400s ("code_challenge is required") and the OAuth code-exchange
POST 401s ("X-Steward-Signature header required").

  the OAuth redirect and send the challenge at /authorize; fail fast when
  it can't be persisted.
- cloud-api: the nonce-exchange route bypasses the /steward/* signing
  proxy, so sign its direct /auth/oauth/exchange POST (new sign.ts, kept
  byte-for-byte in lockstep with embedded.ts) and forward code_verifier.

canonical order + an independently-verifiable signature + body-tamper
rejection.

Refs #8257.

fix(cloud-api/steward): sign mutating proxy requests + idempotency-key

Steward backend gates mutating sensitive paths (/auth, /agents, /vault,
/trade, /wallets/batch, /accounts, /adapters, /policies, /secrets,
/approvals, /intents, /audit, /global-wallet — see Steward
packages/api/src/middleware/sensitive-paths.ts) on THREE guards:

  - request-expiry.ts requires X-Steward-Request-Expires-At
  - authorization-signature.ts requires X-Steward-Signature: v1=<hmac-hex>
  - idempotency.ts requires Idempotency-Key on every signed request

Before this change the cloud-api embedded Steward proxy forwarded the
request verbatim with only X-Steward-Tenant patched in, so any browser-
driven mutating call (Magic Link 'send', passkey register, etc.) returned
HTTP 400 'Request expiry header required' or 'Signed requests require an
Idempotency-Key header' after the Steward deploy that flipped the guards
from advisory to required. The bug was masked when users had a live
Steward session cookie — only first sign-in / token refresh surfaced it.

Fix:
- When STEWARD_REQUEST_SIGNING_SECRET is configured AND the inbound
  method is mutating, the proxy stamps the freshness header (60s TTL),
  preserves the SPA-supplied Idempotency-Key (or stamps a fresh UUID v4
  when absent), then HMACs the upstream-shaped canonical string (method,
  pathname+search, tenant + all SHA-256-hashed sensitive headers,
  timestamps, idempotency key, body hash) exactly the same way the
  Steward middleware verifies it.
- Skipping the signing when the secret is absent keeps the rollback path
  one wrangler secret deletion away.

Verified end-to-end: manually-signed POST /steward/auth/email/send with
all three headers + the shared secret now returns 200 from staging
Steward and queues the Magic Link email.

Synthetic test secret literal is wrapped in 'gitleaks:allow' magic
comment so the test file can't be confused with a real leaked secret on
future scans.

7 sociable unit tests cover: header injection, canonical-string parity
with the Steward verifier, GET-skip, secret-absent skip (rollback path),
idempotency-key auto-stamp (UUID v4 shape), SPA-supplied idempotency
passthrough (retry dedup), public tenant-config short-circuit unchanged.

Deploy steps (operator):
  - Worker secret STEWARD_REQUEST_SIGNING_SECRET set on staging + prod
    matching the value the Railway-deployed Steward already has.
  - No Steward backend changes needed — the secret was already present.
  - CI cloud-cf-deploy.yml auto-redeploys the Worker on merge.

fix(cloud-shared): allow third-party app origins on the public API (CORS)

The global CORS middleware (app.use("*", corsMiddleware) in
cloud-api/src/bootstrap-app.ts) only reflected Access-Control-Allow-Origin for
first-party origins (elizacloud.ai + localhost + pages previews) with
credentials:true, and omitted the header for everyone else. So registered
third-party browser apps (e.g. supakan.nubs.site, *.apps.elizacloud.ai) were
blocked by CORS on the public token-authed API (/api/v1/chat/completions,
/api/v1/app-credits/*, /api/v1/models, ...), even though they authenticate with
a Bearer eliza_* key — defeating the documented "CORS open; security via auth
tokens" model in lib/middleware/cors-apps.ts.

Split the policy by origin class:
- first-party origins: reflect origin + credentials:true (unchanged; cookie auth)
- any other origin: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * WITHOUT credentials, so
  token-authed apps can call the API from the browser. Safe: a cross-origin page
  still cannot read a response it has no valid token to request, and no cookies
  are sent to a non-first-party origin.

The public path uses origin:"*" (not a reflecting function) on purpose: it sets
Access-Control-Allow-Origin on every request, including no-Origin requests,
BEFORE next(). That preserves the invariant secureHeaders (registered right
after CORS) depends on — CORS must touch c.res so Hono re-wraps handler
responses with mutable Headers. A reflecting function writes nothing on a
no-Origin request, leaving raw Response.json(...) passthrough responses frozen,
so the downstream secureHeaders write threw 'Can't modify immutable headers' and
500'd the /api/v1/voice/* routes for Bearer-token (no Origin) requests.

Tests cover first-party (credentialed), third-party (wildcard, no credentials),
preflight with X-App-Id, and the no-Origin invariant guard.

zai-glm-4.7), but getLanguageModel sent every model through the BitRouter
catch-all (when BITROUTER_API_KEY is set) BEFORE reaching the Cerebras branch,

BitRouter's catalog (it carries the prefixed `openai/gpt-oss-120b`), so the
Cerebras branch was unreachable in prod and default inference would fail.

BitRouter catch-all in both getLanguageModel (routing) and
resolveAiProviderSource (billing attribution), mirroring the existing
Groq/Vast native checks. isCerebrasNativeModel matches ONLY the two bare
default IDs and requiresBitRouterRouting is false for them, so non-Cerebras
models still hit BitRouter unchanged — tight blast radius. Billing now
attributes these defaults to `cerebras` (matching where they actually run).

Note: hasLanguageModelProviderConfigured has the same Groq→BitRouter→Cerebras
ordering; left as-is (config-presence check, not routing) but worth a follow-up
for full consistency.

fix(agent/cloud-sso): wire /pair handler into the real HTTP server

The cloud SSO popup hands the token off to the agent at `<webui>/pair?token=X`.
The handler exists in `packages/app-core/src/api/cloud-pair-route.ts`, but
the previous registration was on `packages/app-core/src/api/server.ts` — a
DIFFERENT HTTP server than the one the cloud agent runtime actually exposes.

The agent runtime entrypoint is `packages/agent/dist/bin.js start`, which
serves over `packages/agent/src/api/server.ts`. That server's dispatch chain
falls through to `serveStaticUi` for any non-API GET, which returns the SPA
index.html as a catch-all — so `/pair?token=X` was getting served as the
SPA login screen and the popup ended up at the password gate.

Fix:
- Export `./api/cloud-pair-route` as a subpath from @elizaos/app-core.
- Import the handler in the agent server and call it BEFORE `serveStaticUi`.

The 10 existing unit tests in cloud-pair-route.test.ts still cover the handler
itself; verification of the wiring is post-build curl + Playwright (see PR body).

fix(dev): reliable agent hot-reload via source-only watcher

The dev API child ran with watch off by default (and auto-disabled whenever a
concurrent build was detected), so agent/plugin source edits never reached the
running agent. `node --watch` followed imports into dist/ and hot-reloaded
mid-build, which is why it had to stay disabled.

Replace it with a source-only watcher (packages/*/src + plugins/*/src,
excluding frontend packages, dist, node_modules, and tests) that bounces the
supervised API child on change — decoupled from dist churn, so concurrent
builds never trigger it. Add an intentional restart() to the API supervisor
that relaunches immediately without counting toward the crash-loop streak.
On by default; opt out with ELIZA_DEV_NO_WATCH=1.

fix(plugin-task-coordinator): reset CompareView round on slot-set changes

Three adversarially-verified bugs in the odysseus Compare arena, all one root
cause: a vote result is tracked by INDEX (winnerIdx) + a revealed flag, but the
slot-set mutators never cleared it, so a stale verdict survived structural
changes to the lineup:

- removing a pane after voting shifted the array → winnerIdx mis-highlighted
  the wrong pane;
- Shuffle after a vote re-randomized the lineup but kept the stale winner AND
  left reveal on, leaking the freshly-randomized blind names;
- Adding a pane after a vote rendered the brand-new pane as a loser.

Fix: a shared resetRound() (clear revealed + winnerIdx) called from addSlot,
removeSlot, and shuffleFill — a reveal/winner only applies to the exact lineup
that was voted on. Minimal, single-file, no behavior change to an in-progress
(un-voted) round.

fix(dev): ignore bulk file churn in agent hot-reload

In a tree the swarm continuously rewrites (git resets/checkouts/builds),
the source watcher fired on every mass rewrite → the agent API restarted →
the browser stormed with 502/503 + WebSocket failures while it rebooted.

The watcher now reports how many DISTINCT files changed per debounce window;
dev-ui skips the reload when that exceeds a threshold (default 8, override
ELIZA_DEV_HOT_RELOAD_BULK_LIMIT) — a reset/checkout/build touches many files at
once, a human edit touches one or a few. Combined with the existing ready-gate
(only restart a healthy agent) this keeps backend hot-reload working for real
edits while ignoring churn.

feat(cloud-frontend): wizard exposes Shared vs Dedicated execution mode explicitly (#8261)

* feat(cloud-frontend): wizard exposes Shared vs Dedicated execution mode explicitly

PR #8223 introduced agent tiering (cloud-shared/agent-tier.ts): an agent
without a docker image runs container-free on the shared multi-tenant
runtime; an agent with one gets its own Docker container on Hetzner. The
wizard hid that choice behind a flavor dropdown — picking the default
'Eliza Agent' silently created a Shared agent (no node_id, no chat works
via the Open Web UI flow because the agent UUID subdomain doesn't resolve
to anything), and picking 'Eliza Agent (Develop)' or 'Custom Image'
escalated to Docker. The user couldn't tell from the UI which one they
were getting.

Refactor — single dialog, no extra step:

- Add an 'Execution mode' radio-card group (Shared default, Dedicated
  opt-in) with hierarchical labels, icons (Cloud/Server lucide), and
  per-mode pricing chip (free vs hourly).
- Each card's description names what the mode is good for and why you'd
  pick it: Shared → multi-tenant chat/webhook/cron, Dedicated → required
  for custom images, persistent-connection plugins, BYO runtime.
- Image selector + custom-image input collapse under the Dedicated card,
  so a Shared agent literally cannot have an image attached.
- Auto-start toggle and hourly-rate cost notice are dedicated-only — for
  shared we surface 'No compute cost. You only pay for LLM tokens.' so
  free doesn't read as misleading.
- Send dockerImage in the create body iff the user picked Dedicated,
  matching cloud-shared/agent-tier.ts (empty dockerImage → tier=shared).
- CTA label now reflects the actual outcome:
    Shared    → 'Create shared agent'
    Dedicated → 'Deploy Docker container' (autoStart on)
              → 'Create (don't start)' (autoStart off)

Keeps the existing ProvisioningProgress flow unchanged for the dedicated
path, and the existing i18n key prefix cloud.createAgent.* with new keys:
modeSharedTitle/Description/Price, modeDedicatedTitle/Description, image,
deployDedicated, createDedicated, createShared, sharedCostNote.

Tested: cloud-frontend typecheck passes against the unrelated pre-existing
core/i18n missing-generated-file error; biome --write applied auto-fixes.

The dashboard custom-image E2E used the old flat flavor dropdown + 'Deploy'

so the test now selects the Dedicated radio first, opens the 'Image' selector

* fix(cloud-api): prefer agent bridge_url over broken UUID subdomain for pairing

The pairing-token endpoint returned redirectUrl=<uuid>.<ELIZA_CLOUD_AGENT_BASE_DOMAIN>/pair?token=…
for Docker-backed agents. That hostname only resolves to the agent if a
wildcard Worker / signed tunnel-proxy entry is in place — none currently
exists. The old behavior was masked by a wildcard Worker route on
*.elizacloud.ai that returned cloud-api root JSON (so the popup loaded
*something* even though it wasn't the agent UI). That wildcard was removed
to unblock staging Pages, surfacing the underlying gap: every fresh
'Open Web UI' click now lands on a Vercel 404.

The agent's bridge_url (e.g. http://168.119.244.189:19027) is the
Hetzner public IP+port and already serves the in-container HTTP server,
including the /pair handler from PR #8236 — verified via curl on the
existing sso-mpzfnjwv sandbox (returns 403 'Sign-in link expired' for a
bogus token, which proves the handler is wired and the cloud-api proxy
flow works end-to-end).

Fix: in resolveManagedWebUiUrl, return the parsed bridge_url origin
first (validated as http/https) and fall back to the legacy
<uuid>.<baseDomain> string only when no bridge URL is stored — keeping
that as a forward-compatibility hook for when a signed tunnel-proxy
hostname gets written to the sandbox row by a future Hetzner provisioner
revision.

6 unit tests cover the parser contract: valid http URL, path stripping,
whitespace trimming, null/empty handling, non-http(s) rejection, garbage
rejection.

Behavior unchanged for callers because resolveSandboxBridgeUrl is the

fix(cloud): send PKCE on Steward OAuth + sign the nonce-exchange call (#8259)

Steward's auth hardening (3faf518) made /auth/oauth/:provider/authorize
require a PKCE code_challenge and made mutating /auth/* require an HMAC
request signature. The Eliza Cloud client never sent either, so Google
login 400s ("code_challenge is required") and the OAuth code-exchange
POST 401s ("X-Steward-Signature header required").

- cloud-frontend: generate / store / replay a PKCE S256 verifier across
  the OAuth redirect and send the challenge at /authorize; fail fast when
  it can't be persisted.
- cloud-api: the nonce-exchange route bypasses the /steward/* signing
  proxy, so sign its direct /auth/oauth/exchange POST (new sign.ts, kept
  byte-for-byte in lockstep with embedded.ts) and forward code_verifier.

Tests: PKCE S256 locked to the RFC 7636 Appendix B vector; signer
canonical order + an independently-verifiable signature + body-tamper
rejection.

Refs #8257.

feat(cloud-auth): mint agent tokens with trade:order scope (#8254)

Cloud-provisioned agents are trading agents. Steward's hyperliquid order
endpoint (POST /v1/trade/hyperliquid/order) gates on a `trade:order` scope
claim in the agent JWT (added in Steward's security hardening). The cloud
agent-token issuer previously minted tokens with only `agent_id` and no scope
claim, so every order was rejected with 'Token missing required trade:order
scope'.

Add `scope: "agent"` + `scopes: ["trade:order"]` to the minted token.
Steward still enforces per-agent policy caps + owner-authorized trade sessions
on top of this; the scope only permits reaching the order route.

Verified end-to-end: owner session -> POST /v1/trade/sessions = 201, order
submission previously 403'd purely on the missing scope.

fix(cloud-api/steward): sign mutating proxy requests + idempotency-key (#8256)

Steward backend gates mutating sensitive paths (/auth, /agents, /vault,
/trade, /wallets/batch, /accounts, /adapters, /policies, /secrets,
/approvals, /intents, /audit, /global-wallet — see Steward
packages/api/src/middleware/sensitive-paths.ts) on THREE guards:

  - request-expiry.ts requires X-Steward-Request-Expires-At
  - authorization-signature.ts requires X-Steward-Signature: v1=<hmac-hex>
  - idempotency.ts requires Idempotency-Key on every signed request

Before this change the cloud-api embedded Steward proxy forwarded the
request verbatim with only X-Steward-Tenant patched in, so any browser-
driven mutating call (Magic Link 'send', passkey register, etc.) returned
HTTP 400 'Request expiry header required' or 'Signed requests require an
Idempotency-Key header' after the Steward deploy that flipped the guards
from advisory to required. The bug was masked when users had a live
Steward session cookie — only first sign-in / token refresh surfaced it.

Fix:
- When STEWARD_REQUEST_SIGNING_SECRET is configured AND the inbound
  method is mutating, the proxy stamps the freshness header (60s TTL),
  preserves the SPA-supplied Idempotency-Key (or stamps a fresh UUID v4
  when absent), then HMACs the upstream-shaped canonical string (method,
  pathname+search, tenant + all SHA-256-hashed sensitive headers,
  timestamps, idempotency key, body hash) exactly the same way the
  Steward middleware verifies it.
- Skipping the signing when the secret is absent keeps the rollback path
  one wrangler secret deletion away.

Verified end-to-end: manually-signed POST /steward/auth/email/send with
all three headers + the shared secret now returns 200 from staging
Steward and queues the Magic Link email.

Synthetic test secret literal is wrapped in 'gitleaks:allow' magic
comment so the test file can't be confused with a real leaked secret on
future scans.

7 sociable unit tests cover: header injection, canonical-string parity
with the Steward verifier, GET-skip, secret-absent skip (rollback path),
idempotency-key auto-stamp (UUID v4 shape), SPA-supplied idempotency
passthrough (retry dedup), public tenant-config short-circuit unchanged.

Deploy steps (operator):
  - Worker secret STEWARD_REQUEST_SIGNING_SECRET set on staging + prod
    matching the value the Railway-deployed Steward already has.
  - No Steward backend changes needed — the secret was already present.
  - CI cloud-cf-deploy.yml auto-redeploys the Worker on merge.

fix(dev-ui): stop injecting tsx loader when API runs under Bun

resolveApiRuntimeCommand began returning the absolute bun path from
which("bun") instead of the literal "bun", so the caller's
apiRuntimeIsBun = (apiRuntimeCmd === "bun") check went false even when
Bun was selected. The API child was then spawned with `--import tsx`,
and Bun chokes on tsx's CJS loader entry — crashing the dev API at boot
with `Cannot find module './cjs/index.cjs' from ''`, which crash-loops
the orchestrator and SIGTERMs vite (Dev Smoke failure).

Return { runtime, command } from resolveApiRuntimeCommand and derive
apiRuntimeIsBun from the runtime kind, decoupling the bun/node decision
from the resolved executable path string.

#8233 flipped the default text models to bare Cerebras IDs (gpt-oss-120b,
zai-glm-4.7), but getLanguageModel sent every model through the BitRouter
catch-all (when BITROUTER_API_KEY is set) BEFORE reaching the Cerebras branch,
and toBitRouterModelId passes those bare IDs through unchanged. In production
both BITROUTER_API_KEY and CEREBRAS_API_KEY are set, so default inference was
routed to BitRouter as bare `gpt-oss-120b`/`zai-glm-4.7` — IDs absent from
BitRouter's catalog (it carries the prefixed `openai/gpt-oss-120b`), so the
Cerebras branch was unreachable in prod and default inference would fail.

BitRouter catch-all in both getLanguageModel (routing) and
resolveAiProviderSource (billing attribution), mirroring the existing
Groq/Vast native checks. isCerebrasNativeModel matches ONLY the two bare
default IDs and requiresBitRouterRouting is false for them, so non-Cerebras
models still hit BitRouter unchanged — tight blast radius. Billing now
attributes these defaults to `cerebras` (matching where they actually run).

Note: hasLanguageModelProviderConfigured has the same Groq→BitRouter→Cerebras
ordering; left as-is (config-presence check, not routing) but worth a follow-up
for full consistency.

SPA login screen and the popup ended up at the password gate.

- Export `./api/cloud-pair-route` as a subpath from @elizaos/app-core.
- Import the handler in the agent server and call it BEFORE `serveStaticUi`.

itself; verification of the wiring is post-build curl + Playwright (see PR body).

fix(dev): reliable agent hot-reload via source-only watcher (#8228)

The dev API child ran with watch off by default (and auto-disabled whenever a
concurrent build was detected), so agent/plugin source edits never reached the
running agent. `node --watch` followed imports into dist/ and hot-reloaded
mid-build, which is why it had to stay disabled.

Replace it with a source-only watcher (packages/*/src + plugins/*/src,
excluding frontend packages, dist, node_modules, and tests) that bounces the
supervised API child on change — decoupled from dist churn, so concurrent
builds never trigger it. Add an intentional restart() to the API supervisor
that relaunches immediately without counting toward the crash-loop streak.
On by default; opt out with ELIZA_DEV_NO_WATCH=1.

fix(orchestrator): honor the configured session timeout for the ACP initialize handshake

NativeAcpClient.connect() sent the `initialize` JSON-RPC request without a
timeout, so it always used the hardcoded 300s DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS and ignored the
per-session `timeoutMs` (set from ACPX_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS / ELIZA_ACP_PROMPT_TIMEOUT_MS)
that already governs `session/prompt`. A cold first spawn that compiles the
agent's TS tree and installs its provider npm package (e.g. @ai-sdk/cerebras) can
exceed 300s, so the handshake aborted with "ACP request timed out: initialize"
before the agent was ever usable.

the 300s default when unset), and add a regression test that proves the
handshake survives past 300s and still times out at the configured budget.

fix(orchestrator): forward Windows env (Path casing) to ACP sub-agents

`shouldForwardEnv` matched the OS search path as `key === "PATH"`,
case-sensitively. The repo runtime is Bun, and Bun on Windows reports the key as
`Path` (not `PATH`) — so `buildEnv` forwarded NONE of it, and every spawned ACP
sub-agent inherited an empty PATH. The vendored opencode shim then died at spawn
with `'bun' is not recognized as an internal or external command`, making
ACP-driven coding agents unusable on Windows.

Match the OS system vars case-insensitively (a Set keyed by uppercase name),
broaden the set to the Windows essentials cmd.exe + Bun + the agent's
config/cache resolution need (PATHEXT, SYSTEMROOT, COMSPEC, TEMP, USERPROFILE,
APPDATA, …), and canonicalize each forwarded system var to its uppercase form in
`buildEnv` so a child never inherits two casings of the same var (the winner is
undefined on Windows) and JS consumers that read `env.PATH` resolve it. The
projection is extracted into the pure, exported `forwardableSubAgentEnv` /
`canonicalForwardedEnvKey` and covered by unit tests. The deny-list still runs
first (deny wins over allow), so no secret is newly forwarded.

Surfaced spawning a real opencode/Cerebras sub-agent on Windows.

fix(cloud): consume Steward OAuth code from URL fragment (#code=)

Steward's OAuth callback now returns the one-time authorization code in the
URL fragment (`https://elizacloud.ai/login#code=<NONCE>`) rather than the
query string. This is the same fragment-delivery rationale already used for
`#token=` — the fragment never reaches the server (no access logs, no Referer)
— but `consumeStewardCodeFromQuery()` only read `?code=` from the query, and
`consumeStewardTokensFromHash()` only matches `#token=`, so a `#code=`
fragment was silently dropped: Google/Discord/GitHub sign-in completed the
provider round-trip, landed back on `/login#code=...`, and never exchanged the
code — leaving the user stuck on the login screen.

Extend the existing reader to accept the code from either carrier: try
`?code=` first, then fall back to the `#code=` fragment, stripping whichever
it consumed (preserving any non-OAuth query/fragment params) so the code never
lingers in history. The index.html pre-init script only snapshots/strips
`#token=`, so a `#code=` fragment is intact on `location.hash` when React
mounts.

Adds steward-session.test.ts covering both carriers, the
prefer-query-when-both case, and that a `#token=` fragment is left untouched
for consumeStewardTokensFromHash().

Steward's `GET /auth/callback/email` redirects login failures back with
`?error=email_auth_failed&reason=<code>`, but the SPA's reason→message map
only handled invalid_token / expired_token / email_mismatch / server_error.
Every other reason Steward actually emits — invalid_link, tenant_mismatch,
rate_limited, method_disabled, sso_required, tenant_not_found,
tenant_forbidden, missing_params, mfa_required — fell through to the generic
"Couldn't complete sign-in. Try again.", hiding the true cause (this is why a
failing magic link only ever said "Try again").

Add a case for each. `invalid_link` copy is intentionally neutral: the link
isn't necessarily expired/used (it can fail when the verification store can't
resolve the token), so "request a new one" alone could be a dead end — point
the user at support if it persists. Copy-only; no auth/behavioral change.

feat(orchestrator): bridge child USE_SKILL parent-agent to the broker

A spawned coding agent (over ACP) cannot run account-bound Cloud commands
itself; SKILLS.md tells it to emit `USE_SKILL parent-agent <json>` instead.
Nothing parsed that, so runParentAgentBroker (the only emitter of
`spend_auto_authorized`) had no production caller — the autonomy mechanism
was unit-tested but unreachable by a live agent.

Add parent-agent-dispatch.ts: a string/escape-aware extractor that pulls a
complete `USE_SKILL parent-agent {json}` directive out of streamed child
text, plus a dispatch helper that runs it through runParentAgentBroker and
streams `result.text` back via acp.sendToSession (never throws — broker
failures are reported back to the child).

Wire it into SubAgentRouter.handleEvent: accumulate the child's `message`
chunks per session, dispatch on the first complete directive, and cap
round-trips with ACPX_SUB_AGENT_ROUND_TRIP_CAP. Detection is marker-guarded
(only acts on text containing `USE_SKILL parent-agent`, which ordinary tasks
never emit) so the hot path stays inert for every other flow. The buffer is
trimmed synchronously before any await, so out-of-order chunks cannot
re-dispatch a directive.

fix(orchestrator): deliver the parent-agent reply once the child turn is idle

A spawned coding agent streams its `USE_SKILL parent-agent` directive mid-turn,
then ends the turn to await the reply. Delivering that reply via
`acp.sendToSession` is itself a new prompt, which the native ACP transport
rejects with "session is already busy" until the current turn finishes. The
dispatcher delivered once and dropped the reply on that error, so a live
economics loop stalled on its very first directive (the child never received the
cloud-command result and could not continue).

`deliverReplyToChild` now retries delivery until the session goes idle, bounded
by the prompt timeout; a terminal (non-busy) error or the deadline returns a
logged failure without throwing. Covered by new dispatch tests (retry-then-
succeed, deadline-expiry, terminal-error-no-retry).

Surfaced running the economics goal loop end-to-end against cloud:mock with a
real opencode/Cerebras sub-agent.

fix(cloud-api): bill containers when earnings conversion fails

redeemableEarningsService.convertToCredits THROWS on insufficient/contended
earnings for a positive amount (it never returns success=false), so the old
`if (!conversion.success)` branch was dead and the throw propagated out of the
handler — the container was recorded as errored and never billed (free hosting
for the day). The unconditional `+ fromEarnings` in newBalance would also have
inflated the balance by earnings that were never debited. Catch the failure and
charge the full day to credits (fromEarnings=0), matching the documented intent.
fix(cloud-api): bill containers when earnings conversion fails

feat(cloud-shared): idempotent earnings conversion + billing-period helper

Add the building blocks for making the container-billing cron safe to
re-run without double-debiting:

- convertToCredits gains an optional `idempotencyKey`. When set, the
  conversion looks up a prior credit_conversion ledger entry (under the
  per-user advisory lock) and returns it instead of debiting earnings
  again. Backed by a partial unique index on
  redeemable_earnings_ledger((metadata->>'idempotency_key')).
- computeContainerBillingPeriod normalizes a run timestamp to its UTC day
  so the period (and the idempotency key derived from it) is deterministic
  across same-day re-runs.
- container_billing_records gains a partial unique index on
  (container_id, billing_period_start) WHERE status='success' so at most
  one successful charge per container per period can be recorded.

Migration 0139 adds both indexes and dedupes any pre-existing duplicate
success rows first so the unique index can be created on existing data.
All changes are additive/backward-compatible; callers are wired next.

feat(cloud-api): make the container-billing cron idempotent per period

Wire the day-aligned period and idempotency primitives into the daily
billing run so a re-run (manual trigger, overlapping cron, retry) cannot
double-debit:

- listBillableContainers(now) now gates on next_billing_at — containers
  already paid for the current period are skipped, not re-billed.
- recordSuccessfulDailyBilling row-locks the container and no-ops if the
  period is already billed, closing the read->write race between listing
  and charging.
- The credit_transaction now records -fromCredits (the actual credit
  balance movement) instead of -dailyCost, so credit_balance reconciles
  with sum(credit_transactions); the earnings portion stays on the
  earnings ledger. dailyCost/split are kept in metadata.
- The cron derives one runNow and one UTC-day period per run, passes the
  period to both billing paths, and keys convertToCredits by
  container+period so the earnings conversion is idempotent too.

fix(cloud-api): sign /api/auth/steward-refresh upstream call to Steward (#8287)

Same bypass-route signing bug as #8259 (nonce-exchange) but on
steward-refresh. The /steward/* embedded proxy signs every mutating
request automatically; bypass routes that forward to Steward themselves
have to call signStewardMutatingRequest or Steward's
authorization-signature middleware 502s with
{error:'Request expiry header required', code:'internal_error'}.

After yesterday's magic-link callback fix (#8282), the verify path lands
on /api/auth/steward-session and immediately tries
/api/auth/steward-refresh to rotate the freshly-issued tokens — that
unsigned call now 502s, the SPA's session-bootstrap rejects, and the
user gets kicked back to /login?returnTo=/dashboard with the Steward
error surfaced inline ('Request expiry header required').

Plumb c.env.STEWARD_REQUEST_SIGNING_SECRET into callStewardRefresh and

The step assumed *.elizacloud.ai/* would be a Worker route that returns
'agent not found or not running' for non-existent agent UUIDs. That
contract was never wired — the only handler that returns that string is
the Hetzner-side agent-router daemon

cloud-api Worker. So in practice the Worker wildcard returned its root
JSON ({name:'eliza-cloud-api', …}) instead.

Each time someone added the route back to satisfy the verifier — most
recently overnight — it caught staging.elizacloud.ai/* before Pages
could serve the SPA, so the dashboard returned cloud-api JSON and every
SPA-dependent flow (Magic Link callback, agents list, etc.) broke at
once. Manual deletes by me yesterday and today both got reverted because
the verifier kept telling whoever was deploying that 'something was
missing'.

Drop the step + leave a NOTE explaining the trap so the next person
doesn't reach for the wildcard. When the Worker is taught to handle
agent UUID hostnames (forward to the matching sandbox bridge_url, or
return a real 404), reintroduce a route + verifier together. Until then,
agent subdomains live on the agents-staging.elizacloud.ai and
agents.elizacloud.ai zones (existing Worker routes that point to
waifu-dev-router), and staging/prod dashboards fall through to Pages.

* cleanup: drop the NOTE that replaced the broken verify step

fix(cloud-frontend): staging SPA hits staging Worker (not prod) for Steward auth (#8282)

resolveStewardAuthEndpoint mapped staging.elizacloud.ai onto the same
ELIZA_CLOUD_DIRECT_AUTH_BASE as the prod hosts — https://api.elizacloud.ai.
Each Worker pins its Steward tenant via STEWARD_TENANT_ID
(elizacloud-staging vs elizacloud), and the embedded /steward proxy and
the steward-nonce-exchange bypass route both forward that header to
Steward. A code minted by the staging tenant therefore 401s when the
exchange happens against the prod tenant. The bypass route's response is
{error:'Invalid or already-used code', code:'code_invalid'} and the SPA
silently lands back on /login — exactly the magic-link callback bug.

Replace the single shared base string with a per-host map so
staging.elizacloud.ai routes to https://api-staging.elizacloud.ai
(matching what the Pages Function _proxy.ts already does for the
same-origin /api/* calls).

Verified live via Playwright: opening /login#code=… on staging previously
POSTed to https://api.elizacloud.ai/api/auth/steward-nonce-exchange (prod
Worker, prod tenant). After this change it goes to api-staging where the
code's tenant context matches.

Existing resolveStewardAuthEndpoint test was actively asserting the bug —
it expected staging.elizacloud.ai to map to api.elizacloud.ai. Updated to
keep the prod cases and add a tenant-isolation case covering all three
endpoints on staging.

fix(cloud): accept ?token= on SSE GETs so EventSource clients can authenticate

WHY:
EventSource (the browser SSE client) cannot set request headers, so it has
no way to send `Authorization: Bearer <ELIZA_API_TOKEN>`. The global auth
gate in server.ts only inspects headers via extractAuthToken(req), so every
SSE handshake from the cloud web UI 401s before the route handler runs
(local-inference + computer-use stream endpoints inherit the same gate).
The token itself is correct -- it's the same `agent_<uuid>` value the REST
chat path accepts as a Bearer -- only the transport is wrong.

WHAT:
Extend extractAuthToken() with a tightly-scoped SSE query-token fallback,
mirroring the existing ELIZA_ALLOW_WS_QUERY_TOKEN=1 path that already ships
for WebSockets. The fallback is gated on:
  - ELIZA_ALLOW_WS_QUERY_TOKEN=1 (cloud-only opt-in, no regression elsewhere),
  - method === GET (read-only),
  - Accept header contains text/event-stream (scope strictly to SSE so a
    stray ?token= on a JSON endpoint cannot bypass the header path or leak
    via proxy access logs),
  - token length <= 1024 (mirrors the header cap).
Validation still goes through tokenMatches() -> crypto.timingSafeEqual,
identical to the Bearer path; no new comparison semantics.

  including 6 new SSE cases:
  * ?token=<good> + Accept: text/event-stream + flag on -> authorized
  * ?token=<wrong> + same setup -> 401
  * ?token=<good> but flag unset -> 401 (non-cloud deploys stay locked)
  * ?token=<good> but Accept: application/json -> 401 (SSE-scope only)
  * POST + SSE Accept + ?token=<good> -> 401 (read-only safety)
  * Bearer takes precedence over ?token= when both present

fix(cloud): pass WS auth token via query param so cloud staging WS handshake succeeds

WHY
The SPA in packages/ui/src/api/client-base.ts opens `new WebSocket(ws://<host>/ws?clientId=...)` with no auth in the URL. Browsers cannot set the Authorization header on `new WebSocket(url)`, so the only handshake-time channel is the query string. Cloud-provisioned containers set ELIZA_ALLOW_WS_QUERY_TOKEN=1 (see packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services/managed-eliza-config.ts) and require a handshake token because there is no trusted upstream proxy authenticating the upgrade. Result on staging: every WS upgrade hits resolveWebSocketUpgradeRejection() with no handshake token and is rejected 401, blocking the realtime channel for every managed agent.

A second, latent issue made the obvious client-side fix risky: server-auth.ts and server-helpers-auth.ts (two near-duplicate copies kept in sync) actively *rejected* upgrades whose URL carried a token when ELIZA_ALLOW_WS_QUERY_TOKEN was unset — so adding the token blindly would 401 every self-hosted user who had ELIZA_API_TOKEN set but not the WS flag.

WHAT
- packages/ui/src/api/client-base.ts (connectWs): append `?token=<apiToken>` (URLSearchParams handles encoding) when an apiToken is available. The post-open `{type:"auth"}` send stays as the fallback for non-cloud servers where the query token is ignored.
- packages/agent/src/api/server-auth.ts and packages/agent/src/api/server-helpers-auth.ts: drop the `if (flag !== "1" && hasWsQueryToken) return 401` veto. extractWsQueryToken() already returns null when the flag is off, so handshakeToken cleanly falls back to header-or-null. The veto only existed to surface mis-config and now actively breaks any client that cannot set Authorization on a WebSocket — i.e. every browser.

After both changes: cloud staging unblocks (query token consumed during handshake), prod stays green (same code path), self-hosted users see no behavior change (their token is ignored at handshake, post-open auth still works).

TEST PLAN
- Staging: open a cloud-provisioned agent in the SPA; confirm WS connects (no 401 in network log on `/ws`), realtime events flow, no reconnect storm.
- Self-hosted with ELIZA_API_TOKEN set and ELIZA_ALLOW_WS_QUERY_TOKEN unset: confirm WS still connects via the post-open `{type:"auth"}` path (server ignores the URL token, handshake passes with no token because no isCloudProvisionedContainer, post-open auth message authorizes the session).
- Self-hosted with no ELIZA_API_TOKEN: confirm WS connects as before (no token sent, expected=null path).

fix(cloud): provision agents via Steward platform-key path

The daemon was hitting `POST /agents` (tenant-scoped) which Steward gates
behind `requireTenantAdminSession`:

  authType === "session-jwt" && (tenantRole === "owner" | "admin")

A backend daemon doesn't have a session-jwt and can't impersonate a
tenant owner. Steward exposes the right endpoints for this exact use
case (commented "Used by platform operators, e.g. Milady Cloud
provisioner"):

  POST   /platform/tenants/:id/agents               (scope: platform:agent:create)
  POST   /platform/tenants/:id/agents/:id/token     (scope: platform:agent-token:create)
  DELETE /platform/tenants/:id/agents/:id           (scope: platform:agent:delete)

These authenticate via `X-Steward-Platform-Key` (scoped via
`STEWARD_PLATFORM_KEY_SCOPES` JSON map on the Steward backend) and
bypass the session-jwt gate.

Switch `registerAgentWithSteward` + `buildSignedDeleteAgentCurl` to
these paths. Read `STEWARD_PLATFORM_KEY` (or `STEWARD_PLATFORM_KEYS`,
first entry) from the daemon env. The tenant `X-Steward-Key` header is
dropped — the platform key now carries the auth context, scoped to
exactly what a provisioner needs.

Signing chain is unchanged: `signStewardMutatingRequest` builds the
canonical request, the platform-key hash slot picks up the actual
header value via `headers.get("x-steward-platform-key")` (already
hashed by the shared helper in cloud-shared/lib/steward/sign.ts).

Tested live before this commit: with `STEWARD_PLATFORM_KEY_SCOPES`
configured on Steward Railway (granting platform:* to our key), the
POST returns 201 Created and Steward provisions EVM + Solana wallets
for the agent.

Pre-req for the merge: set
  STEWARD_PLATFORM_KEY_SCOPES = {"<keyHashOrRaw>":["platform:*"]}
on the Steward backend (env var on steward-eliza/steward-api Railway
service) — done for production. Same value needs to land on any
staging-isolated Steward deployment.

fix(cloud): align Steward agent register/cleanup signing with shared helper

The daemon's Steward agent registration and the two best-effort
cleanup DELETEs were rolling their own HMAC canonical request via a
local `buildStewardCanonicalRequest` that included an
`X-Steward-Request-Timestamp` field. Upstream Steward's
authorization-signature middleware (which `cloud-api/src/steward/sign.ts`
already mirrors correctly for the Worker bypass routes) does NOT include
that header in the canonical hash, so daemon-signed requests verify as
invalid signature. Steward then falls through to the session-owner
check and returns 403 "owner or admin session required" — the exact
error blocking Dedicated agent provisioning on staging today.

Move the working `signStewardMutatingRequest` helper from cloud-api to
cloud-shared (`lib/steward/sign.ts`) so the daemon can use the same
canonical-request shape as the Worker. Replace the local
`buildStewardCanonicalRequest` / `buildStewardSignedHeaders` in
`docker-sandbox-provider.ts` with calls to the shared helper, and add a
small `buildSignedDeleteAgentCurl` wrapper for the two cleanup-path
curls that were sending DELETE with no signing at all (which is why
failed registrations stayed as Steward ghost records and the dashboard
shows agents stuck in `deletion_pending`).

Worker imports (`auth/steward-refresh`, `auth/steward-nonce-exchange`)
are repointed at the new shared location. The unit test
(`__tests__/steward-sign.test.ts`) follows.

registrations without calling Cloudflare. The domains/buy route debits the org's

shouldBlockUnsafeWebhookSkip footgun guards) throws from the registrar and DNS

checkAvailability() before any credit debit, so a misconfigured prod fails loudly
with no charge instead of silently faking registrations. Dev/test/staging
(NODE_ENV=test, ENVIRONMENT!=production) keep using the stub unchanged.

fix(core): bound the rolling-summary prompt and first-store offset

the advanced-memory summaryEvaluator had two coupled bugs that surface in busy
rooms:

1. prompt() rendered the full allDialogueMessages (fetched with limit:1000,
   unbounded by tokens) on the no-existing-summary branch, while the stored
   lastMessageOffset only advances by summaryMaxNewMessages (default 50 /
   service config 20). a busy room's first summary therefore sent
   multi-million-token requests -> context_length_exceeded 400 -> the summary
   never stored -> the same oversized request retried forever, and messages were
   double-counted on the next run.

2. the first store set lastMessageOffset = totalDialogueCount (the whole backlog)
   while only the bounded slice was summarized, so every message past the slice
   was silently skipped on subsequent runs.

fix: always prompt with the bounded summarizationMessages slice, and advance the
first-store offset/messageCount by that slice (matching the existing-summary
branch's newOffset) so the rolling summary builds up incrementally and bounded.
drop the now-unused allDialogueMessages field from SummaryPrepared. add
regression tests for the bounded prompt and the first-store offset.

New `@elizaos/cloud-sdk/app-auth` sub-export: a small, dependency-free client
for third-party apps to authenticate their users through Eliza Cloud, wrapping
the already-live app-auth flow.

Flow (no PKCE — consent is gated by the user's existing Eliza Cloud session and
redirect_uri is validated against the app's allowed origins):
  1. buildAppAuthorizeUrl({ appId, redirectUri, state })
       → https://www.elizacloud.ai/app-auth/authorize?app_id=…&redirect_uri=…&state=…
  2. Eliza redirects back: <redirectUri>?code=eac_…&state=…  (or ?error=access_denied)
  3. exchangeAppAuthorizeCode(code)
       → GET /api/v1/app-auth/session (Authorization: Bearer eac_…)
       → { user: { id, email, name, avatar, createdAt }, app }

parseCallback / exchangeCode / completeSignIn) plus standalone functions,
`ElizaCloudAuthError`, and the `APP_AUTH_*` constants. All accept an optional
`fetchImpl` / `baseUrl` / `apiBaseUrl` for tests and custom origins. Built and
verified against the real connect/session route + consent-page contract.

15 unit tests (URL build, callback parse across input shapes, code exchange +
header/binding assertions, error paths). Pure TS, zero new deps.

This is slice 1 of the "Eliza Cloud Apps" direction (turnkey auth for hosted
apps); it touches no server/data-plane code.

fix(cloud): accept ?token= on SSE GETs so EventSource clients can authenticate (#8309)

WHY:
EventSource (the browser SSE client) cannot set request headers, so it has
no way to send `Authorization: Bearer <ELIZA_API_TOKEN>`. The global auth
gate in server.ts only inspects headers via extractAuthToken(req), so every
SSE handshake from the cloud web UI 401s before the route handler runs
(local-inference + computer-use stream endpoints inherit the same gate).
The token itself is correct -- it's the same `agent_<uuid>` value the REST
chat path accepts as a Bearer -- only the transport is wrong.

WHAT:
Extend extractAuthToken() with a tightly-scoped SSE query-token fallback,
mirroring the existing ELIZA_ALLOW_WS_QUERY_TOKEN=1 path that already ships
for WebSockets. The fallback is gated on:
  - ELIZA_ALLOW_WS_QUERY_TOKEN=1 (cloud-only opt-in, no regression elsewhere),
  - method === GET (read-only),
  - Accept header contains text/event-stream (scope strictly to SSE so a
    stray ?token= on a JSON endpoint cannot bypass the header path or leak
    via proxy access logs),
  - token length <= 1024 (mirrors the header cap).
Validation still goes through tokenMatches() -> crypto.timingSafeEqual,
identical to the Bearer path; no new comparison semantics.

TEST PLAN:
- bunx vitest run test/api/server-helpers-auth.test.ts -> 21/21 pass,
  including 6 new SSE cases:
  * ?token=<good> + Accept: text/event-stream + flag on -> authorized
  * ?token=<wrong> + same setup -> 401
  * ?token=<good> but flag unset -> 401 (non-cloud deploys stay locked)
  * ?token=<good> but Accept: application/json -> 401 (SSE-scope only)
  * POST + SSE Accept + ?token=<good> -> 401 (read-only safety)
  * Bearer takes precedence over ?token= when both present

fix(cloud): pass WS auth token via query param so cloud staging WS handshake succeeds (#8308)

WHY
The SPA in packages/ui/src/api/client-base.ts opens `new WebSocket(ws://<host>/ws?clientId=...)` with no auth in the URL. Browsers cannot set the Authorization header on `new WebSocket(url)`, so the only handshake-time channel is the query string. Cloud-provisioned containers set ELIZA_ALLOW_WS_QUERY_TOKEN=1 (see packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services/managed-eliza-config.ts) and require a handshake token because there is no trusted upstream proxy authenticating the upgrade. Result on staging: every WS upgrade hits resolveWebSocketUpgradeRejection() with no handshake token and is rejected 401, blocking the realtime channel for every managed agent.

A second, latent issue made the obvious client-side fix risky: server-auth.ts and server-helpers-auth.ts (two near-duplicate copies kept in sync) actively *rejected* upgrades whose URL carried a token when ELIZA_ALLOW_WS_QUERY_TOKEN was unset — so adding the token blindly would 401 every self-hosted user who had ELIZA_API_TOKEN set but not the WS flag.

WHAT
- packages/ui/src/api/client-base.ts (connectWs): append `?token=<apiToken>` (URLSearchParams handles encoding) when an apiToken is available. The post-open `{type:"auth"}` send stays as the fallback for non-cloud servers where the query token is ignored.
- packages/agent/src/api/server-auth.ts and packages/agent/src/api/server-helpers-auth.ts: drop the `if (flag !== "1" && hasWsQueryToken) return 401` veto. extractWsQueryToken() already returns null when the flag is off, so handshakeToken cleanly falls back to header-or-null. The veto only existed to surface mis-config and now actively breaks any client that cannot set Authorization on a WebSocket — i.e. every browser.

After both changes: cloud staging unblocks (query token consumed during handshake), prod stays green (same code path), self-hosted users see no behavior change (their token is ignored at handshake, post-open auth still works).

TEST PLAN

- Self-hosted with ELIZA_API_TOKEN set and ELIZA_ALLOW_WS_QUERY_TOKEN unset: confirm WS still connects via the post-open `{type:"auth"}` path (server ignores the URL token, handshake passes with no token because no isCloudProvisionedContainer, post-open auth message authorizes the session).
- Self-hosted with no ELIZA_API_TOKEN: confirm WS connects as before (no token sent, expected=null path).

fix(cloud): provision agents via Steward platform-key path (#8301)

The daemon was hitting `POST /agents` (tenant-scoped) which Steward gates
behind `requireTenantAdminSession`:

  authType === "session-jwt" && (tenantRole === "owner" | "admin")

A backend daemon doesn't have a session-jwt and can't impersonate a
tenant owner. Steward exposes the right endpoints for this exact use
case (commented "Used by platform operators, e.g. Milady Cloud
provisioner"):

  POST   /platform/tenants/:id/agents               (scope: platform:agent:create)
  POST   /platform/tenants/:id/agents/:id/token     (scope: platform:agent-token:create)
  DELETE /platform/tenants/:id/agents/:id           (scope: platform:agent:delete)

These authenticate via `X-Steward-Platform-Key` (scoped via
`STEWARD_PLATFORM_KEY_SCOPES` JSON map on the Steward backend) and
bypass the session-jwt gate.

Switch `registerAgentWithSteward` + `buildSignedDeleteAgentCurl` to
these paths. Read `STEWARD_PLATFORM_KEY` (or `STEWARD_PLATFORM_KEYS`,
first entry) from the daemon env. The tenant `X-Steward-Key` header is
dropped — the platform key now carries the auth context, scoped to
exactly what a provisioner needs.

Signing chain is unchanged: `signStewardMutatingRequest` builds the
canonical request, the platform-key hash slot picks up the actual
header value via `headers.get("x-steward-platform-key")` (already
hashed by the shared helper in cloud-shared/lib/steward/sign.ts).

Tested live before this commit: with `STEWARD_PLATFORM_KEY_SCOPES`
configured on Steward Railway (granting platform:* to our key), the
POST returns 201 Created and Steward provisions EVM + Solana wallets
for the agent.

Pre-req for the merge: set
  STEWARD_PLATFORM_KEY_SCOPES = {"<keyHashOrRaw>":["platform:*"]}
on the Steward backend (env var on steward-eliza/steward-api Railway
service) — done for production. Same value needs to land on any
staging-isolated Steward deployment.

feat(apps): tenant-DB teardown — deprovision + release slot on cleanup

Closes the isolated-DB leak half of #8342: deleting an app with its own
per-tenant Postgres never DROPped the DATABASE/ROLE and never released the
cluster slot (`deprovision` had zero callers; there was no `releaseSlot` —
only `tryClaimSlot` incremented). So every deleted isolated app stranded a
live DB we keep paying for AND burned one of the cluster's finite slots
forever.

- `tenantDbClustersRepository.releaseSlot(clusterId)` — the counterpart to
  `tryClaimSlot`, `GREATEST(0, count-1)` so a double-release can't go
  negative — plus `findByHost(host)` to resolve the owning cluster from the
  host in the app's stored DSN.
- `deprovisionTenantDbForApp` (pure, DI'd) — parse the DSN host, resolve the
  cluster, DROP the DB+role, THEN release the slot (order matters: a failed
  DROP leaves the slot counted, never frees a slot for a live DB). Fail-safe
  no-ops for a shared/unknown DSN.
- `SqlTenantDbProvisioning.deprovisionForApp` wires it over the repo +
  admin executor; `make-tenant-db-provisioning` injects the real backends.
- `UserDatabaseService.cleanupDatabase` now tears down the isolated path
  (previously Neon-only) when the provisioning backend is wired (the daemon
  — DROP needs `pg`); Worker-side it's a no-op.

Tests: DSN-host parse, drop-then-release order, fail-safe no-ops, the
composer path, and the not-configured guard. 31 pass / 0 fail; typecheck +
biome clean.

NOTE: the deprovision fires when cleanupDatabase runs on the DAEMON. Wiring
app-delete to trigger a daemon-side cleanup (an enqueue) is the final
integration step — gated on the live daemon, like the rest of the apps lane.

feat(apps): make the per-tenant database opt-in (mode none|isolated)

The deploy orchestrator unconditionally provisioned an isolated per-tenant
Postgres for every app and injected DATABASE_URL/POSTGRES_URL. That forces
a database (and a tenant-DB cluster) on apps that don't need one — e.g. a
stateless SPA + stateless API like elocute.

Make the database a per-app choice via `apps.metadata.databaseMode`
(jsonb — no schema migration):
  - "none" (DEFAULT): stateless — no DB provisioned, no DATABASE_URL.
  - "isolated": the app's OWN per-tenant Postgres, injected under both vars.

`deployApp` reads the mode and only calls `ensureTenantDb` (and injects the
DSN) when isolated; the DefaultAppDeployRunner resolves the mode from the
app. The load-bearing invariant is preserved: an isolated app gets its OWN
DSN under DATABASE_URL + POSTGRES_URL, never the shared agent URL and never
a silent fallback.

Add-a-DB-later is seamless and lossless: PUT /api/v1/apps/:id/database
{mode:"isolated"} then redeploy — `ensureTenantDb` is create-if-not-exists,
so the DB materializes and wires in; flipping back to "none" stops
injecting the DSN but leaves the database intact (destroying tenant data is
a separate explicit action). The endpoint is Worker-safe (only writes the
metadata flag; provisioning happens on the next deploy on the daemon).

Tests: pure mode resolver (default/garbage -> none); orchestrator both
paths (isolated -> ensureTenantDb + both DSN vars; none -> no provision, no
DATABASE_URL, deploy still succeeds). 9/9 green, 100% line coverage on the
new + changed service files; typecheck + biome clean.

the buy/verify flow all exist), but nothing ever served it — the domain

import) and the whole path is still gated on APPS_CADDY_ADMIN_URL (no-op

fix(apps): inject the tenant DSN under both DATABASE_URL and POSTGRES_URL

Closes the P0 isolation-contract gap from the apps scaling audit (#8321 item 3).
The deploy injected ONLY DATABASE_URL. Eliza-based images map DATABASE_URL ->
POSTGRES_URL, but the product is ARBITRARY user apps — and plugin-sql + many app
images read POSTGRES_URL directly. Such an app would miss its isolated DB and
silently fall back to a throwaway local store, so per-tenant isolation would not
actually be active for it.

- app-deploy-orchestrator: inject the per-tenant DSN under BOTH DATABASE_URL and
  POSTGRES_URL, so an app hits its isolated DB whichever var it reads.
- app-container-provider: the DB ambassador now rewrites BOTH vars to the
  ambassador host (an un-rewritten POSTGRES_URL would target the real cluster
  host, which is unreachable from the app's --internal network — a real bug the
  single-var rewrite would have introduced alongside this change).

Tests: orchestrator asserts both vars carry the isolated DSN; provider asserts
both are rewritten to the ambassador and neither points at the cluster host.
17/17 pass, biome + typecheck clean.

fix(ci/docker): hoist plugin-wallet transitives so @lifi/sdk resolves in runtime image (#8333)

Root cause: plugin-wallet was added to the build-agent-image workflow in
PR #8331 but never added to the two hand-maintained lists that drive the
Docker runtime closure — LINKED_WORKSPACE_PACKAGES in
collect-docker-runtime-deps.mjs (which emits the install specifiers npm
resolves into /app/node_modules) and localPackages in
link-docker-local-app-packages.mjs (which symlinks the workspace folder
into /app/node_modules/@elizaos/*). The two lists already carry an
explicit "MUST stay in sync" warning at the head of the collector script;
this PR restores that invariant for plugin-wallet.

Without these entries, @lifi/sdk (declared in exactly one package —
plugins/plugin-wallet/package.json) and the 10+ other wallet-only deps
(@coral-xyz/anchor, @meteora-ag/dlmm, @raydium-io/raydium-sdk,
@solana/spl-token, @steerprotocol/sdk, bignumber.js, bs58, ethers,
tweetnacl, viem, ...) never land in the runtime image and the agent
boots crash on import "@lifi/sdk". plugin-elizacloud avoids the problem
only because its transitives also leak in via other workspaces in the
list.

Chosen fix shape (D, minimum surface): add "plugins/plugin-wallet" to
both arrays, alphabetical slot between plugin-video and plugin-whatsapp.
No new dependency declarations, no Dockerfile changes — the existing
derived-closure machinery picks everything up automatically.

Test plan:
- node packages/app-core/scripts/collect-docker-runtime-deps.mjs |
  grep -E '@lifi/sdk|@coral-xyz/anchor|@meteora-ag/dlmm|...' confirms
  all wallet third-party deps are emitted (13 deps verified locally,
  total count 124 -> 132 across 40 -> 41 linked packages)
- The build-agent-image workflow's boot-verify step exercises the real
  entrypoint and will surface any remaining missing transitives.

Follow-up (not in this PR): the two hand-maintained lists are a recurring
drift source. Worth factoring them into a single shared constant module
to prevent this class of regression entirely.
